# Awesome SwiftUI Components: every component with its source

Copy-paste SwiftUI components for iOS 18 through iOS 27. Swift 6, MIT. A component with a shader has two files: copy both.

## Breathing Guide Circle

A circle that expands and contracts through breathe in, hold and breathe out phases, with a label and a countdown.

Category: Animations. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Animations/BreathingGuideCircle/BreathingGuideCircle.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum BreathingGuideCirclePhase: String {
    case inhale = "Breathe In"
    case hold = "Hold"
    case exhale = "Breathe Out"
}

struct BreathingGuideCircleState: Equatable {
    let phase: BreathingGuideCirclePhase
    let secondsLeft: Int
    /// 0 is fully contracted and 1 is fully expanded.
    let expansion: Double
}

enum BreathingGuideCircleMath {
    /// Where the cycle is after `elapsed` seconds. Invalid durations count as zero.
    static func state(at elapsed: TimeInterval, inhale: Double, hold: Double, exhale: Double) -> BreathingGuideCircleState {
        let inhale = sanitized(inhale)
        let hold = sanitized(hold)
        let exhale = sanitized(exhale)
        let total = inhale + hold + exhale
        guard total > 0, elapsed.isFinite else {
            return BreathingGuideCircleState(phase: .inhale, secondsLeft: 0, expansion: 0)
        }

        var time = elapsed.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: total)
        if time < 0 { time += total }

        if time < inhale {
            return BreathingGuideCircleState(phase: .inhale, secondsLeft: Int((inhale - time).rounded(.up)), expansion: eased(time / inhale))
        }
        time -= inhale
        if time < hold {
            return BreathingGuideCircleState(phase: .hold, secondsLeft: Int((hold - time).rounded(.up)), expansion: 1)
        }
        time -= hold
        let progress = exhale > 0 ? min(time / exhale, 1) : 1
        return BreathingGuideCircleState(phase: .exhale, secondsLeft: Int((exhale - time).rounded(.up)), expansion: 1 - eased(progress))
    }

    private static func sanitized(_ duration: Double) -> Double {
        duration.isFinite ? min(max(duration, 0), 3_600) : 0
    }

    private static func eased(_ progress: Double) -> Double {
        progress * progress * (3 - 2 * progress)
    }
}

/// A circle that expands and contracts through breathing phases, with a label and a countdown.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the circle stays still and the label keeps guiding.
struct BreathingGuideCircle: View {
    var inhale = 4.0
    var hold = 4.0
    var exhale = 6.0
    var tint: Color = .teal
    var diameter: CGFloat = 260

    @State private var start = Date.now
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// How much the scale of every ring grows from contracted to expanded.
    private let ringGrowth = 0.38

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: reduceMotion ? 0.25 : 1.0 / 30.0)) { timeline in
            let state = BreathingGuideCircleMath.state(
                at: timeline.date.timeIntervalSince(start),
                inhale: inhale,
                hold: hold,
                exhale: exhale
            )

            VStack(spacing: 36) {
                circle(expansion: reduceMotion ? 0.6 : state.expansion)

                VStack(spacing: 6) {
                    Text(state.phase.rawValue)
                        .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .semibold))
                        .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                    Text(state.secondsLeft, format: .number)
                        .font(.system(.title2, design: .rounded).monospacedDigit())
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
            }
            .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
            .accessibilityLabel("Breathing guide")
            .accessibilityValue(state.phase.rawValue)
        }
    }

    private func circle(expansion: Double) -> some View {
        let size = max(diameter, 0)

        return ZStack {
            Circle()
                .fill(tint.opacity(0.14))
                .scaleEffect(0.62 + ringGrowth * expansion)
            Circle()
                .fill(tint.opacity(0.26))
                .scaleEffect(0.5 + ringGrowth * expansion)
            Circle()
                .fill(.linearGradient(colors: [tint, .blue], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
                .scaleEffect(0.38 + ringGrowth * expansion)
        }
        .frame(width: size, height: size)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct BreathingGuideCircleDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        BreathingGuideCircle(inhale: 1.6, hold: 0.8, exhale: 1.6)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
    }
}

#Preview {
    BreathingGuideCircleDemo()
}
```

## Keyframe Timeline Showcase

A view animated by keyframe tracks for scale, offset and color, with the tracks and a playhead drawn on one shared timeline.

Category: Animations. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Animations/KeyframeTimelineShowcase/KeyframeTimelineShowcase.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct KeyframeTimelineShowcaseValues {
    var scale = 1.0
    var offset = 0.0
    var tint = 0.0
    var playhead = 0.0
}

/// The length of each keyframe in seconds. Every track adds up to the same total, so the loop closes.
private enum KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming {
    static let scale = [0.3, 0.45, 0.35, 0.9]
    static let offset = [0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.8]
    static let tint = [0.75, 0.5, 0.75]
    static let total = 2.0

    static func ticks(_ durations: [Double]) -> [Double] {
        var elapsed = 0.0
        return durations.map { duration in
            elapsed += duration
            return elapsed / total
        }
    }
}

/// Plays scale, offset and color tracks on one shared keyframe timeline, and draws the tracks below.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the content rests and the timeline stays still.
struct KeyframeTimelineShowcase<Content: View>: View {
    var restColor: Color = .indigo
    var peakColor: Color = .pink
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var tileSize = 120.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            stage(KeyframeTimelineShowcaseValues())
        } else {
            KeyframeAnimator(initialValue: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseValues(), repeating: true) { values in
                stage(values)
            } keyframes: { _ in
                KeyframeTrack(\.scale) {
                    CubicKeyframe(0.8, duration: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.scale[0])
                    SpringKeyframe(1.25, duration: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.scale[1], spring: .bouncy)
                    CubicKeyframe(0.92, duration: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.scale[2])
                    SpringKeyframe(1, duration: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.scale[3], spring: .bouncy)
                }
                KeyframeTrack(\.offset) {
                    LinearKeyframe(0, duration: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.offset[0])
                    CubicKeyframe(-90, duration: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.offset[1])
                    CubicKeyframe(0, duration: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.offset[2])
                    LinearKeyframe(0, duration: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.offset[3])
                }
                KeyframeTrack(\.tint) {
                    CubicKeyframe(1, duration: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.tint[0])
                    LinearKeyframe(1, duration: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.tint[1])
                    CubicKeyframe(0, duration: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.tint[2])
                }
                KeyframeTrack(\.playhead) {
                    // Each loop starts from the last value, so the playhead has to jump back.
                    MoveKeyframe(0)
                    LinearKeyframe(1, duration: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.total)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private func stage(_ values: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseValues) -> some View {
        VStack(spacing: 32) {
            content()
                .frame(width: tileSize, height: tileSize)
                .background(
                    restColor.mix(with: peakColor, by: values.tint),
                    in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: tileSize * 0.26, style: .continuous)
                )
                .scaleEffect(values.scale)
                .offset(y: values.offset)
                .frame(height: tileSize + 150, alignment: .bottom)

            VStack(spacing: 12) {
                lane("Scale", color: .orange, ticks: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.ticks(KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.scale))
                lane("Offset", color: .teal, ticks: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.ticks(KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.offset))
                lane("Color", color: peakColor, ticks: KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.ticks(KeyframeTimelineShowcaseTiming.tint))
            }
            .overlay(alignment: .leading) {
                GeometryReader { proxy in
                    Capsule()
                        .fill(.primary)
                        .frame(width: 2)
                        .offset(x: proxy.size.width * values.playhead - 1)
                }
            }
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
    }

    private func lane(_ title: String, color: Color, ticks: [Double]) -> some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
            Text(title)
                .font(.caption.weight(.semibold))
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)

            Canvas { context, size in
                let track = CGRect(x: 0, y: size.height / 2 - 2, width: size.width, height: 4)
                context.fill(Path(roundedRect: track, cornerRadius: 2), with: .color(color.opacity(0.3)))
                for tick in ticks {
                    let dot = CGRect(x: size.width * tick - 5, y: size.height / 2 - 5, width: 10, height: 10)
                    context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: dot), with: .color(color))
                }
            }
            .frame(height: 12)
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct KeyframeTimelineShowcaseDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        KeyframeTimelineShowcase {
            Image(systemName: "sparkles")
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .accessibilityLabel("Animated tile")
        }
        .padding(28)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
    }
}

#Preview {
    KeyframeTimelineShowcaseDemo()
}
```

## Phase Animator Cycle

A card that loops through several phases of scale, rotation and color.

Category: Animations. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Animations/PhaseAnimatorCycle/PhaseAnimatorCycle.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

private enum PhaseAnimatorCyclePhase: CaseIterable {
    case rest, lift, tilt, shrink

    var scale: Double {
        switch self {
        case .rest: 1
        case .lift: 1.14
        case .tilt: 1.04
        case .shrink: 0.88
        }
    }

    var rotation: Angle {
        switch self {
        case .rest: .zero
        case .lift: .degrees(-7)
        case .tilt: .degrees(9)
        case .shrink: .degrees(-3)
        }
    }

    var color: Color {
        switch self {
        case .rest: .indigo
        case .lift: .purple
        case .tilt: .pink
        case .shrink: .orange
        }
    }

    var animation: Animation {
        switch self {
        case .rest, .tilt: .spring(duration: 0.6, bounce: 0.4)
        case .lift, .shrink: .easeInOut(duration: 0.55)
        }
    }
}

/// A card that loops through phases of scale, rotation and color.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the card stays in its first phase.
struct PhaseAnimatorCycle<Content: View>: View {
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat = 32
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            card(.rest)
        } else {
            PhaseAnimator(PhaseAnimatorCyclePhase.allCases) { phase in
                card(phase)
            } animation: { phase in
                phase.animation
            }
        }
    }

    private func card(_ phase: PhaseAnimatorCyclePhase) -> some View {
        content()
            .background {
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: max(0, cornerRadius), style: .continuous)
                    .fill(phase.color)
                    .overlay {
                        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: max(0, cornerRadius), style: .continuous)
                            .fill(.linearGradient(colors: [.white.opacity(0.3), .clear], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
                    }
                    .shadow(color: phase.color.opacity(0.45), radius: 24, y: 14)
            }
            .scaleEffect(phase.scale)
            .rotationEffect(phase.rotation)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct PhaseAnimatorCycleDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        PhaseAnimatorCycle {
            VStack(spacing: 14) {
                Image(systemName: "wand.and.stars")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                Text("Four phases, one loop")
                    .font(.system(.title3, design: .rounded, weight: .semibold))
                    .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .padding(.horizontal, 32)
            .padding(.vertical, 56)
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
    }
}

#Preview {
    PhaseAnimatorCycleDemo()
}
```

## Split Flap Counter

A split-flap display where each digit flips down to its new value.

Category: Animations. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Animations/SplitFlapCounter/SplitFlapCounter.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum SplitFlapCounterMath {
    /// More places than any `Int` needs, so a huge `minimumDigits` cannot allocate without limit.
    static let maximumDigits = 20

    /// One cell per character, padded with zeros on the left and with a leading minus when negative.
    static func cells(for value: Int, minimumDigits: Int) -> [String] {
        let digits = String(value.magnitude).map(String.init)
        let wanted = min(max(minimumDigits, 0), maximumDigits)
        let padding = max(0, wanted - digits.count)
        return (value < 0 ? ["-"] : []) + Array(repeating: "0", count: padding) + digits
    }
}

/// A split-flap display where each digit flips down to its new value.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, digits change without flipping.
struct SplitFlapCounter: View {
    let value: Int
    var minimumDigits = 1

    var body: some View {
        let cells = SplitFlapCounterMath.cells(for: value, minimumDigits: minimumDigits)

        ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
            row(cells)
            ScrollView(.horizontal, showsIndicators: false) {
                row(cells)
            }
        }
        .accessibilityRepresentation { Text(value.formatted()) }
    }

    private func row(_ cells: [String]) -> some View {
        // Identified by their place from the right, so the units stay put when the number grows.
        HStack(spacing: 6) {
            ForEach(Array(cells.indices.reversed()), id: \.self) { place in
                SplitFlapCounterCell(text: cells[cells.count - 1 - place])
            }
        }
    }
}

private struct SplitFlapCounterCell: View {
    let text: String

    @State private var shown: String
    @State private var previous: String
    @State private var flips = 0.0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var height = 92.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    init(text: String) {
        self.text = text
        _shown = State(initialValue: text)
        _previous = State(initialValue: text)
    }

    var body: some View {
        SplitFlapCounterFace(flips: flips, shown: shown, previous: previous, height: height)
            .onChange(of: text) { _, newText in
                if reduceMotion {
                    previous = newText
                    shown = newText
                } else {
                    previous = shown
                    shown = newText
                    withAnimation(.easeIn(duration: 0.42)) { flips += 1 }
                }
            }
    }
}

/// `flips` grows by one per change. Its fractional part is how far the current flip has gone.
private struct SplitFlapCounterFace: View, Animatable {
    var flips: Double
    let shown: String
    let previous: String
    let height: Double

    nonisolated var animatableData: Double {
        get { flips }
        set { flips = newValue }
    }

    var body: some View {
        let progress = flips - flips.rounded(.down)
        let isFlipping = progress > 0
        let topAngle = isFlipping ? -180 * min(progress, 0.5) : -90
        let bottomAngle = isFlipping ? 180 * (1 - max(progress, 0.5)) : 0

        ZStack {
            VStack(spacing: 2) {
                half(shown, isTop: true)
                half(isFlipping ? previous : shown, isTop: false)
            }

            VStack(spacing: 2) {
                half(previous, isTop: true)
                    .brightness(-0.25 * min(progress * 2, 1))
                    .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(topAngle), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0), anchor: .bottom, perspective: 0.5)
                    .opacity(topAngle > -90 ? 1 : 0)
                half(shown, isTop: false)
                    .brightness(isFlipping ? -0.25 * (1 - progress) : 0)
                    .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(bottomAngle), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0), anchor: .top, perspective: 0.5)
                    .opacity(bottomAngle < 90 ? 1 : 0)
            }
        }
    }

    private func half(_ text: String, isTop: Bool) -> some View {
        let radius = height * 0.1

        return Text(text)
            .font(.system(size: height * 0.68, weight: .bold, design: .rounded).monospacedDigit())
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .frame(width: height * 0.68, height: height)
            .frame(height: height / 2, alignment: isTop ? .top : .bottom)
            .clipped()
            .background(
                Color(white: isTop ? 0.2 : 0.16),
                in: UnevenRoundedRectangle(
                    topLeadingRadius: isTop ? radius : 0,
                    bottomLeadingRadius: isTop ? 0 : radius,
                    bottomTrailingRadius: isTop ? 0 : radius,
                    topTrailingRadius: isTop ? radius : 0,
                    style: .continuous
                )
            )
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SplitFlapCounterDemo: View {
    @State private var value = 1_284
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 24) {
            Text("Passengers today")
                .font(.system(.title3, design: .rounded, weight: .semibold))
                .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.7))

            SplitFlapCounter(value: value, minimumDigits: 5)
                .padding(.horizontal, 16)
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(white: 0.06))
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                value += 37
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    SplitFlapCounterDemo()
}
```

## Spring Study Playground

Sliders for response and damping that show how a spring moves a view and draw its curve.

Category: Animations. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Animations/SpringStudyPlayground/SpringStudyPlayground.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum SpringStudyPlaygroundMath {
    static let responseRange = 0.1...1.5
    static let dampingRange = 0.1...1.0

    static func clamped(_ value: Double, to range: ClosedRange<Double>) -> Double {
        value.isNaN ? range.lowerBound : min(max(value, range.lowerBound), range.upperBound)
    }

    /// The position of a spring going from 0 to 1, sampled evenly over `duration` seconds.
    static func samples(response: Double, damping: Double, count: Int, duration: Double) -> [Double] {
        guard count > 1, duration > 0, duration.isFinite else { return [] }
        let spring = Spring(
            response: clamped(response, to: responseRange),
            dampingRatio: clamped(damping, to: dampingRange)
        )
        let last = min(count, 512) - 1
        return (0...last).map { spring.value(target: 1.0, time: duration * Double($0) / Double(last)) }
    }
}

nonisolated private struct SpringStudyPlaygroundCurve: Shape {
    let samples: [Double]
    let maximum: Double

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        var path = Path()
        guard samples.count > 1, maximum > 0 else { return path }
        let points = samples.enumerated().map { index, value in
            CGPoint(
                x: rect.minX + rect.width * Double(index) / Double(samples.count - 1),
                y: rect.maxY - rect.height * value / maximum
            )
        }
        path.addLines(points)
        return path
    }
}

/// Sliders for response and damping that show how a spring moves a view, with its curve drawn below.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the ball jumps and the curve still shows what the spring would do.
struct SpringStudyPlayground: View {
    private enum Preset: String, CaseIterable, Identifiable {
        case smooth = "Smooth"
        case bouncy = "Bouncy"
        case stiff = "Stiff"

        var id: Self { self }

        var values: (response: Double, damping: Double) {
            switch self {
            case .smooth: (0.8, 1)
            case .bouncy: (0.75, 0.3)
            case .stiff: (0.2, 0.75)
            }
        }
    }

    /// The curve's scale. A spring with the lowest damping overshoots to almost this.
    private static let curveMaximum = 1.9
    private static let presetSpacing: CGFloat = 10

    @State private var response: Double
    @State private var damping: Double
    @State private var isAtEnd = false
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title2) private var ballSize = 44.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    init(response: Double = 0.55, damping: Double = 0.55) {
        _response = State(initialValue: SpringStudyPlaygroundMath.clamped(response, to: SpringStudyPlaygroundMath.responseRange))
        _damping = State(initialValue: SpringStudyPlaygroundMath.clamped(damping, to: SpringStudyPlaygroundMath.dampingRange))
    }

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(spacing: 24) {
                stage
                curve
                slider("Response", value: $response, range: SpringStudyPlaygroundMath.responseRange, unit: " s")
                slider("Damping", value: $damping, range: SpringStudyPlaygroundMath.dampingRange, unit: "")
                presets
            }
            .padding(20)
        }
    }

    private var stage: some View {
        Circle()
            .fill(.linearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
            .frame(width: ballSize, height: ballSize)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: isAtEnd ? .trailing : .leading)
            .padding(10)
            .background(.quaternary, in: Capsule())
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private var curve: some View {
        let samples = SpringStudyPlaygroundMath.samples(response: response, damping: damping, count: 120, duration: 2)
        let settling = Spring(response: response, dampingRatio: damping).settlingDuration

        return VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10) {
            ZStack {
                GeometryReader { proxy in
                    Path { path in
                        let y = proxy.size.height * (1 - 1 / Self.curveMaximum)
                        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: y))
                        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: proxy.size.width, y: y))
                    }
                    .stroke(.secondary, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 1, dash: [4, 4]))
                }

                SpringStudyPlaygroundCurve(samples: samples, maximum: Self.curveMaximum)
                    .stroke(.pink, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 3, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
            }
            .frame(height: 150)
            .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Text("Settles in \(settling.formatted(.number.precision(.fractionLength(1)))) s")
                .font(.footnote)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
    }

    private func slider(_ title: String, value: Binding<Double>, range: ClosedRange<Double>, unit: String) -> some View {
        let text = value.wrappedValue.formatted(.number.precision(.fractionLength(2))) + unit

        return VStack(spacing: 4) {
            HStack {
                Text(title).font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                Spacer()
                Text(text).font(.subheadline.monospacedDigit()).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
            .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Slider(value: value, in: range) { Text(title) }
                .accessibilityValue(text)
                .tint(.pink)
        }
    }

    private var presets: some View {
        ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
            HStack(spacing: Self.presetSpacing) { presetButtons }
            VStack(spacing: Self.presetSpacing) { presetButtons }
        }
    }

    @ViewBuilder private var presetButtons: some View {
        ForEach(Preset.allCases) { preset in
            Button(preset.rawValue) {
                response = preset.values.response
                damping = preset.values.damping
                play()
            }
            .buttonStyle(.bordered)
            // In a narrow row a name shrinks a little before it would break in two.
            .lineLimit(1)
            .minimumScaleFactor(0.75)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
        }

        Button("Play", action: play)
            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
            .tint(.pink)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
    }

    private func play() {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(response: response, dampingFraction: damping)) {
            isAtEnd.toggle()
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SpringStudyPlaygroundDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        SpringStudyPlayground()
    }
}

#Preview {
    SpringStudyPlaygroundDemo()
}
```

## Symbol Effect Gallery

A gallery of SF Symbol effects, each played on demand and labeled with its name.

Category: Animations. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Animations/SymbolEffectGallery/SymbolEffectGallery.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

private enum SymbolEffectGalleryEffect: String, CaseIterable, Identifiable {
    case bounce = "Bounce"
    case pulse = "Pulse"
    case variableColor = "Variable Color"
    case wiggle = "Wiggle"
    case rotate = "Rotate"
    case breathe = "Breathe"

    var id: Self { self }

    var symbol: String {
        switch self {
        case .bounce: "arrow.down.circle.fill"
        case .pulse: "heart.fill"
        case .variableColor: "wifi"
        case .wiggle: "bell.fill"
        case .rotate: "gearshape.2.fill"
        case .breathe: "moon.stars.fill"
        }
    }

    var color: Color {
        switch self {
        case .bounce: .blue
        case .pulse: .pink
        case .variableColor: .teal
        case .wiggle: .orange
        case .rotate: .indigo
        case .breathe: .purple
        }
    }
}

/// A gallery of SF Symbol effects. Tapping a tile plays its effect once.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the effects are removed and the symbols stay still.
struct SymbolEffectGallery: View {
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) private var minimumColumn = 150.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            LazyVGrid(columns: [GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: minimumColumn), spacing: 14)], spacing: 14) {
                ForEach(SymbolEffectGalleryEffect.allCases) { effect in
                    SymbolEffectGalleryTile(effect: effect)
                }
            }
            .padding(20)
        }
        .symbolEffectsRemoved(reduceMotion)
    }
}

private struct SymbolEffectGalleryTile: View {
    let effect: SymbolEffectGalleryEffect

    @State private var plays = 0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var height = 68.0

    var body: some View {
        Button {
            plays += 1
        } label: {
            VStack(spacing: 14) {
                symbol
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .foregroundStyle(effect.color)
                    .frame(height: height)

                Text(effect.rawValue)
                    .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.primary)
                    .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
            }
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .padding(.vertical, 22)
            .padding(.horizontal, 12)
            .background(effect.color.opacity(0.12), in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 22, style: .continuous))
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(effect.rawValue)
        .accessibilityHint("Plays the effect")
    }

    @ViewBuilder private var symbol: some View {
        let image = Image(systemName: effect.symbol).accessibilityHidden(true)

        switch effect {
        case .bounce: image.symbolEffect(.bounce, value: plays)
        case .pulse: image.symbolEffect(.pulse, value: plays)
        case .variableColor: image.symbolEffect(.variableColor.iterative, value: plays)
        case .wiggle: image.symbolEffect(.wiggle, value: plays)
        case .rotate: image.symbolEffect(.rotate, value: plays)
        case .breathe: image.symbolEffect(.breathe, value: plays)
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SymbolEffectGalleryDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
            Text("Symbol Effects")
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .padding(.horizontal, 20)
                .padding(.top, 12)

            SymbolEffectGallery()
        }
    }
}

    SymbolEffectGalleryDemo()
}
```

## Animated Gradient Background

A linear gradient that slowly drifts its colors and turns its direction.

Category: Backgrounds. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Backgrounds/AnimatedGradientBackground/AnimatedGradientBackground.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum AnimatedGradientBackgroundMath {
    /// The palette index for a position, also when a negative speed runs time backwards.
    static func index(at position: Double, count: Int) -> Int {
        (Int(floor(position)) % count + count) % count
    }
}

/// A linear gradient whose colors drift along it while its direction slowly turns.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, it shows a still gradient.
struct AnimatedGradientBackground: View {
    var colors: [Color] = [.indigo, .purple, .pink, .orange]
    /// How many color steps pass each second.
    var speed: Double = 0.2

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            let angle = time * 0.5
            let reach = CGSize(width: cos(angle) * 0.75, height: sin(angle) * 0.75)

            LinearGradient(
                colors: driftedColors(at: time),
                startPoint: UnitPoint(x: 0.5 - reach.width, y: 0.5 - reach.height),
                endPoint: UnitPoint(x: 0.5 + reach.width, y: 0.5 + reach.height)
            )
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    /// Each stop blends from one palette color to the next, wrapping around so the drift never ends.
    private func driftedColors(at time: Double) -> [Color] {
        guard colors.count > 1 else { return colors + colors }

        return colors.indices.map { index in
            let position = time + Double(index)
            let lower = AnimatedGradientBackgroundMath.index(at: position, count: colors.count)
            let upper = (lower + 1) % colors.count
            return colors[lower].mix(with: colors[upper], by: position - floor(position))
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct AnimatedGradientBackgroundDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            AnimatedGradientBackground()

            VStack(spacing: 6) {
                Text("Good Evening")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                Text("Colors that never sit still")
                    .font(.headline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.8))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    AnimatedGradientBackgroundDemo()
}
```

## Aurora Mesh Background

An animated aurora background made with a mesh gradient.

Category: Backgrounds. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Backgrounds/AuroraMeshBackground/AuroraMeshBackground.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A slowly moving aurora built with a mesh gradient.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, it shows a still gradient.
struct AuroraMeshBackground: View {
    var first: Color = .indigo
    var second: Color = .purple
    var third: Color = .teal
    var speed: Double = 0.6

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            MeshGradient(
                width: AuroraMesh.size,
                height: AuroraMesh.size,
                points: AuroraMesh.points(at: reduceMotion ? 0 : context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed),
                colors: [
                    first, second, first,
                    third, second, first,
                    second, first, third,
                ]
            )
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

enum AuroraMesh {
    static let size = 3

    /// Corners stay fixed and edge points slide along their edge, so the mesh always fills the view.
    static func points(at time: TimeInterval) -> [SIMD2<Float>] {
        func wave(speed: Double, phase: Double) -> Double {
            0.5 + sin(time * speed + phase) * 0.2
        }

        let positions: [(Double, Double)] = [
            (0, 0), (wave(speed: 0.8, phase: 2.1), 0), (1, 0),
            (0, wave(speed: 0.9, phase: 0)), (wave(speed: 1, phase: 0.7), wave(speed: 0.6, phase: 4.2)), (1, wave(speed: 0.7, phase: 1.3)),
            (0, 1), (wave(speed: 1.1, phase: 3.4), 1), (1, 1),
        ]
        return positions.map { SIMD2(Float($0.0), Float($0.1)) }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct AuroraMeshBackgroundDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            AuroraMeshBackground()

            Text("Aurora")
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    AuroraMeshBackgroundDemo()
}
```

## Bubbles Background

Translucent bubbles that rise and sway across the screen.

Category: Backgrounds. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Backgrounds/BubblesBackground/BubblesBackground.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Translucent bubbles that rise and sway. Larger bubbles rise faster.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the bubbles hold still.
struct BubblesBackground: View {
    var color: Color = .white
    var count: Int = 36
    var speed: Double = 1

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private static let margin = 40.0

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 60.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            Canvas { context, size in
                let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
                let tint = Gradient(colors: [color.opacity(0.02), color.opacity(0.26)])

                for index in 0..<count {
                    let scale = noise(index, 1)
                    let radius = 6 + scale * scale * 28
                    let center = position(of: index, scale: scale, at: time, in: size)
                    let bubble = Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(
                        x: center.x - radius,
                        y: center.y - radius,
                        width: radius * 2,
                        height: radius * 2
                    ))

                    context.fill(
                        bubble,
                        with: .radialGradient(tint, center: center, startRadius: radius * 0.3, endRadius: radius)
                    )
                    context.stroke(bubble, with: .color(color.opacity(0.5)), lineWidth: 1)

                    let shine = radius * 0.22
                    context.fill(
                        Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(
                            x: center.x - radius * 0.55,
                            y: center.y - radius * 0.6,
                            width: shine,
                            height: shine
                        )),
                        with: .color(color.opacity(0.75))
                    )
                }
            }
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func position(of index: Int, scale: Double, at time: Double, in size: CGSize) -> CGPoint {
        let travel = size.height + Self.margin * 2
        let rise = 35 + scale * 70
        let climbed = (noise(index, 2) * travel + time * rise).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: travel)
        let sway = sin(time * (0.7 + noise(index, 3)) + noise(index, 4) * 2 * .pi) * (10 + noise(index, 5) * 18)

        return CGPoint(x: noise(index, 6) * size.width + sway, y: size.height + Self.margin - climbed)
    }

    /// A repeatable pseudo-random value in 0..<1 for one bubble and one property.
    private func noise(_ index: Int, _ salt: Double) -> Double {
        let value = sin(Double(index) * 127.1 + salt * 311.7) * 43758.5453
        return value - floor(value)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct BubblesBackgroundDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [.cyan, .blue, Color(red: 0.03, green: 0.12, blue: 0.4)],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )
            .ignoresSafeArea()

            BubblesBackground()

            Text("Deep Blue")
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    BubblesBackgroundDemo()
}
```

## Color Orbs Background

Large, soft colored orbs drifting slowly over a dark base.

Category: Backgrounds. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Backgrounds/ColorOrbsBackground/ColorOrbsBackground.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Large, soft colored orbs drifting slowly over a dark base.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the orbs hold still.
struct ColorOrbsBackground: View {
    /// One orb per color.
    var colors: [Color] = [.pink, .purple, .blue, .teal, .orange]
    var base: Color = Color(red: 0.05, green: 0.04, blue: 0.13)
    var speed: Double = 0.4

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            Canvas(opaque: true) { context, size in
                let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed

                context.fill(Path(CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size)), with: .color(base))
                context.blendMode = .screen

                for (index, color) in colors.enumerated() {
                    drawOrb(index: index, color: color, at: time, in: context, size: size)
                }
            }
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    /// A radial falloff to clear looks like a heavy blur and costs far less to redraw each frame.
    private func drawOrb(index: Int, color: Color, at time: Double, in context: GraphicsContext, size: CGSize) {
        let center = CGPoint(
            x: (0.5 + 0.42 * sin(time * (0.5 + noise(index, 1) * 0.5) + noise(index, 2) * 2 * .pi)) * size.width,
            y: (0.5 + 0.42 * cos(time * (0.4 + noise(index, 3) * 0.5) + noise(index, 4) * 2 * .pi)) * size.height
        )
        let radius = max(size.width, size.height) * (0.34 + noise(index, 5) * 0.14)
        let falloff = Gradient(stops: [
            .init(color: color.opacity(0.9), location: 0),
            .init(color: color.opacity(0.45), location: 0.5),
            .init(color: color.opacity(0), location: 1),
        ])

        context.fill(
            Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: center.x - radius, y: center.y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)),
            with: .radialGradient(falloff, center: center, startRadius: 0, endRadius: radius)
        )
    }

    /// A repeatable pseudo-random value in 0..<1 for one orb and one property.
    private func noise(_ index: Int, _ salt: Double) -> Double {
        let value = sin(Double(index) * 127.1 + salt * 311.7) * 43758.5453
        return value - floor(value)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ColorOrbsBackgroundDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            ColorOrbsBackground()

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
                Image(systemName: "moon.stars.fill")
                    .font(.title)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                Text("Evening Focus")
                    .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                Text("Soft color moves behind your content without getting in its way.")
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.8))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .padding(24)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            .background(.ultraThinMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 28))
            .environment(\.colorScheme, .dark)
            .padding(24)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ColorOrbsBackgroundDemo()
}
```

## Grid Pulse Background

A grid of dots with a pulse of light spreading out from the center.

Category: Backgrounds. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Backgrounds/GridPulseBackground/GridPulseBackground.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum GridPulseBackgroundMath {
    /// How many dots fit on each side of the center, or `nil` when `spacing` cannot lay out a grid.
    static func dotsPerSide(extent: Double, spacing: Double) -> Int? {
        guard spacing.isFinite, spacing > 0 else { return nil }
        return Int(extent / 2 / spacing) + 1
    }
}

/// A grid of dots with a pulse of light spreading from the center.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, it shows one still ring.
struct GridPulseBackground: View {
    var color: Color = .cyan
    var spacing: Double = 26
    /// Seconds for the pulse to travel from the center to the corners.
    var period: Double = 2.6

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private static let dotRadius = 2.0
    private static let restingOpacity = 0.32
    private static let bandWidth = 80.0

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            Canvas { context, size in
                let cycle = timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate / period
                let progress = reduceMotion ? 0.4 : cycle - floor(cycle)
                draw(progress: progress, in: context, size: size)
            }
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func draw(progress: Double, in context: GraphicsContext, size: CGSize) {
        guard
            let columns = GridPulseBackgroundMath.dotsPerSide(extent: size.width, spacing: spacing),
            let rows = GridPulseBackgroundMath.dotsPerSide(extent: size.height, spacing: spacing)
        else { return }

        let center = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
        let front = progress * (hypot(size.width, size.height) / 2 + Self.bandWidth)
        var resting = Path()

        for row in -rows...rows {
            for column in -columns...columns {
                let dot = CGPoint(x: center.x + Double(column) * spacing, y: center.y + Double(row) * spacing)
                let gap = (hypot(dot.x - center.x, dot.y - center.y) - front) / Self.bandWidth
                let glow = exp(-gap * gap) * (1 - pow(progress, 4))

                if glow < 0.02 {
                    resting.addEllipse(in: circle(at: dot, radius: Self.dotRadius))
                } else {
                    context.fill(
                        Path(ellipseIn: circle(at: dot, radius: Self.dotRadius * (1 + glow * 1.6))),
                        with: .color(color.opacity(Self.restingOpacity + glow * (1 - Self.restingOpacity)))
                    )
                }
            }
        }

        context.fill(resting, with: .color(color.opacity(Self.restingOpacity)))
    }

    private func circle(at center: CGPoint, radius: Double) -> CGRect {
        CGRect(x: center.x - radius, y: center.y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct GridPulseBackgroundDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Color(red: 0.03, green: 0.05, blue: 0.1)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            GridPulseBackground()

            VStack(spacing: 10) {
                Image(systemName: "dot.radiowaves.left.and.right")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                Text("Signal")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .padding(.horizontal, 28)
            .padding(.vertical, 20)
            .background(.ultraThinMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 24))
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    GridPulseBackgroundDemo()
}
```

## Image Derived Gradient Background

A full-screen gradient whose colors are sampled from the pixels of an image and cross-fade when the image changes.

Category: Backgrounds. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Backgrounds/ImageDerivedGradientBackground/ImageDerivedGradientBackground.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct ImageDerivedGradientBackgroundSample: Equatable {
    let red: Double
    let green: Double
    let blue: Double
}

enum ImageDerivedGradientBackgroundMath {
    static let bytesPerPixel = 4

    /// Averages horizontal bands of premultiplied RGBA pixels, from top to bottom.
    ///
    /// Saturated pixels count for more, so a photo gives vivid colors instead of grey.
    /// Fully transparent bands are left out.
    static func bands(pixels: [UInt8], width: Int, height: Int, count: Int) -> [ImageDerivedGradientBackgroundSample] {
        guard width > 0, height > 0, count > 0, pixels.count / bytesPerPixel / width >= height else { return [] }
        let bandCount = min(count, height)

        return (0..<bandCount).compactMap { band in
            var red: Double = 0, green: Double = 0, blue: Double = 0, total: Double = 0

            for row in (band * height / bandCount)..<((band + 1) * height / bandCount) {
                for column in 0..<width {
                    let offset = (row * width + column) * bytesPerPixel
                    let alpha = Double(pixels[offset + 3])
                    guard alpha > 0 else { continue }

                    let r = Double(pixels[offset]) / alpha
                    let g = Double(pixels[offset + 1]) / alpha
                    let b = Double(pixels[offset + 2]) / alpha
                    let weight = alpha / 255 * (0.15 + max(r, g, b) - min(r, g, b))
                    red += r * weight
                    green += g * weight
                    blue += b * weight
                    total += weight
                }
            }

            guard total > 0 else { return nil }
            return ImageDerivedGradientBackgroundSample(red: red / total, green: green / total, blue: blue / total)
        }
    }
}

/// A full-screen gradient whose colors are sampled from an image and cross-fade when it changes.
///
/// Keep passing the same `Image` value while the picture is the same, or it is sampled again.
/// With Reduce Motion on, the colors change without fading.
struct ImageDerivedGradientBackground: View {
    private struct Request: Equatable {
        let image: Image
        let bands: Int
    }

    let image: Image
    var bands = 3
    var fallback: [Color] = [.indigo, .black]

    @State private var colors: [Color]?
    @State private var previous: [Color]?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        let shown = colors ?? fallback

        ZStack {
            Color.black

            // The gradient before stays underneath while the new one fades in over it.
            // Fading one out as the other fades in would dip through the black.
            LinearGradient(colors: previous ?? shown, startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)

            LinearGradient(colors: shown, startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .id(shown)
                .transition(.opacity)
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
        .task(id: Request(image: image, bands: bands)) {
            let sampled = sampledColors()
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            previous = colors ?? fallback
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: 0.8)) { colors = sampled }
        }
    }

    /// Draws the image small and reads its pixels. Returns nil when it cannot be rendered.
    private func sampledColors() -> [Color]? {
        let renderer = ImageRenderer(content: image.resizable().scaledToFill().frame(width: 24, height: 24).clipped())
        renderer.scale = 1

        guard let cgImage = renderer.cgImage,
              let space = CGColorSpace(name: CGColorSpace.sRGB) else { return nil }

        let width = cgImage.width
        let height = cgImage.height
        var pixels = [UInt8](repeating: 0, count: width * height * ImageDerivedGradientBackgroundMath.bytesPerPixel)
        let didDraw = pixels.withUnsafeMutableBytes { buffer -> Bool in
            guard let context = CGContext(
                data: buffer.baseAddress,
                width: width,
                height: height,
                bitsPerComponent: 8,
                bytesPerRow: width * ImageDerivedGradientBackgroundMath.bytesPerPixel,
                space: space,
                bitmapInfo: CGImageAlphaInfo.premultipliedLast.rawValue
            ) else { return false }

            context.draw(cgImage, in: CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: width, height: height))
            return true
        }
        guard didDraw else { return nil }

        let samples = ImageDerivedGradientBackgroundMath.bands(pixels: pixels, width: width, height: height, count: max(bands, 1))
        return samples.isEmpty ? nil : samples.map { Color(.sRGB, red: $0.red, green: $0.green, blue: $0.blue) }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ImageDerivedGradientBackgroundDemo: View {
    @State private var photos = Self.makePhotos()
    @State private var index = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            if let photo = photos.isEmpty ? nil : photos[index % photos.count] {
                ImageDerivedGradientBackground(image: photo)

                photo
                    .resizable()
                    .scaledToFill()
                    .frame(width: 240, height: 240)
                    .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 36, style: .continuous))
                    .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.35), radius: 28, y: 16)
                    .id(index)
                    .transition(.opacity)
                    .accessibilityLabel("Placeholder photo")
            }
        }
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.5))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.8)) { index += 1 }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Stands in for real photos: gradients and symbols rendered into images.
    private static func makePhotos() -> [Image] {
        let scenes: [(colors: [Color], symbol: String)] = [
            ([.orange, .pink, .purple], "sun.horizon.fill"),
            ([.teal, .blue, .indigo], "water.waves"),
            ([.mint, .green, .teal], "leaf.fill"),
        ]

        return scenes.compactMap { scene in
            let content = ZStack {
                LinearGradient(colors: scene.colors, startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                Image(systemName: scene.symbol)
                    .font(.system(size: 120))
                    .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.85))
            }
            .frame(width: 240, height: 240)

            let renderer = ImageRenderer(content: content)
            renderer.scale = 2
            return renderer.cgImage.map { Image(decorative: $0, scale: 2) }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ImageDerivedGradientBackgroundDemo()
}
```

## Particle Field Background

Drifting points that are joined by faint lines when they come close.

Category: Backgrounds. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Backgrounds/ParticleFieldBackground/ParticleFieldBackground.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Drifting points joined by faint lines when they come close.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the field holds still.
struct ParticleFieldBackground: View {
    var color: Color = .white
    var count: Int = 70
    var linkDistance: Double = 105
    var speed: Double = 1

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            Canvas { context, size in
                let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
                let points = (0..<count).map { position(of: $0, at: time, in: size) }

                drawLinks(between: points, in: context)

                for (index, point) in points.enumerated() {
                    let radius = 1.2 + noise(index, 5) * 1.6
                    let dot = CGRect(x: point.x - radius, y: point.y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)
                    context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: dot), with: .color(color.opacity(0.85)))
                }
            }
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    /// Links are grouped into a few opacity levels, so a frame strokes four paths and not hundreds.
    private func drawLinks(between points: [CGPoint], in context: GraphicsContext) {
        var levels = Array(repeating: Path(), count: 4)

        for first in points.indices {
            for second in points.indices where second > first {
                let distance = hypot(points[first].x - points[second].x, points[first].y - points[second].y)
                guard distance < linkDistance else { continue }

                let closeness = 1 - distance / linkDistance
                let level = min(Int(closeness * Double(levels.count)), levels.count - 1)
                levels[level].move(to: points[first])
                levels[level].addLine(to: points[second])
            }
        }

        for (level, path) in levels.enumerated() {
            context.stroke(path, with: .color(color.opacity(0.1 * Double(level + 1))), lineWidth: 0.8)
        }
    }

    private func position(of index: Int, at time: Double, in size: CGSize) -> CGPoint {
        CGPoint(
            x: bounce(noise(index, 1) + time * (noise(index, 2) - 0.5) * 0.08) * size.width,
            y: bounce(noise(index, 3) + time * (noise(index, 4) - 0.5) * 0.04) * size.height
        )
    }

    /// A triangle wave from 0 to 1, so a point turns around at the edge instead of jumping and snapping its links.
    private func bounce(_ value: Double) -> Double {
        abs((value - floor(value)) * 2 - 1)
    }

    /// A repeatable pseudo-random value in 0..<1 for one point and one property.
    private func noise(_ index: Int, _ salt: Double) -> Double {
        let value = sin(Double(index) * 127.1 + salt * 311.7) * 43758.5453
        return value - floor(value)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ParticleFieldBackgroundDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [Color(red: 0.05, green: 0.08, blue: 0.22), Color(red: 0.16, green: 0.06, blue: 0.34)],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )
            .ignoresSafeArea()

            ParticleFieldBackground()

            VStack(spacing: 6) {
                Text("Particle Field")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                Text("Points that find each other")
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.75))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ParticleFieldBackgroundDemo()
}
```

## Snowfall Background

Snowflakes falling at different speeds across three layers of depth.

Category: Backgrounds. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Backgrounds/SnowfallBackground/SnowfallBackground.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Snow in three depths: small and slow far away, large, fast and slightly blurred up close.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the flakes hold still.
struct SnowfallBackground: View {
    var color: Color = .white
    /// Multiplies the number of flakes in every depth.
    var density: Double = 1
    var speed: Double = 1

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private struct Depth {
        let count: Int
        let radius: ClosedRange<Double>
        let fall: Double
        let sway: Double
        let opacity: Double
        let blur: Double
    }

    private static let depths = [
        Depth(count: 110, radius: 0.8...1.5, fall: 26, sway: 6, opacity: 0.45, blur: 0),
        Depth(count: 60, radius: 1.8...3, fall: 55, sway: 12, opacity: 0.7, blur: 0),
        Depth(count: 18, radius: 3.5...6, fall: 105, sway: 22, opacity: 0.9, blur: 1.5),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 60.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            Canvas { context, size in
                let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed

                for (layer, depth) in Self.depths.enumerated() {
                    context.drawLayer { layerContext in
                        if depth.blur > 0 {
                            layerContext.addFilter(.blur(radius: depth.blur))
                        }
                        layerContext.fill(
                            flakes(of: depth, layer: layer, at: time, in: size),
                            with: .color(color.opacity(depth.opacity))
                        )
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    /// One path holds every flake of a depth, so each depth is a single fill.
    private func flakes(of depth: Depth, layer: Int, at time: Double, in size: CGSize) -> Path {
        var path = Path()
        let margin = depth.radius.upperBound * 2
        let travel = size.height + margin * 2

        for index in 0..<Int(Double(depth.count) * density) {
            let seed = layer * 1000 + index
            let fallen = (noise(seed, 1) * travel + time * depth.fall).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: travel)
            let sway = sin(time * (0.5 + noise(seed, 2)) + noise(seed, 3) * 2 * .pi) * depth.sway
            let radius = depth.radius.lowerBound + noise(seed, 4) * (depth.radius.upperBound - depth.radius.lowerBound)

            path.addEllipse(in: CGRect(
                x: noise(seed, 5) * size.width + sway - radius,
                y: fallen - margin - radius,
                width: radius * 2,
                height: radius * 2
            ))
        }
        return path
    }

    /// A repeatable pseudo-random value in 0..<1 for one flake and one property.
    private func noise(_ index: Int, _ salt: Double) -> Double {
        let value = sin(Double(index) * 127.1 + salt * 311.7) * 43758.5453
        return value - floor(value)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SnowfallBackgroundDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [Color(red: 0.07, green: 0.11, blue: 0.27), Color(red: 0.3, green: 0.4, blue: 0.6)],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )
            .ignoresSafeArea()

            SnowfallBackground()

            VStack(spacing: 10) {
                Image(systemName: "snowflake")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                Text("First Snow")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
    }
}

    SnowfallBackgroundDemo()
}
```

## Starfield Background

Stars streaking toward the viewer with a simple perspective projection.

Category: Backgrounds. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Backgrounds/StarfieldBackground/StarfieldBackground.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Stars rushing toward the viewer, each one a streak along its line of flight.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, it shows a still field of dots.
struct StarfieldBackground: View {
    var color: Color = .white
    var count: Int = 320
    /// Depth covered per second, where 1 is the whole way from the horizon to the viewer.
    var speed: Double = 0.22

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            Canvas { context, size in
                let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
                let center = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
                let focalLength = max(size.width, size.height) * 0.12
                let trail = reduceMotion ? 0.004 : 0.04

                for index in 0..<count {
                    let cycle = noise(index, 3) + time
                    let depth = max(1 - (cycle - floor(cycle)), 0.02)
                    let angle = noise(index, 1) * 2 * .pi
                    let spread = (0.15 + noise(index, 2) * 1.25) * focalLength

                    func point(atDepth depth: Double) -> CGPoint {
                        CGPoint(
                            x: center.x + cos(angle) * spread / depth,
                            y: center.y + sin(angle) * spread / depth
                        )
                    }

                    var streak = Path()
                    streak.move(to: point(atDepth: min(depth + trail, 1)))
                    streak.addLine(to: point(atDepth: depth))

                    let closeness = 1 - depth
                    context.stroke(
                        streak,
                        with: .color(color.opacity(min(0.15 + closeness * 1.3, 1))),
                        style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 0.6 + closeness * 2.2, lineCap: .round)
                    )
                }
            }
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    /// A repeatable pseudo-random value in 0..<1 for one star and one property.
    private func noise(_ index: Int, _ salt: Double) -> Double {
        let value = sin(Double(index) * 127.1 + salt * 311.7) * 43758.5453
        return value - floor(value)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct StarfieldBackgroundDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            RadialGradient(
                colors: [Color(red: 0.1, green: 0.1, blue: 0.3), .black],
                center: .center,
                startRadius: 0,
                endRadius: 480
            )
            .ignoresSafeArea()

            StarfieldBackground()

            VStack(spacing: 10) {
                Image(systemName: "sparkles")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                Text("Warp Speed")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.7), radius: 12)
        }
    }
}

    StarfieldBackgroundDemo()
}
```
