## Shrinking Extended Button

An extended floating button that collapses from a labeled pill to a plain icon as the scroll view moves down.

Category: Buttons. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Buttons/ShrinkingExtendedButton/ShrinkingExtendedButton.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum ShrinkingExtendedButtonMath {
    /// Rubber-banding past the top gives a negative offset, which counts as being at the top.
    static func shouldExtend(offset: CGFloat, threshold: CGFloat) -> Bool {
        offset <= max(threshold, 0)
    }
}

/// An extended floating button that shrinks from a labeled pill to a plain icon.
///
/// Pass `isExtended`, or drive it from a scroll view with `ShrinkingExtendedButtonScrollTracker`.
/// With Reduce Motion on, it changes shape without animating.
struct ShrinkingExtendedButton: View {
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let systemImage: String
    var isExtended = true
    var tint: Color = .indigo
    let action: () -> Void

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .headline) private var height = 58.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Button(action: action) {
            HStack(spacing: 10) {
                Image(systemName: systemImage)
                    .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))

                if isExtended {
                    Text(title)
                        .font(.headline)
                        .transition(.opacity.combined(with: .scale(scale: 0.8, anchor: .leading)))
                }
            }
            .foregroundStyle(ShrinkingExtendedButtonContrastingForeground(background: tint))
            .padding(.horizontal, isExtended ? 22 : 0)
            .frame(minWidth: height, minHeight: height)
            .background(tint.gradient, in: Capsule())
            .shadow(color: tint.opacity(0.35), radius: 12, y: 6)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(title)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.35, bounce: 0.15), value: isExtended)
    }
}

/// Apply to a scroll view to set `isExtended` from how far it has moved from the top.
struct ShrinkingExtendedButtonScrollTracker: ViewModifier {
    @Binding var isExtended: Bool
    var threshold: CGFloat = 40

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.onScrollGeometryChange(for: Bool.self) { geometry in
            ShrinkingExtendedButtonMath.shouldExtend(
                offset: geometry.contentOffset.y + geometry.contentInsets.top,
                threshold: threshold
            )
        } action: { _, shouldExtend in
            isExtended = shouldExtend
        }
    }
}

/// White or black, whichever reads better on `background`. Black only on a
/// light color, so the system's own colors keep white.
nonisolated struct ShrinkingExtendedButtonContrastingForeground: ShapeStyle {
    let background: Color

    func resolve(in environment: EnvironmentValues) -> Color {
        let color = background.resolve(in: environment)
        let luminance = 0.2126 * color.linearRed + 0.7152 * color.linearGreen + 0.0722 * color.linearBlue
        return luminance > 0.5 ? .black : .white
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ShrinkingExtendedButtonDemo: View {
    @State private var isExtended = true

    var body: some View {
        ZStack(alignment: .bottomTrailing) {
            ScrollView {
                LazyVStack(spacing: 12) {
                    ForEach(0..<30, id: \.self) { index in
                        HStack(spacing: 14) {
                            Circle()
                                .fill(Color(hue: Double(index % 8) / 8, saturation: 0.55, brightness: 0.9))
                                .frame(width: 44, height: 44)
                                .accessibilityHidden(true)
                            Text("Message \(index + 1)")
                                .font(.headline)
                            Spacer(minLength: 0)
                        }
                        .padding(14)
                        .background(.quaternary.opacity(0.6), in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 18, style: .continuous))
                    }
                }
                .padding(16)
            }
            .modifier(ShrinkingExtendedButtonScrollTracker(isExtended: $isExtended))

            ShrinkingExtendedButton(title: "New Message", systemImage: "square.and.pencil", isExtended: isExtended) {}
                .padding(24)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ShrinkingExtendedButtonDemo()
}
```

## Calendar Month Grid

A month calendar for picking one day, with swipe paging between months.

Category: Calendars. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Calendars/CalendarMonthGrid/CalendarMonthGrid.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum CalendarMonthGridMath {
    /// Six weeks, so every month is the same height.
    static let cellCount = 42

    /// The cells of a month: nil before its first day and after its last.
    static func days(inMonthContaining date: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> [Date?] {
        guard let first = calendar.dateInterval(of: .month, for: date)?.start else {
            return Array(repeating: nil, count: cellCount)
        }

        let leading = (calendar.component(.weekday, from: first) - calendar.firstWeekday + 7) % 7
        let dayCount = calendar.range(of: .day, in: .month, for: first)?.count ?? 0
        let days = (0..<dayCount).map { calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: $0, to: first) }
        let cells = Array(repeating: nil, count: leading) + days
        return Array(cells.prefix(cellCount)) + Array(repeating: nil, count: max(0, cellCount - cells.count))
    }

    /// The weekday initials, starting on the calendar's first day of the week.
    static func weekdaySymbols(calendar: Calendar) -> [String] {
        let symbols = calendar.veryShortStandaloneWeekdaySymbols
        guard !symbols.isEmpty else { return [] }
        let start = min(max(calendar.firstWeekday - 1, 0), symbols.count - 1)
        return Array(symbols[start...] + symbols[..<start])
    }

    /// What VoiceOver reads for a day, in the same calendar and time zone as the grid.
    static func dayLabel(for day: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> String {
        day.formatted(Date.FormatStyle(date: .complete, time: .omitted, calendar: calendar, timeZone: calendar.timeZone))
    }
}

/// A month calendar for picking one day, with swipe paging between months.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the arrows change the month without sliding.
struct CalendarMonthGrid: View {
    @Binding var selection: Date?
    var anchor: Date = .now
    /// How many months can be reached in each direction.
    var monthRange = 24
    var tint: Color = .indigo

    var body: some View {
        CalendarMonthGridStage(selection: $selection, anchor: anchor, monthRange: monthRange, tint: tint)
            // Seven columns cannot hold accessibility sizes, so growth stops here, row height included.
            .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.xxxLarge)
    }
}

private struct CalendarMonthGridStage: View {
    @Binding var selection: Date?
    let anchor: Date
    let monthRange: Int
    let tint: Color

    @State private var page = 0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) private var rowHeight = 44.0
    @Environment(\.calendar) private var calendar
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let rowSpacing = 4.0
    private var reach: Int { min(max(monthRange, 0), 600) }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 12) {
            header
            weekdays

            TabView(selection: $page) {
                ForEach(-reach...reach, id: \.self) { offset in
                    grid(for: month(at: offset))
                        .tag(offset)
                }
            }
            .tabViewStyle(.page(indexDisplayMode: .never))
            .frame(height: rowHeight * 6 + rowSpacing * 5)
        }
    }

    private var header: some View {
        HStack {
            Text(month(at: page).formatted(monthStyle))
                .font(.system(.title3, design: .rounded, weight: .semibold))
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)

            arrow("chevron.backward", label: "Previous month", to: page - 1)
            arrow("chevron.forward", label: "Next month", to: page + 1)
        }
    }

    private var monthStyle: Date.FormatStyle {
        var style = Date.FormatStyle().month(.wide).year()
        style.calendar = calendar
        style.timeZone = calendar.timeZone
        return style
    }

    private func arrow(_ systemImage: String, label: String, to target: Int) -> some View {
        Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth) { page = target }
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: systemImage)
                .font(.body.weight(.semibold))
                .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44)
        }
        .tint(tint)
        .disabled(abs(target) > reach)
        .accessibilityLabel(label)
    }

    private var weekdays: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 0) {
            ForEach(Array(CalendarMonthGridMath.weekdaySymbols(calendar: calendar).enumerated()), id: \.offset) { _, symbol in
                Text(symbol)
                    .font(.caption.weight(.semibold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func grid(for month: Date) -> some View {
        let cells = CalendarMonthGridMath.days(inMonthContaining: month, calendar: calendar)
        let columns = Array(repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: 0), count: 7)

        return LazyVGrid(columns: columns, spacing: rowSpacing) {
            ForEach(Array(cells.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { _, day in
                if let day {
                    dayButton(day)
                } else {
                    Color.clear
                        .frame(height: rowHeight)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private func dayButton(_ day: Date) -> some View {
        let isSelected = selection.map { calendar.isDate($0, inSameDayAs: day) } ?? false
        let isToday = calendar.isDateInToday(day)

        return Button {
            selection = day
        } label: {
            Text(calendar.component(.day, from: day), format: .number.grouping(.never))
                .font(.body.weight(isSelected || isToday ? .semibold : .regular))
                .minimumScaleFactor(0.7)
                .lineLimit(1)
                .foregroundStyle(isSelected ? AnyShapeStyle(.white) : isToday ? AnyShapeStyle(tint) : AnyShapeStyle(.primary))
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                .frame(height: rowHeight)
                .background {
                    if isSelected { Circle().fill(tint) }
                }
                .contentShape(.rect)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(CalendarMonthGridMath.dayLabel(for: day, calendar: calendar))
        .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])
    }

    private func month(at offset: Int) -> Date {
        calendar.date(byAdding: .month, value: offset, to: anchor) ?? anchor
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CalendarMonthGridDemo: View {
    @State private var selection: Date?

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 20) {
            CalendarMonthGrid(selection: $selection)
                .padding(16)
                .background(.background, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 28, style: .continuous))
                .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.08), radius: 20, y: 10)

            Text(selection?.formatted(date: .long, time: .omitted) ?? "Pick a day")
                .font(.headline)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
        .padding(16)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(.indigo.opacity(0.08))
    }
}

#Preview {
    CalendarMonthGridDemo()
}
```

## Calendar Range Selector

A month calendar that picks a start and an end day and shades the days between them.

Category: Calendars. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Calendars/CalendarRangeSelector/CalendarRangeSelector.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A month calendar that picks a start and an end day and shades the days between them.
///
/// The first tap sets the start and the second sets the end. Tapping a day before the
/// start, or any day once the range is complete, starts a new range.
struct CalendarRangeSelector: View {
    @Binding var start: Date?
    @Binding var end: Date?
    var calendar: Calendar
    var tint: Color

    @State private var month: Date
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) private var dayHeight = 46.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.locale) private var locale

    init(
        start: Binding<Date?>,
        end: Binding<Date?>,
        month: Date = .now,
        calendar: Calendar = .current,
        tint: Color = .indigo
    ) {
        _start = start
        _end = end
        self.calendar = calendar
        self.tint = tint
        _month = State(initialValue: month)
    }

    private var selection: CalendarRangeSelectorLogic.Selection {
        .init(start: start, end: end)
    }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 12) {
            header

            HStack(spacing: 0) {
                ForEach(Array(CalendarRangeSelectorLogic.weekdaySymbols(calendar: calendar).enumerated()), id: \.offset) { _, symbol in
                    Text(symbol)
                        .font(.caption.weight(.semibold))
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                }
            }
            .accessibilityHidden(true)

            LazyVGrid(columns: Array(repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: 0), count: 7), spacing: 4) {
                ForEach(0..<CalendarRangeSelectorLogic.leadingBlanks(inMonthOf: month, calendar: calendar), id: \.self) { _ in
                    Color.clear.frame(height: dayHeight)
                }
                ForEach(CalendarRangeSelectorLogic.days(inMonthOf: month, calendar: calendar), id: \.self) { day in
                    dayCell(day)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private var header: some View {
        HStack {
            monthButton(systemImage: "chevron.backward", label: "Previous month", offset: -1)
            Spacer()
            Text(format(month, Date.FormatStyle().month(.wide).year()))
                .font(.headline)
                .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)
            Spacer()
            monthButton(systemImage: "chevron.forward", label: "Next month", offset: 1)
        }
    }

    private func monthButton(systemImage: String, label: String, offset: Int) -> some View {
        Button {
            guard let next = calendar.date(byAdding: .month, value: offset, to: month) else { return }
            month = next
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: systemImage)
                .font(.body.weight(.semibold))
                .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44)
                .contentShape(.rect)
        }
        .tint(tint)
        .accessibilityLabel(label)
    }

    private func dayCell(_ day: Date) -> some View {
        let role = CalendarRangeSelectorLogic.role(of: day, in: selection, calendar: calendar)
        let isEndpoint = role == .start || role == .end || role == .single
        let band = tint.opacity(0.18)

        return Button {
            choose(day)
        } label: {
            ZStack {
                HStack(spacing: 0) {
                    (role == .middle || role == .end ? band : Color.clear)
                    (role == .middle || role == .start ? band : Color.clear)
                }
                .padding(.vertical, 2)

                if isEndpoint {
                    Circle().fill(tint).padding(2)
                }

                Text(verbatim: String(calendar.component(.day, from: day)))
                    .font(.body.weight(isEndpoint ? .semibold : .regular))
                    .lineLimit(1)
                    .minimumScaleFactor(0.5)
                    .foregroundStyle(isEndpoint ? Color.white : Color.primary)
            }
            .frame(height: dayHeight)
            .contentShape(.rect)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(format(day, Date.FormatStyle().weekday(.wide).day().month(.wide).year()))
        .accessibilityValue(accessibilityValue(for: role))
        .accessibilityAddTraits(isEndpoint ? .isSelected : [])
    }

    private func choose(_ day: Date) {
        let next = CalendarRangeSelectorLogic.selecting(day, in: selection, calendar: calendar)
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.25)) {
            start = next.start
            end = next.end
        }
    }

    private func accessibilityValue(for role: CalendarRangeSelectorLogic.Role) -> String {
        switch role {
        case .outside: ""
        case .start: "Start of range"
        case .middle: "In range"
        case .end: "End of range"
        case .single: "Selected"
        }
    }

    private func format(_ date: Date, _ base: Date.FormatStyle) -> String {
        var style = base
        style.calendar = calendar
        style.timeZone = calendar.timeZone
        style.locale = locale
        return date.formatted(style)
    }
}

/// The date math of the calendar, apart from the view so it can be tested.
enum CalendarRangeSelectorLogic {
    struct Selection: Equatable {
        var start: Date?
        var end: Date?
    }

    enum Role: Equatable {
        case outside, start, middle, end, single
    }

    static func selecting(_ day: Date, in selection: Selection, calendar: Calendar) -> Selection {
        let day = calendar.startOfDay(for: day)
        guard let start = selection.start.map({ calendar.startOfDay(for: $0) }), selection.end == nil, day >= start else {
            return Selection(start: day, end: nil)
        }
        return Selection(start: start, end: day)
    }

    static func role(of day: Date, in selection: Selection, calendar: Calendar) -> Role {
        let day = calendar.startOfDay(for: day)
        guard let start = selection.start.map({ calendar.startOfDay(for: $0) }) else { return .outside }
        guard let end = selection.end.map({ calendar.startOfDay(for: $0) }), end != start else {
            return day == start ? .single : .outside
        }

        let lower = min(start, end)
        let upper = max(start, end)
        if day == lower { return .start }
        if day == upper { return .end }
        return day > lower && day < upper ? .middle : .outside
    }

    static func days(inMonthOf date: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> [Date] {
        guard let first = calendar.dateInterval(of: .month, for: date)?.start,
              let range = calendar.range(of: .day, in: .month, for: date) else { return [] }
        return range.compactMap { calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: $0 - range.lowerBound, to: first) }
    }

    /// The empty cells before day one, given the calendar's first weekday.
    static func leadingBlanks(inMonthOf date: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> Int {
        guard let first = calendar.dateInterval(of: .month, for: date)?.start else { return 0 }
        return (calendar.component(.weekday, from: first) - calendar.firstWeekday + 7) % 7
    }

    static func weekdaySymbols(calendar: Calendar) -> [String] {
        let symbols = calendar.veryShortStandaloneWeekdaySymbols
        let offset = min(max(calendar.firstWeekday - 1, 0), symbols.count)
        return Array(symbols[offset...] + symbols[..<offset])
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CalendarRangeSelectorDemo: View {
    @State private var start: Date?
    @State private var end: Date?

    private let calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)

    private var firstOfMarch: Date {
        calendar.date(from: DateComponents(year: 2026, month: 3, day: 1)) ?? .now
    }

    private var summary: String {
        guard let start else { return "Pick your arrival" }
        guard let end else { return "Now pick your departure" }
        let nights = calendar.dateComponents([.day], from: start, to: end).day ?? 0
        return nights == 1 ? "1 night" : "\(nights) nights"
    }

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 20) {
                Text("Book your stay")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())

                CalendarRangeSelector(start: $start, end: $end, month: firstOfMarch, calendar: calendar)
                    .padding(16)
                    .background(.background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 24))

                Label(summary, systemImage: "moon.stars.fill")
                    .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.indigo)
            }
            .padding(20)
        }
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo.opacity(0.25), .pink.opacity(0.15)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
        .environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "en_US"))
    }
}

#Preview {
    CalendarRangeSelectorDemo()
}
```

## Date Strip Picker

A horizontal strip of days that keeps the selected day centered as you scroll.

Category: Calendars. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Calendars/DateStripPicker/DateStripPicker.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A horizontal strip of days that keeps the selected day centered as you scroll.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, tapping a day jumps to it without scrolling.
struct DateStripPicker: View {
    @Binding var selection: Date
    var tint: Color

    private let days: [Date]
    private let calendar: Calendar

    @State private var centeredDay: Date?
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title2) private var itemWidth = 58.0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title2) private var itemHeight = 84.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let spacing = 10.0

    init(
        selection: Binding<Date>,
        center: Date = .now,
        daysBefore: Int = 30,
        daysAfter: Int = 30,
        calendar: Calendar = .current,
        tint: Color = .indigo
    ) {
        _selection = selection
        self.tint = tint
        self.calendar = calendar
        days = DateStripPickerLogic.days(around: center, before: daysBefore, after: daysAfter, calendar: calendar)
    }

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            ScrollView(.horizontal) {
                LazyHStack(spacing: spacing) {
                    ForEach(days, id: \.self) { dayCell($0) }
                }
                .scrollTargetLayout()
            }
            .contentMargins(.horizontal, max(0, (proxy.size.width - itemWidth) / 2), for: .scrollContent)
            .scrollIndicators(.hidden)
            .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)
            .scrollPosition(id: $centeredDay, anchor: .center)
        }
        .frame(height: itemHeight)
        .onAppear { centeredDay = closestDay(to: selection) }
        .onChange(of: centeredDay) { _, day in
            guard let day, day != calendar.startOfDay(for: selection) else { return }
            selection = day
        }
        .onChange(of: selection) { _, newValue in
            let day = closestDay(to: newValue)
            guard day != centeredDay else { return }
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy) { centeredDay = day }
        }
        .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: centeredDay) { old, new in old != nil && new != nil }
    }

    private func dayCell(_ day: Date) -> some View {
        let isSelected = day == calendar.startOfDay(for: selection)
        let isToday = calendar.isDateInToday(day)

        return Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy) { centeredDay = day }
        } label: {
            VStack(spacing: 4) {
                Text(format(day, Date.FormatStyle().weekday(.abbreviated)))
                    .font(.caption.weight(.medium))
                Text(format(day, Date.FormatStyle().day()))
                    .font(.title2.weight(.bold))
                Circle()
                    .fill(isToday ? (isSelected ? Color.white : tint) : Color.clear)
                    .frame(width: 5, height: 5)
            }
            .lineLimit(1)
            .minimumScaleFactor(0.7)
            .foregroundStyle(isSelected ? Color.white : Color.primary)
            .frame(width: itemWidth, height: itemHeight)
            .background(isSelected ? AnyShapeStyle(tint.gradient) : AnyShapeStyle(.thinMaterial), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 18))
            .scaleEffect(isSelected || reduceMotion ? 1 : 0.92)
            .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy, value: isSelected)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(format(day, Date.FormatStyle().weekday(.wide).day().month(.wide)))
        .accessibilityValue(isToday ? "Today" : "")
        .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])
    }

    private func closestDay(to date: Date) -> Date? {
        DateStripPickerLogic.closestDay(to: date, in: days, calendar: calendar)
    }

    private func format(_ date: Date, _ base: Date.FormatStyle) -> String {
        var style = base
        style.calendar = calendar
        style.timeZone = calendar.timeZone
        return date.formatted(style)
    }
}

/// The date math of the strip, apart from the view so it can be tested.
enum DateStripPickerLogic {
    /// Keeps a very wide request from building an enormous array.
    static let maximumDaysPerSide = 3_650

    static func days(around center: Date, before: Int, after: Int, calendar: Calendar) -> [Date] {
        let before = min(max(before, 0), maximumDaysPerSide)
        let after = min(max(after, 0), maximumDaysPerSide)
        let start = calendar.startOfDay(for: center)
        return (-before...after).compactMap { offset in
            calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: offset, to: start).map { calendar.startOfDay(for: $0) }
        }
    }

    /// The same day when it is in the strip, otherwise the nearest end of the strip.
    static func closestDay(to date: Date, in days: [Date], calendar: Calendar) -> Date? {
        let day = calendar.startOfDay(for: date)
        return days.first { $0 >= day } ?? days.last
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct DateStripPickerDemo: View {
    @State private var selection = Date.now

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo.opacity(0.3), .teal.opacity(0.2)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            DateStripPicker(selection: $selection)

            VStack {
                Text("Your agenda")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                Spacer()
                Text(selection, format: .dateTime.weekday(.wide).day().month(.wide))
                    .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))
                    .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
            }
            .padding(32)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    DateStripPickerDemo()
}
```

## Avatar Stack

Overlapping avatars of initials with a badge counting the rest.

Category: Cards. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Cards/AvatarStack/AvatarStack.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum AvatarStackMath {
    /// Splits a number of people into the avatars to draw and the count for the badge.
    static func visibleAndOverflow(count: Int, maxVisible: Int) -> (visible: Int, overflow: Int) {
        let visible = min(max(count, 0), max(maxVisible, 0))
        return (visible, max(count, 0) - visible)
    }

    /// The first letters of the first and last words of a name.
    static func initials(of name: String) -> String {
        let words = name.split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace)
        guard let first = words.first?.first else { return "?" }
        guard words.count > 1, let last = words.last?.first else { return String(first).uppercased() }
        return "\(first)\(last)".uppercased()
    }
}

/// Overlapping avatars of initials, with a +N badge for everyone who does not fit.
struct AvatarStack: View {
    let names: [String]
    var maxVisible = 4
    var diameter: CGFloat = 48

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) private var textScale = 1.0

    private var size: CGFloat { diameter * textScale }

    private static var palette: [Color] { [.indigo, .pink, .orange, .teal, .purple, .blue] }

    private var split: (visible: Int, overflow: Int) {
        AvatarStackMath.visibleAndOverflow(count: names.count, maxVisible: maxVisible)
    }

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: -size * 0.28) {
            ForEach(Array(names.prefix(split.visible).enumerated()), id: \.offset) { index, name in
                circle(AvatarStackMath.initials(of: name), fill: color(for: name))
                    .zIndex(Double(-index))
                    .transition(.scale.combined(with: .opacity))
            }

            if split.overflow > 0 {
                circle("+\(split.overflow)", fill: .gray)
                    .contentTransition(.numericText())
                    .zIndex(Double(-split.visible))
                    .transition(.scale.combined(with: .opacity))
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(names.isEmpty ? "No people" : names.formatted(.list(type: .and)))
    }

    private func circle(_ text: String, fill: Color) -> some View {
        Text(text)
            .font(.system(.title3, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            .minimumScaleFactor(0.6)
            .lineLimit(1)
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .frame(width: size, height: size)
            .background(fill.gradient, in: .circle)
            .overlay { Circle().strokeBorder(.background, lineWidth: 3) }
    }

    private func color(for name: String) -> Color {
        let total = name.unicodeScalars.reduce(0) { $0 + Int($1.value) }
        return Self.palette[total % Self.palette.count]
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct AvatarStackDemo: View {
    private let everyone = ["Ana Ruiz", "Luis Vega", "Marta Gil", "Omar Haddad", "Nora Lind", "Pablo Sanz", "Yuki Mori", "Sara Blanco", "Tomás Rey"]

    @State private var count = 3
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 28) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
                Text("Design review")
                    .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                Text("Today at 16:30")
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)

                AvatarStack(names: Array(everyone.prefix(count)), diameter: 64)
                    .padding(.top, 8)
            }
            .padding(24)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            .background(.background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 28))
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.12), radius: 18, y: 10)

            HStack(spacing: 14) {
                Button("Remove", systemImage: "person.badge.minus") { change(by: -1) }
                    .disabled(count == 0)
                Button("Add", systemImage: "person.badge.plus") { change(by: 1) }
                    .disabled(count == everyone.count)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
            .controlSize(.large)
        }
        .padding(24)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: [.purple.opacity(0.4), .orange.opacity(0.3)], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
    }

    private func change(by amount: Int) {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .bouncy(duration: 0.4)) { count += amount }
    }
```

```swift
/// White or black, whichever reads better on `background`. Black only on a
/// light color, so the system's own colors keep white.
nonisolated struct ExpandableInfoCardContrastingForeground: ShapeStyle {
    let background: Color

    func resolve(in environment: EnvironmentValues) -> Color {
        let color = background.resolve(in: environment)
        let luminance = 0.2126 * color.linearRed + 0.7152 * color.linearGreen + 0.0722 * color.linearBlue
        return luminance > 0.5 ? .black : .white
    }
}
```

## Holographic Card

A card with a holographic foil whose colors, glints and glare shift as you tilt it by dragging, drawn by a Metal shader.

Category: Cards. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Cards/HolographicCard/HolographicCard.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum HolographicCardMath {
    /// How far the card leans for a drag, from -1 to 1 on each axis.
    /// Dragging half the card's size leans it all the way.
    static func tilt(for translation: CGSize, in size: CGSize) -> CGSize {
        guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0 else { return .zero }
        return CGSize(
            width: min(max(translation.width / (size.width / 2), -1), 1),
            height: min(max(translation.height / (size.height / 2), -1), 1)
        )
    }

    /// The degrees the card turns around its vertical axis for a lean from -1 to 1.
    /// `rotation3DEffect` mirrors in a right-to-left layout and a drag does not, so the turn is reversed there.
    static func yaw(for lean: Double, maxAngle: Double, layoutDirection: LayoutDirection) -> Double {
        let turn = lean * maxAngle
        return layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? -turn : turn
    }

    /// The function in `HolographicCard.metal`, with its arguments in the order it declares them.
    static func shader(size: CGSize, tilt: CGSize, intensity: Double) -> Shader {
        ShaderLibrary.HolographicCardFoil(.float2(size), .float2(tilt), .float(intensity))
    }
}

/// A card with a holographic foil that shifts as you tilt it by dragging, drawn by a Metal shader.
///
/// Copy two files into the same target: `HolographicCard.swift` and `HolographicCard.metal`.
/// A shader draws what SwiftUI draws itself: a view backed by UIKit, such as a map, shows a placeholder.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the card stays flat and the foil stays still.
struct HolographicCard<Content: View>: View {
    /// The degrees the card leans at the end of a drag.
    var maxAngle: Double = 16
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat = 28
    /// How much foil the card has, from 0 for none to 1.
    var intensity: Double = 1
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @GestureState private var tilt = CGSize.zero
    @State private var size = CGSize.zero
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self) { $0.size } action: { size = $0 }
            .modifier(
                HolographicCardSurface(
                    tilt: reduceMotion ? .zero : tilt,
                    size: size,
                    maxAngle: maxAngle,
                    cornerRadius: cornerRadius,
                    intensity: intensity
                )
            )
            .gesture(drag)
            .animation(.spring(duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.3), value: tilt)
    }

    private var drag: some Gesture {
        DragGesture(coordinateSpace: .global)
            .updating($tilt) { value, tilt, _ in
                tilt = HolographicCardMath.tilt(for: value.translation, in: size)
            }
    }
}

/// `Animatable`, so the foil follows the same spring as the lean: a shader's arguments do not animate by themselves.
private struct HolographicCardSurface: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var tilt: CGSize
    let size: CGSize
    let maxAngle: Double
    let cornerRadius: CGFloat
    let intensity: Double

    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    nonisolated var animatableData: CGSize.AnimatableData {
        get { tilt.animatableData }
        set { tilt.animatableData = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .colorEffect(HolographicCardMath.shader(size: size, tilt: tilt, intensity: intensity))
            .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.4), radius: 24, y: 16)
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(-tilt.height * maxAngle), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0), perspective: 0.6)
            .rotation3DEffect(
                .degrees(HolographicCardMath.yaw(for: tilt.width, maxAngle: maxAngle, layoutDirection: layoutDirection)),
                axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0),
                perspective: 0.6
            )
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct HolographicCardDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [Color(red: 0.04, green: 0.04, blue: 0.09), Color(red: 0.14, green: 0.09, blue: 0.27)],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )
            .ignoresSafeArea()

            HolographicCard {
                card
            }

        }
    }

        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
            HStack {
                Image(systemName: "sparkles")
                    .font(.title)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text("No. 001")
                    .font(.footnote.monospaced())
                    .opacity(0.7)
            }

            Spacer()

            Text("Prism Pass")
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            Text("Drag to tilt the card")
                .font(.subheadline)
                .opacity(0.8)
        }
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .padding(24)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
        .aspectRatio(0.68, contentMode: .fit)
        .background(
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [
                    Color(red: 0.1, green: 0.12, blue: 0.3),
                    Color(red: 0.32, green: 0.12, blue: 0.42),
                    Color(red: 0.06, green: 0.06, blue: 0.14),
                ],
                startPoint: .topLeading,
                endPoint: .bottomTrailing
            )
        )
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
    }
}
```

Shader: Components/Cards/HolographicCard/HolographicCard.metal

```metal
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>

using namespace metal;

// A repeatable pseudo-random number from 0 to 1 for each cell of a grid.
static float HolographicCardRandom(float2 cell) {
    uint2 seed = uint2(int2(cell));
    uint mixed = (seed.x * 0x9E3779B1u) ^ (seed.y * 0x85EBCA77u);
    mixed ^= mixed >> 15;
    mixed *= 0x2C1B3C6Du;
    mixed ^= mixed >> 12;
    return float(mixed & 0xFFFFu) / 65535.0;
}

// For SwiftUI's `colorEffect`. Adds a holographic foil to each pixel of a view
// of `size` points. `tilt` runs from -1 to 1 on each axis, and moves the colors
// and the glare as a real card does when it turns under a light.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 HolographicCardFoil(float2 position, half4 color, float2 size, float2 tilt, float intensity) {
    if (color.a <= 0.0) {
        return color;
    }
    float2 fromCenter = position / max(size, float2(1.0)) - 0.5;

    // A diffraction foil changes hue with the viewing angle, so its bands of
    // color slide across the card as it tilts.
    float angle = dot(fromCenter, float2(0.9, 0.5)) * 1.4 + dot(tilt, float2(0.8, 0.6));
    float3 spectrum = 0.5 + 0.5 * cos(6.2831853 * (angle + float3(0.0, 0.33, 0.67)));

    // Specks of glitter, one in each cell of a grid and somewhere off its
    // center. Each catches the light at its own angle, so they twinkle in turn.
    float2 grid = position / 5.0;
    float2 cell = floor(grid);
    float2 speck = 0.5 + 0.56 * (float2(HolographicCardRandom(cell + 17.0), HolographicCardRandom(cell + 43.0)) - 0.5);
    float shape = saturate(1.0 - length(grid - cell - speck) / 0.22);
    float facing = 0.5 + 0.5 * cos(6.2831853 * (HolographicCardRandom(cell) + angle * 2.0));
    float glint = smoothstep(0.55, 1.0, facing) * shape * shape;

    // The glare of a light above the card slides against the tilt.
    float2 fromGlare = fromCenter + tilt * 0.35;
    float glare = exp(-6.0 * dot(fromGlare, fromGlare));

    float3 foil = intensity * (spectrum * (0.14 + 0.4 * glare) + glint * (0.3 + 0.7 * glare));

    // Screen the foil over the pixel, so it only ever adds light. Colors come
    // premultiplied by their alpha.
    float3 base = float3(color.rgb) / color.a;
    float3 lit = 1.0 - (1.0 - base) * (1.0 - saturate(foil));
    return half4(half3(lit * color.a), color.a);
}
```

## Swipeable Card Stack

A deck of cards you swipe away to reveal the next one.

Category: Cards. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Cards/SwipeableCardStack/SwipeableCardStack.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum SwipeableCardStackDirection: Equatable, Sendable {
    case left, right

    var sign: CGFloat { self == .left ? -1 : 1 }
}

enum SwipeableCardStackLogic {
    /// Decides where a released card goes from where its momentum would carry it,
    /// so both a long drag and a short flick count, and a flick back cancels.
    static func direction(predictedEnd: CGFloat, width: CGFloat, threshold: CGFloat = 0.35) -> SwipeableCardStackDirection? {
        guard width > 0, abs(predictedEnd) >= width * threshold else { return nil }
        return predictedEnd > 0 ? .right : .left
    }

    /// One swiped card still flying away, the top card and three behind it.
    /// Empty when the deck shrank below the cards already swiped.
    static func positions(top: Int, count: Int, loops: Bool) -> [Int] {
        guard count > 0 else { return [] }
        let start = max(top - 1, 0)
        let end = loops ? top + 4 : min(top + 4, count)
        return start < end ? Array(start..<end) : []
    }
}

/// A deck of cards. Swipe the top one away to reveal the next.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, a swiped card fades out instead of flying away.
struct SwipeableCardStack<Item, Card: View>: View {
    let items: [Item]
    var loops = false
    var threshold: CGFloat = 0.35
    var onSwipe: (Item, SwipeableCardStackDirection) -> Void = { _, _ in }
    @ViewBuilder var card: (Item) -> Card

    @State private var top = 0
    @State private var drag = CGSize.zero
    @State private var lastDirection = SwipeableCardStackDirection.right
    @State private var size = CGSize.zero
    @GestureState private var isDragging = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    private var width: CGFloat { size.width }

    /// Gestures and swipe directions are in screen terms, but layout mirrors in right-to-left
    /// layouts: 1 or -1 converts between them.
    private var forward: CGFloat { layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? -1 : 1 }

    private var hasTopCard: Bool { !items.isEmpty && (loops || top < items.count) }

    private var positions: [Int] {
        SwipeableCardStackLogic.positions(top: top, count: items.count, loops: loops)
    }

    private var dragProgress: CGFloat {
        min(abs(drag.width) / max(width * threshold, 1), 1)
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            ForEach(positions, id: \.self) { position in
                let depth = max(CGFloat(position - top) - dragProgress, 0)

                card(items[position % items.count])
                    .scaleEffect(1 - depth * 0.06)
                    .offset(offset(of: position, depth: depth))
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(rotation(of: position)))
                    .opacity(position < top || position - top > 2 ? 0 : 1)
                    .zIndex(Double(-position))
                    .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
                    .accessibilityHidden(position != top)
                    .accessibilityAction(named: "Swipe left") { swipe(.left) }
                    .accessibilityAction(named: "Swipe right") { swipe(.right) }
            }
        }
        .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self) { $0.size } action: { size = $0 }
        .contentShape(.rect)
        .gesture(dragGesture)
        .onChange(of: isDragging) { _, dragging in
            if !dragging {
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.3)) { drag = .zero }
            }
        }
    }

    private func offset(of position: Int, depth: CGFloat) -> CGSize {
        if position < top {
            return CGSize(width: reduceMotion ? 0 : lastDirection.sign * forward * width * 1.5, height: 0)
        }
        if position == top {
            return CGSize(width: drag.width, height: drag.height * 0.25)
        }
        // Scaling shrinks a card around its center, so move it down by that amount plus the visible peek.
        return CGSize(width: 0, height: depth * (size.height * 0.03 + 14))
    }

    private func rotation(of position: Int) -> Double {
        guard !reduceMotion, width > 0 else { return 0 }
        if position < top { return Double(lastDirection.sign * forward) * 18 }
        return position == top ? Double(drag.width / width) * 14 : 0
    }

    private var dragGesture: some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 8)
            .updating($isDragging) { _, state, _ in state = true }
            .onChanged { value in
                if hasTopCard { drag = CGSize(width: value.translation.width * forward, height: value.translation.height) }
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                let predictedEnd = value.predictedEndTranslation.width
                if let direction = SwipeableCardStackLogic.direction(predictedEnd: predictedEnd, width: width, threshold: threshold) {
                    swipe(direction)
                }
            }
    }

    private func swipe(_ direction: SwipeableCardStackDirection) {
        guard hasTopCard else { return }
        let item = items[top % items.count]
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .snappy(duration: 0.4)) {
            lastDirection = direction
            top += 1
            drag = .zero
        }
        onSwipe(item, direction)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

}
```

## Tilt Card

A card that tilts in 3D toward the finger with a moving highlight.

Category: Cards. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Cards/TiltCard/TiltCard.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A card that leans in 3D toward the finger, with a highlight that follows it.
///
/// `restingPoint` is where the card leans while nobody touches it. `nil` keeps it flat.
/// With Reduce Motion on, the card stays flat and only the highlight moves.
struct TiltCard<Content: View>: View {
    var maxAngle: Double = 14
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat = 28
    var restingPoint: UnitPoint?
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @GestureState private var touchPoint: UnitPoint?
    @State private var size = CGSize.zero
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    private var focus: UnitPoint? { touchPoint ?? restingPoint }

    private var pitch: Double {
        guard let focus, !reduceMotion else { return 0 }
        return (0.5 - focus.y) * 2 * maxAngle
    }

    private var yaw: Double {
        guard let focus, !reduceMotion else { return 0 }
        return (focus.x - 0.5) * 2 * maxAngle
    }

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .overlay { highlight }
            .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self) { $0.size } action: { size = $0 }
            .gesture(tilt)
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.35), radius: 24, y: 16)
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(pitch), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0), perspective: 0.6)
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(yaw), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0), perspective: 0.6)
            .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.3), value: touchPoint)
    }

    private var highlight: some View {
        RadialGradient(
            colors: [.white.opacity(0.35), .white.opacity(0)],
            center: focus ?? .center,
            startRadius: 0,
            endRadius: max(size.width, size.height) * 0.8
        )
        .blendMode(.plusLighter)
        .opacity(focus == nil ? 0 : 1)
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private var tilt: some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
            .updating($touchPoint) { value, state, _ in
                guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0 else { return }
                // Gestures report screen points, but a unit point counts from the leading edge.
                let x = min(max(value.location.x / size.width, 0), 1)
                state = UnitPoint(
                    x: layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? 1 - x : x,
                    y: min(max(value.location.y / size.height, 0), 1)
                )
            }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct TiltCardDemo: View {
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 60.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
                let time = context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * 1.6

                TiltCard(restingPoint: reduceMotion ? nil : UnitPoint(x: 0.5 + 0.45 * cos(time), y: 0.5 + 0.45 * sin(time))) {
                    card
                }
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 44)
        }
    }

    private var card: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
            Image(systemName: "sparkles")
                .font(.largeTitle)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Spacer()

            Text("Aurora Pass")
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            Text("Touch and move your finger")
                .font(.subheadline)
                .opacity(0.8)
        }
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .padding(24)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
        .aspectRatio(0.68, contentMode: .fit)
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: [.purple, .pink, .orange], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
    }
}
```

## Wallet Card Stack

A stack of cards where the one you tap rises to the top with its details and the rest wait in a pile below.

Category: Cards. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Cards/WalletCardStack/WalletCardStack.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum WalletCardStackMath {
    /// The distance between the tops of two cards in the stack.
    ///
    /// It is `peek`, or less when the stack would not fit in `height`.
    static func step(count: Int, peek: Double, cardHeight: Double, height: Double) -> Double {
        guard count > 1, peek.isFinite, cardHeight.isFinite, height.isFinite else { return 0 }
        let room = max(height - cardHeight, 0)
        return min(max(peek, 0), room / Double(count - 1))
    }

    /// Where the top of each card goes.
    ///
    /// With no card open they sit one below another, `step` apart. With one open, it goes to the
    /// top and the others gather in a pile that keeps `pileHeight` at the bottom of `height`.
    static func tops(count: Int, selected: Int?, step: Double, height: Double, pileHeight: Double, pileStep: Double = 14) -> [Double] {
        guard count > 0 else { return [] }
        guard let selected, (0..<count).contains(selected) else {
            return (0..<count).map { Double($0) * step }
        }

        let others = count - 1
        let gap = others > 0 ? min(max(pileStep, 0), max(pileHeight, 0) / Double(others)) : 0
        var place = 0
        return (0..<count).map { index in
            guard index != selected else { return 0 }
            defer { place += 1 }
            return height - pileHeight + Double(place) * gap
        }
    }
}

/// A stack of cards, each one showing its top edge above the next. Tap a card and it rises to the
/// top with its details below, while the others wait in a pile at the bottom. Tap again to close.
///
/// Give it the height it can use: the stack tightens to fit, and the pile sits at the bottom edge.
/// With Reduce Motion on, the cards change places without sliding.
struct WalletCardStack<Item: Identifiable, Card: View, Detail: View>: View {
    let items: [Item]
    /// The card that is open, or `nil` when all of them are in the stack.
    @Binding var selection: Item.ID?
    var cardHeight: CGFloat = 200
    /// How much of a card shows above the next one in the stack. It grows with Dynamic Type.
    var peek: CGFloat = 64
    /// How much room the other cards keep at the bottom while one is open.
    var pileHeight: CGFloat = 76
    @ViewBuilder var card: (Item) -> Card
    @ViewBuilder var detail: (Item) -> Detail

    private let spacing: CGFloat = 16
    private let shadowRoom: CGFloat = 40

    @State private var height: CGFloat = 0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .headline) private var textScale = 1.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        let selected = items.firstIndex { $0.id == selection }
        let step = WalletCardStackMath.step(count: items.count, peek: peek * textScale, cardHeight: cardHeight, height: height)
        let tops = WalletCardStackMath.tops(count: items.count, selected: selected, step: step, height: height, pileHeight: pileHeight)

        ZStack(alignment: .top) {
            if let selected {
                detail(items[selected])
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .top)
                    .frame(height: max(height - cardHeight - pileHeight - spacing * 2, 0), alignment: .top)
                    .clipped()
                    .offset(y: cardHeight + spacing)
                    .transition(.opacity)
            }

            ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, item in
                // In the stack only the top edge of a card is free, so that is where assistive touches land.
                let shown = selected == nil && index < items.count - 1 ? min(step, cardHeight) : cardHeight

                Button {
                    selection = selection == nil ? item.id : nil
                } label: {
                    card(item)
                        .frame(height: cardHeight)
                }
                .buttonStyle(WalletCardStackPressStyle())
                .offset(y: tops[index])
                .zIndex(Double(index + 1))
                .accessibilityActivationPoint(UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: cardHeight > 0 ? shown / cardHeight / 2 : 0.5))
                .accessibilityAddTraits(index == selected ? .isSelected : [])
                .accessibilityHint(index == selected ? "Returns to the stack" : "Shows its details")
                .accessibilityHidden(selected != nil && index != selected)
                .accessibilitySortPriority(index == selected ? 1 : 0)
            }
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .top)
        .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.height } action: { height = $0 }
        // Cuts the pile at the bottom edge and leaves room for the shadows of the cards everywhere else.
        .mask { Rectangle().padding(.horizontal, -shadowRoom).padding(.top, -shadowRoom) }
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.2), value: selection)
        .accessibilityAction(.escape) { selection = nil }
    }
}

private struct WalletCardStackPressStyle: ButtonStyle {
    func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
        configuration.label
            .scaleEffect(configuration.isPressed ? 0.98 : 1)
            .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.15), value: configuration.isPressed)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

    let id: Int
    let name: String

    let payments: [(place: String, symbol: String, amount: Double)]
}
```

## Animated Bar Chart

Bars that grow from the baseline one after another with a spring.

Category: Charts. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Charts/AnimatedBarChart/AnimatedBarChart.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct AnimatedBarChartEntry: Hashable {
    let label: String
    let value: Double
}

/// Bars that grow from the baseline one after another, and again whenever the data changes.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the bars are drawn at their final height.
struct AnimatedBarChart: View {
    let entries: [AnimatedBarChartEntry]
    var tint: Color = .indigo
    var stagger: Double = 0.09

    @State private var isRevealed = false
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption2) private var valueHeight = 22.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 8) {
            GeometryReader { proxy in
                HStack(spacing: 10) {
                    ForEach(Array(entries.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { index, entry in
                        column(entry, index: index, plotHeight: max(0, proxy.size.height - valueHeight))
                    }
                }
            }

            HStack(spacing: 10) {
                ForEach(Array(entries.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { _, entry in
                    Text(entry.label)
                        .font(.caption)
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                        .lineLimit(1)
                        .minimumScaleFactor(0.6)
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                }
            }
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
        .task(id: entries) {
            guard !reduceMotion else {
                isRevealed = true
                return
            }
            var reset = Transaction()
            reset.disablesAnimations = true
            withTransaction(reset) { isRevealed = false }
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(50))
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            isRevealed = true
        }
    }

    private func column(_ entry: AnimatedBarChartEntry, index: Int, plotHeight: CGFloat) -> some View {
        let isShown = isRevealed || reduceMotion
        let ratio = AnimatedBarChartLogic.ratio(of: entry.value, in: entries.map(\.value))
        let valueText = entry.value.formatted()

        return VStack(spacing: 4) {
            Text(valueText)
                .font(.caption2.weight(.semibold))
                .lineLimit(1)
                .minimumScaleFactor(0.6)
                .opacity(isShown ? 1 : 0)

            UnevenRoundedRectangle(topLeadingRadius: 8, topTrailingRadius: 8)
                .fill(tint.gradient)
                .frame(height: isShown ? plotHeight * ratio : 0)
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .bottom)
        .animation(
            reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.6, bounce: 0.3).delay(Double(index) * max(0, stagger)),
            value: isRevealed
        )
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(entry.label)
        .accessibilityValue(valueText)
    }
}

enum AnimatedBarChartLogic {
    /// How tall a bar is compared with the tallest, from 0 to 1.
    static func ratio(of value: Double, in values: [Double]) -> Double {
        guard value.isFinite, value > 0,
              let highest = values.filter(\.isFinite).max(), highest > 0 else { return 0 }
        return min(value / highest, 1)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct AnimatedBarChartDemo: View {
    @State private var index = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let weeks: [(title: String, values: [Double])] = [
        ("This week", [12, 19, 8, 24, 16, 30, 22]),
        ("Last week", [20, 11, 27, 14, 29, 9, 17]),
    ]

    private var week: (title: String, values: [Double]) {
        weeks[index % weeks.count]
    }

    private var entries: [AnimatedBarChartEntry] {
        zip(["M", "T", "W", "T", "F", "S", "S"], week.values).map { AnimatedBarChartEntry(label: $0, value: $1) }
    }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
            Text("Workouts")
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            Text(week.title)
                .font(.title3)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)

            AnimatedBarChart(entries: entries)
                .padding(.top, 24)
        }
        .padding(24)
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2.6))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                index = (index + 1) % weeks.count
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    AnimatedBarChartDemo()
}
```

## Animated Donut Chart

A donut chart whose segments grow in one by one, and the selected segment lifts out.

Category: Charts. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Charts/AnimatedDonutChart/AnimatedDonutChart.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import Charts
import SwiftUI

struct AnimatedDonutChartSegment: Identifiable, Hashable {
    let id: String
    let value: Double
    let color: Color
}

/// A donut chart whose segments grow in one by one, and the selected segment lifts out.
///
/// Tap a segment or its legend row to select it. With Reduce Motion on, the whole donut
/// appears at once.
struct AnimatedDonutChart: View {
    let segments: [AnimatedDonutChartSegment]
    @Binding var selection: String?

    @State private var revealedCount = 0
    @State private var touchedAngle: Double?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var visibleCount: Int { reduceMotion ? segments.count : revealedCount }
    private var total: Double { AnimatedDonutChartLogic.total(of: segments) }

    private var visibleTotal: Double {
        AnimatedDonutChartLogic.total(of: Array(segments.prefix(visibleCount)))
    }

    private var selectedSegment: AnimatedDonutChartSegment? {
        segments.first { $0.id == selection }
    }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 24) {
            ZStack {
                chart
                centerLabel
            }
            .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)

            legend
        }
        .task(id: segments) {
            guard !reduceMotion else {
                revealedCount = segments.count
                return
            }
            var reset = Transaction()
            reset.disablesAnimations = true
            withTransaction(reset) { revealedCount = 0 }

            for count in segments.indices {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(count == 0 ? 60 : 260))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.35)) { revealedCount = count + 1 }
            }
        }
        .onChange(of: touchedAngle) { oldValue, newValue in
            guard let newValue,
                  let id = AnimatedDonutChartLogic.segmentID(atAngleValue: newValue, in: segments) else { return }
            selection = oldValue == nil && selection == id ? nil : id
        }
    }

    private var chart: some View {
        Chart {
            ForEach(Array(segments.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, segment in
                SectorMark(
                    angle: .value("Value", index < visibleCount ? AnimatedDonutChartLogic.sanitized(segment.value) : 0),
                    innerRadius: .ratio(0.62),
                    outerRadius: .ratio(selection == segment.id ? 1 : 0.9),
                    angularInset: 1.5
                )
                .cornerRadius(5)
                .foregroundStyle(segment.color)
                .opacity(selection == nil || selection == segment.id ? 1 : 0.4)
            }

            // The empty part of the ring, so that early segments do not fill the circle.
            SectorMark(
                angle: .value("Remaining", total > 0 ? max(total - visibleTotal, 0) : 1),
                innerRadius: .ratio(0.62),
                outerRadius: .ratio(0.9)
            )
            .foregroundStyle(total > 0 ? Color.clear : Color.secondary.opacity(0.2))
        }
        .chartLegend(.hidden)
        .chartAngleSelection(value: $touchedAngle)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy, value: selection)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private var centerLabel: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 2) {
            Text(selectedSegment?.id ?? "Total")
                .font(.subheadline)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            Text((selectedSegment?.value ?? total).formatted())
                .font(.title.bold())
                .contentTransition(reduceMotion ? .identity : .numericText())
                .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy, value: selection)
        }
        .lineLimit(1)
        .minimumScaleFactor(0.5)
        .frame(maxWidth: 130)
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private var legend: some View {
        LazyVGrid(columns: [GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: 150), alignment: .leading)], alignment: .leading, spacing: 10) {
            ForEach(segments) { segment in
                let isSelected = selection == segment.id
                let percent = AnimatedDonutChartLogic.share(of: segment, in: segments).formatted(.percent.precision(.fractionLength(0)))

                Button {
                    selection = isSelected ? nil : segment.id
                } label: {
                    HStack(spacing: 8) {
                        Circle().fill(segment.color).frame(width: 10, height: 10)
                        Text(segment.id)
                        Spacer(minLength: 4)
                        Text(percent).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    }
                    .font(isSelected ? .subheadline.weight(.semibold) : .subheadline)
                    // A row is too short to hit. The padding widens what answers to a touch,
                    // and the same padding taken back keeps the legend as compact as it was.
                    .padding(.vertical, 13)
                    .contentShape(.rect)
                    .padding(.vertical, -13)
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
                .accessibilityLabel(segment.id)
                .accessibilityValue("\(segment.value.formatted()), \(percent)")
                .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])
            }
        }
    }
}

enum AnimatedDonutChartLogic {
    static func sanitized(_ value: Double) -> Double {
        value.isFinite ? max(value, 0) : 0
    }

    static func total(of segments: [AnimatedDonutChartSegment]) -> Double {
        segments.reduce(0) { $0 + sanitized($1.value) }
    }

    static func share(of segment: AnimatedDonutChartSegment, in segments: [AnimatedDonutChartSegment]) -> Double {
        let total = total(of: segments)
        return total > 0 ? sanitized(segment.value) / total : 0
    }

    /// Finds the segment under an angle, given in the same units as the values.
    static func segmentID(atAngleValue angle: Double, in segments: [AnimatedDonutChartSegment]) -> String? {
        guard angle.isFinite, angle >= 0 else { return nil }
        var cumulative = 0.0
        for segment in segments where sanitized(segment.value) > 0 {
            cumulative += sanitized(segment.value)
            if angle <= cumulative { return segment.id }
        }
        return nil
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct AnimatedDonutChartDemo: View {
    @State private var selection: String?
    @State private var isAlternate = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var segments: [AnimatedDonutChartSegment] {
        let values: [Double] = isAlternate ? [980, 240, 310, 160] : [1_120, 420, 180, 290]
        return zip(zip(["Housing", "Food", "Travel", "Fun"], values), [Color.indigo, .teal, .orange, .pink])
            .map { AnimatedDonutChartSegment(id: $0.0, value: $0.1, color: $1) }
    }

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 24) {
                Text("Spending")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())

                AnimatedDonutChart(segments: segments, selection: $selection)
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.5))
                for id in ["Housing", "Travel"] {
                    guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                    selection = id
                    try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.8))
                }
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                selection = nil
                isAlternate.toggle()
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    AnimatedDonutChartDemo()
}
```

## Candlestick Chart

A candlestick chart of open, high, low and close prices, with a rule that reads the day under the finger.

Category: Charts. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Charts/CandlestickChart/CandlestickChart.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import Charts
import SwiftUI

nonisolated struct CandlestickChartCandle: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable {
    var date: Date
    var open: Double
    var high: Double
    var low: Double
    var close: Double

    var id: Date { date }
    var isRising: Bool { close >= open }
}

nonisolated enum CandlestickChartMath {
    /// The prices the chart shows: from the lowest low to the highest high, with some room at
    /// both ends so no candle touches the edge.
    static func domain(of candles: [CandlestickChartCandle], padding: Double = 0.08) -> ClosedRange<Double> {
        guard let low = candles.map(\.low).min(), let high = candles.map(\.high).max(), high >= low else { return 0...1 }
        let room = max(high - low, abs(high) * 0.01, 0.01) * max(padding, 0)
        return (low - room)...(high + room)
    }

    /// The two ends of the body of a candle. A day that closed where it opened still gets a body
    /// `minimum` tall, so it shows as a line instead of vanishing.
    static func body(of candle: CandlestickChartCandle, minimum: Double) -> ClosedRange<Double> {
        let low = min(candle.open, candle.close)
        let high = max(candle.open, candle.close)
        let missing = max(minimum - (high - low), 0)
        return (low - missing / 2)...(high + missing / 2)
    }

    /// How much the price moved from open to close, as a share of the open.
    static func change(of candle: CandlestickChartCandle) -> Double {
        candle.open != 0 ? (candle.close - candle.open) / candle.open : 0
    }

    /// The candle of the day closest to a date, which is how a touch between two days picks one.
    static func nearest(to date: Date, in candles: [CandlestickChartCandle]) -> CandlestickChartCandle? {
        candles.min { abs($0.date.timeIntervalSince(date)) < abs($1.date.timeIntervalSince(date)) }
    }
}

/// A candlestick chart: each day is a thin line from its low to its high and a body from its
/// open to its close, in one color when the price rose and another when it fell.
///
/// Drag over it to read a day: a rule follows the finger and `selection` gets its candle.
/// VoiceOver reads the four prices of each day. With Differentiate Without Color on, the days
/// that fell are drawn lighter, so the two kinds do not depend on the color alone.
struct CandlestickChart: View {
    let candles: [CandlestickChartCandle]
    @Binding var selection: CandlestickChartCandle?
    var risingColor = Color.green
    var fallingColor = Color.red

    @State private var selectedDate: Date?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityDifferentiateWithoutColor) private var differentiateWithoutColor

    var body: some View {
        let domain = CandlestickChartMath.domain(of: candles)
        let minimumBody = (domain.upperBound - domain.lowerBound) * 0.004

        Chart {
            ForEach(candles) { candle in
                let color = candle.isRising ? risingColor : fallingColor
                let prices = CandlestickChartMath.body(of: candle, minimum: minimumBody)

                RuleMark(
                    x: .value("Day", candle.date, unit: .day),
                    yStart: .value("Low", candle.low),
                    yEnd: .value("High", candle.high)
                )
                .lineStyle(StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 1.5, lineCap: .round))
                .foregroundStyle(color)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

                RectangleMark(
                    x: .value("Day", candle.date, unit: .day),
                    yStart: .value("Open", prices.lowerBound),
                    yEnd: .value("Close", prices.upperBound),
                    width: .ratio(0.62)
                )
                .foregroundStyle(color.opacity(!candle.isRising && differentiateWithoutColor ? 0.45 : 1))
                .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 1.5))
                .accessibilityLabel(candle.date.formatted(date: .abbreviated, time: .omitted))
                .accessibilityValue(description(of: candle))
            }

            if let selection {
                RuleMark(x: .value("Selected", selection.date, unit: .day))
                    .lineStyle(StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 1, dash: [3, 3]))
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
        }
        .chartYScale(domain: domain)
        .chartXAxis {
            AxisMarks(preset: .aligned)
        }
        .chartXSelection(value: $selectedDate)
        .onChange(of: selectedDate) { _, date in
            selection = date.flatMap { CandlestickChartMath.nearest(to: $0, in: candles) }
        }
        .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: selection)
    }

    private func description(of candle: CandlestickChartCandle) -> String {
        let prices = [("Open", candle.open), ("high", candle.high), ("low", candle.low), ("close", candle.close)]
        return prices.map { "\($0.0) \($0.1.formatted(.number.precision(.fractionLength(2))))" }.joined(separator: ", ")
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CandlestickChartDemo: View {
    @State private var selection: CandlestickChartCandle?

    /// A month of made-up prices, the same on every run.
    private let candles: [CandlestickChartCandle] = {
        var seed: UInt64 = 42
        func next() -> Double {
            seed = seed &* 6_364_136_223_846_793_005 &+ 1_442_695_040_888_963_407
            return Double(seed >> 33) / Double(1 << 31)
        }
        let start = Date(timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate: 815_000_000)
        var price = 182.0
        return (0..<30).map { day in
            let open = price
            let close = open + (next() - 0.47) * 9
            let high = max(open, close) + next() * 4
            let low = min(open, close) - next() * 4
            price = close
            return CandlestickChartCandle(date: start.addingTimeInterval(Double(day) * 86_400), open: open, high: high, low: low, close: close)
        }
    }()

    private var shown: CandlestickChartCandle? { selection ?? candles.last }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 18) {
            if let shown {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                    Text("ACME")
                        .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline) {
                        Text(shown.close, format: .currency(code: "USD"))
                            .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                        Text(CandlestickChartMath.change(of: shown), format: .percent.precision(.fractionLength(1)).sign(strategy: .always()))
                            .font(.headline)
                            .foregroundStyle(shown.isRising ? .green : .red)
                    }
                    .monospacedDigit()
                    .contentTransition(.numericText())
                    Text(selection == nil ? "Last close · drag to read a day" : shown.date.formatted(date: .abbreviated, time: .omitted))
                        .font(.footnote)
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
                .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)

                CandlestickChart(candles: candles, selection: $selection)
                    .frame(height: 280)

                HStack {
                    price("Open", shown.open)
                    price("High", shown.high)
                    price("Low", shown.low)
                    price("Close", shown.close)
                }
            }
        }
        .padding(20)
        .background(.background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 24))
        .padding(16)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground))
    }

    private func price(_ title: String, _ value: Double) -> some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
            Text(title)
                .font(.caption)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            Text(value, format: .number.precision(.fractionLength(2)))
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                .monospacedDigit()
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
    }
}

    CandlestickChartDemo()
}
```
