## Contribution Heatmap

A calendar grid of colored cells whose intensity shows the activity of each day.

Category: Charts. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Charts/ContributionHeatmap/ContributionHeatmap.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A calendar grid of colored cells whose intensity shows the activity of each day.
///
/// It opens scrolled to the newest week. VoiceOver reads the whole grid as one summary,
/// and with Reduce Motion on the cells appear without animating.
struct ContributionHeatmap: View {
    let activity: [Date: Int]
    var endDate: Date = .now
    var weeks: Int = 26
    var calendar: Calendar = .current
    var tint: Color = .green
    var cellSize: CGFloat = 18
    var spacing: CGFloat = 4

    @State private var isRevealed = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let levels = 4

    var body: some View {
        let days = ContributionHeatmapLogic.days(endingAt: endDate, weeks: weeks, calendar: calendar)
        let counts = ContributionHeatmapLogic.counts(for: days, activity: activity, calendar: calendar)
        let highest = counts.max() ?? 0
        let size = max(cellSize, 1)
        let gap = max(spacing, 0)

        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
            ScrollView(.horizontal) {
                LazyHGrid(rows: Array(repeating: GridItem(.fixed(size), spacing: gap), count: ContributionHeatmapLogic.daysPerWeek), spacing: gap) {
                    ForEach(Array(counts.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { index, count in
                        cell(
                            level: ContributionHeatmapLogic.level(count: count, highest: highest, levels: levels),
                            delay: Double((counts.count - 1 - index) / ContributionHeatmapLogic.daysPerWeek) * 0.03
                        )
                    }
                }
            }
            .defaultScrollAnchor(.trailing)
            .scrollIndicators(.hidden)

            legend
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel("Activity over the last \(max(weeks, 1)) weeks")
        .accessibilityValue(summary(counts))
        .task(id: activity) {
            guard !reduceMotion else {
                isRevealed = true
                return
            }
            var reset = Transaction()
            reset.disablesAnimations = true
            withTransaction(reset) { isRevealed = false }
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(50))
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            isRevealed = true
        }
    }

    private func cell(level: Int, delay: Double) -> some View {
        let isShown = isRevealed || reduceMotion

        return RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 4)
            .fill(color(for: level))
            .scaleEffect(isShown ? 1 : 0.3)
            .opacity(isShown ? 1 : 0)
            .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.3).delay(delay), value: isRevealed)
    }

    private var legend: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 4) {
            Text("Less")
            ForEach(0...levels, id: \.self) { level in
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 3)
                    .fill(color(for: level))
                    .frame(width: 12, height: 12)
            }
            Text("More")
        }
        .font(.caption)
        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .trailing)
    }

    private func color(for level: Int) -> Color {
        guard level > 0 else { return Color.secondary.opacity(0.15) }
        return tint.opacity(0.25 + 0.75 * Double(level) / Double(levels))
    }

    private func summary(_ counts: [Int]) -> String {
        let activeDays = counts.count { $0 > 0 }
        return "\(ContributionHeatmapLogic.sum(counts)) contributions on \(activeDays) days"
    }
}

/// The grid math, apart from the view so it can be tested.
enum ContributionHeatmapLogic {
    static let daysPerWeek = 7

    /// Every day shown, oldest first. The first day starts a week, so columns line up.
    static func days(endingAt end: Date, weeks: Int, calendar: Calendar) -> [Date] {
        let weeks = min(max(weeks, 1), 530)
        let last = calendar.startOfDay(for: end)
        let daysIntoWeek = (calendar.component(.weekday, from: last) - calendar.firstWeekday + daysPerWeek) % daysPerWeek
        let count = (weeks - 1) * daysPerWeek + daysIntoWeek + 1
        return (0..<count).compactMap { calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: $0 - count + 1, to: last) }
    }

    /// The count of each day. Dates are matched by day, and repeated days keep the highest.
    static func counts(for days: [Date], activity: [Date: Int], calendar: Calendar) -> [Int] {
        var byDay: [Date: Int] = [:]
        for (date, count) in activity {
            let day = calendar.startOfDay(for: date)
            byDay[day] = max(byDay[day] ?? 0, count)
        }
        return days.map { byDay[calendar.startOfDay(for: $0)] ?? 0 }
    }

    /// The color step of a count: 0 for nothing, then 1 up to `levels`.
    static func level(count: Int, highest: Int, levels: Int) -> Int {
        guard count > 0, highest > 0, levels > 0 else { return 0 }
        let ratio = Double(count) / Double(highest)
        return min(max(Int((ratio * Double(levels)).rounded(.up)), 1), levels)
    }

    /// Adds positive counts and stops at `Int.max` instead of overflowing.
    static func sum(_ counts: [Int]) -> Int {
        counts.reduce(0) { total, count in
            let (result, overflow) = total.addingReportingOverflow(max(count, 0))
            return overflow ? Int.max : result
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ContributionHeatmapDemo: View {
    @State private var seed = 1.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var activity: [Date: Int] {
        let today = Calendar.current.startOfDay(for: .now)
        var result: [Date: Int] = [:]
        for offset in 0..<210 {
            guard let day = Calendar.current.date(byAdding: .day, value: -offset, to: today) else { continue }
            let wave = sin(Double(offset) * 0.9 * seed) + cos(Double(offset) * 0.23 + seed)
            result[day] = max(0, Int(wave * 5))
        }
        return result
    }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 24) {
            Spacer()
            Text("Commits")
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            Text("Your last 30 weeks of work")
                .font(.title3)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)

            ContributionHeatmap(activity: activity, weeks: 30)
            Spacer()
        }
        .padding(24)
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2.4))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                seed = seed > 1.3 ? 1 : seed + 0.17
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ContributionHeatmapDemo()
}
```

## Gauge Chart

A half-moon gauge with colored zones and a needle that swings to the value.

Category: Charts. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Charts/GaugeChart/GaugeChart.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated struct GaugeChartZone: Identifiable, Sendable {
    var name: String
    /// Where the zone ends. It starts where the one before it ends, or at the start of the range.
    var upTo: Double
    var color: Color

    var id: String { name }
}

nonisolated enum GaugeChartMath {
    /// How far along the dial a value is, from 0 at its start to 1 at its end.
    static func share(of value: Double, in range: ClosedRange<Double>) -> Double {
        let length = range.upperBound - range.lowerBound
        guard length > 0, value.isFinite else { return 0 }
        return min(max((value - range.lowerBound) / length, 0), 1)
    }

    /// The turn of the needle in degrees: -90 at the start of the dial, 0 straight up, 90 at its end.
    static func needleAngle(share: Double) -> Double {
        -90 + 180 * min(max(share, 0), 1)
    }

    /// The zone a value falls in: the first one that ends at or after it, or the last one for a
    /// value beyond them all.
    static func zone(for value: Double, in zones: [GaugeChartZone]) -> GaugeChartZone? {
        let sorted = zones.sorted { $0.upTo < $1.upTo }
        return sorted.first { value <= $0.upTo } ?? sorted.last
    }

    /// Where each zone starts and ends along the dial, as shares from 0 to 1.
    static func spans(of zones: [GaugeChartZone], in range: ClosedRange<Double>) -> [(zone: GaugeChartZone, start: Double, end: Double)] {
        var start = 0.0
        return zones.sorted { $0.upTo < $1.upTo }.compactMap { zone in
            let end = share(of: zone.upTo, in: range)
            defer { start = max(start, end) }
            return end > start ? (zone, start, end) : nil
        }
    }
}

/// A half-moon gauge for a panel: a dial split into colored zones and a needle that swings to
/// the value. For a small control inside a row, SwiftUI's own `Gauge` is the one to use.
///
/// VoiceOver reads the value and the name of its zone, so the reading does not depend on the
/// color. With Reduce Motion on, the needle goes to its place without swinging.
struct GaugeChart: View {
    var value: Double
    var range: ClosedRange<Double> = 0...100
    let zones: [GaugeChartZone]
    var label = "Gauge"
    var valueText: (Double) -> String = { $0.formatted(.number.precision(.fractionLength(0))) }

    private let lineWidth: CGFloat = 26
    private let gap = 0.004

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        let share = GaugeChartMath.share(of: value, in: range)
        let zone = GaugeChartMath.zone(for: value, in: zones)

        GeometryReader { proxy in
            let width = proxy.size.width

            ZStack(alignment: .bottom) {
                ZStack {
                    ForEach(GaugeChartMath.spans(of: zones, in: range), id: \.zone.id) { span in
                        // A circle starts at three o'clock. Half a turn makes it start at nine, where the dial does.
                        Circle()
                            .inset(by: lineWidth / 2)
                            .trim(from: span.start / 2 + gap, to: span.end / 2 - gap)
                            .stroke(span.zone.color, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .butt))
                            .rotationEffect(.degrees(180))
                    }
                }
                .frame(width: width, height: width)
                .frame(height: width / 2, alignment: .top)
                .clipped()

                Capsule()
                    .fill(.primary)
                    .frame(width: 5, height: width / 2 - lineWidth - 10)
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(GaugeChartMath.needleAngle(share: share)), anchor: .bottom)
                    .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.9, bounce: 0.35), value: share)

                Circle()
                    .fill(.primary)
                    .frame(width: 18, height: 18)
                    .offset(y: 9)
            }
        }
        .aspectRatio(2, contentMode: .fit)
        // A dial reads from left to right in every language, like a speedometer.
        .environment(\.layoutDirection, .leftToRight)
        .padding(.bottom, 9)
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel(label)
        .accessibilityValue([valueText(value), zone?.name].compactMap { $0 }.joined(separator: ", "))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct GaugeChartDemo: View {
    private let zones = [
        GaugeChartZone(name: "Good", upTo: 50, color: .green),
        GaugeChartZone(name: "Moderate", upTo: 100, color: .yellow),
        GaugeChartZone(name: "Unhealthy", upTo: 150, color: .orange),
        GaugeChartZone(name: "Hazardous", upTo: 200, color: .red),
    ]
    private let readings: [(place: String, value: Double)] = [("Harbor", 32), ("Old Town", 118), ("Ring Road", 171), ("Hillside", 74)]

    @State private var index = 0

    var body: some View {
        let reading = readings[index]
        let zone = GaugeChartMath.zone(for: reading.value, in: zones)

        VStack(spacing: 18) {
            VStack(spacing: 4) {
                Text("Air Quality")
                    .font(.title2.bold())
                Text(reading.place)
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .contentTransition(.opacity)
            }

            GaugeChart(value: reading.value, range: 0...200, zones: zones, label: "Air quality index")
                .padding(.horizontal, 12)

            VStack(spacing: 2) {
                Text(reading.value, format: .number)
                    .font(.system(size: 52, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
                    .contentTransition(.numericText())
                Text(zone?.name ?? "")
                    .font(.headline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
            .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Button("Next Station", systemImage: "arrow.right") {
                withAnimation(.snappy) { index = (index + 1) % readings.count }
            }
            .buttonStyle(.bordered)
        }
        .padding(24)
        .background(.background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 24))
        .padding(16)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground))
    }
}

#Preview {
    GaugeChartDemo()
}
```

## Interactive Line Chart

A line chart that shows a rule and a value tooltip under the finger as it scrubs along the time axis.

Category: Charts. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Charts/InteractiveLineChart/InteractiveLineChart.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import Charts
import SwiftUI

struct InteractiveLineChartPoint: Identifiable, Hashable {
    let date: Date
    let value: Double

    var id: Date { date }
}

/// A line chart that shows a rule and a value tooltip under the finger as it scrubs.
///
/// The tooltip only exists during the touch, and nothing animates on its own.
struct InteractiveLineChart: View {
    let points: [InteractiveLineChartPoint]
    var tint: Color = .indigo
    var format: (Double) -> String = { $0.formatted() }

    @State private var touchedDate: Date?
    @State private var tooltipWidth: CGFloat = 0
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) private var tooltipHeadroom = 60.0

    private var selected: InteractiveLineChartPoint? {
        touchedDate.flatMap { InteractiveLineChartLogic.nearest(to: $0, in: points) }
    }

    var body: some View {
        let domain = InteractiveLineChartLogic.domain(for: points)

        Chart {
            ForEach(points) { point in
                AreaMark(
                    x: .value("Date", point.date),
                    yStart: .value("Baseline", domain.lowerBound),
                    yEnd: .value("Value", point.value)
                )
                .foregroundStyle(.linearGradient(colors: [tint.opacity(0.3), tint.opacity(0)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
                .interpolationMethod(.monotone)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

                LineMark(x: .value("Date", point.date), y: .value("Value", point.value))
                    .foregroundStyle(tint)
                    .lineStyle(StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 3, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
                    .interpolationMethod(.monotone)
                    .accessibilityLabel(point.date.formatted(date: .abbreviated, time: .omitted))
                    .accessibilityValue(format(point.value))
            }

            if let selected {
                RuleMark(x: .value("Selected", selected.date))
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .lineStyle(StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 1, dash: [4, 4]))
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                PointMark(x: .value("Selected", selected.date), y: .value("Value", selected.value))
                    .symbolSize(140)
                    .foregroundStyle(tint)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
        }
        .chartYScale(domain: domain, range: .plotDimension(endPadding: tooltipHeadroom))
        // Keeps the last date inside the plot. Before iOS 26 it is drawn half cut at the trailing edge.
        .chartXAxis { AxisMarks(preset: .aligned) }
        .chartXSelection(value: $touchedDate)
        // Drawn over the chart and not as an annotation of the rule: on iOS 27 that
        // annotation is not drawn at all.
        .chartOverlay { proxy in
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                if let selected, let plotFrame = proxy.plotFrame, let x = proxy.position(forX: selected.date) {
                    let plot = geometry[plotFrame]
                    tooltip(for: selected)
                        .environment(\.layoutDirection, layoutDirection)
                        .fixedSize()
                        .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.width } action: { tooltipWidth = $0 }
                        .position(
                            x: InteractiveLineChartLogic.tooltipX(at: plot.minX + x, width: tooltipWidth, in: plot.minX...plot.maxX),
                            y: plot.minY + tooltipHeadroom / 2
                        )
                        .allowsHitTesting(false)
                }
            }
            // The chart reports screen points, and a position is mirrored in a right-to-left
            // layout. Left to right here keeps the tooltip over the rule.
            .environment(\.layoutDirection, .leftToRight)
        }
        .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: selected?.id)
    }

    private func tooltip(for point: InteractiveLineChartPoint) -> some View {
        VStack(spacing: 2) {
            Text(format(point.value))
                .font(.headline)
            Text(point.date, format: .dateTime.day().month())
                .font(.caption)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
        .padding(.horizontal, 12)
        .padding(.vertical, 6)
        // A material does not draw inside a chart annotation: it comes out black, or not at all.
        .background(Color(.secondarySystemBackground), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 12))
        .overlay { RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12).strokeBorder(.separator) }
    }
}

enum InteractiveLineChartLogic {
    static func nearest(to date: Date, in points: [InteractiveLineChartPoint]) -> InteractiveLineChartPoint? {
        points.min { abs($0.date.timeIntervalSince(date)) < abs($1.date.timeIntervalSince(date)) }
    }

    /// The center of the tooltip: over the point, but never past either end of the plot.
    static func tooltipX(at x: CGFloat, width: CGFloat, in plot: ClosedRange<CGFloat>) -> CGFloat {
        let half = max(width, 0) / 2
        guard plot.upperBound - plot.lowerBound > half * 2 else { return (plot.lowerBound + plot.upperBound) / 2 }
        return min(max(x, plot.lowerBound + half), plot.upperBound - half)
    }

    /// The vertical range with some breathing room. A flat or empty series still gets a valid range.
    static func domain(for points: [InteractiveLineChartPoint]) -> ClosedRange<Double> {
        let values = points.map(\.value).filter(\.isFinite)
        guard let low = values.min(), let high = values.max() else { return 0...1 }
        guard high - low > 0, (high - low).isFinite else { return (low - 1)...(high + 1) }
        let padding = (high - low) * 0.15
        return (low - padding)...(high + padding)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct InteractiveLineChartDemo: View {
    @State private var points: [InteractiveLineChartPoint] = {
        let start = Calendar.current.startOfDay(for: .now)
        return (0..<36).compactMap { day in
            guard let date = Calendar.current.date(byAdding: .day, value: day - 35, to: start) else { return nil }
            let value = 1_200 + Double(day) * 14 + sin(Double(day) * 0.55) * 120 + cos(Double(day) * 1.7) * 40
            return InteractiveLineChartPoint(date: date, value: value.rounded())
        }
    }()

    private func euros(_ value: Double) -> String {
        value.formatted(.currency(code: "EUR").precision(.fractionLength(0)))
    }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
            Text("Savings")
                .font(.title3)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            Text(euros(points.last?.value ?? 0))
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            Text("Drag along the chart")
                .font(.subheadline)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)

            InteractiveLineChart(points: points, format: euros)
                .padding(.vertical, 12)
        }
        .padding(24)
    }
}

#Preview {
    InteractiveLineChartDemo()
}
```

## Line Chart Draw In

A line chart whose line draws in from left to right while a dot follows its tip.

Category: Charts. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Charts/LineChartDrawIn/LineChartDrawIn.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A line chart whose line draws in from left to right while a dot follows its tip.
///
/// It draws again whenever the values change. With Reduce Motion on, the finished chart appears.
struct LineChartDrawIn: View {
    let values: [Double]
    var tint: Color = .indigo
    var duration: Double = 1.6

    @State private var progress = 0.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let inset = 12.0
    private var shownProgress: Double { reduceMotion ? 1 : progress }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LineChartDrawInArea(values: values, inset: inset)
                .fill(.linearGradient(colors: [tint.opacity(0.28), tint.opacity(0)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
                .opacity(shownProgress)

            LineChartDrawInLine(values: values, inset: inset)
                .trim(from: 0, to: shownProgress)
                .stroke(tint, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 3.5, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))

            LineChartDrawInDot(values: values, inset: inset, radius: 12, progress: shownProgress)
                .fill(tint.opacity(0.25))

            LineChartDrawInDot(values: values, inset: inset, radius: 6, progress: shownProgress)
                .fill(tint)
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel("Line chart")
        .accessibilityValue(LineChartDrawInLogic.summary(of: values))
        .task(id: values) {
            guard !reduceMotion else {
                progress = 1
                return
            }
            var reset = Transaction()
            reset.disablesAnimations = true
            withTransaction(reset) { progress = 0 }
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(50))
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: max(duration, 0))) { progress = 1 }
        }
    }
}

nonisolated private struct LineChartDrawInLine: Shape {
    let values: [Double]
    let inset: CGFloat

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        var path = Path()
        path.addLines(LineChartDrawInLogic.points(for: values, in: rect.insetBy(dx: inset, dy: inset)))
        return path
    }
}

nonisolated private struct LineChartDrawInArea: Shape {
    let values: [Double]
    let inset: CGFloat

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let points = LineChartDrawInLogic.points(for: values, in: rect.insetBy(dx: inset, dy: inset))
        guard let first = points.first, let last = points.last else { return Path() }

        var path = Path()
        path.addLines(points)
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: last.x, y: rect.maxY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: first.x, y: rect.maxY))
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

/// A circle that re-computes its position for every animation frame, so it stays on the tip.
nonisolated private struct LineChartDrawInDot: Shape {
    let values: [Double]
    let inset: CGFloat
    let radius: CGFloat
    var progress: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let points = LineChartDrawInLogic.points(for: values, in: rect.insetBy(dx: inset, dy: inset))
        guard let center = LineChartDrawInLogic.point(at: progress, along: points) else { return Path() }
        return Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: center.x - radius, y: center.y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2))
    }
}

/// The geometry of the chart, apart from the view so it can be tested.
nonisolated enum LineChartDrawInLogic {
    static func points(for values: [Double], in rect: CGRect) -> [CGPoint] {
        let values = values.filter(\.isFinite)
        guard !rect.isNull, rect.width > 0, rect.height > 0,
              let low = values.min(), let high = values.max() else { return [] }

        let span = high - low
        let step = values.count > 1 ? rect.width / CGFloat(values.count - 1) : 0
        return values.enumerated().map { index, value in
            let ratio = span > 0 && span.isFinite ? (value - low) / span : 0.5
            return CGPoint(x: rect.minX + CGFloat(index) * step, y: rect.maxY - CGFloat(ratio) * rect.height)
        }
    }

    /// The point at a fraction of the line's length, which is how `trim` measures it too.
    static func point(at progress: Double, along points: [CGPoint]) -> CGPoint? {
        guard let first = points.first else { return nil }
        let lengths = zip(points, points.dropFirst()).map { hypot($1.x - $0.x, $1.y - $0.y) }
        let total = lengths.reduce(0, +)
        guard total > 0 else { return first }

        var remaining = total * CGFloat(min(max(progress, 0), 1))
        for (index, length) in lengths.enumerated() where length > 0 {
            if remaining <= length {
                let fraction = remaining / length
                let start = points[index]
                let end = points[index + 1]
                return CGPoint(x: start.x + (end.x - start.x) * fraction, y: start.y + (end.y - start.y) * fraction)
            }
            remaining -= length
        }
        return points.last
    }

    static func summary(of values: [Double]) -> String {
        let values = values.filter(\.isFinite)
        guard let first = values.first, let last = values.last,
              let low = values.min(), let high = values.max() else { return "No data" }
        return "From \(first.formatted()) to \(last.formatted()). Lowest \(low.formatted()), highest \(high.formatted())."
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct LineChartDrawInDemo: View {
    @State private var isAlternate = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var values: [Double] {
        isAlternate
            ? [62, 58, 70, 64, 80, 76, 66, 72, 88, 84, 96, 90]
            : [20, 34, 28, 46, 40, 58, 52, 74, 66, 82, 78, 96]
    }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
            Text("Active users")
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            Text(isAlternate ? "Europe" : "Americas")
                .font(.title3)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)

            LineChartDrawIn(values: values)
                .padding(.vertical, 24)
        }
        .padding(24)
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2.8))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                isAlternate.toggle()
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    LineChartDrawInDemo()
}
```

## Radar Chart

A radar chart with an axis per quality around a center and a shape per series that grows out when it appears.

Category: Charts. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Charts/RadarChart/RadarChart.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated struct RadarChartSeries: Identifiable, Sendable {
    var name: String
    /// One value per axis, in the order of the axes.
    var values: [Double]
    var color: Color

    var id: String { name }
}

nonisolated enum RadarChartMath {
    /// The direction of an axis in radians, with the first one pointing up and the rest going clockwise.
    static func angle(of axis: Int, count: Int) -> Double {
        guard count > 0 else { return -.pi / 2 }
        return Double(axis) / Double(count) * 2 * .pi - .pi / 2
    }

    /// How far along its axis a value is, from 0 at the center to 1 at the edge.
    static func share(of value: Double, maximum: Double) -> Double {
        guard maximum > 0, value.isFinite else { return 0 }
        return min(max(value / maximum, 0), 1)
    }

    /// The point `share` of the way along an axis, in a circle of `radius` around `center`.
    static func point(axis: Int, count: Int, share: Double, center: CGPoint, radius: Double) -> CGPoint {
        let angle = angle(of: axis, count: count)
        return CGPoint(x: center.x + cos(angle) * radius * share, y: center.y + sin(angle) * radius * share)
    }

    /// The corners of the shape of a series: one per axis. A series with fewer values than axes
    /// is at the center on the rest.
    static func corners(values: [Double], axes: Int, maximum: Double, center: CGPoint, radius: Double) -> [CGPoint] {
        (0..<max(axes, 0)).map { axis in
            let value = axis < values.count ? values[axis] : 0
            return point(axis: axis, count: axes, share: share(of: value, maximum: maximum), center: center, radius: radius)
        }
    }
}

/// A radar chart: one axis per quality, spread around a center, and a shape per series that
/// reaches further along an axis the higher its value. It compares two or three profiles at a glance.
///
/// The shapes grow from the center when they appear. VoiceOver reads each axis with the value
/// of every series. With Reduce Motion on, the shapes are there from the start.
struct RadarChart: View {
    let axes: [String]
    let series: [RadarChartSeries]
    var maximum = 100.0
    /// How many rings the grid has, the outer one included.
    var rings = 4

    private let labelRoom: CGFloat = 34

    @State private var growth = 0.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            let center = CGPoint(x: proxy.size.width / 2, y: proxy.size.height / 2)
            let radius = max(min(proxy.size.width, proxy.size.height) / 2 - labelRoom, 0)

            ZStack {
                RadarChartGrid(axes: axes.count, rings: rings)
                    .stroke(.quaternary, lineWidth: 1)
                    .padding(labelRoom)

                ForEach(series) { series in
                    let shape = RadarChartShape(values: series.values, axes: axes.count, maximum: maximum, growth: reduceMotion ? 1 : growth)

                    shape
                        .fill(series.color.opacity(0.22))
                        .padding(labelRoom)
                    shape
                        .stroke(series.color, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 2, lineJoin: .round))
                        .padding(labelRoom)
                }

                ForEach(Array(axes.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { index, axis in
                    Text(axis)
                        .font(.caption.weight(.medium))
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                        .lineLimit(1)
                        .minimumScaleFactor(0.7)
                        .position(RadarChartMath.point(axis: index, count: axes.count, share: 1, center: center, radius: radius + labelRoom * 0.55))
                }
            }
        }
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        // The axes go clockwise from the top in every language, like the hours of a clock.
        .environment(\.layoutDirection, .leftToRight)
        .onAppear {
            withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.9, bounce: 0.25)) { growth = 1 }
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel("Radar chart")
        .accessibilityChildren {
            ForEach(Array(axes.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { index, axis in
                Text(axis)
                    .accessibilityValue(description(ofAxis: index))
            }
        }
    }

    private func description(ofAxis axis: Int) -> String {
        series
            .map { "\($0.name) \((axis < $0.values.count ? $0.values[axis] : 0).formatted())" }
            .joined(separator: ", ")
    }
}

/// The grid behind the shapes: a polygon per ring and a spoke per axis.
nonisolated struct RadarChartGrid: Shape {
    var axes: Int
    var rings: Int

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let center = CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
        let radius = min(rect.width, rect.height) / 2
        var path = Path()
        guard axes > 2 else { return path }

        for ring in 1...max(rings, 1) {
            let share = Double(ring) / Double(max(rings, 1))
            path.addLines((0..<axes).map { RadarChartMath.point(axis: $0, count: axes, share: share, center: center, radius: radius) })
            path.closeSubpath()
        }
        for axis in 0..<axes {
            path.move(to: center)
            path.addLine(to: RadarChartMath.point(axis: axis, count: axes, share: 1, center: center, radius: radius))
        }
        return path
    }
}

/// The shape of one series. `growth` animates it out from the center.
nonisolated struct RadarChartShape: Shape {
    var values: [Double]
    var axes: Int
    var maximum: Double
    var growth: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { growth }
        set { growth = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        var path = Path()
        guard axes > 2 else { return path }
        let center = CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
        path.addLines(RadarChartMath.corners(values: values, axes: axes, maximum: maximum, center: center, radius: min(rect.width, rect.height) / 2 * growth))
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct RadarChartDemo: View {
    private let axes = ["Speed", "Power", "Range", "Comfort", "Price", "Design"]
    private let bikes = [
        RadarChartSeries(name: "City", values: [55, 40, 62, 90, 85, 70], color: .teal),
        RadarChartSeries(name: "Trail", values: [80, 92, 78, 50, 45, 82], color: .orange),
    ]

    @State private var run = 0

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 20) {
            VStack(spacing: 4) {
                Text("Which e-bike?")
                    .font(.title2.bold())
                Text("Two models, six things that matter")
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }

            RadarChart(axes: axes, series: bikes)
                .id(run)

            HStack(spacing: 20) {
                ForEach(bikes) { bike in
                    Label {
                        Text(bike.name)
                    } icon: {
                        Circle()
                            .fill(bike.color)
                            .frame(width: 10, height: 10)
                    }
                    .font(.subheadline.weight(.medium))
                }
            }
            .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Button("Replay", systemImage: "arrow.clockwise") {
                run += 1
            }
            .buttonStyle(.bordered)
        }
        .padding(20)
        .background(.background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 24))
        .padding(16)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground))
    }
}

#Preview {
    RadarChartDemo()
}
```

## Scrollable Bar Chart

A bar chart that scrolls sideways a week at a time and marks the average of the days in sight.

Category: Charts. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Charts/ScrollableBarChart/ScrollableBarChart.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import Charts
import SwiftUI

nonisolated struct ScrollableBarChartEntry: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable {
    var date: Date
    var value: Double

    var id: Date { date }
}

nonisolated enum ScrollableBarChartMath {
    static let secondsPerDay = 86_400.0

    /// The entries of the days in sight: those from `start` up to `days` later.
    static func visible(_ entries: [ScrollableBarChartEntry], from start: Date, days: Int) -> [ScrollableBarChartEntry] {
        let end = start.addingTimeInterval(Double(max(days, 0)) * secondsPerDay)
        return entries.filter { $0.date >= start && $0.date < end }
    }

    /// The mean of the values, or `nil` when there are none.
    static func average(of entries: [ScrollableBarChartEntry]) -> Double? {
        entries.isEmpty ? nil : entries.map(\.value).reduce(0, +) / Double(entries.count)
    }

    /// Where the chart starts so that its last `days` are the ones in sight.
    static func lastStart(of entries: [ScrollableBarChartEntry], days: Int) -> Date? {
        guard let last = entries.map(\.date).max() else { return nil }
        return last.addingTimeInterval(-Double(max(days, 1) - 1) * secondsPerDay)
    }

    /// The top of the value axis: the highest value of all, with some room, so the bars keep
    /// their scale while the chart scrolls.
    static func ceiling(of entries: [ScrollableBarChartEntry]) -> Double {
        max((entries.map(\.value).max() ?? 0) * 1.12, 1)
    }
}

/// A bar chart with more days than fit, which scrolls sideways and settles on whole days, a
/// week at a time. A line marks the average of the days in sight and `visible` reports them.
///
/// It starts on the latest days. Swift Charts gives VoiceOver every bar and an audio graph.
struct ScrollableBarChart: View {
    let entries: [ScrollableBarChartEntry]
    /// The entries of the days in sight, kept up to date as the chart scrolls.
    @Binding var visible: [ScrollableBarChartEntry]
    var visibleDays = 7

    @State private var position = Date.now

    var body: some View {
        let average = ScrollableBarChartMath.average(of: visible)

        Chart {
            ForEach(entries) { entry in
                BarMark(
                    x: .value("Day", entry.date, unit: .day),
                    y: .value("Value", entry.value)
                )
                .foregroundStyle(.tint)
                .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 5))
            }

            if let average {
                RuleMark(y: .value("Average", average))
                    .lineStyle(StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 1.5, dash: [4, 4]))
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .accessibilityLabel("Average of the days in sight")
            }
        }
        .chartYScale(domain: 0...ScrollableBarChartMath.ceiling(of: entries))
        .chartScrollableAxes(.horizontal)
        .chartXVisibleDomain(length: Double(visibleDays) * ScrollableBarChartMath.secondsPerDay)
        .chartScrollPosition(x: $position)
        .chartScrollTargetBehavior(.valueAligned(matching: DateComponents(hour: 0), majorAlignment: .matching(DateComponents(weekday: Calendar.current.firstWeekday))))
        .chartXAxis {
            AxisMarks(values: .stride(by: .day)) { _ in
                AxisValueLabel(format: .dateTime.weekday(.narrow), centered: true)
            }
        }
        .onAppear {
            if let start = ScrollableBarChartMath.lastStart(of: entries, days: visibleDays) { position = start }
        }
        .onChange(of: position, initial: true) { _, start in
            let shown = ScrollableBarChartMath.visible(entries, from: start, days: visibleDays)
            if shown != visible { visible = shown }
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ScrollableBarChartDemo: View {
    @State private var visible: [ScrollableBarChartEntry] = []

    /// Eight weeks of made-up step counts, the same on every run.
    private let entries: [ScrollableBarChartEntry] = {
        var seed: UInt64 = 7
        let start = Calendar.current.startOfDay(for: Date(timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate: 815_000_000))
        return (0..<56).map { day in
            seed = seed &* 6_364_136_223_846_793_005 &+ 1_442_695_040_888_963_407
            let noise = Double(seed >> 33) / Double(1 << 31)
            let weekend = day % 7 >= 5 ? 0.7 : 1
            return ScrollableBarChartEntry(date: start.addingTimeInterval(Double(day) * 86_400), value: (4_500 + noise * 7_500) * weekend)
        }
    }()

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                Text("Steps")
                    .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: 6) {
                    Text(ScrollableBarChartMath.average(of: visible) ?? 0, format: .number.precision(.fractionLength(0)))
                        .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                        .monospacedDigit()
                        .contentTransition(.numericText())
                    Text("a day")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
                Text(range)
                    .font(.footnote)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
            .animation(.snappy, value: visible)
            .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)

            ScrollableBarChart(entries: entries, visible: $visible)
                .frame(height: 260)
        }
        .padding(20)
        .background(.background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 24))
        .padding(16)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground))
        .tint(.orange)
    }

    private var range: String {
        guard let first = visible.first?.date, let last = visible.last?.date else { return " " }
        return (first..<last).formatted(.interval.month(.abbreviated).day())
    }
}
```

## Sparkline Stat Tile

A stat tile with a small trend line behind its value.

Category: Charts. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Charts/SparklineStatTile/SparklineStatTile.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import Charts
import SwiftUI

/// A stat tile with a small trend line behind its value.
///
/// VoiceOver reads the title, the value and the change as one element. With Reduce Motion
/// on, new values appear without animating the line.
struct SparklineStatTile: View {
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let value: String
    let trend: [Double]
    var systemImage: String = "chart.line.uptrend.xyaxis"
    var tint: Color = .indigo

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var minimumHeight = 150.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var change: Double? { SparklineStatTileLogic.change(in: trend) }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
            Label(title, systemImage: systemImage)
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.medium))
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)

            Text(value)
                .font(.title.bold())
                .minimumScaleFactor(0.7)
                .contentTransition(reduceMotion ? .identity : .numericText())
                .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth, value: value)

            if let change {
                changeLabel(change)
            }

            Spacer(minLength: 0)
        }
        .padding(16)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: minimumHeight, alignment: .topLeading)
        .background(alignment: .bottom) { sparkline }
        .background(.thinMaterial)
        .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 22))
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(title)
        .accessibilityValue(accessibilityValue)
    }

    private func changeLabel(_ change: Double) -> some View {
        Label(percent(change), systemImage: change >= 0 ? "arrow.up.right" : "arrow.down.right")
            .font(.caption.weight(.semibold))
            .foregroundStyle(change >= 0 ? .green : .red)
    }

    @ViewBuilder
    private var sparkline: some View {
        let values = trend.filter(\.isFinite)
        if values.count > 1 {
            let domain = SparklineStatTileLogic.domain(for: values)

            Chart(Array(values.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { index, value in
                AreaMark(x: .value("Index", index), yStart: .value("Low", domain.lowerBound), yEnd: .value("Value", value))
                    .foregroundStyle(.linearGradient(colors: [tint.opacity(0.3), tint.opacity(0)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
                    .interpolationMethod(.catmullRom)

                LineMark(x: .value("Index", index), y: .value("Value", value))
                    .foregroundStyle(tint)
                    .lineStyle(StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 2.5, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
                    .interpolationMethod(.catmullRom)
            }
            .chartXAxis(.hidden)
            .chartYAxis(.hidden)
            .chartLegend(.hidden)
            .chartXScale(domain: 0...(values.count - 1))
            .chartYScale(domain: domain)
            .frame(height: minimumHeight * 0.55)
            .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth, value: values)
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
    }

    private var accessibilityValue: String {
        guard let change else { return value }
        return "\(value), \(change >= 0 ? "up" : "down") \(abs(change).formatted(.percent.precision(.fractionLength(1))))"
    }

    private func percent(_ change: Double) -> String {
        change.formatted(.percent.precision(.fractionLength(1)).sign(strategy: .always()))
    }
}

enum SparklineStatTileLogic {
    /// The change from the first value to the last, or `nil` when it cannot be computed.
    static func change(in values: [Double]) -> Double? {
        let values = values.filter(\.isFinite)
        guard values.count > 1, let first = values.first, let last = values.last, first != 0 else { return nil }
        let change = (last - first) / abs(first)
        return change.isFinite ? change : nil
    }

    /// A valid vertical range, also for a flat series, with room so the line is not cut off.
    static func domain(for values: [Double]) -> ClosedRange<Double> {
        guard let low = values.min(), let high = values.max() else { return 0...1 }
        guard high - low > 0, (high - low).isFinite else { return (low - 1)...(high + 1) }
        return (low - (high - low) * 0.1)...(high + (high - low) * 0.5)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SparklineStatTileDemo: View {
    @State private var tick = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.dynamicTypeSize) private var dynamicTypeSize

    private func series(base: Double, swing: Double, slope: Double, phase: Double) -> [Double] {
        (0..<14).map { index in
            let position = Double(index + tick)
            return (base + position * slope + sin(position * 0.8 + phase) * swing).rounded()
        }
    }

    private var columns: [GridItem] {
        Array(repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: 14), count: dynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize ? 1 : 2)
    }

    private func tile(_ title: LocalizedStringResource, _ systemImage: String, _ tint: Color, _ trend: [Double], suffix: String = "") -> some View {
        SparklineStatTile(
            title: title,
            value: (trend.last ?? 0).formatted() + suffix,
            trend: trend,
            systemImage: systemImage,
            tint: tint
        )
    }

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 20) {
                Text("Overview")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())

                LazyVGrid(columns: columns, spacing: 14) {
                    tile("Revenue", "eurosign.circle", .indigo, series(base: 4_200, swing: 320, slope: 60, phase: 0))
                    tile("Signups", "person.badge.plus", .teal, series(base: 310, swing: 40, slope: 8, phase: 1.4))
                    tile("Churn", "arrow.uturn.left.circle", .pink, series(base: 60, swing: 7, slope: -1.5, phase: 2.2), suffix: " users")
                    tile("Sessions", "waveform.path.ecg", .orange, series(base: 1_900, swing: 240, slope: 18, phase: 3.1))
                    tile("Orders", "shippingbox", .green, series(base: 840, swing: 90, slope: 12, phase: 4.3))
                    tile("Tickets", "lifepreserver", .purple, series(base: 120, swing: 22, slope: -2, phase: 5))
                }
            }
            .padding(20)
        }
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo.opacity(0.18), .teal.opacity(0.12)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                tick = (tick + 1) % 1_000
            }
        }
    }
}

    SparklineStatTileDemo()
}
```

## Surface 3D Chart

A 3D surface plot that rotates when dragged, with buttons for preset viewing angles.

Category: Charts. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Charts/Surface3DChart/Surface3DChart.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import Charts
import Spatial
import SwiftUI

@available(iOS 26, *)
enum Surface3DChartPreset: String, CaseIterable, Identifiable {
    case angled = "Angled"
    case front = "Front"
    case top = "Top"
    case side = "Side"

    var id: Self { self }

    var pose: Chart3DPose {
        switch self {
        case .angled: Chart3DPose(azimuth: .degrees(35), inclination: .degrees(25))
        case .front: .front
        case .top: .top
        case .side: .right
        }
    }
}

/// A 3D surface plot that rotates when dragged, with buttons for preset viewing angles.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the presets jump to their angle.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct Surface3DChart: View {
    var domain: ClosedRange<Double> = -3...3
    var gradient = Gradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple, .pink, .orange])
    let function: @Sendable (Double, Double) -> Double

    @State private var pose = Surface3DChartPreset.angled.pose
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var safeDomain: ClosedRange<Double> {
        domain.lowerBound < domain.upperBound ? domain : -1...1
    }

    private var currentPreset: Surface3DChartPreset? {
        Surface3DChartPreset.allCases.first { $0.pose == pose }
    }

    var body: some View {
        let function = self.function

        VStack(spacing: 20) {
            Chart3D {
                SurfacePlot(x: "X", y: "Height", z: "Z") { x, z in
                    let height = function(x, z)
                    return height.isFinite ? height : 0
                }
                .foregroundStyle(.heightBased(gradient))
                .roughness(0.35)
            }
            .chartXScale(domain: safeDomain)
            .chartZScale(domain: safeDomain)
            .chart3DPose($pose)
            .accessibilityLabel("3D surface plot")
            .accessibilityValue(currentPreset.map { "\($0.rawValue) view" } ?? "Custom view")
            .accessibilityHint("Use the view buttons to change the angle")

            ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
                presetRow
                ScrollView(.horizontal) { presetRow }.scrollIndicators(.hidden)
            }
        }
    }

    private var presetRow: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 8) {
            ForEach(Surface3DChartPreset.allCases) { preset in
                Button {
                    withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.6)) { pose = preset.pose }
                } label: {
                    Text(preset.rawValue)
                        .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                        .padding(.horizontal, 16)
                        .frame(minHeight: 44)
                        .foregroundStyle(preset == currentPreset ? Color.white : Color.primary)
                        .background(preset == currentPreset ? AnyShapeStyle(.indigo) : AnyShapeStyle(.thinMaterial), in: .capsule)
                        .contentShape(.capsule)
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
                .accessibilityAddTraits(preset == currentPreset ? .isSelected : [])
            }
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct Surface3DChartDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
            Text("Ripple")
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            Text("Drag to rotate, or pick a view")
                .font(.title3)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)

            Surface3DChart { x, z in
                let radius = (x * x + z * z).squareRoot()
                return sin(radius * 2.2) * exp(-radius * 0.28)
            }
            .padding(.top, 16)
        }
        .padding(24)
    }
```
