## Polygon Morph Shape

A shape that smoothly morphs between a square, a circle and a star using a custom animatable vector.

Category: Drawing. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Drawing/PolygonMorphShape/PolygonMorphShape.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum PolygonMorphShapeForm: String, CaseIterable, Hashable {
    case square = "Square"
    case circle = "Circle"
    case star = "Star"

    /// One sample per degree, so square corners and star tips land exactly on a sample.
    static let sampleCount = 360

    /// The outline's distance from the center, from 0 to 1, in a direction measured clockwise from the top.
    func radius(atDegrees degrees: Double) -> Double {
        let radians = degrees * .pi / 180

        switch self {
        case .square:
            return 0.7071 / max(abs(cos(radians)), abs(sin(radians)))
        case .circle:
            return 0.85
        case .star:
            return Self.starRadius(atDegrees: degrees)
        }
    }

    var radii: PolygonMorphShapeRadii {
        PolygonMorphShapeRadii(
            values: (0..<Self.sampleCount).map { radius(atDegrees: Double($0) * 360 / Double(Self.sampleCount)) }
        )
    }

    /// Finds where a ray from the center crosses the straight edge from a tip to its inner corner.
    private static func starRadius(atDegrees degrees: Double) -> Double {
        let sector = 72.0
        let wrapped = degrees.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: sector)
        let positive = wrapped < 0 ? wrapped + sector : wrapped
        let folded = min(positive, sector - positive) * .pi / 180

        let outer = 1.0
        let inner = 0.46
        let halfSector = sector / 2 * .pi / 180
        let edgeX = inner * cos(halfSector) - outer
        let edgeY = inner * sin(halfSector)

        return (outer * edgeY) / (cos(folded) * edgeY - sin(folded) * edgeX)
    }
}

/// A list of radii that SwiftUI can interpolate, which is what makes the morph work between any two forms.
nonisolated struct PolygonMorphShapeRadii: VectorArithmetic {
    var values: [Double]

    static var zero: Self { Self(values: []) }

    static func + (lhs: Self, rhs: Self) -> Self { combine(lhs, rhs, +) }
    static func - (lhs: Self, rhs: Self) -> Self { combine(lhs, rhs, -) }

    mutating func scale(by rhs: Double) {
        values = values.map { $0 * rhs }
    }

    var magnitudeSquared: Double {
        values.reduce(0) { $0 + $1 * $1 }
    }

    /// `zero` is empty, so a missing value on either side counts as 0.
    private static func combine(_ lhs: Self, _ rhs: Self, _ operation: (Double, Double) -> Double) -> Self {
        let count = max(lhs.values.count, rhs.values.count)
        return Self(
            values: (0..<count).map { index in
                operation(
                    index < lhs.values.count ? lhs.values[index] : 0,
                    index < rhs.values.count ? rhs.values[index] : 0
                )
            }
        )
    }
}

/// A shape that morphs smoothly between a square, a circle and a star when its form changes.
///
/// Every form is sampled at the same angles, so morphing is only interpolating distances.
nonisolated struct PolygonMorphShape: Shape {
    var radii: PolygonMorphShapeRadii

    init(form: PolygonMorphShapeForm) {
        radii = form.radii
    }

    var animatableData: PolygonMorphShapeRadii {
        get { radii }
        set { radii = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let count = radii.values.count
        let scale = min(rect.width, rect.height) / 2
        guard count > 0, scale > 0 else { return Path() }

        var path = Path()
        for (index, radius) in radii.values.enumerated() {
            let angle = 2 * Double.pi * Double(index) / Double(count)
            let point = CGPoint(
                x: rect.midX + radius * scale * sin(angle),
                y: rect.midY - radius * scale * cos(angle)
            )
            if index == 0 {
                path.move(to: point)
            } else {
                path.addLine(to: point)
            }
        }
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct PolygonMorphShapeDemo: View {
    @State private var form = PolygonMorphShapeForm.square
    @State private var isAutoPlaying = true
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var nextForm: PolygonMorphShapeForm {
        let forms = PolygonMorphShapeForm.allCases
        let index = forms.firstIndex(of: form) ?? 0
        return forms[(index + 1) % forms.count]
    }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 36) {
            PolygonMorphShape(form: form)
                .fill(LinearGradient(colors: [.purple, .pink, .orange], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
                .shadow(color: .pink.opacity(0.4), radius: 24, y: 12)
                .frame(maxWidth: 280, maxHeight: 280)
                .accessibilityElement()
                .accessibilityLabel(form.rawValue)

            ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
                HStack(spacing: 10) { buttons }
                VStack(spacing: 10) { buttons }
            }
        }
        .padding(24)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color.purple.opacity(0.08).ignoresSafeArea())
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.9, bounce: 0.25), value: form)
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }

            while isAutoPlaying {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.3))
                guard !Task.isCancelled, isAutoPlaying else { return }
                form = nextForm
            }
        }
    }

    private var buttons: some View {
        ForEach(PolygonMorphShapeForm.allCases, id: \.self) { option in
            Button(option.rawValue) {
                isAutoPlaying = false
                form = option
            }
            .buttonStyle(.bordered)
            .tint(option == form ? .pink : .secondary)
            .accessibilityAddTraits(option == form ? .isSelected : [])
        }
    }
}
```

## Border Beam Modifier

A light beam with a fading tail that travels continuously around a rounded border.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/BorderBeamModifier/BorderBeamModifier.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum BorderBeamModifierMath {
    /// How far around the border the beam's head is, from 0 up to 1.
    static func head(time: Double, duration: Double) -> Double {
        guard duration > 0, time.isFinite else { return 0 }
        return wrapped(time / duration)
    }

    /// The trim ranges that cover `start` to `end` on a closed path, in two parts across the seam.
    static func trims(from start: Double, to end: Double) -> [ClosedRange<Double>] {
        let from = wrapped(start)
        let to = wrapped(end)
        if from == to { return [] }
        if from < to { return [from...to] }
        return to > 0 ? [from...1, 0...to] : [from...1]
    }

    private static func wrapped(_ value: Double) -> Double {
        value - floor(value)
    }
}

/// A light beam that travels around a rounded border at a steady speed, with a fading tail.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the beam stays still.
struct BorderBeamModifier: ViewModifier {
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat = 20
    var lineWidth: CGFloat = 2
    var head: Color = .cyan
    var tail: Color = .purple
    var duration: Double = 3.5
    var length: Double = 0.3

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.overlay {
            TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 60.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
                let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate

                Canvas { context, size in
                    drawBeam(in: context, size: size, position: BorderBeamModifierMath.head(time: time, duration: duration))
                }
            }
            .allowsHitTesting(false)
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
    }

    private func drawBeam(in context: GraphicsContext, size: CGSize, position: Double) {
        let width = max(lineWidth, 0)
        let rect = CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size).insetBy(dx: width / 2, dy: width / 2)
        let beam = min(max(length, 0), 1)
        guard width > 0, beam > 0, rect.width > 0, rect.height > 0 else { return }

        let radius = min(max(cornerRadius - width / 2, 0), min(rect.width, rect.height) / 2)
        let border = RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: radius, style: .continuous).path(in: rect)

        let slices = 32
        var segments: [(path: Path, shading: GraphicsContext.Shading)] = []
        for slice in 0..<slices {
            let fraction = Double(slice + 1) / Double(slices)
            let start = position - beam * (1 - Double(slice) / Double(slices))
            let end = position - beam * (1 - fraction) + 0.001
            let shading = GraphicsContext.Shading.color(tail.mix(with: head, by: fraction).opacity(fraction))

            for trim in BorderBeamModifierMath.trims(from: start, to: end) {
                segments.append((border.trimmedPath(from: trim.lowerBound, to: trim.upperBound), shading))
            }
        }

        var glow = context
        glow.addFilter(.blur(radius: width * 2.5))
        glow.drawLayer { layer in
            for segment in segments {
                layer.stroke(segment.path, with: segment.shading, lineWidth: width * 2)
            }
        }

        for segment in segments {
            context.stroke(segment.path, with: segment.shading, lineWidth: width)
        }
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Sends a light beam around this view's border. Match `cornerRadius` to the view's shape.
    func borderBeam(
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 20,
        lineWidth: CGFloat = 2,
        head: Color = .cyan,
        tail: Color = .purple,
        duration: Double = 3.5,
        length: Double = 0.3
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(
            BorderBeamModifier(
                cornerRadius: cornerRadius,
                lineWidth: lineWidth,
                head: head,
                tail: tail,
                duration: duration,
                length: length
            )
        )
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct BorderBeamModifierDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(spacing: 32) {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
                    Image(systemName: "bolt.fill")
                        .font(.title)
                        .foregroundStyle(.cyan)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)

                    Text("Introducing Beam")
                        .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                    Text("A quiet way to draw the eye to what matters most on the screen.")
                        .font(.body)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.7))
                }
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .padding(24)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                .background(.white.opacity(0.07), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 28, style: .continuous))
                .borderBeam(cornerRadius: 28, lineWidth: 2.5)

                Text("Get early access")
                    .font(.headline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    .padding(.horizontal, 28)
                    .padding(.vertical, 14)
                    .background(.white.opacity(0.07), in: .capsule)
                    .borderBeam(cornerRadius: 200, head: .orange, tail: .pink, duration: 2.5, length: 0.4)
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
        .defaultScrollAnchor(.center, for: .alignment)
        .background(Color(red: 0.05, green: 0.05, blue: 0.1).ignoresSafeArea())
    }
}

#Preview {
    BorderBeamModifierDemo()
}
```

## Coin Flip View

A coin that flips in 3D over several turns and lands on heads or tails.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/CoinFlipView/CoinFlipView.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum CoinFlipViewSide: String, CaseIterable, Hashable {
    case heads = "Heads"
    case tails = "Tails"

    var symbolName: String {
        switch self {
        case .heads: "crown.fill"
        case .tails: "leaf.fill"
        }
    }
}

enum CoinFlipViewMath {
    /// Heads faces the viewer on even half turns.
    static func visibleSide(at angle: Double) -> CoinFlipViewSide {
        cos(angle * .pi / 180) >= 0 ? .heads : .tails
    }

    /// An angle at least `turns` full turns ahead that rests on the landing side.
    static func targetAngle(from angle: Double, landing: CoinFlipViewSide, turns: Int) -> Double {
        let halfTurns = (angle / 180).rounded()
        let target = halfTurns * 180 + Double(min(max(turns, 1), 100)) * 360
        return visibleSide(at: target) == landing ? target : target + 180
    }
}

/// A coin that flips in 3D over several turns and lands on heads or tails. Tap it to flip.
///
/// A tap during a flip is ignored, so each flip reports one result.
/// With Reduce Motion on, the coin shows the result at once.
struct CoinFlipView: View {
    @Binding var side: CoinFlipViewSide
    var size: CGFloat = 180
    var turns: Int = 5
    var onLanded: ((CoinFlipViewSide) -> Void)?

    @State private var angle: Double
    @State private var isFlipping = false
    @State private var flipCount = 0
    @State private var landedCount = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let flipDuration = 1.5

    init(
        side: Binding<CoinFlipViewSide>,
        size: CGFloat = 180,
        turns: Int = 5,
        onLanded: ((CoinFlipViewSide) -> Void)? = nil
    ) {
        _side = side
        self.size = size
        self.turns = turns
        self.onLanded = onLanded
        _angle = State(initialValue: side.wrappedValue == .heads ? 0 : 180)
    }

    private var diameter: CGFloat { max(size, 1) }

    var body: some View {
        Button(action: flip) {
            CoinFlipViewCoin(angle: angle, diameter: diameter)
                .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: 0.0, trigger: flipCount) { [diameter] coin, height in
                    coin.offset(y: -height * diameter * 1.1)
                } keyframes: { _ in
                    CubicKeyframe(1, duration: 0.65)
                    CubicKeyframe(0, duration: 0.85)
                }
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel("Flip coin")
        .accessibilityValue(side.rawValue)
        .sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .medium), trigger: landedCount)
        .onChange(of: side) { _, newSide in
            guard !isFlipping, CoinFlipViewMath.visibleSide(at: angle) != newSide else { return }
            angle += 180
        }
    }

    private func flip() {
        guard !isFlipping else { return }

        let landing = CoinFlipViewSide.allCases.randomElement() ?? .heads
        let target = CoinFlipViewMath.targetAngle(from: angle, landing: landing, turns: turns)

        guard !reduceMotion else {
            angle = target
            land(on: landing)
            return
        }

        isFlipping = true
        flipCount += 1
        withAnimation(.timingCurve(0.2, 0.7, 0.3, 1, duration: flipDuration)) {
            angle = target
        } completion: {
            land(on: landing)
        }
    }

    private func land(on landing: CoinFlipViewSide) {
        isFlipping = false
        side = landing
        landedCount += 1
        onLanded?(landing)
    }
}

/// Animatable so its body runs on every frame and can swap the face at the edge-on moment.
private struct CoinFlipViewCoin: View, Animatable {
    var angle: Double
    let diameter: CGFloat

    nonisolated var animatableData: Double {
        get { angle }
        set { angle = newValue }
    }

    var body: some View {
        let visible = CoinFlipViewMath.visibleSide(at: angle)

        face(visible)
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(visible == .heads ? 0 : 180), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0))
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(angle), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0), perspective: 0.4)
    }

    private func face(_ side: CoinFlipViewSide) -> some View {
        ZStack {
            Circle()
                .fill(
                    LinearGradient(
                        colors: [Color(red: 1, green: 0.86, blue: 0.45), Color(red: 0.85, green: 0.58, blue: 0.13)],
                        startPoint: .topLeading,
                        endPoint: .bottomTrailing
                    )
                )

            Circle()
                .strokeBorder(.white.opacity(0.5), lineWidth: diameter * 0.03)
                .padding(diameter * 0.07)

            Image(systemName: side.symbolName)
                .font(.system(size: diameter * 0.38, weight: .bold))
                .foregroundStyle(Color(red: 0.55, green: 0.33, blue: 0.05))
        }
        .frame(width: diameter, height: diameter)
        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.25), radius: 12, y: 8)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CoinFlipViewDemo: View {
    @State private var side = CoinFlipViewSide.heads
    @State private var flips = 0

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(spacing: 40) {
                Text("Tap the coin")
                    .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                CoinFlipView(side: $side) { _ in
                    flips += 1
                }
                .padding(.top, 180)

                VStack(spacing: 4) {
                    Text(flips == 0 ? "Ready" : side.rawValue)
                        .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                    Text("Flips: \(flips)")
                        .font(.body)
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
            }
            .padding(24)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
        }
        .defaultScrollAnchor(.center, for: .alignment)
        .background(
            LinearGradient(colors: [.yellow.opacity(0.18), .orange.opacity(0.12)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()
        )
    }
}

#Preview {
    CoinFlipViewDemo()
}
```

## Color Reveal Image

A black and white image that gains its color as it scrolls toward the middle or when tapped.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/ColorRevealImage/ColorRevealImage.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum ColorRevealImageMath {
    /// Full color near the middle of the scroll view, fading to none toward its edges.
    static func saturation(distanceFromCenter distance: CGFloat, viewportHeight: CGFloat) -> Double {
        guard viewportHeight > 0, distance.isFinite else { return 0 }

        let clearZone = viewportHeight * 0.12
        let fade = viewportHeight * 0.3
        return Double(min(max(1 - (abs(distance) - clearZone) / fade, 0), 1))
    }
}

/// A black and white image that gains its color as it nears the middle of a scroll view.
/// Tapping it shows the full color until tapped again.
///
/// Outside a scroll view it stays black and white until tapped. With Reduce Motion
/// on, a tap changes it at once. Scrolling still fades the color, which adds no movement.
struct ColorRevealImage: View {
    let image: Image
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    var aspectRatio: CGFloat = 4.0 / 3.0
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat = 24

    @State private var isRevealed = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: 0.5)) {
                isRevealed.toggle()
            }
        } label: {
            Color.clear
                .aspectRatio(aspectRatio > 0 ? aspectRatio : 1, contentMode: .fit)
                .overlay {
                    ZStack {
                        image
                            .resizable()
                            .scaledToFill()
                            .visualEffect { effect, proxy in
                                let viewport = proxy.bounds(of: .scrollView(axis: .vertical))
                                let distance = (viewport?.midY ?? 0) - proxy.size.height / 2

                                return effect.saturation(
                                    ColorRevealImageMath.saturation(
                                        distanceFromCenter: distance,
                                        viewportHeight: viewport?.height ?? 0
                                    )
                                )
                            }

                        image
                            .resizable()
                            .scaledToFill()
                            .opacity(isRevealed ? 1 : 0)
                    }
                    // The button already reads the title, so the images add nothing to VoiceOver.
                    .accessibilityRepresentation { EmptyView() }
                }
                .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: max(cornerRadius, 0), style: .continuous))
                .contentShape(.rect(cornerRadius: max(cornerRadius, 0), style: .continuous))
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(title)
        .accessibilityValue(isRevealed ? "In full color" : "Color follows scrolling")
    }
}
```

## Confetti Burst

A one-shot confetti burst with simple physics, fired by changing a trigger.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/ConfettiBurst/ConfettiBurst.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Fires a one-shot burst of confetti every time `trigger` changes.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the pieces appear scattered and fade out without moving.
struct ConfettiBurst: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Int
    var count: Int = 120
    /// Where the burst starts, as a fraction of the view.
    var origin: UnitPoint = UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 0.68)
    var colors: [Color] = [.pink, .yellow, .mint, .cyan, .orange, .purple]
    var lifetime: Double = 3

    @State private var start: Date?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private static let motion = ConfettiBurstMotion()
    private static let pieceWidth: CGFloat = 8

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                TimelineView(.animation(paused: start == nil)) { timeline in
                    Canvas { context, size in
                        guard let start else { return }
                        draw(elapsed: timeline.date.timeIntervalSince(start), in: context, size: size)
                    }
                }
                .ignoresSafeArea()
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .onChange(of: trigger) { start = .now }
            .task(id: start) {
                guard start != nil else { return }
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(lifetime))
                if !Task.isCancelled { start = nil }
            }
    }

    private func draw(elapsed: Double, in context: GraphicsContext, size: CGSize) {
        guard elapsed < lifetime, !colors.isEmpty else { return }

        let time = reduceMotion ? 0.6 : elapsed
        let fade = min((lifetime - elapsed) / (lifetime * 0.3), 1)

        for index in 0..<count {
            let offset = Self.motion.offset(
                // Two random values added together cluster the pieces around straight up.
                angle: (noise(index, 1) + noise(index, 7) - 1) * 0.9,
                speed: 500 + noise(index, 2) * 1900,
                at: time
            )

            var piece = context
            piece.opacity = fade
            piece.translateBy(x: origin.x * size.width + offset.x, y: origin.y * size.height + offset.y)
            piece.rotate(by: .radians(time * (noise(index, 3) * 8 - 4) + noise(index, 4) * 2 * .pi))
            piece.scaleBy(x: cos(time * (4 + noise(index, 5) * 8) + noise(index, 6) * 2 * .pi), y: 1)

            let color = GraphicsContext.Shading.color(colors[index % colors.count])
            if index.isMultiple(of: 3) {
                piece.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: -Self.pieceWidth / 2, y: -Self.pieceWidth / 2, width: Self.pieceWidth, height: Self.pieceWidth)), with: color)
            } else {
                piece.fill(Path(CGRect(x: -Self.pieceWidth / 2, y: -6.5, width: Self.pieceWidth, height: 13)), with: color)
            }
        }
    }

    /// A repeatable pseudo-random value in 0..<1, different for each burst.
    private func noise(_ index: Int, _ salt: Double) -> Double {
        let value = sin(Double(index) * 127.1 + (salt + Double(trigger) * 0.37) * 311.7) * 43758.5453
        return value - floor(value)
    }
}

/// The flight of one piece: thrown from the origin, slowed by air and pulled down by gravity.
struct ConfettiBurstMotion {
    /// Points per second squared.
    var gravity: Double = 900
    /// How quickly air slows a piece, per second.
    var drag: Double = 2.6

    /// The offset from the origin, with y growing downward.
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - angle: The launch direction in radians: 0 is straight up, positive leans right.
    ///   - speed: The launch speed in points per second.
    ///   - time: The seconds since launch.
    func offset(angle: Double, speed: Double, at time: Double) -> CGPoint {
        let time = max(time, 0)
        let drag = max(drag, 0.001)
        let travelled = (1 - exp(-drag * time)) / drag

        return CGPoint(
            x: sin(angle) * speed * travelled,
            y: -cos(angle) * speed * travelled + gravity / drag * (time - travelled)
        )
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Fires a one-shot burst of confetti over this view every time `trigger` changes.
    func confettiBurst(trigger: Int, count: Int = 120, origin: UnitPoint = UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 0.68)) -> some View {
        modifier(ConfettiBurst(trigger: trigger, count: count, origin: origin))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ConfettiBurstDemo: View {
    @State private var bursts = 0

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [Color(red: 0.13, green: 0.09, blue: 0.33), Color(red: 0.36, green: 0.13, blue: 0.45)],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )
            .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 14) {
                Spacer()

                Image(systemName: "trophy.fill")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, weight: .bold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.yellow)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                Text("You Did It")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)

                Spacer()

                Button("Celebrate") { bursts += 1 }
                    .font(.headline)
                    .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                    .controlSize(.large)
                    .tint(.pink)
                    .padding(.bottom, 32)
            }
        }
        .confettiBurst(trigger: bursts)
        .task {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.3))
            bursts += 1
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ConfettiBurstDemo()
}
```

## Fireworks Burst

Rockets that climb to where you tap and explode into particle sparks.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/FireworksBurst/FireworksBurst.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum FireworksBurstMath {
    enum Stage: Equatable {
        case climbing(Double)
        case bursting(Double)
        case finished
    }

    static let climbDuration = 0.65
    static let burstDuration = 1.5
    static var lifetime: Double { climbDuration + burstDuration }

    /// Where a rocket is in its life. Without a climb, it bursts as soon as it is launched.
    static func stage(elapsed: Double, skipsClimb: Bool = false) -> Stage {
        let afterClimb = skipsClimb ? max(elapsed, 0) : elapsed - climbDuration

        if !skipsClimb, afterClimb < 0 {
            return .climbing(min(max(elapsed / climbDuration, 0), 1))
        }
        return afterClimb < burstDuration ? .bursting(afterClimb / burstDuration) : .finished
    }

    /// A spark races outward, slows down and then droops under gravity.
    static func sparkOffset(angle: Double, speed: CGFloat, progress: Double) -> CGSize {
        let travel = speed * (1 - pow(1 - progress, 3))
        return CGSize(
            width: travel * cos(angle),
            height: travel * sin(angle) + 70 * progress * progress
        )
    }
}

private struct FireworksBurstSpark {
    let angle: Double
    let speed: CGFloat
    let size: CGFloat
}

private struct FireworksBurstRocket: Identifiable {
    let id = UUID()
    let launchDate: Date
    let start: CGPoint
    let target: CGPoint
    let color: Color
    let sparks: [FireworksBurstSpark]
}

/// Rockets that climb to where you tap and explode into sparks.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, each burst appears in place and fades without moving.
struct FireworksBurst: View {
    var sparkCount: Int = 64
    var colors: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .yellow, .mint, .cyan, .purple]

    @State private var rockets: [FireworksBurstRocket] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let maximumRockets = 12

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            TimelineView(.animation(paused: rockets.isEmpty)) { timeline in
                Canvas { context, _ in
                    context.blendMode = .plusLighter
                    for rocket in rockets {
                        draw(rocket, at: timeline.date, in: context)
                    }
                }
            }
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .gesture(
                SpatialTapGesture().onEnded { launch(to: $0.location, groundY: proxy.size.height) }
            )
            .accessibilityElement()
            .accessibilityLabel("Night sky")
            .accessibilityHint("Launches a firework")
            .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)
            .accessibilityAction {
                launch(to: CGPoint(x: proxy.size.width / 2, y: proxy.size.height / 3), groundY: proxy.size.height)
            }
        }
        .task(id: rockets.last?.id) {
            guard !rockets.isEmpty else { return }

            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(FireworksBurstMath.lifetime + 0.1))
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }

            let now = Date.now
            rockets.removeAll { now.timeIntervalSince($0.launchDate) >= FireworksBurstMath.lifetime }
        }
    }

    private func launch(to target: CGPoint, groundY: CGFloat) {
        let count = min(max(sparkCount, 1), 300)
        let sparks = (0..<count).map { index in
            FireworksBurstSpark(
                angle: Double(index) / Double(count) * 2 * .pi + .random(in: -0.08...0.08),
                speed: .random(in: 70...170),
                size: .random(in: 1.5...3.5)
            )
        }

        rockets.append(
            FireworksBurstRocket(
                launchDate: .now,
                start: CGPoint(x: target.x + .random(in: -24...24), y: groundY),
                target: target,
                color: colors.randomElement() ?? .white,
                sparks: sparks
            )
        )
        if rockets.count > maximumRockets {
            rockets.removeFirst(rockets.count - maximumRockets)
        }
    }

    private func draw(_ rocket: FireworksBurstRocket, at date: Date, in context: GraphicsContext) {
        let elapsed = date.timeIntervalSince(rocket.launchDate)

        switch FireworksBurstMath.stage(elapsed: elapsed, skipsClimb: reduceMotion) {
        case .climbing(let progress):
            let eased = 1 - (1 - progress) * (1 - progress)
            let head = CGPoint(
                x: rocket.start.x + (rocket.target.x - rocket.start.x) * eased,
                y: rocket.start.y + (rocket.target.y - rocket.start.y) * eased
            )
            var trail = Path()
            trail.move(to: CGPoint(x: head.x, y: head.y + 26))
            trail.addLine(to: head)
            context.stroke(trail, with: .color(.white.opacity(0.8)), style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 2.5, lineCap: .round))

        case .bursting(let progress):
            let shading = GraphicsContext.Shading.color(rocket.color.opacity(1 - progress))
            for spark in rocket.sparks {
                let shown = reduceMotion ? 0.8 : progress
                let offset = FireworksBurstMath.sparkOffset(angle: spark.angle, speed: spark.speed, progress: shown)
                let center = CGPoint(x: rocket.target.x + offset.width, y: rocket.target.y + offset.height)
                let dot = CGRect(x: center.x - spark.size / 2, y: center.y - spark.size / 2, width: spark.size, height: spark.size)
                context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: dot), with: shading)
            }

        case .finished:
            break
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct FireworksBurstDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack(alignment: .top) {
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [Color(red: 0.03, green: 0.03, blue: 0.14), Color(red: 0.13, green: 0.07, blue: 0.3)],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )
            .ignoresSafeArea()

            FireworksBurst()
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            Text("Tap the sky")
                .font(.system(.title2, design: .rounded, weight: .semibold))
                .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.75))
                .padding(.top, 24)
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    FireworksBurstDemo()
}
```

## Floating Reactions Emitter

Emoji that float up from the tap point with a random drift and fade out.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/FloatingReactionsEmitter/FloatingReactionsEmitter.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum FloatingReactionsEmitterMath {
    /// How far a reaction has moved from its origin, weaving side to side as it rises.
    static func offset(progress: Double, rise: CGFloat, drift: CGFloat, swayPhase: Double) -> CGSize {
        let clamped = min(max(progress, 0), 1)
        let sway = sin(clamped * 3 * .pi + swayPhase) * 16 * clamped
        return CGSize(width: drift * clamped + sway, height: -rise * clamped)
    }

    /// Solid for most of the way, then fading out.
    static func opacity(progress: Double) -> Double {
        let clamped = min(max(progress, 0), 1)
        return clamped < 0.6 ? 1 : (1 - clamped) / 0.4
    }

    static func scale(progress: Double) -> Double {
        0.4 + 0.6 * min(max(progress, 0) / 0.15, 1)
    }
}

private struct FloatingReactionsEmitterReaction: Identifiable {
    let id = UUID()
    let emoji: String
    let origin: CGPoint
    let start: Date
    let drift: CGFloat
    let swayPhase: Double
}

/// Wraps content so that a tap sends an emoji floating up from that point.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the emoji stays where it was tapped and fades out.
struct FloatingReactionsEmitter<Content: View>: View {
    var emojis: [String] = ["❤️", "🔥", "👏", "😂", "🎉"]
    var lifetime: Double = 1.8
    var rise: CGFloat = 320
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @State private var reactions: [FloatingReactionsEmitterReaction] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    private let maximumReactions = 40
    private var duration: Double { lifetime > 0 ? lifetime : 1 }

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            content()
                .frame(width: proxy.size.width, height: proxy.size.height)
                .contentShape(.rect)
                .gesture(SpatialTapGesture().onEnded { value in
                    // Gestures report screen points, but `position` mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
                    let x = layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? proxy.size.width - value.location.x : value.location.x
                    emit(from: CGPoint(x: x, y: value.location.y))
                })
                .overlay {
                    TimelineView(.animation(paused: reactions.isEmpty)) { timeline in
                        ZStack {
                            ForEach(reactions) { reaction in
                                bubble(for: reaction, at: timeline.date)
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
                .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
                    Color.clear
                        .frame(height: 44)
                        .allowsHitTesting(false)
                        .accessibilityElement()
                        .accessibilityLabel("Send reaction")
                        .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)
                        .accessibilityAction {
                            emit(from: CGPoint(x: proxy.size.width / 2, y: proxy.size.height * 0.75))
                        }
                }
        }
        .task(id: reactions.last?.id) {
            guard !reactions.isEmpty else { return }

            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(duration + 0.1))
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }

            let now = Date.now
            reactions.removeAll { now.timeIntervalSince($0.start) >= duration }
        }
    }

    private func bubble(for reaction: FloatingReactionsEmitterReaction, at date: Date) -> some View {
        let progress = date.timeIntervalSince(reaction.start) / duration
        let offset = reduceMotion
            ? .zero
            : FloatingReactionsEmitterMath.offset(progress: progress, rise: rise, drift: reaction.drift, swayPhase: reaction.swayPhase)

        return Text(reaction.emoji)
            .font(.largeTitle)
            .scaleEffect(reduceMotion ? 1 : FloatingReactionsEmitterMath.scale(progress: progress))
            .opacity(FloatingReactionsEmitterMath.opacity(progress: progress))
            .position(x: reaction.origin.x + offset.width, y: reaction.origin.y + offset.height)
    }

    private func emit(from location: CGPoint) {
        guard let emoji = emojis.randomElement() else { return }

        reactions.append(
            FloatingReactionsEmitterReaction(
                emoji: emoji,
                origin: location,
                start: .now,
                drift: .random(in: -70...70),
                swayPhase: .random(in: 0...(2 * .pi))
            )
        )
        if reactions.count > maximumReactions {
            reactions.removeFirst(reactions.count - maximumReactions)
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct FloatingReactionsEmitterDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        FloatingReactionsEmitter {
            ZStack {
                LinearGradient(colors: [.purple, .pink, .orange], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)

                VStack(spacing: 14) {
                    Image(systemName: "dot.radiowaves.left.and.right")
                        .font(.largeTitle)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)

                    Text("Live now")
                        .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                    Text("Tap anywhere to react")
                        .font(.body)
                        .opacity(0.85)
                }
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                .padding(24)
            }
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    }
}

#Preview {
    FloatingReactionsEmitterDemo()
}
```

## Flow Field Particles

Particles that drift along a smooth field of angles computed from position and time.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/FlowFieldParticles/FlowFieldParticles.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Particles that drift along a smooth field of angles.
///
/// Every frame is computed from the time alone, so there is no state to keep.
/// With Reduce Motion on, it draws one still frame. It looks best on a dark background.
struct FlowFieldParticles: View {
    var count = 260
    var colors: [Color] = [.cyan, .indigo, .pink]
    var speed = 1.0

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 8 : context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * max(speed, 0)

            Canvas { canvas, size in
                canvas.blendMode = .plusLighter
                let palette = colors.isEmpty ? [Color.white] : colors
                for index in 0..<FlowFieldParticlesMath.clampedCount(count) {
                    let streak = FlowFieldParticlesMath.streak(index: index, time: time, size: size)
                    guard !streak.points.isEmpty else { continue }

                    var path = Path()
                    path.addLines(streak.points)
                    canvas.stroke(
                        path,
                        with: .color(palette[index % palette.count].opacity(streak.opacity)),
                        style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 1.5, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round)
                    )
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

struct FlowFieldParticlesStreak {
    var points: [CGPoint]
    var opacity: Double
}

enum FlowFieldParticlesMath {
    static func clampedCount(_ count: Int) -> Int {
        min(max(count, 0), 2_000)
    }

    /// The part of `value` after the decimal point, always in `0..<1`.
    static func fraction(_ value: Double) -> Double {
        guard value.isFinite else { return 0 }
        let part = value - floor(value)
        return part < 1 ? part : 0
    }

    /// The direction of the flow, in radians, at a point of the canvas.
    static func angle(x: Double, y: Double, time: Double) -> Double {
        let across = sin(x * 0.007 + time * 0.13) + cos(y * 0.009 - time * 0.11)
        let diagonal = sin((x + y) * 0.004 + time * 0.07)
        return (across + diagonal) * .pi * 0.7
    }

    /// Follows the field from where a particle was born to where it is now, and keeps its tail.
    static func streak(
        index: Int,
        time: Double,
        size: CGSize,
        steps: Int = 24,
        trail: Int = 8
    ) -> FlowFieldParticlesStreak {
        guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0, steps > 0, trail > 0 else {
            return FlowFieldParticlesStreak(points: [], opacity: 0)
        }

        let seed = Double(index)
        let lifetime = 3 + fraction(seed * 0.317) * 3
        let clock = time / lifetime + fraction(seed * 0.131)
        let age = fraction(clock)
        let generation = clock.isFinite ? floor(clock) : 0

        let margin = 60.0
        var x = fraction(0.5 + seed * 0.754_877 + generation * 0.37) * (size.width + margin * 2) - margin
        var y = fraction(0.5 + seed * 0.569_840 + generation * 0.61) * (size.height + margin * 2) - margin
        let stepLength = age * 150 / Double(steps)

        var points: [CGPoint] = []
        points.reserveCapacity(min(trail, steps) + 1)
        for step in 0...steps {
            if step >= steps - trail {
                points.append(CGPoint(x: x, y: y))
            }
            let direction = angle(x: x, y: y, time: time)
            x += cos(direction) * stepLength
            y += sin(direction) * stepLength
        }
        return FlowFieldParticlesStreak(points: points, opacity: sin(age * .pi) * 0.9)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct FlowFieldParticlesDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [Color(red: 0.03, green: 0.02, blue: 0.1), .black],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )
            .ignoresSafeArea()

            FlowFieldParticles(count: 420)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            Text("Flow Field")
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.7), radius: 12)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    FlowFieldParticlesDemo()
}
```

## Globe 3D Wireframe

A wireframe globe drawn on a Canvas that spins by itself and turns and tilts as the finger drags it.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/Globe3DWireframe/Globe3DWireframe.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct Globe3DWireframePin {
    var latitude: Double
    var longitude: Double
}

/// A wireframe globe drawn on a Canvas. Drag it to spin and tilt it.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, it stops spinning by itself and only moves with the finger.
struct Globe3DWireframe: View {
    var meridians = 12
    var parallels = 7
    var color: Color = .cyan
    var pins: [Globe3DWireframePin] = []
    var autoRotates = true
    var label = "Globe"

    @State private var yaw = 0.0
    @State private var pitch = 0.35
    @GestureState private var drag = CGSize.zero
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let radiansPerPoint = 0.008
    private var isSpinning: Bool { autoRotates && !reduceMotion }

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: !isSpinning)) { context in
            let spin = isSpinning ? context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * 0.35 : 0
            let currentYaw = yaw + spin + drag.width * radiansPerPoint
            let currentPitch = Globe3DWireframeMath.clampedPitch(pitch + drag.height * radiansPerPoint)

            Canvas { canvas, size in
                let radius = min(size.width, size.height) / 2 * 0.94
                guard radius > 0 else { return }
                let center = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
                let disc = Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(
                    x: center.x - radius,
                    y: center.y - radius,
                    width: radius * 2,
                    height: radius * 2
                ))
                let wires = Globe3DWireframeMath.wires(
                    meridians: meridians,
                    parallels: parallels,
                    yaw: currentYaw,
                    pitch: currentPitch,
                    center: center,
                    radius: radius
                )
                let lineWidth = max(0.6, radius * 0.006)

                canvas.stroke(wires.back, with: .color(color.opacity(0.18)), lineWidth: lineWidth)
                canvas.fill(disc, with: .radialGradient(
                    Gradient(colors: [color.opacity(0.22), color.opacity(0.04)]),
                    center: CGPoint(x: center.x - radius * 0.3, y: center.y - radius * 0.3),
                    startRadius: 0,
                    endRadius: radius * 1.3
                ))
                canvas.stroke(wires.front, with: .color(color.opacity(0.85)), lineWidth: lineWidth)
                canvas.stroke(disc, with: .color(color.opacity(0.6)), lineWidth: lineWidth * 1.5)

                for pin in pins {
                    let point = Globe3DWireframeMath.project(
                        latitude: pin.latitude,
                        longitude: pin.longitude,
                        yaw: currentYaw,
                        pitch: currentPitch
                    )
                    guard point.z > 0 else { continue }
                    let screen = CGPoint(x: center.x + point.x * radius, y: center.y - point.y * radius)
                    let glow = radius * 0.05
                    let dot = radius * 0.018
                    canvas.fill(
                        Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: screen.x - glow, y: screen.y - glow, width: glow * 2, height: glow * 2)),
                        with: .color(.white.opacity(0.25))
                    )
                    canvas.fill(
                        Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: screen.x - dot, y: screen.y - dot, width: dot * 2, height: dot * 2)),
                        with: .color(.white)
                    )
                }
            }
        }
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .contentShape(.circle)
        .gesture(
            DragGesture(minimumDistance: 4)
                .updating($drag) { value, state, _ in
                    state = value.translation
                }
                .onEnded { value in
                    yaw += value.translation.width * radiansPerPoint
                    pitch = Globe3DWireframeMath.clampedPitch(pitch + value.translation.height * radiansPerPoint)
                }
        )
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel(label)
        .accessibilityValue("Rotated \(Globe3DWireframeMath.degrees(yaw)) degrees")
        .accessibilityAdjustableAction { direction in
            switch direction {
            case .increment: yaw += .pi / 12
            case .decrement: yaw -= .pi / 12
            @unknown default: break
            }
        }
    }
}

enum Globe3DWireframeMath {
    struct Point {
        var x: Double
        var y: Double
        var z: Double
    }

    static let maximumPitch = 1.4

    static func clampedPitch(_ pitch: Double) -> Double {
        min(max(pitch, -maximumPitch), maximumPitch)
    }

    /// The rotation as a whole number of degrees from 0 to 359.
    static func degrees(_ radians: Double) -> Int {
        guard radians.isFinite else { return 0 }
        let degrees = (radians * 180 / .pi).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 360)
        return (Int(degrees.rounded()) + 360) % 360
    }

    /// Turns a point of the sphere around its axis, then tilts the sphere toward the viewer.
    /// `x` points right, `y` points up and `z` points at the viewer.
    static func project(latitude: Double, longitude: Double, yaw: Double, pitch: Double) -> Point {
        let lat = latitude * .pi / 180
        let lon = longitude * .pi / 180 + yaw
        let x = cos(lat) * sin(lon)
        let y = sin(lat)
        let z = cos(lat) * cos(lon)
        return Point(x: x, y: y * cos(pitch) - z * sin(pitch), z: y * sin(pitch) + z * cos(pitch))
    }

    /// The globe's lines, split into the half that faces the viewer and the half behind it.
    static func wires(
        meridians: Int,
        parallels: Int,
        yaw: Double,
        pitch: Double,
        center: CGPoint,
        radius: Double
    ) -> (front: Path, back: Path) {
        var front = Path()
        var back = Path()

        func addLine(samples: Int, coordinate: (Double) -> (latitude: Double, longitude: Double)) {
            var previous: Point?
            for sample in 0...samples {
                let position = coordinate(Double(sample) / Double(samples))
                let point = project(latitude: position.latitude, longitude: position.longitude, yaw: yaw, pitch: pitch)
                if let previous {
                    let start = CGPoint(x: center.x + previous.x * radius, y: center.y - previous.y * radius)
                    let end = CGPoint(x: center.x + point.x * radius, y: center.y - point.y * radius)
                    if previous.z + point.z >= 0 {
                        front.move(to: start)
                        front.addLine(to: end)
                    } else {
                        back.move(to: start)
                        back.addLine(to: end)
                    }
                }
                previous = point
            }
        }

        let meridianCount = min(max(meridians, 0), 90)
        for index in 0..<meridianCount {
            let longitude = 360 * Double(index) / Double(meridianCount)
            addLine(samples: 40) { (latitude: -90 + 180 * $0, longitude: longitude) }
        }

        let parallelCount = min(max(parallels, 0), 90)
        for index in 0..<parallelCount {
            let latitude = -90 + 180 * Double(index + 1) / Double(parallelCount + 1)
            addLine(samples: 72) { (latitude: latitude, longitude: 360 * $0) }
        }
        return (front, back)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct Globe3DWireframeDemo: View {
    private let cities = [
        Globe3DWireframePin(latitude: 40.4, longitude: -3.7),
        Globe3DWireframePin(latitude: 35.7, longitude: 139.7),
        Globe3DWireframePin(latitude: -33.9, longitude: 151.2),
        Globe3DWireframePin(latitude: 40.7, longitude: -74),
        Globe3DWireframePin(latitude: -23.5, longitude: -46.6),
        Globe3DWireframePin(latitude: -1.3, longitude: 36.8),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {

                colors: [Color(red: 0.05, green: 0.12, blue: 0.25), .black],

                endRadius: 520
            )

                .padding(24)
```

## Intelligence Glow Border

A soft band of color that travels around a view's edge and spreads inward, like an assistant that is listening.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/IntelligenceGlowBorder/IntelligenceGlowBorder.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum IntelligenceGlowBorderMath {
    /// The mesh is 3 by 3: four corners, four edge points and a center.
    static let side = 3

    /// The points on the border in the order the colors travel, as indices into the mesh.
    static let perimeter = [0, 1, 2, 5, 8, 7, 6, 3]

    /// How far around the border the colors have travelled, from 0 up to 1.
    static func phase(time: Double, period: Double) -> Double {
        guard period > 0, time.isFinite else { return 0 }
        return wrapped(time / period)
    }

    /// The two colors of a palette of `count` that meet at `position`, and how much of the second one shows.
    /// The palette is a loop, so the last color blends back into the first.
    static func blend(at position: Double, count: Int) -> (lower: Int, upper: Int, fraction: Double) {
        guard count > 1, position.isFinite else { return (0, 0, 0) }

        let scaled = wrapped(position) * Double(count)
        let lower = min(Int(scaled), count - 1)
        return (lower, (lower + 1) % count, scaled - Double(lower))
    }

    /// Corners stay put and edge points slide along their edge, so the mesh always covers the border.
    static func points(phase: Double) -> [SIMD2<Float>] {
        func slide(_ offset: Double) -> Double {
            0.5 + sin((phase + offset) * 2 * .pi) * 0.16
        }

        let positions: [(Double, Double)] = [
            (0, 0), (slide(0), 0), (1, 0),
            (0, slide(0.75)), (0.5, 0.5), (1, slide(0.25)),
            (0, 1), (slide(0.5), 1), (1, 1),
        ]
        return positions.map { SIMD2(Float($0.0), Float($0.1)) }
    }

    private static func wrapped(_ value: Double) -> Double {
        value - floor(value)
    }
}

/// A soft band of moving color around the edge of a view, like the glow of an assistant that is listening.
///
/// The colors travel around the border and the light spreads inward. With Reduce Motion on, the
/// glow is still.
struct IntelligenceGlowBorder: ViewModifier {
    var isActive = true
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat = 28
    var lineWidth: CGFloat = 3
    var colors: [Color] = [.purple, .pink, .orange, .yellow, .cyan, .blue]
    /// Seconds for the colors to travel once around the border.
    var period: Double = 6

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                if isActive {
                    TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
                        let time = context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
                        glow(phase: reduceMotion ? 0 : IntelligenceGlowBorderMath.phase(time: time, period: period))
                    }
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                    .transition(.opacity)
                }
            }
            .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: 0.6), value: isActive)
    }

    private func glow(phase: Double) -> some View {
        let width = max(lineWidth, 0)
        let shape = RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: max(cornerRadius, 0), style: .continuous)

        return MeshGradient(
            width: IntelligenceGlowBorderMath.side,
            height: IntelligenceGlowBorderMath.side,
            points: IntelligenceGlowBorderMath.points(phase: phase),
            colors: meshColors(phase: phase)
        )
        .mask {
            // A crisp line at the edge, and two wider and softer ones that carry the light inward.
            ZStack {
                shape.strokeBorder(lineWidth: width)
                shape.strokeBorder(lineWidth: width * 3).blur(radius: width * 2)
                shape.strokeBorder(lineWidth: width * 7).blur(radius: width * 5).opacity(0.7)
            }
        }
        // The blur also spreads outward, where the view's square frame would cut it in a straight line.
        .clipShape(shape)
    }

    /// The palette laid around the border, moved on by `phase`.
    private func meshColors(phase: Double) -> [Color] {
        let palette = colors.isEmpty ? [Color.accentColor] : colors
        let perimeter = IntelligenceGlowBorderMath.perimeter
        var mesh = Array(repeating: palette[0], count: IntelligenceGlowBorderMath.side * IntelligenceGlowBorderMath.side)

        for (step, index) in perimeter.enumerated() {
            let position = Double(step) / Double(perimeter.count) - phase
            let blend = IntelligenceGlowBorderMath.blend(at: position, count: palette.count)
            mesh[index] = palette[blend.lower].mix(with: palette[blend.upper], by: blend.fraction)
        }
        return mesh
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Draws a moving glow around this view's edge while `isActive` is true. Match `cornerRadius` to the view's shape.
    func intelligenceGlowBorder(isActive: Bool = true, cornerRadius: CGFloat = 28, lineWidth: CGFloat = 3) -> some View {
        modifier(IntelligenceGlowBorder(isActive: isActive, cornerRadius: cornerRadius, lineWidth: lineWidth))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct IntelligenceGlowBorderDemo: View {
    @State private var isListening = true

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 28) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 14) {
                Label(isListening ? "Listening" : "Ask anything", systemImage: "sparkles")
                    .font(.headline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.7))

                Text("Plan a weekend in Lisbon with two museums and somewhere good for dinner.")
                    .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
            }
            .padding(24)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            .background(.white.opacity(0.08), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 32, style: .continuous))
            .intelligenceGlowBorder(isActive: isListening, cornerRadius: 32)

            Button(isListening ? "Stop" : "Start listening", systemImage: isListening ? "stop.fill" : "mic.fill") {
                isListening.toggle()
            }
            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
            .tint(.white.opacity(0.18))
            .controlSize(.large)
        }
        .padding(24)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(red: 0.04, green: 0.04, blue: 0.09).ignoresSafeArea())
    }
}

#Preview {
    IntelligenceGlowBorderDemo()
}
```

## Jiggle Edit Modifier

A view modifier that makes views wobble slightly, like app icons in edit mode.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/JiggleEditModifier/JiggleEditModifier.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

extension View {
    /// Wobbles the view, like an app icon in edit mode.
    ///
    /// Give each view a different `seed` so they do not move in step.
    func jiggleEditing(_ isActive: Bool, amplitude: Double = 2.4, seed: Int = 0) -> some View {
        modifier(JiggleEditModifier(isActive: isActive, amplitude: amplitude, seed: seed))
    }
}

/// With Reduce Motion on, the view stays still.
struct JiggleEditModifier: ViewModifier {
    var isActive: Bool
    var amplitude: Double
    var seed: Int

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var isJiggling: Bool { isActive && !reduceMotion }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 60.0, paused: !isJiggling)) { context in
            let phase = context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * 22 + Double(seed) * 2.4

            content
                .rotationEffect(.degrees(isJiggling ? sin(phase) * amplitude : 0))
                .offset(y: isJiggling ? cos(phase * 0.9) * 0.6 : 0)
                .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.2), value: isJiggling)
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct JiggleEditDemoApp: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let systemImage: String
    let colors: [Color]
}

struct JiggleEditModifierDemo: View {
    private static let allApps = [
        JiggleEditDemoApp(id: "Mail", systemImage: "envelope.fill", colors: [.cyan, .blue]),
        JiggleEditDemoApp(id: "Music", systemImage: "music.note", colors: [.pink, .red]),
        JiggleEditDemoApp(id: "Photos", systemImage: "camera.macro", colors: [.yellow, .orange]),
        JiggleEditDemoApp(id: "Maps", systemImage: "map.fill", colors: [.mint, .green]),
        JiggleEditDemoApp(id: "Notes", systemImage: "note.text", colors: [.yellow, .brown]),
        JiggleEditDemoApp(id: "Clock", systemImage: "clock.fill", colors: [.gray, .black]),
        JiggleEditDemoApp(id: "Health", systemImage: "heart.fill", colors: [.red, .pink]),
        JiggleEditDemoApp(id: "Files", systemImage: "folder.fill", colors: [.blue, .indigo]),
        JiggleEditDemoApp(id: "Books", systemImage: "book.fill", colors: [.orange, .red]),
        JiggleEditDemoApp(id: "Wallet", systemImage: "wallet.pass.fill", colors: [.indigo, .black]),
        JiggleEditDemoApp(id: "Home", systemImage: "house.fill", colors: [.orange, .yellow]),
        JiggleEditDemoApp(id: "Weather", systemImage: "cloud.sun.fill", colors: [.teal, .blue]),
    ]

    @State private var apps = Self.allApps
    @State private var isEditing = true
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) private var iconSize = 66.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var columns: [GridItem] { [GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: iconSize + 10), spacing: 16)] }
    private var animation: Animation? { reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack(alignment: .top) {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            ScrollView {
                VStack(spacing: 28) {
                    HStack {
                        Button {
                            withAnimation(animation) { apps = Self.allApps }
                        } label: {
                            touchTarget(Text("Reset"))
                        }
                        Spacer()
                        Button {
                            isEditing.toggle()
                        } label: {
                            touchTarget(Text(isEditing ? "Done" : "Edit"))
                        }
                        .fontWeight(.bold)
                    }
                    .font(.headline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)

                    LazyVGrid(columns: columns, spacing: 24) {
                        ForEach(Array(apps.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, app in
                            icon(for: app)
                                .jiggleEditing(isEditing, seed: index)
                        }
                    }
                }
                .padding(20)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Widens what answers to a touch around something small, without moving the layout.
    private func touchTarget(_ content: some View) -> some View {
        content
            .padding(12)
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .padding(-12)
    }

    private func icon(for app: JiggleEditDemoApp) -> some View {
        VStack(spacing: 6) {
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: iconSize * 0.23, style: .continuous)
                .fill(LinearGradient(colors: app.colors, startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
                .frame(width: iconSize, height: iconSize)
                .overlay {
                    Image(systemName: app.systemImage)
                        .font(.title)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
                .overlay(alignment: .topLeading) {
                    if isEditing {
                        Button {
                            withAnimation(animation) { apps.removeAll { $0.id == app.id } }
                        } label: {
                            touchTarget(
                                Image(systemName: "minus.circle.fill")
                                    .font(.title3)
                                    .symbolRenderingMode(.palette)
                                    .foregroundStyle(.white, .black.opacity(0.7))
                            )
                        }
                        .accessibilityLabel("Remove \(app.id)")
                        .offset(x: -8, y: -8)
                    }
                }

            Text(app.id)
                .font(.caption)
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .lineLimit(1)
        }
    }
}
```

## Metaball Lava Lamp

Round blobs that merge and separate like a lava lamp, drawn with a blur and alpha threshold on a Canvas.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/MetaballLavaLamp/MetaballLavaLamp.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Round blobs that merge and separate like a lava lamp.
///
/// The blobs are blurred and then cut at half their opacity, so two blobs that
/// touch join with a smooth neck. With Reduce Motion on, it shows a still frame.
struct MetaballLavaLamp: View {
    var blobCount = 7
    var colors: [Color] = [.red, .orange, .yellow]
    var speed = 1.0

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        LinearGradient(colors: colors.isEmpty ? [.orange] : colors, startPoint: .bottom, endPoint: .top)
            .mask {
                TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
                    let time = reduceMotion ? 12 : context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * max(speed, 0)

                    Canvas { canvas, size in
                        let side = min(size.width, size.height)
                        guard side > 0 else { return }

                        canvas.addFilter(.alphaThreshold(min: 0.5, color: .white))
                        canvas.addFilter(.blur(radius: max(1, side * 0.05)))
                        canvas.drawLayer { layer in
                            for blob in MetaballLavaLampMath.blobs(count: blobCount, time: time, size: size) {
                                layer.fill(Path(ellipseIn: blob), with: .color(.white))
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

enum MetaballLavaLampMath {
    /// The frames of the rising blobs, plus a pool of wax at the top and at the bottom.
    static func blobs(count: Int, time: Double, size: CGSize) -> [CGRect] {
        guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0 else { return [] }
        let width = size.width
        let height = size.height

        var frames = [
            CGRect(x: -width * 0.1, y: height * 0.9, width: width * 1.2, height: height * 0.25),
            CGRect(x: -width * 0.1, y: -height * 0.17, width: width * 1.2, height: height * 0.25),
        ]

        for index in 0..<min(max(count, 0), 48) {
            let seed = Double(index)
            let radius = width * (0.1 + 0.09 * unit(seed * 0.618 + 0.2))
            let rate = 0.28 + 0.2 * unit(seed * 0.37 + 0.5)
            let x = width * (0.5 + 0.32 * sin(time * 0.21 + seed * 1.7))
            let y = height * (0.5 + 0.47 * sin(time * rate + seed * 2.4))
            frames.append(CGRect(x: x - radius, y: y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2))
        }
        return frames
    }

    /// A smooth value from 0 to 1 that differs from one blob to the next.
    private static func unit(_ value: Double) -> Double {
        (sin(value * 12.9) + 1) / 2
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct MetaballLavaLampDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [Color(red: 0.22, green: 0.03, blue: 0.3), Color(red: 0.07, green: 0.02, blue: 0.16)],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )

            MetaballLavaLamp(blobCount: 9, colors: [.red, .orange, .pink], speed: 1.6)
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    }
}

#Preview {
    MetaballLavaLampDemo()
}
```

## Noise Grain Overlay

A view modifier that lays a subtle animated film grain over any view.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/NoiseGrainOverlay/NoiseGrainOverlay.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A subtle film grain over any view: tiny light and dark specks redrawn a few times a second.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the grain is still.
struct NoiseGrainOverlay: ViewModifier {
    var intensity: Double = 0.16
    var grainSize: Double = 1.25
    var framesPerSecond: Double = 12

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// A tiny seeded generator: the same frame number always gives the same grain.
    private struct Generator: RandomNumberGenerator {
        var state: UInt64

        mutating func next() -> UInt64 {
            state ^= state << 13
            state ^= state >> 7
            state ^= state << 17
            return state
        }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.overlay {
            TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1 / framesPerSecond, paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
                Canvas { context, size in
                    let frame = reduceMotion ? 0 : UInt64(timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * framesPerSecond)
                    drawGrain(frame: frame, in: context, size: size)
                }
            }
            .allowsHitTesting(false)
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
    }

    /// Every speck goes into one of two paths, so a frame is only two fills.
    private func drawGrain(frame: UInt64, in context: GraphicsContext, size: CGSize) {
        var generator = Generator(state: (frame &+ 1) &* 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)
        var light = Path()
        var dark = Path()

        for index in 0..<min(Int(size.width * size.height / 18), 20_000) {
            let speck = CGRect(
                x: Double.random(in: 0..<max(size.width, 1), using: &generator),
                y: Double.random(in: 0..<max(size.height, 1), using: &generator),
                width: grainSize,
                height: grainSize
            )
            if index.isMultiple(of: 2) {
                light.addRect(speck)
            } else {
                dark.addRect(speck)
            }
        }

        context.fill(light, with: .color(.white.opacity(intensity)))
        context.fill(dark, with: .color(.black.opacity(intensity)))
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Adds a subtle animated film grain on top of this view.
    func noiseGrainOverlay(intensity: Double = 0.16, grainSize: Double = 1.25) -> some View {
        modifier(NoiseGrainOverlay(intensity: intensity, grainSize: grainSize))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct NoiseGrainOverlayDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink, .indigo], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
```

## Pixelate Shader Effect

A view modifier that draws a view in big square blocks, like a spoiler, and brings it into focus as they shrink, drawn by a Metal shader.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/PixelateShaderEffect/PixelateShaderEffect.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum PixelateShaderEffectMath {
    /// The side of the blocks for an amount of pixelation: one point, which changes nothing, at
    /// 0, and `maximum` at 1.
    static func blockSize(amount: Double, maximum: Double) -> Double {
        guard amount.isFinite else { return 1 }
        return 1 + (max(maximum, 1) - 1) * min(max(amount, 0), 1)
    }

    /// The center of the block a point falls in, which gives its color to the whole block.
    /// The shader does the same sum.
    static func blockCenter(of point: CGPoint, size: Double) -> CGPoint {
        guard size > 1 else { return point }
        return CGPoint(x: ((point.x / size).rounded(.down) + 0.5) * size, y: ((point.y / size).rounded(.down) + 0.5) * size)
    }

    /// The function in `PixelateShaderEffect.metal`, with its arguments in the order it declares them.
    static func shader(size: Double, bounds: CGSize) -> Shader {
        ShaderLibrary.PixelateShaderEffectBlocks(.float(size), .float2(bounds))
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Draws this view in big square blocks, like a censored picture, by a Metal shader.
    /// `amount` goes from 0, untouched, to 1, in blocks of `blockSize` points, and animates:
    /// the blocks shrink until the view comes into focus.
    ///
    /// Copy two files into the same target: `PixelateShaderEffect.swift` and `PixelateShaderEffect.metal`.
    /// A shader draws what SwiftUI draws itself: a view backed by UIKit, such as a map, shows a placeholder.
    ///
    /// It only changes how the view looks: hide it from VoiceOver yourself while it is a secret.
    /// With Reduce Motion on, the view goes from blocks to sharp in one step.
    func pixelate(_ amount: Double, blockSize: CGFloat = 22) -> some View {
        modifier(PixelateShaderEffectModifier(amount: amount, blockSize: blockSize))
    }
}

/// `Animatable`, so the shader gets every step of the change: a shader's arguments do not animate by themselves.
private struct PixelateShaderEffectModifier: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var amount: Double
    let blockSize: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    nonisolated var animatableData: Double {
        get { amount }
        set { amount = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // With Reduce Motion the blocks do not shrink step by step: they are there or they are not.
        let shown = reduceMotion ? (amount > 0.5 ? 1 : 0) : amount
        let size = PixelateShaderEffectMath.blockSize(amount: shown, maximum: blockSize)

        content
            // `visualEffect` gives the shader the size of the view, which it needs at the edges.
            .visualEffect { view, proxy in
                view.layerEffect(
                    PixelateShaderEffectMath.shader(size: size, bounds: proxy.size),
                    maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: size, height: size),
                    isEnabled: size > 1
                )
            }
            // The first use of a shader waits for it to compile. Doing that now keeps the first frames smooth.
            .task {
                try? await PixelateShaderEffectMath.shader(size: blockSize, bounds: .zero).compile(as: .layerEffect)
            }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct PixelateShaderEffectDemo: View {
    @State private var isHidden = true

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 24) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10) {
                ZStack {
                    LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple, .orange], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                    Image(systemName: "trophy.fill")
                        .font(.system(size: 84))
                        .foregroundStyle(.yellow.gradient)
                        .shadow(radius: 8)
                }
                .frame(height: 220)
                .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 18))

                Text("Season finale")
                    .font(.title2.bold())
                Text("Rivera wins the final in the last minute, after trailing for the whole second half.")
                    .font(.body)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
            .padding(16)
            .background(.background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 26))
            .pixelate(isHidden ? 1 : 0)
            .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
            .accessibilityHidden(isHidden)

            Button(isHidden ? "Reveal Spoiler" : "Hide Again", systemImage: isHidden ? "eye.fill" : "eye.slash.fill") {
                withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.8)) { isHidden.toggle() }
            }
            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
            .controlSize(.large)
        }
        .padding(20)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground))
    }
}
```
