Shader: Components/Effects/PixelateShaderEffect/PixelateShaderEffect.metal

```metal
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>

using namespace metal;

// For SwiftUI's `layerEffect`. Draws the view in square blocks of `size`
// points, each one in the color of the point at its center. A block that
// sticks out of the view, which is `bounds` in size, takes the color of the
// last point inside, so the edges are not cut. A size of one point or less
// leaves the view as it is.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 PixelateShaderEffectBlocks(
    float2 position,
    SwiftUI::Layer layer,
    float size,
    float2 bounds
) {
    if (size <= 1.0) {
        return layer.sample(position);
    }
    float2 center = (floor(position / size) + 0.5) * size;
    return layer.sample(min(center, bounds - 0.5));
}
```

## Progressive Blur Header

A blur that grows toward the top edge of a scroll view, drawn by a Metal shader, so what scrolls under a header melts away.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/ProgressiveBlurHeader/ProgressiveBlurHeader.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum ProgressiveBlurHeaderMath {
    /// How much of the blur a point gets at a distance from the top edge: all of it at the edge
    /// and none from `height` down, along the same smooth curve the shader uses.
    static func strength(at distance: Double, height: Double) -> Double {
        guard height > 0, distance.isFinite else { return 0 }
        let share = min(max(distance / height, 0), 1)
        return 1 - share * share * (3 - 2 * share)
    }

    /// The function in `ProgressiveBlurHeader.metal`, with its arguments in the order it declares them.
    static func shader(top: Double, height: Double, radius: Double, isHorizontal: Bool) -> Shader {
        ShaderLibrary.ProgressiveBlurHeaderPass(
            .float(top),
            .float(max(height, 0)),
            .float(max(radius, 0)),
            .float2(isHorizontal ? 1 : 0, isHorizontal ? 0 : 1)
        )
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Blurs this view more and more toward the top edge of the scroll view it is in, drawn by a
    /// Metal shader, so what scrolls under a header melts away instead of meeting a hard bar.
    /// Put it on the content of a `ScrollView`, not on the scroll view.
    ///
    /// Copy two files into the same target: `ProgressiveBlurHeader.swift` and `ProgressiveBlurHeader.metal`.
    /// A shader draws what SwiftUI draws itself: a view backed by UIKit, such as a map or the
    /// scroll view itself, comes out empty.
    ///
    /// With Reduce Transparency on, the content is left sharp.
    func progressiveBlurHeader(height: CGFloat = 130, radius: CGFloat = 14) -> some View {
        modifier(ProgressiveBlurHeaderModifier(height: height, radius: radius))
    }
}

private struct ProgressiveBlurHeaderModifier: ViewModifier {
    let height: CGFloat
    let radius: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceTransparency) private var reduceTransparency

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            // `visualEffect` knows where the content is in the scroll view on every frame, with no state to update.
            .visualEffect { [height, radius, reduceTransparency] view, proxy in
                // The line of the content that sits at the top edge of the scroll view.
                let top = -proxy.frame(in: .scrollView(axis: .vertical)).minY

                return view
                    .layerEffect(
                        ProgressiveBlurHeaderMath.shader(top: top, height: height, radius: radius, isHorizontal: true),
                        maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: radius, height: 0),
                        isEnabled: !reduceTransparency
                    )
                    .layerEffect(
                        ProgressiveBlurHeaderMath.shader(top: top, height: height, radius: radius, isHorizontal: false),
                        maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: 0, height: radius),
                        isEnabled: !reduceTransparency
                    )
            }
            // The first use of a shader waits for it to compile. Doing that now keeps the first frames smooth.
            .task {
                try? await ProgressiveBlurHeaderMath.shader(top: 0, height: height, radius: radius, isHorizontal: true).compile(as: .layerEffect)
            }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ProgressiveBlurHeaderDemo: View {
    private let entries: [(title: String, text: String, colors: [Color])] = [
        ("Morning Light", "The harbor before the boats go out.", [.orange, .pink]),
        ("Slow Roads", "Three days with no highway in sight.", [.teal, .blue]),
        ("Market Day", "Peaches, noise and a very loud rooster.", [.yellow, .orange]),
        ("High Tide", "A beach that is only there at noon.", [.cyan, .indigo]),
        ("Old Stones", "A wall that outlived the town it kept.", [.gray, .brown]),
        ("Night Train", "Twelve hours, one window, no hurry.", [.indigo, .purple]),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            LazyVStack(spacing: 16) {
                ForEach(entries, id: \.title) { entry in
                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
                        Spacer()
                        Text(entry.title)
                            .font(.title2.bold())
                        Text(entry.text)
                            .font(.subheadline)
                    }
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    .padding(18)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: 170, alignment: .leading)
                    .background(LinearGradient(colors: entry.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 22))
                    .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
                }
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 16)
            .padding(.top, 130)
            .progressiveBlurHeader()
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea(edges: .top)
        .overlay(alignment: .top) {
            HStack {
                Text("Journal")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                Spacer()
                Image(systemName: "square.and.pencil")
                    .font(.title2)
                    .accessibilityLabel("New entry")
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 20)
            .padding(.top, 4)
            .padding(.bottom, 44)
            .background {
                // A veil over the blur keeps the title readable whatever scrolls under it.
                LinearGradient(colors: [Color(.systemBackground).opacity(0.9), Color(.systemBackground).opacity(0)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                    .ignoresSafeArea(edges: .top)
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
            }
        }
        .background(Color(.systemBackground))
    }
```

Shader: Components/Effects/ProgressiveBlurHeader/ProgressiveBlurHeader.metal

```metal
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>

using namespace metal;

// For SwiftUI's `layerEffect`. Blurs along `direction` with a reach that is
// `radius` at `top`, the line where the header starts, and falls smoothly to
// nothing `height` points below it. One pass across and one pass down make
// the whole blur, with far fewer samples than doing both at once.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 ProgressiveBlurHeaderPass(
    float2 position,
    SwiftUI::Layer layer,
    float top,
    float height,
    float radius,
    float2 direction
) {
    float reach = radius * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, height, position.y - top));
    if (reach < 0.5) {
        return layer.sample(position);
    }

    // Samples spread over the reach, weighted like a bell so the middle counts most.
    const int steps = 8;
    half4 total = half4(0.0);
    float weights = 0.0;
    for (int step = -steps; step <= steps; step++) {
        float offset = float(step) / float(steps);
        float weight = exp(-2.0 * offset * offset);
        total += layer.sample(position + direction * offset * reach) * half(weight);
        weights += weight;
    }
    return total / half(weights);
}
```

## Ripple Shader Effect

A view modifier that sends a wave from the tapped point and bends the view as it passes, drawn by a Metal shader.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/RippleShaderEffect/RippleShaderEffect.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Where a wave is at one instant: how far its crest has travelled and how strong it still is.
nonisolated struct RippleShaderEffectWave: Equatable {
    var radius = 0.0
    var strength = 0.0

    /// The same wave held at its origin. With no bending either, all it leaves is a light that fades.
    var still: RippleShaderEffectWave {
        RippleShaderEffectWave(radius: 0, strength: strength)
    }
}

nonisolated enum RippleShaderEffectMath {
    /// How far a wave from `origin` travels until all of it has left a view of `size`.
    static func reach(from origin: CGPoint, in size: CGSize, wavelength: Double) -> Double {
        let horizontal = max(abs(origin.x), abs(size.width - origin.x))
        let vertical = max(abs(origin.y), abs(size.height - origin.y))
        return hypot(horizontal, vertical) + max(wavelength, 0)
    }

    /// The seconds a wave takes to cover `reach` points. A wave that cannot move lasts one frame.
    static func travelTime(reach: Double, speed: Double) -> Double {
        let frame = 1.0 / 60.0
        guard speed > 0, reach.isFinite else { return frame }
        return max(reach / speed, frame)
    }

    /// The function in `RippleShaderEffect.metal`, with its arguments in the order it declares them.
    static func shader(wave: RippleShaderEffectWave, origin: CGPoint, amplitude: Double, wavelength: Double) -> Shader {
        ShaderLibrary.RippleShaderEffectDistortion(
            .boundingRect,
            .float2(origin),
            .float(wave.radius),
            .float(wave.strength),
            .float(amplitude),
            .float(max(wavelength, 1))
        )
    }
}

/// A wave that spreads from a point and bends the view as it passes, drawn by a Metal shader.
///
/// Copy two files into the same target: `RippleShaderEffect.swift` and `RippleShaderEffect.metal`.
/// `.rippleShaderEffect()` starts a wave wherever the view is tapped, and
/// `.rippleShaderEffect(at:trigger:)` starts one from code.
/// A shader draws what SwiftUI draws itself: a view backed by UIKit, such as a map, shows a placeholder.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, a soft light fades where the wave would start, and nothing moves.
struct RippleShaderEffect<Trigger: Equatable & Sendable>: ViewModifier {
    /// Where the wave starts, in the view's own coordinates.
    var origin: CGPoint
    var trigger: Trigger
    /// How many points the wave moves what is under it.
    var amplitude: Double = 10
    /// The width of the wave, in points.
    var wavelength: Double = 110
    /// Points per second.
    var speed: Double = 650

    @State private var size = CGSize.zero
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let origin = origin
        let amplitude = amplitude
        let wavelength = wavelength
        let reduceMotion = reduceMotion
        let reach = RippleShaderEffectMath.reach(from: origin, in: size, wavelength: wavelength)
        let travel = RippleShaderEffectMath.travelTime(reach: reach, speed: speed)

        content
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self) { $0.size } action: { size = $0 }
            .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: RippleShaderEffectWave(), trigger: trigger) { view, wave in
                view.layerEffect(
                    RippleShaderEffectMath.shader(
                        wave: reduceMotion ? wave.still : wave,
                        origin: origin,
                        amplitude: reduceMotion ? 0 : amplitude,
                        wavelength: wavelength
                    ),
                    maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: abs(amplitude), height: abs(amplitude)),
                    isEnabled: wave.strength > 0
                )
            } keyframes: { _ in
                KeyframeTrack(\.radius) {
                    MoveKeyframe(0)
                    LinearKeyframe(reach, duration: travel)
                }
                KeyframeTrack(\.strength) {
                    MoveKeyframe(1)
                    LinearKeyframe(1, duration: travel * 0.35)
                    CubicKeyframe(0, duration: travel * 0.65)
                }
            }
            // The first use of a shader waits for it to compile. Doing that now keeps the first wave on time.
            .task {
                let shader = RippleShaderEffectMath.shader(wave: RippleShaderEffectWave(), origin: .zero, amplitude: 0, wavelength: 1)
                try? await shader.compile(as: .layerEffect)
            }
    }
}

private struct RippleShaderEffectOnTap: ViewModifier {
    let amplitude: Double
    let wavelength: Double
    let speed: Double

    @State private var origin = CGPoint.zero
    @State private var taps = 0

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .modifier(RippleShaderEffect(origin: origin, trigger: taps, amplitude: amplitude, wavelength: wavelength, speed: speed))
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .simultaneousGesture(
                SpatialTapGesture().onEnded { tap in
                    origin = tap.location
                    taps += 1
                }
            )
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Starts a wave wherever this view is tapped, without blocking its own controls.
    func rippleShaderEffect(amplitude: Double = 10, wavelength: Double = 110, speed: Double = 650) -> some View {
        modifier(RippleShaderEffectOnTap(amplitude: amplitude, wavelength: wavelength, speed: speed))
    }

    /// Starts a wave at `origin`, in this view's own coordinates, every time `trigger` changes.
    func rippleShaderEffect(
        at origin: CGPoint,
        trigger: some Equatable & Sendable,
        amplitude: Double = 10,
        wavelength: Double = 110,
        speed: Double = 650
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(RippleShaderEffect(origin: origin, trigger: trigger, amplitude: amplitude, wavelength: wavelength, speed: speed))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct RippleShaderEffectDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            RippleShaderEffectDemoTiles()

            VStack(spacing: 10) {
                Image(systemName: "drop.fill")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                Text("Tap the Water")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.35), radius: 8, y: 4)
        }
        .rippleShaderEffect()
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    }
}

/// The floor of a pool: a grid whose straight lines show how the wave bends them.
private struct RippleShaderEffectDemoTiles: View {
    var body: some View {
        Canvas { context, size in
            let side = 46.0
            let columns = Int((size.width / side).rounded(.up))
            let rows = Int((size.height / side).rounded(.up))

            for row in 0..<rows {
                for column in 0..<columns {
                    let tile = CGRect(x: Double(column) * side, y: Double(row) * side, width: side, height: side)
                    let shade = Double((row * 7 + column * 13) % 5) / 4
                    let color = Color(hue: 0.52 + 0.03 * shade, saturation: 0.7, brightness: 0.72 + 0.2 * shade)
                    context.fill(Path(roundedRect: tile.insetBy(dx: 2, dy: 2), cornerRadius: 6), with: .color(color))
                }
            }
        }
        .background(Color(hue: 0.56, saturation: 0.8, brightness: 0.42))
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}
```

Shader: Components/Effects/RippleShaderEffect/RippleShaderEffect.metal

```metal
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>

using namespace metal;

// For SwiftUI's `layerEffect`. Bends the layer where a ring of `radius` points
// around `origin` passes, and lights the crest of that wave. `strength` fades
// the whole wave from 1 to 0, and `bounds` is the frame of the layer.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 RippleShaderEffectDistortion(
    float2 position,
    SwiftUI::Layer layer,
    float4 bounds,
    float2 origin,
    float radius,
    float strength,
    float amplitude,
    float wavelength
) {
    float2 offset = position - origin;
    float fromOrigin = length(offset);
    float2 outward = fromOrigin > 0.0 ? offset / fromOrigin : float2(0.0);

    // How far this pixel is from the crest, in wavelengths. The wave is one
    // crest between two shallow troughs, and the layer is flat everywhere else.
    float phase = (fromOrigin - radius) / wavelength;
    float window = exp(-4.0 * phase * phase) * strength;
    float height = cos(6.2831853 * phase) * window;
    float slope = sin(6.2831853 * phase) * window;

    // Water refracts along its slope. Sampling a little toward the crest
    // magnifies what lies under it, as a ridge of water does. Staying a point
    // inside the layer keeps the wave from pulling in the emptiness around it.
    float2 source = position - outward * slope * amplitude;
    half4 color = layer.sample(clamp(source, bounds.xy + 1.0, bounds.xy + bounds.zw - 1.0));

    // Light the crest and shade the troughs. Colors come premultiplied by their alpha.
    color.rgb = max(color.rgb + half3(0.12 * height) * color.a, half3(0.0));
    return color;
}
```

## Ripple Tap Effect

A view modifier that spawns an expanding ripple wherever the user taps.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/RippleTapEffect/RippleTapEffect.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Spawns an expanding ripple wherever the user taps, without blocking the view's own controls.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, a ripple fades in place instead of expanding.
struct RippleTapEffect: ViewModifier {
    var color: Color = .white
    var maxRadius: Double = 170
    var duration: Double = 0.9
    var cornerRadius: Double = 0

    private struct Ripple: Identifiable {
        let id = UUID()
        let location: CGPoint
        let start: Date
    }

    @State private var ripples: [Ripple] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                TimelineView(.animation(paused: ripples.isEmpty)) { timeline in
                    Canvas { context, _ in
                        for ripple in ripples {
                            draw(ripple, at: timeline.date, in: context)
                        }
                    }
                }
                .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .contentShape(.rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
            .simultaneousGesture(SpatialTapGesture().onEnded { spawn(at: $0.location) })
    }

    private func spawn(at location: CGPoint) {
        let ripple = Ripple(location: location, start: .now)
        ripples.append(ripple)

        Task {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(duration))
            ripples.removeAll { $0.id == ripple.id }
        }
    }

    private func draw(_ ripple: Ripple, at date: Date, in context: GraphicsContext) {
        let progress = min(max(date.timeIntervalSince(ripple.start) / duration, 0), 1)
        let eased = 1 - pow(1 - progress, 3)
        let fade = 1 - progress

        for (scale, width) in [(1.0, 2.5), (0.62, 1.5)] {
            let radius = (reduceMotion ? 0.45 : eased) * maxRadius * scale
            let circle = Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(
                x: ripple.location.x - radius,
                y: ripple.location.y - radius,
                width: radius * 2,
                height: radius * 2
            ))
            context.fill(circle, with: .color(color.opacity(0.1 * fade)))
            context.stroke(circle, with: .color(color.opacity(0.75 * fade)), lineWidth: width)
        }
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Spawns a ripple at every tap on this view.
    func rippleTapEffect(color: Color = .white, maxRadius: Double = 170, cornerRadius: Double = 0) -> some View {
        modifier(RippleTapEffect(color: color, maxRadius: maxRadius, cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct RippleTapEffectDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [.teal, .blue, Color(red: 0.14, green: 0.1, blue: 0.45)],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )

            VStack(spacing: 10) {
                Image(systemName: "hand.tap.fill")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                Text("Tap Anywhere")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
        .rippleTapEffect()
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    }
}
```

## Spotlight Overlay

A dark overlay with a soft hole that follows the finger.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/SpotlightOverlay/SpotlightOverlay.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A dark overlay with a soft hole that follows the finger.
///
/// The hole only moves with the finger, so it needs no change for Reduce Motion.
struct SpotlightOverlay: ViewModifier {
    /// The center of the hole, as a fraction of the view.
    @Binding var center: UnitPoint
    var radius: Double = 130
    /// How much of the radius is the soft edge, from 0 to 1.
    var softness: Double = 0.55
    var dimming: Color = .black.opacity(0.88)

    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.overlay {
            GeometryReader { proxy in
                // Past its end radius the gradient keeps its last color, so one fill is both the hole and the dark.
                Rectangle()
                    .fill(RadialGradient(
                        stops: [
                            .init(color: dimming.opacity(0), location: 1 - softness),
                            .init(color: dimming, location: 1),
                        ],
                        center: center,
                        startRadius: 0,
                        endRadius: radius
                    ))
                    .contentShape(.rect)
                    .gesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { value in
                        // Gestures report screen points, but a unit point counts from the leading edge.
                        let x = value.location.x / max(proxy.size.width, 1)
                        center = UnitPoint(
                            x: layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? 1 - x : x,
                            y: value.location.y / max(proxy.size.height, 1)
                        )
                    })
            }
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Darkens this view except for a soft hole at `center`, which follows the finger.
    func spotlightOverlay(
        center: Binding<UnitPoint>,
        radius: Double = 130,
        softness: Double = 0.55,
        dimming: Color = .black.opacity(0.88)
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(SpotlightOverlay(center: center, radius: radius, softness: softness, dimming: dimming))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SpotlightOverlayDemo: View {
    @State private var center = UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 0.45)
    @State private var isAutoPlaying = true
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let symbols = [
        "star.fill", "heart.fill", "bolt.fill", "leaf.fill", "flame.fill", "drop.fill", "moon.fill",
        "sun.max.fill", "cloud.fill", "snowflake", "key.fill", "crown.fill", "gift.fill", "bell.fill",
        "camera.fill", "music.note", "paperplane.fill", "globe.americas.fill", "pawprint.fill", "fish.fill",
        "tortoise.fill", "hare.fill", "ladybug.fill", "ant.fill", "sparkles", "diamond.fill", "gamecontroller.fill",
        "airplane",
    ]
    private let palette: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .yellow, .mint, .teal, .blue, .purple]

    /// Lets a finger take over from the automatic movement.
    private var touchCenter: Binding<UnitPoint> {
        Binding(
            get: { center },
            set: { newValue in
                isAutoPlaying = false
                center = newValue
            }
        )
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Color(red: 0.08, green: 0.08, blue: 0.16)

            LazyVGrid(columns: Array(repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: 12), count: 4), spacing: 12) {
                ForEach(symbols.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 18)
                        .fill(palette[index % palette.count].gradient)
                        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
                        .overlay {
                            Image(systemName: symbols[index])
                                .font(.title)
                                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        }
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 16)
        }
        .spotlightOverlay(center: touchCenter)
        .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
            Text("Drag to explore")
                .font(.headline)
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .padding(.bottom, 44)
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
        .task(id: reduceMotion) { await autoPlay() }
    }

    /// Only the demo moves the hole by itself, until the first touch.
    private func autoPlay() async {
        guard !reduceMotion else { return }

        let start = Date.now
        while isAutoPlaying, !Task.isCancelled {
            let time = Date.now.timeIntervalSince(start)
            center = UnitPoint(x: 0.5 + 0.3 * sin(time * 1.7), y: 0.45 + 0.27 * sin(time * 1.1 + 0.6))
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(16))
        }
    }
}
```

## Touch Particle Trail

A trail of fading particles that follows the finger while it drags.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/TouchParticleTrail/TouchParticleTrail.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Leaves a trail of fading particles behind the finger while it drags over the content.
///
/// The content keeps receiving its own touches. With Reduce Motion on, the
/// particles stay where they were left and only fade.
struct TouchParticleTrail<Content: View>: View {
    var colors: [Color] = [.cyan, .purple, .pink]
    var lifetime = 0.9
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @State private var emitter = TouchParticleTrailEmitter()
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .overlay {
                TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 60.0, paused: emitter.particles.isEmpty)) { context in
                    Canvas { canvas, _ in
                        canvas.blendMode = .plusLighter
                        let palette = colors.isEmpty ? [Color.white] : colors
                        for particle in emitter.particles {
                            guard let frame = particle.frame(at: context.date) else { continue }
                            let color = palette[particle.colorIndex % palette.count]
                            let glow = frame.rect.insetBy(dx: -frame.rect.width * 0.8, dy: -frame.rect.height * 0.8)
                            canvas.fill(Path(ellipseIn: glow), with: .color(color.opacity(frame.opacity * 0.25)))
                            canvas.fill(Path(ellipseIn: frame.rect), with: .color(color.opacity(frame.opacity)))
                        }
                    }
                    .onChange(of: context.date) { _, now in
                        if emitter.isFinished(at: now) { emitter.removeAll() }
                    }
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .simultaneousGesture(
                DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
                    .onChanged { value in
                        emitter.emit(at: value.location, now: .now, lifetime: lifetime, drifts: !reduceMotion)
                    }
                    .onEnded { _ in emitter.endStroke() }
            )
    }
}

struct TouchParticleTrailParticle {
    var position: CGPoint
    var velocity: CGVector
    var birth: Date
    var lifetime: Double
    var size: CGFloat
    var colorIndex: Int

    struct Frame {
        var rect: CGRect
        var opacity: Double
    }

    func isExpired(at now: Date) -> Bool {
        now.timeIntervalSince(birth) >= lifetime
    }

    /// Where the particle is drawn at a given moment, or `nil` once it has faded out.
    func frame(at now: Date) -> Frame? {
        let age = now.timeIntervalSince(birth)
        guard age >= 0, age < lifetime, lifetime > 0 else { return nil }

        let progress = age / lifetime
        let side = size * (1 - progress * 0.6)
        return Frame(
            rect: CGRect(
                x: position.x + velocity.dx * age - side / 2,
                y: position.y + velocity.dy * age - side / 2,
                width: side,
                height: side
            ),
            opacity: 1 - progress
        )
    }
}

struct TouchParticleTrailEmitter {
    private(set) var particles: [TouchParticleTrailParticle] = []
    private var lastPoint: CGPoint?
    private var lastEmission: Date?

    private let capacity = 240
    private let spacing: CGFloat = 9
    private let maximumPerEvent = 16
    private let strokeGap = 0.12

    /// Adds particles between the last point and this one, so a fast drag leaves no gaps.
    ///
    /// A long pause starts a new stroke. That also covers a gesture the system
    /// cancelled, which never reports its end.
    mutating func emit(at point: CGPoint, now: Date, lifetime: Double, drifts: Bool) {
        guard point.x.isFinite, point.y.isFinite else { return }
        let lifetime = max(lifetime, 0.05)
        particles.removeAll { $0.isExpired(at: now) }

        let previous = lastEmission.map { now.timeIntervalSince($0) <= strokeGap } == true ? lastPoint : nil
        lastEmission = now

        var count = 1
        if let previous {
            let distance = hypot(point.x - previous.x, point.y - previous.y)
            guard distance >= spacing else { return }
            count = Int(min(distance / spacing, CGFloat(maximumPerEvent)))
        }

        for step in 1...count {
            let progress = CGFloat(step) / CGFloat(count)
            let position = previous.map {
                CGPoint(x: $0.x + (point.x - $0.x) * progress, y: $0.y + (point.y - $0.y) * progress)
            } ?? point
            particles.append(makeParticle(at: position, now: now, lifetime: lifetime, drifts: drifts))
        }
        lastPoint = point

        if particles.count > capacity {
            particles.removeFirst(particles.count - capacity)
        }
    }

    /// Particles are in birth order and share a lifetime, so the last one is the last to go.
    func isFinished(at now: Date) -> Bool {
        particles.last?.isExpired(at: now) ?? false
    }

    /// Lifting the finger ends the stroke, so the next touch is not joined to this one.
    mutating func endStroke() {
        lastPoint = nil
        lastEmission = nil
    }

    mutating func removeAll() {
        particles.removeAll()
        lastPoint = nil
        lastEmission = nil
    }

    private func makeParticle(
        at position: CGPoint,
        now: Date,
        lifetime: Double,
        drifts: Bool
    ) -> TouchParticleTrailParticle {
        let angle = Double.random(in: 0..<(2 * .pi))
        let speed = drifts ? Double.random(in: 10...70) : 0
        return TouchParticleTrailParticle(
            position: position,
            velocity: CGVector(dx: cos(angle) * speed, dy: sin(angle) * speed),
            birth: now,
            lifetime: lifetime,
            size: .random(in: 7...15),
            colorIndex: .random(in: 0..<1_000)
        )
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct TouchParticleTrailDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        TouchParticleTrail {
            ZStack {
                LinearGradient(
                    colors: [Color(red: 0.05, green: 0.03, blue: 0.16), .black],
                    startPoint: .top,
                    endPoint: .bottom
                )

                VStack(spacing: 10) {
                    Image(systemName: "hand.draw.fill")
                        .font(.largeTitle)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                    Text("Drag anywhere")
                        .font(.title2.bold())
                }
                .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.75))
            }
            .ignoresSafeArea()
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    }
}

#Preview {
    TouchParticleTrailDemo()
}
```

## Voice Orb

A glowing orb for a voice assistant whose colors swirl and that swells with the voice while it listens or speaks.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/VoiceOrb/VoiceOrb.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum VoiceOrbState: String, CaseIterable, Sendable {
    case idle = "Idle"
    case listening = "Listening"
    case thinking = "Thinking"
    case speaking = "Speaking"
}

nonisolated enum VoiceOrbMath {
    /// How lively the orb is, from 0 to 1. At rest it barely moves, thinking keeps it halfway,
    /// and while it listens or speaks it follows the level of the voice.
    static func energy(state: VoiceOrbState, level: Double) -> Double {
        let level = level.isFinite ? min(max(level, 0), 1) : 0
        switch state {
        case .idle: return 0.1
        case .thinking: return 0.5
        case .listening, .speaking: return 0.25 + 0.75 * level
        }
    }

    /// How big the orb is drawn for an energy: it swells with the voice.
    static func scale(energy: Double) -> Double {
        0.86 + 0.14 * min(max(energy, 0), 1)
    }

    /// Where a blob of color is inside the orb, with the orb as a circle of radius 1 around zero.
    /// The blobs circle its center, every other one the opposite way, and reach further out the
    /// livelier the orb is.
    static func blobCenter(index: Int, count: Int, time: Double, energy: Double) -> CGPoint {
        let phase = Double(index) / Double(max(count, 1))
        let turns = time * (index.isMultiple(of: 2) ? 0.3 : -0.2) + phase
        let reach = 0.2 + 0.3 * min(max(energy, 0), 1)
        return CGPoint(x: cos(turns * 2 * .pi) * reach, y: sin(turns * 2 * .pi) * reach)
    }
}

/// A glowing orb for a voice assistant: colors swirl inside it, and it swells with the voice
/// while it listens or speaks.
///
/// Give it the level of the voice from 0 to 1, from your own audio code: the orb asks for no
/// microphone. With Reduce Motion on, the colors stay still and the orb brightens instead of
/// swelling.
struct VoiceOrb: View {
    var state = VoiceOrbState.idle
    /// How loud the voice is, from 0 to 1.
    var level = 0.0
    var colors: [Color] = [.blue, .purple, .pink, .cyan]
    var label = "Assistant"

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        let energy = VoiceOrbMath.energy(state: state, level: level)

        VoiceOrbSurface(energy: energy, colors: colors, isStill: reduceMotion)
            .scaleEffect(reduceMotion ? 1 : VoiceOrbMath.scale(energy: energy))
            .brightness(reduceMotion ? energy * 0.2 : 0)
            .saturation(state == .idle ? 0.6 : 1)
            .hueRotation(.degrees(state == .speaking ? 40 : 0))
            .animation(.spring(duration: 0.35), value: energy)
            .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.5), value: state)
            .accessibilityElement()
            .accessibilityLabel(label)
            .accessibilityValue(state.rawValue)
    }
}

/// The inside of the orb. Its energy is animatable, so the blobs glide to their new reach when the
/// state changes instead of jumping.
private struct VoiceOrbSurface: View, Animatable {
    var energy: Double
    let colors: [Color]
    let isStill: Bool

    nonisolated var animatableData: Double {
        get { energy }
        set { energy = newValue }
    }

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: isStill)) { timeline in
            let time = isStill ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate

            Canvas { context, size in
                let radius = min(size.width, size.height) / 2
                let center = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
                let orb = CGRect(x: center.x - radius, y: center.y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)

                context.clip(to: Path(ellipseIn: orb))
                context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: orb), with: .color(colors.first ?? .blue))

                var blurred = context
                blurred.addFilter(.blur(radius: radius * 0.28))
                for (index, color) in colors.enumerated() {
                    let unit = VoiceOrbMath.blobCenter(index: index, count: colors.count, time: time, energy: energy)
                    let blob = CGRect(x: center.x + unit.x * radius - radius * 0.6, y: center.y + unit.y * radius - radius * 0.6, width: radius * 1.2, height: radius * 1.2)
                    blurred.fill(Path(ellipseIn: blob), with: .color(color))
                }

                // A soft light from the top, so the orb reads as a sphere.
                context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: orb), with: .radialGradient(
                    Gradient(colors: [.white.opacity(0.45), .clear]),
                    center: CGPoint(x: center.x - radius * 0.25, y: center.y - radius * 0.4),
                    startRadius: 0,
                    endRadius: radius * 1.1
                ))
            }
        }
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .shadow(color: (colors.first ?? .blue).opacity(0.25 + 0.45 * energy), radius: 30)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct VoiceOrbDemo: View {
    @State private var state = VoiceOrbState.idle
    @State private var level = 0.0

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 36) {
            Spacer()

            VoiceOrb(state: state, level: level)
                .frame(width: 220, height: 220)

            Text(caption)
                .font(.title3.weight(.medium))
                .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.85))
                .contentTransition(.opacity)
                .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3), value: state)

            Spacer()

            Picker("State", selection: $state) {
                ForEach(VoiceOrbState.allCases, id: \.self) { state in
                    Text(state.rawValue)
                }
            }
            .pickerStyle(.segmented)
        }
        .padding(24)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color.black.ignoresSafeArea())
        .preferredColorScheme(.dark)
        .task(id: state) {
            // Stands in for the level a microphone or a speech synthesizer would give.
            guard state == .listening || state == .speaking else {
                level = 0
                return
            }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                level = Double.random(in: state == .speaking ? 0.3...1 : 0.1...0.9)
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(160))
            }
        }
    }

    private var caption: String {
        switch state {
        case .idle: "Tap a state to try it"
        case .listening: "I’m listening…"
        case .thinking: "Let me think…"
        case .speaking: "Here’s what I found"
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    VoiceOrbDemo()
}
```

## Animated Badge Count

A count badge whose number rolls to its new value and whose capsule springs to fit it.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/AnimatedBadgeCount/AnimatedBadgeCount.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A count badge whose number rolls to its new value while the capsule springs to fit.
///
/// It hides at zero. With Reduce Motion on, the number changes without moving.
struct AnimatedBadgeCount: View {
    var count: Int
    var maximum = 99
    var tint: Color = .red
    var unit = "new"

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) private var height = 22.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var text: String? {
        AnimatedBadgeCountFormat.text(count: count, maximum: maximum)
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            if let text {
                Text(text)
                    .font(.caption.weight(.bold))
                    .monospacedDigit()
                    .foregroundStyle(AnimatedBadgeCountContrastingForeground(background: tint))
                    .contentTransition(reduceMotion ? .identity : .numericText(value: Double(count)))
                    .padding(.horizontal, height * 0.32)
                    .frame(minWidth: height, minHeight: height)
                    .background(tint, in: .capsule)
                    .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .scale.combined(with: .opacity))
                    .accessibilityLabel("\(text) \(unit)")
            }
        }
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.45), value: text)
    }
}

enum AnimatedBadgeCountFormat {
    /// The text of the badge, or `nil` when there is nothing to count.
    static func text(count: Int, maximum: Int) -> String? {
        guard count > 0 else { return nil }
        let maximum = max(maximum, 1)
        return count > maximum ? "\(maximum)+" : "\(count)"
    }
}

/// White or black, whichever reads better on `background`. Black only on a
/// light color, so the system's own colors keep white.
nonisolated struct AnimatedBadgeCountContrastingForeground: ShapeStyle {
    let background: Color

    func resolve(in environment: EnvironmentValues) -> Color {
        let color = background.resolve(in: environment)
        let luminance = 0.2126 * color.linearRed + 0.7152 * color.linearGreen + 0.0722 * color.linearBlue
        return luminance > 0.5 ? .black : .white
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct AnimatedBadgeCountDemo: View {
    private static let script = [3, 4, 9, 12, 98, 99, 120, 0, 1, 2]

    @State private var step = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var count: Int { Self.script[step] }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .blue], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            HStack(spacing: 22) {
                icon("bell.fill", label: "Notifications", tint: .red)
                icon("envelope.fill", label: "Mail", tint: .orange)
                icon("cart.fill", label: "Cart", tint: .green)
            }
            .scaleEffect(1.4)
        }
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.75))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                step = (step + 1) % Self.script.count
            }
        }
    }

    private func icon(_ systemImage: String, label: String, tint: Color) -> some View {
        Image(systemName: systemImage)
            .font(.largeTitle)
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .padding(12)
            .accessibilityLabel(label)
            .overlay(alignment: .topTrailing) {
                AnimatedBadgeCount(count: count, tint: tint)
                    .offset(x: 12, y: -6)
            }
    }
}

    AnimatedBadgeCountDemo()
}
```

## Animated Checkmark Badge

A success badge where a circle springs in and the checkmark draws itself inside it.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/AnimatedCheckmarkBadge/AnimatedCheckmarkBadge.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A success badge: a circle springs in and the checkmark draws itself inside it.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the badge fades in and the checkmark does not draw.
struct AnimatedCheckmarkBadge: View {
    var isComplete: Bool
    var tint: Color = .green
    var size: CGFloat = 96
    var completeLabel = "Complete"
    var pendingLabel = "Pending"

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var scale = 1.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var circleAnimation: Animation {
        if reduceMotion { return .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) }
        return isComplete ? .spring(duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.5) : .easeOut(duration: 0.18)
    }

    private var checkAnimation: Animation? {
        if reduceMotion { return nil }
        return isComplete ? .easeOut(duration: 0.3).delay(0.16) : .easeOut(duration: 0.12)
    }

    var body: some View {
        let side = max(size, 0) * scale

        ZStack {
            Circle()
                .fill(tint.gradient)
                .scaleEffect(isComplete || reduceMotion ? 1 : 0.2)
                .opacity(isComplete ? 1 : 0)
                .animation(circleAnimation, value: isComplete)

            AnimatedCheckmarkBadgeCheck()
                .trim(from: 0, to: isComplete ? 1 : 0)
                .stroke(.white, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: side * 0.1, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
                .opacity(isComplete ? 1 : 0)
                .animation(checkAnimation, value: isComplete)
        }
        .frame(width: side, height: side)
        .sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: isComplete) { _, isNowComplete in isNowComplete }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel(isComplete ? completeLabel : pendingLabel)
    }
}

nonisolated private struct AnimatedCheckmarkBadgeCheck: Shape {
    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: rect.minX + rect.width * 0.28, y: rect.minY + rect.height * 0.53))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.minX + rect.width * 0.44, y: rect.minY + rect.height * 0.68))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.minX + rect.width * 0.73, y: rect.minY + rect.height * 0.35))
        return path
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct AnimatedCheckmarkBadgeDemo: View {
    @State private var isDone = false

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.mint.opacity(0.35), .teal.opacity(0.15)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 24) {
                AnimatedCheckmarkBadge(isComplete: isDone, size: 120)
                    .background(Circle().fill(.quaternary))

                VStack(spacing: 6) {
                    Text(isDone ? "Payment sent" : "Review payment")
                        .font(.title2.bold())
                    Text(isDone ? "Your receipt is on its way." : "One tap and it is done.")
                        .font(.body)
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
                .multilineTextAlignment(.center)

                Button(isDone ? "Undo" : "Confirm") {
                    isDone.toggle()
                }
                .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
```

## Dynamic Island Pill

A black capsule at the top of the screen that grows to show a live status and shrinks back to a pill.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/DynamicIslandPill/DynamicIslandPill.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A black capsule that grows to show a live status and shrinks back to a pill.
///
/// Place it at the top of the screen. With Reduce Motion on, it changes size
/// without bouncing and its content only fades.
struct DynamicIslandPill<Content: View>: View {
    var isExpanded: Bool
    var pillSize = CGSize(width: 126, height: 37)
    var expandedCornerRadius: CGFloat = 36
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var width: CGFloat { max(pillSize.width, 0) }
    private var height: CGFloat { max(pillSize.height, 0) }

    var body: some View {
        let shape = RoundedRectangle(
            cornerRadius: isExpanded ? expandedCornerRadius : height / 2,
            style: .continuous
        )

        ZStack {
            if isExpanded {
                content()
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    .environment(\.colorScheme, .dark)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                    .padding(.horizontal, 22)
                    .padding(.vertical, 18)
                    .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .opacity.combined(with: .scale(scale: 0.8, anchor: .top)))
            }
        }
        .frame(width: isExpanded ? nil : width, height: isExpanded ? nil : height)
        .background(.black, in: shape)
        .clipShape(shape)
        .padding(.horizontal, isExpanded ? 10 : 0)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.3), value: isExpanded)
        .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
        .accessibilityHidden(!isExpanded)
    }
}
```

## Rating Stars

Tappable rating stars that pop with a spring and work as an adjustable value in VoiceOver.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/RatingStars/RatingStars.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum RatingStarsValue {
    /// Keeps a rating between zero and the number of stars.
    static func clamped(_ rating: Int, maximum: Int) -> Int {
        min(max(rating, 0), max(maximum, 0))
    }
}

/// A row of tappable stars. Each star pops with a spring when it fills.
///
/// VoiceOver treats the row as one adjustable value. With Reduce Motion on, the stars only change color.
struct RatingStars: View {
    @Binding var rating: Int
    var maximum: Int = 5
    var color: Color = .orange

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 10) {
            ForEach(1...max(maximum, 1), id: \.self) { star in
                starButton(star)
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel("Rating")
        .accessibilityValue("\(rating) of \(maximum) stars")
        .accessibilityAdjustableAction { direction in
            switch direction {
            case .increment: rating = RatingStarsValue.clamped(rating + 1, maximum: maximum)
            case .decrement: rating = RatingStarsValue.clamped(rating - 1, maximum: maximum)
            @unknown default: break
            }
        }
    }

    private func starButton(_ star: Int) -> some View {
        let isFilled = star <= rating

        return Button {
            rating = RatingStarsValue.clamped(star, maximum: maximum)
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: "star.fill")
                .font(.largeTitle)
                .foregroundStyle(isFilled ? AnyShapeStyle(color.gradient) : AnyShapeStyle(.quaternary))
                .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.15), value: isFilled)
                .phaseAnimator([1.0, 1.4], trigger: isFilled) { view, scale in
                    view.scaleEffect(isFilled && !reduceMotion ? scale : 1)
                } animation: { scale in
                    scale > 1 ? .easeOut(duration: 0.1) : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.6)
                }
                // A star answers to a touch up to the middle of the gap to the next one,
                // which makes it as big as a touch target should be. The stars do not move.
                .padding(5)
                .contentShape(.rect)
                .padding(-5)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct RatingStarsDemo: View {
    @State private var rating = 0
    @State private var isAutoPlaying = true

    /// Any change made by the user, by touch or VoiceOver, ends the automatic rating.
    private var userRating: Binding<Int> {
        Binding(
            get: { rating },
            set: { newValue in
                isAutoPlaying = false
                rating = newValue
            }
        )
    }

    private var caption: String {
        ["Tap a star", "Terrible", "Not great", "It was fine", "Really good", "Loved it"][rating]
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.orange.opacity(0.25), .pink.opacity(0.2)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                Image(systemName: "fork.knife.circle.fill")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded))
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .foregroundStyle(.orange.gradient)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text("How was your dinner?")
                    .font(.title2.bold())

                RatingStars(rating: userRating)

                Text(caption)
                    .font(.headline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .contentTransition(.opacity)
                    .animation(.default, value: rating)
            }
            .padding(32)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 28))
            .padding(24)
        }
        .task(id: isAutoPlaying) {
            guard isAutoPlaying else { return }
            let script = [3, 5, 2, 4]
            var step = 0
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.9))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                rating = script[step % script.count]
                step += 1
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    RatingStarsDemo()
}
```

## Shake Error Modifier

A modifier that shakes a view with keyframes whenever a trigger value changes.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/ShakeErrorModifier/ShakeErrorModifier.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Shakes a view sideways each time `trigger` changes, with an error haptic.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the view stays still and only the haptic plays, so also show the error some other way.
struct ShakeErrorModifier<Trigger: Equatable & Sendable>: ViewModifier {
    let trigger: Trigger
    var distance: CGFloat = 10

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let distance = reduceMotion ? 0 : distance

        content
            .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: CGFloat.zero, trigger: trigger) { view, offset in
                view.offset(x: offset)
            } keyframes: { _ in
                KeyframeTrack {
                    LinearKeyframe(-distance, duration: 0.06)
                    LinearKeyframe(distance, duration: 0.1)
                    LinearKeyframe(-distance * 0.7, duration: 0.1)
                    LinearKeyframe(distance * 0.5, duration: 0.08)
                    SpringKeyframe(0, duration: 0.2, spring: .bouncy)
                }
            }
            .sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger: trigger)
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Shakes the view each time `trigger` changes.
    func shakeError(trigger: some Equatable & Sendable, distance: CGFloat = 10) -> some View {
        modifier(ShakeErrorModifier(trigger: trigger, distance: distance))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ShakeErrorModifierDemo: View {
    @State private var email = "hello@"
    @State private var attempts = 0
    @State private var showsError = false

    private var isValid: Bool { email.contains("@") && email.contains(".") }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.pink.opacity(0.2), .orange.opacity(0.2)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 14) {
                Text("Join the beta")
                    .font(.title.bold())

                TextField("Email", text: $email)
                    .textContentType(.emailAddress)
                    .keyboardType(.emailAddress)
                    .textInputAutocapitalization(.never)
                    .autocorrectionDisabled()
                    .padding(16)
                    .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 14))
                    .overlay {
                        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14)
                            .strokeBorder(showsError ? Color.red : Color.clear, lineWidth: 2)
                    }
                    .shakeError(trigger: attempts)

                Text("Enter a complete email address.")
                    .font(.footnote)
                    .foregroundStyle(.red)
                    .opacity(showsError ? 1 : 0)
                    .accessibilityHidden(!showsError)

                Button(action: submit) {
                    Text("Submit")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                        .padding(.vertical, 16)
                        .background(.pink.gradient, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 14))
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
        .onChange(of: email) { showsError = false }
    }

    private func submit() {
        showsError = !isValid
        if !isValid { attempts += 1 }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ShakeErrorModifierDemo()
}
```

## Toast Banner

A toast modifier that slides a banner from the top, announces it to VoiceOver and dismisses by itself.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/ToastBanner/ToastBanner.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// The capsule shown by the `.toast(isPresented:)` modifier.
struct ToastBanner: View {
    let message: LocalizedStringResource
    var systemImage: String = "checkmark.circle.fill"
    var tint: Color = .green

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 10) {
            Image(systemName: systemImage)
                .font(.title3)
                .foregroundStyle(tint.gradient)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Text(message)
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
        }
        .padding(.horizontal, 20)
        .padding(.vertical, 14)
        .background(.regularMaterial, in: .capsule)
        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.15), radius: 14, y: 6)
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
    }
}

private struct ToastBannerModifier: ViewModifier {
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    let message: LocalizedStringResource
    let systemImage: String
    let tint: Color
    let duration: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay(alignment: .top) {
                if isPresented {
                    ToastBanner(message: message, systemImage: systemImage, tint: tint)
                        .padding(.top, 8)
                        .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .move(edge: .top).combined(with: .opacity))
                        .task(id: message) { await announceAndDismiss() }
                }
            }
            .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.3), value: isPresented)
    }

    private func announceAndDismiss() async {
        AccessibilityNotification.Announcement(String(localized: message)).post()
        do {
            try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(duration))
        } catch {
            return
        }
        isPresented = false
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Slides a banner in from the top, announces it to VoiceOver and dismisses it after `duration` seconds.
    ///
    /// With Reduce Motion on, the banner fades instead of sliding.
    func toast(
        isPresented: Binding<Bool>,
        message: LocalizedStringResource,
        systemImage: String = "checkmark.circle.fill",
        tint: Color = .green,
        duration: Double = 2.2
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(ToastBannerModifier(
            isPresented: isPresented,
            message: message,
            systemImage: systemImage,
            tint: tint,
            duration: duration
        ))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ToastBannerDemo: View {
    @State private var showsToast = false

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.mint.opacity(0.35), .teal.opacity(0.25)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 28) {
                Image(systemName: "doc.text.fill")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .foregroundStyle(.teal.gradient)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text("Quarterly notes")
                    .font(.title2.bold())

                Button {
                    showsToast = true
                } label: {
                    Text("Save")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .padding(.horizontal, 48)
                        .padding(.vertical, 16)
                        .background(.teal.gradient, in: .capsule)
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
            }
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        }
        .toast(isPresented: $showsToast, message: "Changes saved")
    }
}
```

## Toast Host

A queue of toasts that show above everything, sheets and full-screen covers included.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/ToastHost/ToastHost.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum ToastHostRole: Equatable, Sendable {
    case info, success, warning, error

    var symbol: String {
        switch self {
        case .info: "info.circle.fill"
        case .success: "checkmark.circle.fill"
        case .warning: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill"
        case .error: "xmark.octagon.fill"
        }
    }

    var color: Color {
        switch self {
        case .info: .blue
        case .success: .green
        case .warning: .orange
        case .error: .red
        }
    }
}

nonisolated struct ToastHostToast: Identifiable, Equatable, Sendable {
    var id = UUID()
    var message: LocalizedStringResource
    var role = ToastHostRole.info
    var duration = Duration.seconds(3)
}

/// The toasts waiting to be shown, one at a time and in the order they arrived.
nonisolated struct ToastHostQueue: Equatable, Sendable {
    private(set) var toasts: [ToastHostToast] = []
    /// How many toasts may wait behind the one on screen. The oldest waiting one makes room.
    var limit = 3

    var current: ToastHostToast? { toasts.first }

    /// Adds a toast, unless it says the same as the last one, which a double tap would repeat.
    mutating func add(_ toast: ToastHostToast) {
        guard toasts.last?.message != toast.message || toasts.last?.role != toast.role else { return }
        toasts.append(toast)
        if toasts.count > max(limit, 0) + 1 { toasts.remove(at: 1) }
    }

    mutating func remove(id: ToastHostToast.ID) {
        toasts.removeAll { $0.id == id }
    }
}

/// Where views send their toasts. `toastHost()` puts one in the environment:
/// `@Environment(ToastHostCenter.self) private var toasts`, then `toasts.show("Saved", role: .success)`.
@MainActor @Observable final class ToastHostCenter {
    private(set) var queue = ToastHostQueue()
    @ObservationIgnored fileprivate var window: ToastHostWindow?

    func show(_ message: LocalizedStringResource, role: ToastHostRole = .info, duration: Duration = .seconds(3)) {
        queue.add(ToastHostToast(message: message, role: role, duration: duration))
    }

    func dismiss(_ toast: ToastHostToast) {
        queue.remove(id: toast.id)
    }

    /// Puts the window of the toasts over everything else in `scene`, once.
    fileprivate func attach(to scene: UIWindowScene) {
        guard window?.windowScene !== scene else { return }
        let host = UIHostingController(rootView: ToastHostOverlay(center: self))
        host.view.backgroundColor = .clear

        let window = ToastHostWindow(windowScene: scene)
        window.windowLevel = .alert - 1
        window.rootViewController = host
        window.isHidden = false
        self.window = window
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Shows the toasts sent to its `ToastHostCenter` above everything, sheets and full-screen
    /// covers included. Put it once on the root view of a scene.
    ///
    /// The toasts live in a window of their own, so a `tint` or a `preferredColorScheme` set
    /// on your views does not reach them.
    func toastHost() -> some View {
        modifier(ToastHostModifier())
    }
}

private struct ToastHostModifier: ViewModifier {
    @State private var center = ToastHostCenter()

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .background { ToastHostSceneReader(center: center) }
            .environment(center)
    }
}

/// A window that lets every touch through to the app, except those on the toast it shows.
private final class ToastHostWindow: UIWindow {
    var toastFrame = CGRect.null

    override func hitTest(_ point: CGPoint, with event: UIEvent?) -> UIView? {
        toastFrame.contains(point) ? super.hitTest(point, with: event) : nil
    }
}

/// An invisible view that finds the scene its window belongs to.
private struct ToastHostSceneReader: UIViewRepresentable {
    let center: ToastHostCenter

    func makeUIView(context: Context) -> ToastHostSceneView {
        let view = ToastHostSceneView()
        view.isUserInteractionEnabled = false
        view.onScene = { [center] scene in center.attach(to: scene) }
        return view
    }

    func updateUIView(_ view: ToastHostSceneView, context: Context) {}
}

private final class ToastHostSceneView: UIView {
    var onScene: ((UIWindowScene) -> Void)?

    override func didMoveToWindow() {
        super.didMoveToWindow()
        if let scene = window?.windowScene { onScene?(scene) }
    }
}

private struct ToastHostOverlay: View {
    let center: ToastHostCenter

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VStack {
            if let toast = center.queue.current {
                banner(toast)
                    .id(toast.id)
                    .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .move(edge: .top).combined(with: .opacity))
                    .task(id: toast.id) {
                        AccessibilityNotification.Announcement(String(localized: toast.message)).post()
                        try? await Task.sleep(for: toast.duration)
                        if !Task.isCancelled { center.dismiss(toast) }
                    }
            }
            Spacer(minLength: 0)
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.25), value: center.queue.current)
    }

    private func banner(_ toast: ToastHostToast) -> some View {
        Label {
            Text(toast.message)
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.medium))
                .foregroundStyle(.primary)
        } icon: {
            Image(systemName: toast.role.symbol)
                .foregroundStyle(toast.role.color)
        }
        .padding(.horizontal, 18)
        .padding(.vertical, 12)
        .background(.regularMaterial, in: .capsule)
        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.15), radius: 12, y: 4)
        .padding(.horizontal, 16)
        .padding(.top, 4)
        .onGeometryChange(for: CGRect.self) { $0.frame(in: .global) } action: { center.window?.toastFrame = $0 }
        .onDisappear { center.window?.toastFrame = .null }
        .onTapGesture { center.dismiss(toast) }
        .gesture(
            DragGesture(minimumDistance: 10).onEnded { value in
                if value.translation.height < 0 { center.dismiss(toast) }
            }
        )
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
        .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)
        .accessibilityHint("Dismisses the message")
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ToastHostDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ToastHostDemoScreen()
            .toastHost()
    }
}

private struct ToastHostDemoScreen: View {
    @State private var isEditing = false
    @Environment(ToastHostCenter.self) private var toasts

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 14) {
            Text("Toasts")
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            Text("They show above sheets too, because they live in a window of their own.")
                .font(.subheadline)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                .padding(.bottom, 10)

            Button("Copy Link") {
                toasts.show("Link copied", role: .success)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)

            Button("Edit Profile") {
                isEditing = true
            }
            .buttonStyle(.bordered)
        }
        .controlSize(.large)
        .padding(32)
```
