## Tooltip Popover

A tooltip bubble that pops out of its arrow next to an anchor view and closes on a tap outside.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/TooltipPopover/TooltipPopover.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

extension View {
    /// Marks this view as the place a tooltip points to.
    func tooltipPopoverAnchor(id: String, text: LocalizedStringResource) -> some View {
        anchorPreference(key: TooltipPopoverAnchorKey.self, value: .bounds) { bounds in
            [id: TooltipPopoverAnchor(text: text, bounds: bounds)]
        }
    }
}

/// Shows the tooltip of the anchor named by `activeID`, and closes it on a tap outside.
///
/// Wrap the whole screen, so the tooltip can draw over everything inside it. It
/// pops out of its arrow. With Reduce Motion on, it only fades.
struct TooltipPopoverHost<Content: View>: View {
    @Binding var activeID: String?
    var tint: Color = .indigo
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .subheadline) private var maximumWidth = 260.0
    @AccessibilityFocusState private var isBubbleFocused: Bool
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .overlayPreferenceValue(TooltipPopoverAnchorKey.self) { anchors in
                GeometryReader { proxy in
                    if let activeID, let tip = anchors[activeID] {
                        tooltip(text: tip.text, anchor: proxy[tip.bounds], container: proxy.size)
                    }
                }
                .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.15) : .spring(duration: 0.32, bounce: 0.35), value: activeID)
            }
    }

    private func tooltip(text: LocalizedStringResource, anchor: CGRect, container: CGSize) -> some View {
        let opensAbove = TooltipPopoverGeometry.opensAbove(anchor: anchor, container: container)
        let scaleAnchor = TooltipPopoverGeometry.arrowTip(anchor: anchor, container: container, opensAbove: opensAbove)

        return ZStack {
            Color.clear
                .contentShape(.rect)
                .onTapGesture { activeID = nil }
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            TooltipPopoverPlacement(anchor: anchor, opensAbove: opensAbove, maximumWidth: maximumWidth) {
                ViewThatFits(in: .vertical) {
                    bubbleText(text)
                    ScrollView { bubbleText(text) }
                }
                .background(tint, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 12, style: .continuous))
                .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
                .accessibilityAddTraits(.isModal)
                .accessibilityAction(named: "Dismiss") { activeID = nil }
                .accessibilityAction(.escape) { activeID = nil }
                .accessibilityFocused($isBubbleFocused)
                .onAppear { isBubbleFocused = true }

                TooltipPopoverArrow(pointsDown: opensAbove)
                    .fill(tint)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
        }
        .id(activeID)
        .transition(
            reduceMotion ? .opacity : .scale(scale: 0.2, anchor: scaleAnchor).combined(with: .opacity)
        )
    }

    private func bubbleText(_ text: LocalizedStringResource) -> some View {
        Text(text)
            .font(.subheadline)
            .foregroundStyle(TooltipPopoverContrastingForeground(background: tint))
            .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
            .padding(.horizontal, 14)
            .padding(.vertical, 10)
    }
}

struct TooltipPopoverAnchor {
    var text: LocalizedStringResource
    var bounds: Anchor<CGRect>
}

struct TooltipPopoverAnchorKey: PreferenceKey {
    static var defaultValue: [String: TooltipPopoverAnchor] { [:] }

    static func reduce(value: inout [String: TooltipPopoverAnchor], nextValue: () -> [String: TooltipPopoverAnchor]) {
        value.merge(nextValue()) { _, new in new }
    }
}

nonisolated enum TooltipPopoverGeometry {
    static let arrowSize = CGSize(width: 18, height: 9)
    static let margin: CGFloat = 12
    private static let cornerInset: CGFloat = 14

    /// The tooltip opens on the side of the anchor with more room.
    static func opensAbove(anchor: CGRect, container: CGSize) -> Bool {
        anchor.minY > container.height - anchor.maxY
    }

    /// Where the arrow touches the anchor, as a fraction of the container.
    static func arrowTip(anchor: CGRect, container: CGSize, opensAbove: Bool) -> UnitPoint {
        guard container.width > 0, container.height > 0 else { return .center }
        return UnitPoint(
            x: anchor.midX / container.width,
            y: (opensAbove ? anchor.minY : anchor.maxY) / container.height
        )
    }

    /// The most room the bubble can take on its side of the anchor.
    static func available(anchor: CGRect, container: CGSize, opensAbove: Bool, maximumWidth: CGFloat) -> CGSize {
        let room = opensAbove ? anchor.minY : container.height - anchor.maxY
        return CGSize(
            width: max(min(maximumWidth, container.width - margin * 2), 0),
            height: max(room - arrowSize.height - margin, 0)
        )
    }

    static func frames(
        anchor: CGRect,
        bubble: CGSize,
        container: CGSize,
        opensAbove: Bool
    ) -> (bubble: CGRect, arrow: CGRect) {
        let x = clamp(anchor.midX - bubble.width / 2, from: margin, to: container.width - margin - bubble.width)
        let y = opensAbove ? anchor.minY - arrowSize.height - bubble.height : anchor.maxY + arrowSize.height
        let bubbleFrame = CGRect(x: x, y: y, width: bubble.width, height: bubble.height)

        let arrowX = clamp(
            anchor.midX - arrowSize.width / 2,
            from: bubbleFrame.minX + cornerInset,
            to: bubbleFrame.maxX - cornerInset - arrowSize.width
        )
        let arrowY = opensAbove ? bubbleFrame.maxY : bubbleFrame.minY - arrowSize.height
        return (bubbleFrame, CGRect(origin: CGPoint(x: arrowX, y: arrowY), size: arrowSize))
    }

    private static func clamp(_ value: CGFloat, from lower: CGFloat, to upper: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        guard lower <= upper else { return lower }
        return min(max(value, lower), upper)
    }
}

/// Places its two subviews, the bubble and then the arrow, next to the anchor.
private struct TooltipPopoverPlacement: Layout {
    var anchor: CGRect
    var opensAbove: Bool
    var maximumWidth: CGFloat

    func sizeThatFits(proposal: ProposedViewSize, subviews: Subviews, cache: inout ()) -> CGSize {
        proposal.replacingUnspecifiedDimensions()
    }

    func placeSubviews(in bounds: CGRect, proposal: ProposedViewSize, subviews: Subviews, cache: inout ()) {
        guard subviews.count == 2 else { return }

        let bubbleProposal = ProposedViewSize(TooltipPopoverGeometry.available(
            anchor: anchor,
            container: bounds.size,
            opensAbove: opensAbove,
            maximumWidth: maximumWidth
        ))
        let frames = TooltipPopoverGeometry.frames(
            anchor: anchor,
            bubble: subviews[0].sizeThatFits(bubbleProposal),
            container: bounds.size,
            opensAbove: opensAbove
        )

        subviews[0].place(
            at: CGPoint(x: bounds.minX + frames.bubble.minX, y: bounds.minY + frames.bubble.minY),
            proposal: bubbleProposal
        )
        subviews[1].place(
            at: CGPoint(x: bounds.minX + frames.arrow.minX, y: bounds.minY + frames.arrow.minY),
            proposal: ProposedViewSize(frames.arrow.size)
        )
    }
}

nonisolated private struct TooltipPopoverArrow: Shape {
    var pointsDown: Bool

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        var path = Path()
        let tipY = pointsDown ? rect.maxY : rect.minY
        let baseY = pointsDown ? rect.minY : rect.maxY
        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: rect.minX, y: baseY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: tipY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: baseY))
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

/// White or black, whichever reads better on `background`. Black only on a
/// light color, so the system's own colors keep white.
nonisolated struct TooltipPopoverContrastingForeground: ShapeStyle {
    let background: Color

    func resolve(in environment: EnvironmentValues) -> Color {
        let color = background.resolve(in: environment)
        let luminance = 0.2126 * color.linearRed + 0.7152 * color.linearGreen + 0.0722 * color.linearBlue
        return luminance > 0.5 ? .black : .white
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct TooltipPopoverDemo: View {
    @State private var activeTip: String?

    var body: some View {
        TooltipPopoverHost(activeID: $activeTip) {
            ZStack {
                LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo.opacity(0.2), .pink.opacity(0.15)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                    .ignoresSafeArea()

                VStack(spacing: 18) {
                    Text("Settings")
                        .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)

                    row("iCloud Backup", id: "backup", tip: "Backups run overnight while the phone is charging on Wi-Fi.")
                    row("Offline Maps", id: "maps", tip: "Keeps recent places on the device, so directions work without a signal.")
                    row("Low Data Mode", id: "data", tip: "Pauses automatic downloads when your connection is limited.")
                }
                .padding(24)
            }
        }
    }

    private func row(_ title: String, id: String, tip: String) -> some View {
        HStack {
            Text(title)
                .font(.headline)
            Spacer()
            Button {
                activeTip = id
            } label: {
                // The icon is too small to hit. The padding widens what answers to a touch,
                // and the same padding taken back keeps the row as it was.
                Image(systemName: "info.circle.fill")
                    .font(.title2)
                    .padding(9)
                    .contentShape(.rect)
                    .padding(-9)
            }
            .accessibilityLabel("About \(title)")
            .tooltipPopoverAnchor(id: id, text: "\(tip)")
        }
        .padding(18)
        .background(.background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 16, style: .continuous))
    }
}

#Preview {
    TooltipPopoverDemo()
}
```

## Undo Snackbar

A bottom bar with an Undo button and a shrinking timer line.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/UndoSnackbar/UndoSnackbar.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A bottom bar with an Undo button and a line that shrinks until the bar expires.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the line stays still and the bar simply fades away on time.
struct UndoSnackbar: View {
    let message: LocalizedStringResource
    var duration: Double = 5
    var tint: Color = .yellow
    let onUndo: () -> Void
    let onExpire: () -> Void

    @State private var remaining = 1.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.accessibilityVoiceOverEnabled) private var voiceOverEnabled

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 12) {
            Text(message)
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.medium))
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)

            Button(action: onUndo) {
                Text("Undo")
                    .font(.subheadline.bold())
                    .foregroundStyle(tint)
                    .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44)
                    .contentShape(.rect)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
        }
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .padding(.horizontal, 18)
        .padding(.vertical, 6)
        .background(.black.opacity(0.85))
        .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
            Rectangle()
                .fill(tint)
                .frame(height: 3)
                .scaleEffect(x: remaining, anchor: .leading)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
        .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 16))
        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.2), radius: 14, y: 6)
        .task { await runTimer() }
    }

    private func runTimer() async {
        AccessibilityNotification.Announcement(String(localized: "\(message). Undo available.")).post()
        let seconds = voiceOverEnabled ? duration * 2 : duration
        if !reduceMotion {
            withAnimation(.linear(duration: seconds)) { remaining = 0 }
        }
        do {
            try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(seconds))
        } catch {
            return
        }
        onExpire()
    }
}

private struct UndoSnackbarModifier: ViewModifier {
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    let message: LocalizedStringResource
    let duration: Double
    let onUndo: () -> Void

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
                if isPresented {
                    UndoSnackbar(message: message, duration: duration) {
                        isPresented = false
                        onUndo()
                    } onExpire: {
                        isPresented = false
                    }
                    .padding(.horizontal, 16)
                    .padding(.bottom, 12)
                    .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .move(edge: .bottom).combined(with: .opacity))
                }
            }
            .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.2), value: isPresented)
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Shows an `UndoSnackbar` at the bottom for `duration` seconds.
    func undoSnackbar(
        isPresented: Binding<Bool>,
        message: LocalizedStringResource,
        duration: Double = 5,
        onUndo: @escaping () -> Void
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(UndoSnackbarModifier(isPresented: isPresented, message: message, duration: duration, onUndo: onUndo))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct UndoSnackbarDemo: View {
    private static let allMessages = ["Team lunch on Friday", "Your flight is confirmed", "Invoice for October"]

    @State private var messages = allMessages
    @State private var lastArchived: String?
    @State private var showsSnackbar = false

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.blue.opacity(0.25), .indigo.opacity(0.2)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 14) {
                HStack {
                    Text("Inbox")
                        .font(.largeTitle.bold())

                    Spacer()

                    Button("Archive", systemImage: "archivebox.fill", action: archive)
                        .font(.headline)
                        .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                        .disabled(showsSnackbar)
                }
                .padding(.bottom, 10)

                ForEach(messages, id: \.self) { message in
                    Label(message, systemImage: "envelope.fill")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .padding(18)
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                        .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 16))
                        .transition(.opacity)
                }

                Spacer()
            }
            .padding(24)
            .animation(.smooth, value: messages)
        }
        .undoSnackbar(isPresented: $showsSnackbar, message: "Conversation archived", duration: 3) {
            if let lastArchived { messages.insert(lastArchived, at: 0) }
        }
    }

    private func archive() {
        if messages.isEmpty { messages = Self.allMessages }
        lastArchived = messages.removeFirst()
        showsSnackbar = true
    }
}

#Preview {
    UndoSnackbarDemo()
}
```

## Completion Swipe Row

A row you swipe to the right to complete, where a checkmark pops in and the row collapses.

Category: Gestures. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Gestures/CompletionSwipeRow/CompletionSwipeRow.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A row you swipe forward to complete, to the right or, in a right-to-left layout, to the left:
/// a checkmark pops in and the row collapses.
///
/// `onComplete` runs once, after the row has collapsed, and is where the caller
/// should remove the row. With Reduce Motion on, the row completes at once.
struct CompletionSwipeRow<Content: View>: View {
    var tint: Color = .green
    var rowBackground: Color = Color(.secondarySystemGroupedBackground)
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat = 16
    var actionName = "Complete"
    var onComplete: () -> Void
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    private enum Phase {
        case idle, checked, collapsed
    }

    @State private var phase = Phase.idle
    @State private var size = CGSize.zero
    @GestureState private var dragX: CGFloat = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    /// Gestures report screen points, but layout mirrors in right-to-left layouts: 1 or -1 converts between them.
    private var forward: CGFloat { layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? -1 : 1 }

    private var isPastThreshold: Bool {
        phase != .idle || CompletionSwipeRowMath.shouldComplete(translation: CGSize(width: dragX, height: 0), width: size.width)
    }

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            .background(rowBackground)
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self, of: \.size) { size = $0 }
            .offset(x: phase == .idle ? dragX : size.width)
            .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.35, bounce: 0.25), value: dragX == 0)
            .background(alignment: .leading) {
                ZStack(alignment: .leading) {
                    tint

                    Image(systemName: "checkmark")
                        .font(.title2.bold())
                        .foregroundStyle(CompletionSwipeRowContrastingForeground(background: tint))
                        .scaleEffect(isPastThreshold ? 1.15 : (reduceMotion ? 1 : 0.5))
                        .opacity(isPastThreshold ? 1 : 0.55)
                        .padding(.leading, 24)
                        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.3, bounce: 0.6), value: isPastThreshold)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
            }
            .frame(height: phase == .idle ? nil : (phase == .collapsed ? 0 : size.height))
            .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
            .simultaneousGesture(swipe)
            .sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .medium), trigger: isPastThreshold) { _, isNowPast in isNowPast }
            .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
            .accessibilityAction(named: actionName) { complete() }
    }

    private var swipe: some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 20)
            .updating($dragX) { value, state, _ in
                let forwardDrag = value.translation.width * forward
                guard phase == .idle, forwardDrag > abs(value.translation.height) else { return }
                state = forwardDrag
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                let translation = CGSize(width: value.translation.width * forward, height: value.translation.height)
                guard CompletionSwipeRowMath.shouldComplete(translation: translation, width: size.width) else { return }
                complete()
            }
    }

    private func complete() {
        guard phase == .idle else { return }

        if reduceMotion {
            phase = .collapsed
            onComplete()
            return
        }

        withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.35, bounce: 0.1)) {
            phase = .checked
        } completion: {
            withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.25).delay(0.12)) {
                phase = .collapsed
            } completion: {
                onComplete()
            }
        }
    }
}

enum CompletionSwipeRowMath {
    static let maximumThreshold: CGFloat = 140

    /// A swipe counts when it goes mostly forward, a positive width, and covers enough of the row.
    static func shouldComplete(translation: CGSize, width: CGFloat) -> Bool {
        guard width > 0, translation.width > abs(translation.height) else { return false }
        return translation.width >= min(width * 0.4, maximumThreshold)
    }
}

/// White or black, whichever reads better on `background`. Black only on a
/// light color, so the system's own colors keep white.
nonisolated struct CompletionSwipeRowContrastingForeground: ShapeStyle {
    let background: Color

    func resolve(in environment: EnvironmentValues) -> Color {
        let color = background.resolve(in: environment)
        let luminance = 0.2126 * color.linearRed + 0.7152 * color.linearGreen + 0.0722 * color.linearBlue
        return luminance > 0.5 ? .black : .white
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct CompletionSwipeRowDemoTask: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let systemImage: String
}

struct CompletionSwipeRowDemo: View {
    private static let allTasks = [
        CompletionSwipeRowDemoTask(id: "Water the plants", systemImage: "drop.fill"),
        CompletionSwipeRowDemoTask(id: "Call the dentist", systemImage: "phone.fill"),
        CompletionSwipeRowDemoTask(id: "Buy groceries", systemImage: "cart.fill"),
        CompletionSwipeRowDemoTask(id: "Send the invoice", systemImage: "doc.text.fill"),
        CompletionSwipeRowDemoTask(id: "Book the flight", systemImage: "airplane"),
    ]

    @State private var tasks = Self.allTasks

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Color(.systemGroupedBackground)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            ScrollView {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
                    Text("Today")
                        .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                        .padding(.bottom, 4)

                    ForEach(tasks) { task in
                        CompletionSwipeRow(onComplete: { tasks.removeAll { $0.id == task.id } }) {
                            Label(task.id, systemImage: task.systemImage)
                                .font(.headline)
                                .padding(.horizontal, 18)
                                .frame(minHeight: 68, alignment: .leading)
                        }
                    }

                    if tasks.isEmpty {
                        Button("Start over") { tasks = Self.allTasks }
                            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                            .padding(.top, 24)
                    }
                }
                .padding(.horizontal, 20)
                .padding(.top, 16)
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    CompletionSwipeRowDemo()
}
```

## Double Tap Heart Overlay

Double tapping a photo throws a heart at the finger and marks the photo as liked.

Category: Gestures. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Gestures/DoubleTapHeartOverlay/DoubleTapHeartOverlay.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Wraps a photo, usually an `Image`. A double tap throws a heart at the finger and marks it as liked.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the heart appears in place and fades out.
struct DoubleTapHeartOverlay<Content: View>: View {
    @Binding var isLiked: Bool
    var tint: Color = .pink
    /// Throws a heart without a touch, for demos. Each new value throws one more.
    var programmaticBurst: DoubleTapHeartOverlayRequest? = nil
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @State private var hearts: [DoubleTapHeartOverlayBurst] = []
    @State private var size = CGSize.zero
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    private let maximumHearts = 12

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .overlay {
                ZStack {
                    ForEach(hearts) { heart in
                        DoubleTapHeartOverlayHeart(rotation: heart.rotation, tint: tint) {
                            hearts.removeAll { $0.id == heart.id }
                        }
                        .position(heart.location)
                    }
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self) { $0.size } action: { size = $0 }
            .gesture(
                SpatialTapGesture(count: 2).onEnded { value in
                    // Gestures report screen points, but `position` mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
                    let x = layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? size.width - value.location.x : value.location.x
                    throwHeart(at: CGPoint(x: x, y: value.location.y))
                }
            )
            .onChange(of: programmaticBurst) { _, request in
                guard let request else { return }
                throwHeart(at: CGPoint(x: request.point.x * size.width, y: request.point.y * size.height))
            }
            .sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .light), trigger: hearts.count) { old, new in new > old }
            .accessibilityAction(named: isLiked ? "Unlike" : "Like") { isLiked.toggle() }
    }

    private func throwHeart(at location: CGPoint) {
        hearts.append(DoubleTapHeartOverlayBurst(location: location, rotation: .random(in: -18...18)))
        if hearts.count > maximumHearts { hearts.removeFirst() }
        isLiked = true
    }
}

struct DoubleTapHeartOverlayRequest: Equatable {
    let id = UUID()
    let point: UnitPoint
}

struct DoubleTapHeartOverlayBurst: Identifiable {
    let id = UUID()
    let location: CGPoint
    let rotation: Double
}

private struct DoubleTapHeartOverlayHeart: View {
    let rotation: Double
    let tint: Color
    let onFinish: () -> Void

    @State private var scale = 0.3
    @State private var opacity = 0.0
    @State private var rise = 0.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Image(systemName: "heart.fill")
            .font(.largeTitle)
            .imageScale(.large)
            .scaleEffect(1.6)
            .foregroundStyle(tint.gradient)
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.3), radius: 8, y: 4)
            .scaleEffect(scale)
            .rotationEffect(.degrees(reduceMotion ? 0 : rotation))
            .offset(y: rise)
            .opacity(opacity)
            .onAppear(perform: run)
    }

    private func run() {
        if reduceMotion {
            scale = 1
            opacity = 1
            withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.8)) {
                opacity = 0
            } completion: {
                onFinish()
            }
            return
        }

        withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.3, bounce: 0.55)) {
            scale = 1
            opacity = 1
        } completion: {
            withAnimation(.easeIn(duration: 0.35).delay(0.15)) {
                rise = -70
                scale = 0.8
                opacity = 0
            } completion: {
                onFinish()
            }
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct DoubleTapHeartOverlayDemo: View {
    @State private var isLiked = false
    @State private var burst: DoubleTapHeartOverlayRequest?
    /// Only for this demo: it plays by itself until someone touches it.
    @State private var isAutoPlaying = true
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Color(.systemGroupedBackground)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 0) {
                DoubleTapHeartOverlay(isLiked: $isLiked, programmaticBurst: burst) {
                    placeholderPhoto
                }

                HStack(spacing: 14) {
                    Button {
                        isLiked.toggle()
                    } label: {
                        // The icon is too small to hit. The padding widens what answers to a
                        // touch, and the same padding taken back keeps the row as it was.
                        Image(systemName: isLiked ? "heart.fill" : "heart")
                            .font(.title2)
                            .foregroundStyle(isLiked ? .pink : .primary)
                            .symbolEffect(.bounce, value: isLiked)
                            .padding(10)
                            .contentShape(.rect)
                            .padding(-10)
                    }
                    .accessibilityLabel(isLiked ? "Unlike" : "Like")

                    Text(isLiked ? "You liked this" : "Double tap the photo")
                        .font(.headline)

                    Spacer()
                }
                .padding(18)
            }
            .background(.background)
            .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 24, style: .continuous))
            .padding(20)
        }
        .simultaneousGesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { _ in isAutoPlaying = false })
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            await playHearts()
        }
    }

    // Only the demo plays by itself, because a real double tap needs a finger.
    private func playHearts() async {
        let points = [UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 0.45), UnitPoint(x: 0.28, y: 0.28), UnitPoint(x: 0.72, y: 0.62)]
        while isAutoPlaying {
            for point in points {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.1))
                guard !Task.isCancelled, isAutoPlaying else { return }
                burst = DoubleTapHeartOverlayRequest(point: point)
            }
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.7))
            guard !Task.isCancelled, isAutoPlaying else { return }
            isLiked = false
        }
    }

    private var placeholderPhoto: some View {
        LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink, .purple], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: 520)
            .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
                Image(systemName: "mountain.2.fill")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .scaleEffect(2.6)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.5))
                    .padding(.bottom, 80)
            }
            .overlay(alignment: .topTrailing) {
                Image(systemName: "sun.max.fill")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .foregroundStyle(.yellow.opacity(0.85))
                    .padding(28)
            }
            .accessibilityElement()
            .accessibilityLabel("Photo of mountains at sunset")
    }
}
```

## Drag Select Grid

A grid where dragging across tiles selects them all in one stroke, as in photo libraries.

Category: Gestures. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Gestures/DragSelectGrid/DragSelectGrid.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A grid where a drag selects every tile from the first to the one under the finger.
///
/// Tiles are square, and a tap toggles one. Starting on a selected tile deselects
/// instead. Keep it out of a `ScrollView`, or the scroll will take the drag.
struct DragSelectGrid<Item: Identifiable, Tile: View>: View {
    let items: [Item]
    @Binding var selection: Set<Item.ID>
    var columns = 4
    var spacing: CGFloat = 4
    @ViewBuilder var tile: (Item, Bool) -> Tile

    private struct Stroke {
        var base: Set<Item.ID>
        var start: Int
        var selecting: Bool
    }

    @State private var stroke: Stroke?
    @State private var gridWidth: CGFloat = 0
    @GestureState private var isDragging = false
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    private var columnCount: Int { DragSelectGridMath.clampedColumns(columns) }
    private var gap: CGFloat { max(spacing, 0) }

    var body: some View {
        LazyVGrid(columns: Array(repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: gap), count: columnCount), spacing: gap) {
            ForEach(items) { item in
                let isSelected = selection.contains(item.id)

                Color.clear
                    .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
                    .overlay { tile(item, isSelected) }
                    .contentShape(.rect)
                    .onTapGesture { toggle(item) }
                    .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
                    .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? [.isButton, .isSelected] : .isButton)
                    .accessibilityAction { toggle(item) }
            }
        }
        .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self, of: \.size.width) { gridWidth = $0 }
        .simultaneousGesture(drag)
        .onChange(of: isDragging) { _, dragging in
            if !dragging { stroke = nil }
        }
        .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: selection.count)
    }

    private var drag: some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 10)
            .updating($isDragging) { _, state, _ in state = true }
            .onChanged { value in
                if stroke == nil, let start = index(at: value.startLocation) {
                    stroke = Stroke(base: selection, start: start, selecting: !selection.contains(items[start].id))
                }
                guard let stroke, let current = index(at: value.location) else { return }
                selection = DragSelectGridMath.selection(
                    base: stroke.base,
                    ids: items.map(\.id),
                    from: stroke.start,
                    to: current,
                    selecting: stroke.selecting
                )
            }
    }

    private func toggle(_ item: Item) {
        if selection.contains(item.id) {
            selection.remove(item.id)
        } else {
            selection.insert(item.id)
        }
    }

    private func index(at point: CGPoint) -> Int? {
        // Gestures report screen points, but the grid mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
        let x = layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? gridWidth - point.x : point.x
        return DragSelectGridMath.index(at: CGPoint(x: x, y: point.y), width: gridWidth, columns: columnCount, spacing: gap, count: items.count)
    }
}

enum DragSelectGridMath {
    static func clampedColumns(_ columns: Int) -> Int {
        min(max(columns, 1), 24)
    }

    /// The tile under a point, or the nearest one when the point is outside the grid.
    static func index(at point: CGPoint, width: CGFloat, columns: Int, spacing: CGFloat, count: Int) -> Int? {
        guard count > 0, width > 0, point.x.isFinite, point.y.isFinite else { return nil }

        let columns = clampedColumns(columns)
        let gap = max(spacing, 0)
        let side = (width - gap * CGFloat(columns - 1)) / CGFloat(columns)
        guard side > 0 else { return nil }

        let rows = (count - 1) / columns + 1
        let column = Int(min(max(point.x / (side + gap), 0), CGFloat(columns - 1)))
        let row = Int(min(max(point.y / (side + gap), 0), CGFloat(rows - 1)))
        return min(row * columns + column, count - 1)
    }

    /// The selection during a stroke: what was selected before, plus or minus the tiles it covers.
    static func selection<ID: Hashable>(
        base: Set<ID>,
        ids: [ID],
        from start: Int,
        to current: Int,
        selecting: Bool
    ) -> Set<ID> {
        guard !ids.isEmpty else { return base }

        let first = min(max(min(start, current), 0), ids.count - 1)
        let last = min(max(max(start, current), 0), ids.count - 1)
        let covered = Set(ids[first...last])
        return selecting ? base.union(covered) : base.subtracting(covered)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct DragSelectGridDemoPhoto: Identifiable {
    let id: Int
    let hue: Double
    let systemImage: String
}

struct DragSelectGridDemo: View {
    private let photos: [DragSelectGridDemoPhoto] = {
        let symbols = ["sun.max.fill", "leaf.fill", "moon.stars.fill", "flame.fill", "cloud.fill", "drop.fill"]
        return (0..<20).map { index in
            DragSelectGridDemoPhoto(id: index, hue: Double(index) / 20, systemImage: symbols[index % symbols.count])
        }
    }()

    @State private var selection: Set<Int> = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 16) {
            HStack {
                Text(selection.isEmpty ? "Drag to select" : "\(selection.count) selected")
                    .font(.title2.bold())
                    .contentTransition(reduceMotion ? .identity : .numericText())
                Spacer()
                Button {
                    selection = []
                } label: {
                    // A word is too small to hit. The padding widens what answers to a touch,
                    // and the same padding taken back keeps the layout as it was.
                    Text("Clear")
                        .padding(12)
                        .contentShape(.rect)
                        .padding(-12)
                }
                .disabled(selection.isEmpty)
            }
            .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy, value: selection.count)
            .padding(.horizontal, 16)

            DragSelectGrid(items: photos, selection: $selection) { photo, isSelected in
                tile(photo, isSelected: isSelected)
            }

            Spacer(minLength: 0)
        }
        .padding(.top, 16)
    }

    private func tile(_ photo: DragSelectGridDemoPhoto, isSelected: Bool) -> some View {
        Rectangle()
            .fill(
                LinearGradient(
                    colors: [Color(hue: photo.hue, saturation: 0.55, brightness: 0.95), Color(hue: photo.hue, saturation: 0.85, brightness: 0.6)],
                    startPoint: .top,
                    endPoint: .bottom
                )
            )
            .overlay {
                Image(systemName: photo.systemImage)
                    .font(.title)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.8))
            }
            .overlay(alignment: .bottomTrailing) {
                if isSelected {
                    Image(systemName: "checkmark.circle.fill")
                        .font(.title3)
                        .symbolRenderingMode(.palette)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white, .blue)
                        .padding(5)
                }
            }
            .scaleEffect(isSelected && !reduceMotion ? 0.9 : 1)
            .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.25, bounce: 0.3), value: isSelected)
            .accessibilityElement()
            .accessibilityLabel("Photo \(photo.id + 1)")
    }
}

}
```

## Drop Zone Highlight

A drop target that highlights and shows a hint while a dragged item hovers over it and clears when the drag leaves.

Category: Gestures. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Gestures/DropZoneHighlight/DropZoneHighlight.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A drop target that lights up and shows a hint while something hovers over it.
///
/// `onDrop` returns whether the drop was accepted. With Reduce Motion on, the
/// highlight changes color without growing.
struct DropZoneHighlight<Payload: Transferable>: View {
    var title = "Drop here"
    var hint = "Release to add"
    var systemImage = "tray.and.arrow.down"
    var tint: Color = .blue
    var onDrop: ([Payload]) -> Bool

    @State private var isTargeted = false
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .headline) private var minimumHeight = 150.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        let shape = RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 22, style: .continuous)

        VStack(spacing: 10) {
            Image(systemName: systemImage)
                .font(.largeTitle)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            Text(isTargeted ? hint : title)
                .font(.headline)
                .contentTransition(.opacity)
        }
        .foregroundStyle(isTargeted ? .white : tint)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: minimumHeight)
        .padding()
        .background(isTargeted ? tint : tint.opacity(0.1), in: shape)
        .overlay {
            shape.strokeBorder(tint, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 2, dash: isTargeted ? [] : [8, 6]))
        }
        .scaleEffect(isTargeted && !reduceMotion ? 1.04 : 1)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.15) : .spring(duration: 0.3, bounce: 0.35), value: isTargeted)
        .contentShape(shape)
        .dropDestination(for: Payload.self) { items, _ in
            guard !items.isEmpty else { return false }
            return onDrop(items)
        } isTargeted: { targeted in
            isTargeted = targeted
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct DropZoneHighlightDemo: View {
    @State private var waiting = ["Report.pdf", "Photo.heic", "Notes.txt", "Budget.xlsx"]
    @State private var dropped: [String] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Color(.systemGroupedBackground)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            ScrollView {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 24) {
                    Text("Files")
                        .font(.largeTitle.bold())

                    ForEach(waiting, id: \.self) { name in
                        chip(name)
                            .draggable(name)
                            .accessibilityAction(named: "Add to the box") { add([name]) }
                    }

                    DropZoneHighlight<String> { items in
                        add(items)
                        return true
                    }

                    Text(dropped.isEmpty ? "Nothing in the box yet" : "In the box: \(dropped.joined(separator: ", "))")
                        .font(.subheadline)
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
                .padding(24)
            }
        }
    }

    private func add(_ items: [String]) {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy) {
            waiting.removeAll(where: items.contains)
            dropped.append(contentsOf: items)
        }
    }

    private func chip(_ name: String) -> some View {
        Label(name, systemImage: "doc.fill")
            .font(.headline)
            .padding(.horizontal, 16)
            .padding(.vertical, 12)
            .background(.background, in: .capsule)
    }
}
```

## Long Press Radial Menu

A long press opens a ring of actions, and dragging onto one of them selects it on release.

Category: Gestures. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Gestures/LongPressRadialMenu/LongPressRadialMenu.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct LongPressRadialMenuItem: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let systemImage: String
    let action: () -> Void
}

/// A long press opens a ring of actions. Drag onto one and let go to choose it.
///
/// VoiceOver offers the same actions in its Actions list. With Reduce Motion on,
/// the ring fades in place.
struct LongPressRadialMenu<Label: View>: View {
    let items: [LongPressRadialMenuItem]
    var radius: CGFloat = 104
    var minimumDuration = 0.35
    var tint: Color = .indigo
    var accessibilityTitle = "Actions"
    @ViewBuilder var label: () -> Label

    private enum Press: Equatable {
        case idle
        case pressing
        case open(CGSize)
    }

    @GestureState private var press = Press.idle
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    private var isOpen: Bool {
        if case .open = press { return true }
        return false
    }

    private var hoveredIndex: Int? {
        guard case .open(let translation) = press else { return nil }
        return LongPressRadialMenuMath.index(translation: translation, count: items.count, radius: radius)
    }

    var body: some View {
        label()
            .scaleEffect(press == .idle || reduceMotion ? 1 : 0.9)
            .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.3, bounce: 0.3), value: press == .idle)
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .overlay { ring.allowsHitTesting(false).accessibilityHidden(true) }
            .gesture(gesture)
            .sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .medium), trigger: isOpen) { _, nowOpen in nowOpen }
            .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: hoveredIndex)
            .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
            .accessibilityLabel(accessibilityTitle)
            .accessibilityActions {
                ForEach(items) { item in
                    Button(item.title, action: item.action)
                }
            }
    }

    private var ring: some View {
        ZStack {
            LongPressRadialMenuBubbles(items: items, radius: radius, tint: tint, isOpen: isOpen, hoveredIndex: hoveredIndex)
                // The bubbles sit on a fixed radius, so they read their size under this cap. The title below does not.
                .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.xxxLarge)

            if let hoveredIndex, items.indices.contains(hoveredIndex) {
                // Its bottom edge clears the largest bubble, so a taller title grows away from the ring.
                Text(items[hoveredIndex].title)
                    .font(.headline)
                    .padding(.horizontal, 14)
                    .padding(.vertical, 8)
                    .background(.regularMaterial, in: .capsule)
                    .alignmentGuide(VerticalAlignment.center) { $0[.bottom] }
                    .offset(y: -(radius + 48))
            }
        }
    }

    private var gesture: some Gesture {
        LongPressGesture(minimumDuration: max(minimumDuration, 0))
            .sequenced(before: DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0))
            .updating($press) { value, state, _ in
                switch value {
                case .first(true): state = .pressing
                case .second(true, let drag): state = .open(layoutTranslation(drag?.translation ?? .zero))
                default: state = .idle
                }
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                guard case .second(true, let drag?) = value,
                      let index = LongPressRadialMenuMath.index(translation: layoutTranslation(drag.translation), count: items.count, radius: radius),
                      items.indices.contains(index)
                else { return }
                items[index].action()
            }
    }

    /// Gestures report screen points, but layout mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
    private func layoutTranslation(_ translation: CGSize) -> CGSize {
        layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? CGSize(width: -translation.width, height: translation.height) : translation
    }
}

private struct LongPressRadialMenuBubbles: View {
    let items: [LongPressRadialMenuItem]
    let radius: CGFloat
    let tint: Color
    let isOpen: Bool
    let hoveredIndex: Int?

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title3) private var bubbleSize = 56.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, item in
            let isHovered = hoveredIndex == index
            let offset = LongPressRadialMenuMath.offset(index: index, count: items.count, radius: radius)

            Image(systemName: item.systemImage)
                .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))
                .foregroundStyle(isHovered ? .white : tint)
                .frame(width: bubbleSize, height: bubbleSize)
                .background(isHovered ? AnyShapeStyle(tint) : AnyShapeStyle(.regularMaterial), in: .circle)
                .scaleEffect(reduceMotion ? 1 : (isOpen ? (isHovered ? 1.2 : 1) : 0.3))
                .offset(isOpen || reduceMotion ? offset : .zero)
                .opacity(isOpen ? 1 : 0)
                .animation(
                    reduceMotion
                        ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.15)
                        : .spring(duration: 0.35, bounce: 0.4).delay(isOpen ? Double(index) * 0.02 : 0),
                    value: isOpen
                )
                .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.2), value: isHovered)
        }
    }
}

enum LongPressRadialMenuMath {
    /// How far the finger must travel, as a share of the radius, to reach the ring.
    static let deadZone = 0.45

    /// The direction of an item in radians, clockwise from the top.
    static func angle(index: Int, count: Int) -> Double {
        guard count > 0 else { return 0 }
        return 2 * .pi * Double(index) / Double(count)
    }

    static func offset(index: Int, count: Int, radius: CGFloat) -> CGSize {
        let angle = angle(index: index, count: count)
        return CGSize(width: sin(angle) * radius, height: -cos(angle) * radius)
    }

    /// The item nearest the finger, or `nil` while the finger is still near the center.
    static func index(translation: CGSize, count: Int, radius: CGFloat) -> Int? {
        guard count > 0, radius > 0 else { return nil }
        guard hypot(translation.width, translation.height) >= radius * deadZone else { return nil }

        let clockwise = atan2(translation.width, -translation.height)
        let positive = clockwise < 0 ? clockwise + 2 * .pi : clockwise
        let step = 2 * .pi / Double(count)
        return Int((positive / step).rounded()) % count
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct LongPressRadialMenuDemo: View {
    @State private var lastAction = "Hold, then drag"

    private var items: [LongPressRadialMenuItem] {
        [
            LongPressRadialMenuItem(id: "camera", title: "Camera", systemImage: "camera.fill") { lastAction = "Camera" },
            LongPressRadialMenuItem(id: "note", title: "Note", systemImage: "note.text") { lastAction = "Note" },
            LongPressRadialMenuItem(id: "share", title: "Share", systemImage: "square.and.arrow.up") { lastAction = "Share" },
            LongPressRadialMenuItem(id: "star", title: "Favorite", systemImage: "star.fill") { lastAction = "Favorite" },
            LongPressRadialMenuItem(id: "trash", title: "Delete", systemImage: "trash.fill") { lastAction = "Delete" },
        ]
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack {
                Text(lastAction)
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    .padding(.top, 48)
                Spacer()
            }

            LongPressRadialMenu(items: items) {
                Image(systemName: "plus")
                    .font(.title.bold())
                    .foregroundStyle(.indigo)
                    .frame(width: 84, height: 84)
                    .background(.white, in: .circle)
                    .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.25), radius: 14, y: 8)
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    LongPressRadialMenuDemo()
}
```

## Pinch Zoom View

A view you pinch to zoom and drag, which springs back to its bounds.

Category: Gestures. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Gestures/PinchZoomView/PinchZoomView.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum PinchZoomViewMath {
    static func clamp(_ value: CGFloat, to range: ClosedRange<CGFloat>) -> CGFloat {
        min(max(value, range.lowerBound), range.upperBound)
    }

    /// Follows the value inside the range and resists beyond it, so a gesture can overshoot a little.
    static func rubberBand(_ value: CGFloat, in range: ClosedRange<CGFloat>, resistance: CGFloat = 0.3) -> CGFloat {
        let limit = clamp(value, to: range)
        return limit + (value - limit) * resistance
    }

    /// How far content filling its container can move before showing an empty edge.
    static func maxOffset(scale: CGFloat, size: CGSize) -> CGSize {
        CGSize(width: max((scale - 1) * size.width / 2, 0), height: max((scale - 1) * size.height / 2, 0))
    }

    static func clampedOffset(_ offset: CGSize, scale: CGFloat, size: CGSize) -> CGSize {
        let limit = maxOffset(scale: scale, size: size)
        return CGSize(
            width: clamp(offset.width, to: -limit.width...limit.width),
            height: clamp(offset.height, to: -limit.height...limit.height)
        )
    }
}

/// Pinch to zoom and drag to pan. Going past the limits springs back when you let go.
///
/// Double tap toggles the zoom. With Reduce Motion on, it settles without a spring.
struct PinchZoomView<Content: View>: View {
    @Binding var scale: CGFloat
    var minScale: CGFloat = 1
    var maxScale: CGFloat = 4
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @State private var pinch: CGFloat = 1
    @State private var offset = CGSize.zero
    @State private var drag = CGSize.zero
    @State private var size = CGSize.zero
    @GestureState private var isGesturing = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    /// Gestures report screen points, but layout mirrors in right-to-left layouts: 1 or -1 converts between them.
    private var forward: CGFloat { layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? -1 : 1 }

    private var settle: Animation {
        reduceMotion ? .easeOut(duration: 0.15) : .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.25)
    }

    private var liveScale: CGFloat {
        PinchZoomViewMath.rubberBand(scale * pinch, in: minScale...maxScale)
    }

    private var liveOffset: CGSize {
        let limit = PinchZoomViewMath.maxOffset(scale: liveScale, size: size)
        return CGSize(
            width: PinchZoomViewMath.rubberBand(offset.width + drag.width, in: -limit.width...limit.width),
            height: PinchZoomViewMath.rubberBand(offset.height + drag.height, in: -limit.height...limit.height)
        )
    }

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .scaleEffect(liveScale)
            .offset(liveOffset)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .clipped()
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self) { $0.size } action: { newSize in
                size = newSize
                offset = PinchZoomViewMath.clampedOffset(offset, scale: scale, size: newSize)
            }
            .gesture(zoomAndPan)
            .onChange(of: isGesturing) { _, gesturing in
                if !gesturing { settleGesture() }
            }
            .onTapGesture(count: 2) { zoom(to: scale > minScale ? minScale : min(2, maxScale)) }
            .onChange(of: scale) { _, newScale in
                withAnimation(settle) { offset = PinchZoomViewMath.clampedOffset(offset, scale: newScale, size: size) }
            }
            .accessibilityValue("\(Int((scale * 100).rounded())) percent")
            .accessibilityZoomAction { action in
                zoom(to: scale + (action.direction == .zoomIn ? 0.5 : -0.5))
            }
    }

    private var zoomAndPan: some Gesture {
        MagnifyGesture()
            .simultaneously(with: DragGesture(minimumDistance: 4))
            .updating($isGesturing) { _, state, _ in state = true }
            .onChanged { value in
                if let magnification = value.first?.magnification { pinch = magnification }
                if let translation = value.second?.translation {
                    drag = CGSize(width: translation.width * forward, height: translation.height)
                }
            }
            .onEnded { _ in settleGesture() }
    }

    /// Commits the live pinch and drag. A gesture the system cancels skips `onEnded`, so this
    /// also runs when `isGesturing` resets. Running it twice changes nothing.
    private func settleGesture() {
        let newScale = PinchZoomViewMath.clamp(scale * pinch, to: minScale...maxScale)
        let target = CGSize(width: offset.width + drag.width, height: offset.height + drag.height)
        withAnimation(settle) {
            scale = newScale
            pinch = 1
            drag = .zero
            offset = PinchZoomViewMath.clampedOffset(target, scale: newScale, size: size)
        }
    }

    private func zoom(to target: CGFloat) {
        withAnimation(settle) { scale = PinchZoomViewMath.clamp(target, to: minScale...maxScale) }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct PinchZoomViewDemo: View {
    @State private var scale: CGFloat = 1
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var zoomText: String {
        Double(scale).formatted(.number.precision(.fractionLength(1)))
    }

    var body: some View {

            PinchZoomView(scale: $scale) { scene }
                .ignoresSafeArea()

                .padding(.bottom, 24)

        .task {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            for target: CGFloat in [2.6, 1, 2.6, 1] {

                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))

        .accessibilityLabel("A mountain at sunset")
    }
}
```

## Scratch To Reveal

A cover you scratch with a finger to uncover the content beneath it.

Category: Gestures. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Gestures/ScratchToReveal/ScratchToReveal.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Tracks how much of a scratch card is uncovered, on a coarse grid of cells.
struct ScratchToRevealCoverage: Equatable {
    let columns: Int
    let rows: Int
    private(set) var cleared: Set<Int> = []

    init(columns: Int = 24, rows: Int = 24) {
        self.columns = min(max(columns, 1), 256)
        self.rows = min(max(rows, 1), 256)
    }

    var fraction: Double {
        Double(cleared.count) / Double(columns * rows)
    }

    /// Clears the cells under a brush line. The points are in a view of the given size.
    mutating func scratch(from start: CGPoint, to end: CGPoint, brushWidth: CGFloat, in size: CGSize) {
        guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0, brushWidth > 0 else { return }
        let distance = hypot(end.x - start.x, end.y - start.y)
        guard distance.isFinite else { return }

        let steps = Int(min(distance / (brushWidth / 2), 256)) + 1
        for step in 0...steps {
            let progress = CGFloat(step) / CGFloat(steps)
            let point = CGPoint(x: start.x + (end.x - start.x) * progress, y: start.y + (end.y - start.y) * progress)
            clear(around: point, radius: brushWidth / 2, in: size)
        }
    }

    private mutating func clear(around point: CGPoint, radius: CGFloat, in size: CGSize) {
        let cell = CGSize(width: size.width / CGFloat(columns), height: size.height / CGFloat(rows))
        let reach = max(radius, hypot(cell.width, cell.height) / 2)

        for row in index((point.y - reach) / cell.height, limit: rows)...index((point.y + reach) / cell.height, limit: rows) {
            for column in index((point.x - reach) / cell.width, limit: columns)...index((point.x + reach) / cell.width, limit: columns) {
                let center = CGPoint(x: (CGFloat(column) + 0.5) * cell.width, y: (CGFloat(row) + 0.5) * cell.height)
                if hypot(center.x - point.x, center.y - point.y) <= reach {
                    cleared.insert(row * columns + column)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private func index(_ value: CGFloat, limit: Int) -> Int {
        Int(min(max(value.rounded(.down), 0), CGFloat(limit - 1)))
    }
}

/// A cover you scratch with a finger to uncover the content beneath it.
///
/// The rest falls away once `revealThreshold` of the cover is gone. To start over, change the
/// view's `id`. VoiceOver users double tap to reveal, and Reduce Motion removes the final fade.
struct ScratchToReveal<Content: View, Cover: View>: View {
    var brushWidth: CGFloat = 44
    var revealThreshold: Double = 0.6
    var onReveal: (() -> Void)? = nil
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content
    @ViewBuilder var cover: () -> Cover

    @State private var strokes: [[CGPoint]] = []
    @State private var strokeStart: CGPoint?
    @State private var coverage = ScratchToRevealCoverage()
    @State private var isRevealed = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var brush: CGFloat { max(brushWidth, 1) }

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .accessibilityHidden(!isRevealed)
            .overlay {
                if !isRevealed {
                    GeometryReader { geometry in
                        cover()
                            .frame(width: geometry.size.width, height: geometry.size.height)
                            .mask { scratchMask }
                            .contentShape(.rect)
                            .gesture(scratch(in: geometry.size))
                    }
                    .transition(.opacity)
                    .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
                    .accessibilityLabel("Scratch card")
                    .accessibilityHint("Double tap to reveal what is underneath")
                    .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)
                    .accessibilityAction { reveal() }
                }
            }
    }

    private var scratchMask: some View {
        Canvas { context, size in
            context.fill(Path(CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size)), with: .color(.black))
            context.blendMode = .destinationOut
            let style = StrokeStyle(lineWidth: brush, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round)
            for stroke in strokes {
                var path = Path()
                path.addLines(stroke)
                context.stroke(path, with: .color(.black), style: style)
            }
        }
    }

    private func scratch(in size: CGSize) -> some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
            .onChanged { value in
                if strokeStart != value.startLocation {
                    strokeStart = value.startLocation
                    strokes.append([value.startLocation])
                }
                guard let last = strokes.indices.last, !isRevealed else { return }

                let previous = strokes[last].last ?? value.location
                strokes[last].append(value.location)
                coverage.scratch(from: previous, to: value.location, brushWidth: brush, in: size)
                if coverage.fraction >= min(max(revealThreshold, 0.01), 1) { reveal() }
            }
            .onEnded { _ in strokeStart = nil }
    }

    private func reveal() {
        guard !isRevealed else { return }
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeOut(duration: 0.35)) { isRevealed = true }
        onReveal?()
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ScratchToRevealDemo: View {
    @State private var round = 0
    @State private var didWin = false

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 24) {
            Text(didWin ? "You found it!" : "Scratch the card")
                .font(.title.bold())

            ScratchToReveal(brushWidth: 56, revealThreshold: 0.7, onReveal: { didWin = true }) {
                prize
            } cover: {
                cover
            }
            .id(round)
            .frame(height: 240)
            .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 28))
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.2), radius: 16, y: 8)
            .padding(.horizontal, 28)

            Button("Try again", systemImage: "arrow.counterclockwise") {
                round += 1
                didWin = false
            }
            .buttonStyle(.bordered)
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
    }

    private var prize: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 8) {
            Image(systemName: "gift.fill")
                .font(.largeTitle)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            Text("50% off")
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            Text("on your next order")
                .font(.headline)
        }
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .minimumScaleFactor(0.5)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: [.pink, .orange], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
    }

    private var cover: some View {
        LinearGradient(
            colors: [Color(white: 0.82), Color(white: 0.62), Color(white: 0.8)],
            startPoint: .topLeading,
            endPoint: .bottomTrailing
        )
        .overlay {
            Label("Scratch here", systemImage: "hand.draw.fill")
                .font(.title3.bold())
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ScratchToRevealDemo()
}
```

## Snap Corner Draggable

A floating view that can be dragged anywhere and springs to the nearest safe-area corner when released.

Category: Gestures. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Gestures/SnapCornerDraggable/SnapCornerDraggable.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum SnapCornerDraggableCorner: CaseIterable, Hashable, Sendable {
    case topLeading, topTrailing, bottomLeading, bottomTrailing

    var alignment: Alignment {
        switch self {
        case .topLeading: .topLeading
        case .topTrailing: .topTrailing
        case .bottomLeading: .bottomLeading
        case .bottomTrailing: .bottomTrailing
        }
    }

    /// The name VoiceOver reads. The leading corners are on the right in a right-to-left layout.
    func title(in layoutDirection: LayoutDirection) -> String {
        let isTop = self == .topLeading || self == .topTrailing
        let isLeading = self == .topLeading || self == .bottomLeading
        let isLeft = isLeading == (layoutDirection == .leftToRight)
        return "\(isTop ? "top" : "bottom") \(isLeft ? "left" : "right")"
    }

    /// The corner of the quadrant a point falls in, in a container of the given size.
    static func nearest(to point: CGPoint, in size: CGSize) -> Self {
        switch (point.x < size.width / 2, point.y < size.height / 2) {
        case (true, true): .topLeading
        case (false, true): .topTrailing
        case (true, false): .bottomLeading
        case (false, false): .bottomTrailing
        }
    }
}

/// A floating view you drag anywhere. It springs to the nearest corner of the safe area when
/// released, taking the speed of the flick into account.
///
/// Use it as an overlay: the empty space lets touches through. VoiceOver offers an action for
/// each corner, and with Reduce Motion on it moves there without a spring.
struct SnapCornerDraggable<Content: View>: View {
    @Binding var corner: SnapCornerDraggableCorner
    var inset: CGFloat = 16
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @State private var containerSize = CGSize.zero
    @GestureState private var translation = CGSize.zero
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    private let space = "SnapCornerDraggable"

    /// Gestures report screen points, but layout mirrors in right-to-left layouts: 1 or -1 converts between them.
    private var forward: CGFloat { layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? -1 : 1 }

    private var animation: Animation? {
        reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.3)
    }

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .offset(translation)
            .animation(animation, value: translation == .zero)
            .gesture(drag)
            .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
            .accessibilityActions {
                ForEach(SnapCornerDraggableCorner.allCases.filter { $0 != corner }, id: \.self) { target in
                    Button("Move to \(target.title(in: layoutDirection))") {
                        withAnimation(animation) { corner = target }
                    }
                }
            }
            .padding(max(inset, 0))
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: corner.alignment)
            .coordinateSpace(.named(space))
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self) { $0.size } action: { containerSize = $0 }
    }

    private var drag: some Gesture {
        DragGesture(coordinateSpace: .named(space))
            .updating($translation) { value, state, _ in
                state = CGSize(width: value.translation.width * forward, height: value.translation.height)
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                var point = value.predictedEndLocation
                if layoutDirection == .rightToLeft { point.x = containerSize.width - point.x }
                let target = SnapCornerDraggableCorner.nearest(to: point, in: containerSize)
                withAnimation(animation) { corner = target }
            }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SnapCornerDraggableDemo: View {
    @State private var corner = SnapCornerDraggableCorner.bottomTrailing
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 8) {
                Image(systemName: "person.2.fill")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded))
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                Text("On a call")
                    .font(.title.bold())
                Text("Drag the tile to any corner")
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .opacity(0.8)
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
            .padding(.horizontal, 32)

            SnapCornerDraggable(corner: $corner) {
                tile
            }
        }
    }

    private var tile: some View {
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 24)
            .fill(LinearGradient(colors: [.teal, .blue], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
            .overlay {
                Image(systemName: "person.crop.circle.fill")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
            }
            .frame(width: 120, height: 170)
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.3), radius: 14, y: 8)
            .accessibilityLabel("Your camera, \(corner.title(in: layoutDirection))")
    }
}

#Preview {
    SnapCornerDraggableDemo()
}
```
