## Swipe Action Row

A row that reveals action buttons under a horizontal swipe and snaps open or closed.

Category: Gestures. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Gestures/SwipeActionRow/SwipeActionRow.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct SwipeActionRowAction: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let systemImage: String
    let tint: Color
    let handler: () -> Void
}

enum SwipeActionRowPhysics {
    /// Where the row sits for a drag, negative toward the buttons: it cannot move past closed and resists past fully open.
    static func offset(resting: CGFloat, translation: CGFloat, revealWidth: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        let raw = resting + translation
        if raw > 0 { return 0 }
        if raw < -revealWidth { return -revealWidth + (raw + revealWidth) * 0.25 }
        return raw
    }

    static func settlesOpen(resting: CGFloat, predictedTranslation: CGFloat, revealWidth: CGFloat) -> Bool {
        revealWidth > 0 && resting + predictedTranslation < -revealWidth / 2
    }
}

/// The one row that is open, shared by every row, so opening another closes it.
@MainActor @Observable private final class SwipeActionRowOpenRow {
    static let shared = SwipeActionRowOpenRow()

    var id: UUID?
}

/// A row that reveals action buttons under a horizontal swipe and snaps open or closed.
///
/// Only one row is open at a time: opening another closes it, as in a system list.
/// Vertical drags are left to the scroll view around it. VoiceOver reaches the same buttons as
/// custom actions, and with Reduce Motion on the row settles without animating.
struct SwipeActionRow<Content: View>: View {
    let actions: [SwipeActionRowAction]
    var buttonWidth: CGFloat = 80
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @State private var id = UUID()
    @GestureState private var translation: CGFloat = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    /// Gestures report screen points, but layout mirrors in right-to-left layouts: 1 or -1 converts between them.
    private var forward: CGFloat { layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? -1 : 1 }

    private var isOpen: Bool { SwipeActionRowOpenRow.shared.id == id }
    private var width: CGFloat { max(buttonWidth, 0) }
    private var revealWidth: CGFloat { CGFloat(actions.count) * width }
    private var resting: CGFloat { isOpen ? -revealWidth : 0 }

    private var animation: Animation? {
        reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.3)
    }

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            .background(Color(uiColor: .secondarySystemGroupedBackground))
            .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
            .accessibilityActions {
                ForEach(actions) { action in
                    Button(action.title, action: action.handler)
                }
            }
            .overlay {
                if isOpen {
                    Color.clear
                        .contentShape(.rect)
                        .onTapGesture { close() }
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
            }
            .offset(x: SwipeActionRowPhysics.offset(resting: resting, translation: translation, revealWidth: revealWidth))
            .background(alignment: .trailing) { buttons }
            .clipped()
            .simultaneousGesture(swipe)
            // A tap on another row closes the one that is open, and still reaches that row.
            .simultaneousGesture(TapGesture().onEnded {
                if !isOpen { withAnimation(animation) { SwipeActionRowOpenRow.shared.id = nil } }
            })
            .animation(animation, value: translation == 0)
    }

    private var buttons: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 0) {
            ForEach(actions) { action in
                Button {
                    close()
                    action.handler()
                } label: {
                    VStack(spacing: 4) {
                        Image(systemName: action.systemImage)
                            .font(.title3)
                        Text(action.title)
                            .font(.caption.weight(.semibold))
                            .lineLimit(1)
                            .minimumScaleFactor(0.6)
                    }
                    .foregroundStyle(SwipeActionRowContrastingForeground(background: action.tint))
                    .padding(.horizontal, 4)
                    .frame(width: width)
                    .frame(maxHeight: .infinity)
                    .background(action.tint)
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private var swipe: some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 14)
            .updating($translation) { value, state, _ in
                if state != 0 || abs(value.translation.width) > abs(value.translation.height) {
                    state = value.translation.width * forward
                }
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                guard abs(value.translation.width) > abs(value.translation.height) else { return }
                let opens = SwipeActionRowPhysics.settlesOpen(
                    resting: resting,
                    predictedTranslation: value.predictedEndTranslation.width * forward,
                    revealWidth: revealWidth
                )
                withAnimation(animation) { setOpen(opens) }
            }
    }

    private func close() {
        withAnimation(animation) { setOpen(false) }
    }

    private func setOpen(_ opens: Bool) {
        let openRow = SwipeActionRowOpenRow.shared
        if opens {
            openRow.id = id
        } else if openRow.id == id {
            openRow.id = nil
        }
    }
}

/// White or black, whichever reads better on `background`. Black only on a
/// light color, so the system's own colors keep white.
nonisolated struct SwipeActionRowContrastingForeground: ShapeStyle {
    let background: Color

    func resolve(in environment: EnvironmentValues) -> Color {
        let color = background.resolve(in: environment)
        let luminance = 0.2126 * color.linearRed + 0.7152 * color.linearGreen + 0.0722 * color.linearBlue
        return luminance > 0.5 ? .black : .white
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SwipeActionRowDemo: View {
    private struct Message: Identifiable {
        let id: String
        let preview: String
    }

    @State private var messages = [
        Message(id: "Weekly report", preview: "The numbers look great this week"),
        Message(id: "Flight update", preview: "Your gate has changed to B12"),
        Message(id: "Dinner on Friday?", preview: "I found a new place downtown"),
        Message(id: "Design review", preview: "Notes from this morning's session"),
    ]
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
                Text("Inbox")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                    .padding(.bottom, 4)

                ForEach(messages) { message in
                    SwipeActionRow(actions: actions(for: message)) {
                        row(message)
                    }
                    .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 18))
                }
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 16)
            .padding(.top, 24)
        }
        .background(Color(uiColor: .systemGroupedBackground))
    }

    private func row(_ message: Message) -> some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
            Text(message.id)
                .font(.headline)
            Text(message.preview)
                .font(.subheadline)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
        .padding(.horizontal, 16)
        .padding(.vertical, 14)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: 84, alignment: .leading)
    }

    private func actions(for message: Message) -> [SwipeActionRowAction] {
        [
            SwipeActionRowAction(id: "archive", title: "Archive", systemImage: "archivebox.fill", tint: .indigo) {
                remove(message)
            },
            SwipeActionRowAction(id: "delete", title: "Delete", systemImage: "trash.fill", tint: .red) {
                remove(message)
            },
        ]
    }

    private func remove(_ message: Message) {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy) {
            messages.removeAll { $0.id == message.id }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    SwipeActionRowDemo()
}
```

## Glass Action Menu

A floating Liquid Glass button whose actions morph out of it.

Category: Glass. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Glass/GlassActionMenu/GlassActionMenu.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassActionItem: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let systemImage: String
    let action: () -> Void
}

/// A floating Liquid Glass button whose actions morph out of it.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the actions appear without morphing.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassActionMenu: View {
    nonisolated private enum GlassID: Hashable, Sendable {
        case toggle
        case item(String)
    }

    let items: [GlassActionItem]

    @State private var isExpanded = false
    @Namespace private var namespace
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var animation: Animation? {
        reduceMotion ? nil : .bouncy(duration: 0.5, extraBounce: 0.05)
    }

    var body: some View {
        // Known issue: iOS 27.2 reports the toggle's accessibility frame as the whole
        // stack when expanded. iOS 26.5 reports it correctly.
        GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 18) {
            VStack(spacing: 14) {
                if isExpanded {
                    ForEach(items) { item in
                        glassButton(id: .item(item.id), systemImage: item.systemImage, label: item.title) {
                            withAnimation(animation) { isExpanded = false }
                            item.action()
                        }
                    }
                }

                glassButton(
                    id: .toggle,
                    systemImage: "plus",
                    label: isExpanded ? "Close actions" : "Show actions",
                    rotation: isExpanded ? 45 : 0
                ) {
                    withAnimation(animation) { isExpanded.toggle() }
                }
            }
        }
        // The buttons only hold icons. Each icon reads its size under this cap, which keeps a tall stack on screen.
        .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.xxxLarge)
    }

    private func glassButton(
        id: GlassID,
        systemImage: String,
        label: LocalizedStringResource,
        rotation: Double = 0,
        action: @escaping () -> Void
    ) -> some View {
        Button(action: action) {
            GlassActionMenuIcon(systemImage: systemImage, rotation: rotation)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(label)
        .glassEffect(.regular.interactive(), in: .circle)
        .glassEffectID(id, in: namespace)
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)
private struct GlassActionMenuIcon: View {
    let systemImage: String
    let rotation: Double

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title2) private var size = 58.0

    var body: some View {
        Image(systemName: systemImage)
            .font(.title2.weight(.semibold))
            .rotationEffect(.degrees(rotation))
            .frame(width: size, height: size)
            .contentShape(.circle)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassActionMenuDemo: View {
    @State private var lastAction = "Tap the button"

    private var items: [GlassActionItem] {
        [
            GlassActionItem(id: "share", title: "Share", systemImage: "square.and.arrow.up") { lastAction = "Share" },
            GlassActionItem(id: "favorite", title: "Favorite", systemImage: "star") { lastAction = "Favorite" },
            GlassActionItem(id: "delete", title: "Delete", systemImage: "trash") { lastAction = "Delete" },
        ]
    }

    var body: some View {

            LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink, .indigo], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
```

## Glass Button Gallery

A reference gallery of the glass and prominent glass button styles in several sizes, shapes and tints.

Category: Glass. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Glass/GlassButtonGallery/GlassButtonGallery.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A tidy reference sheet of the system Liquid Glass button styles.
///
/// The styles draw their own press response, which the system adapts to Reduce Motion.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassButtonGallery: View {
    var tints: [(name: String, color: Color)] = [
        ("Blue", .blue), ("Pink", .pink), ("Orange", .orange), ("Green", .green),
    ]
    var onPress: (String) -> Void = { _ in }

    private let sizes: [(name: String, size: ControlSize)] = [
        ("Mini", .mini), ("Small", .small), ("Regular", .regular), ("Large", .large), ("Extra Large", .extraLarge),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 24) {
            section("Sizes") {
                Grid(horizontalSpacing: 16, verticalSpacing: 10) {
                    ForEach(sizes, id: \.name) { item in
                        GridRow {
                            glassButton(item.name, label: "\(item.name) glass").controlSize(item.size)
                            prominentButton(item.name, label: "\(item.name) prominent").controlSize(item.size)
                        }
                    }
                }
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            }

            section("Shapes") {
                HStack(spacing: 12) {
                    glassButton("Capsule", label: "Capsule").buttonBorderShape(.capsule)
                    prominentButton("Rounded", label: "Rounded").buttonBorderShape(.roundedRectangle(radius: 10))
                    iconButton("star.fill", label: "Circle", prominent: false)
                    iconButton("heart.fill", label: "Filled circle", prominent: true)
                }
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            }

            section("Tints") {
                HStack(spacing: 12) {
                    ForEach(tints, id: \.name) { tint in
                        iconButton("drop.fill", label: "\(tint.name) glass", prominent: false).tint(tint.color)
                        iconButton("drop.fill", label: "\(tint.name) prominent", prominent: true).tint(tint.color)
                    }
                }
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            }
        }
    }

    private func section(_ title: String, @ViewBuilder content: () -> some View) -> some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
            Text(title)
                .font(.headline)
                .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)

            content()
        }
    }

    private func glassButton(_ title: String, label: String) -> some View {
        Button(title) { onPress(label) }
            .buttonStyle(.glass)
            .accessibilityLabel(label)
    }

    private func prominentButton(_ title: String, label: String) -> some View {
        Button(title) { onPress(label) }
            .buttonStyle(.glassProminent)
            .accessibilityLabel(label)
    }

    @ViewBuilder
    private func iconButton(_ systemImage: String, label: String, prominent: Bool) -> some View {
        let button = Button(label, systemImage: systemImage) { onPress(label) }
            .labelStyle(.iconOnly)
            .buttonBorderShape(.circle)

        if prominent {
            button.buttonStyle(.glassProminent)
        } else {
            button.buttonStyle(.glass)
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

    }
```

## Glass Segmented Control

A segmented control with a Liquid Glass thumb that slides between segments.

Category: Glass. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Glass/GlassSegmentedControl/GlassSegmentedControl.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A segmented control with a Liquid Glass thumb that slides between segments.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the thumb jumps to the new segment.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassSegmentedControl<Segment: Hashable>: View {
    let segments: [Segment]
    @Binding var selection: Segment
    var tint: Color?
    let title: (Segment) -> String

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .subheadline) private var height = 44.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 0) {
            ForEach(segments, id: \.self) { segment in
                button(for: segment)
            }
        }
        .background { thumb }
        .padding(4)
        .background(.ultraThinMaterial, in: .capsule)
        .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: selection)
    }

    /// One view that moves, drawn behind the labels so they stay readable on top of it.
    private var thumb: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            let width = proxy.size.width / CGFloat(max(segments.count, 1))
            let index = segments.firstIndex(of: selection) ?? 0

            Color.clear
                .frame(width: width)
                .glassEffect(.regular.tint(tint), in: .capsule)
                .offset(x: width * CGFloat(index))
        }
    }

    private func button(for segment: Segment) -> some View {
        let isSelected = segment == selection

        return Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.4)) {
                selection = segment
            }
        } label: {
            Text(title(segment))
                .font(.subheadline.weight(isSelected ? .semibold : .medium))
                .lineLimit(1)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: height)
                .contentShape(.capsule)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassSegmentedControlDemo: View {
    @State private var period = "Week"
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let steps = ["Day": 8_214, "Week": 61_730, "Month": 248_902, "Year": 2_904_117]

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.teal, .blue, .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 28) {
                VStack(spacing: 4) {
                    Text("Steps walked")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.8))

                    Text(steps[period, default: 0], format: .number)
                        .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                        .contentTransition(.numericText())
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy, value: period)
                }

                GlassSegmentedControl(segments: ["Day", "Week", "Month", "Year"], selection: $period) { $0 }
                    .padding(.horizontal, 24)
            }
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)

    GlassSegmentedControlDemo()
}
```

## Glass Tab Accessory

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A tab view with a Liquid Glass accessory above a tab bar that minimizes on scroll.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the tab bar stays at its full size.
```

## Glass Tag Cloud

Tags of tinted, interactive Liquid Glass that melt together when they get close.

Category: Glass. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Glass/GlassTagCloud/GlassTagCloud.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassTagCloudTag: Identifiable {
    let title: String
    let tint: Color

    var id: String { title }
}

/// Tags of tinted, interactive Liquid Glass that melt together when they get close.
///
/// `mergeDistance` is the gap below which neighbouring tags blend. With Reduce Motion on,
/// selecting a tag changes it without animating.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassTagCloud: View {
    let tags: [GlassTagCloudTag]
    @Binding var selection: Set<String>
    var spacing: CGFloat = 16
    var mergeDistance: CGFloat = 10

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .subheadline) private var horizontalPadding = 16.0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .subheadline) private var verticalPadding = 10.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        GlassEffectContainer(spacing: mergeDistance) {
            GlassTagCloudLayout(spacing: spacing) {
                ForEach(tags) { tag in
                    tagButton(tag)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private func tagButton(_ tag: GlassTagCloudTag) -> some View {
        let isSelected = selection.contains(tag.title)

        return Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy) {
                if isSelected {
                    selection.remove(tag.title)
                } else {
                    selection.insert(tag.title)
                }
            }
        } label: {
            Text(tag.title)
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .padding(.horizontal, horizontalPadding)
                .padding(.vertical, verticalPadding)
                // A little taller for a touch than it looks, up to the size of a touch target.
                .padding(.vertical, 3)
                .contentShape(.capsule)
                .padding(.vertical, -3)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])
        .glassEffect(.regular.tint(tag.tint.opacity(isSelected ? 0.85 : 0.3)).interactive(), in: .capsule)
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)
private struct GlassTagCloudLayout: Layout {
    var spacing: CGFloat

    var animatableData: CGFloat {
        get { spacing }
        set { spacing = newValue }
    }

    func sizeThatFits(proposal: ProposedViewSize, subviews: Subviews, cache: inout ()) -> CGSize {
        let sizes = subviews.map { $0.sizeThatFits(ProposedViewSize(width: proposal.width, height: nil)) }
        return GlassTagCloudFlow.arrange(sizes, width: proposal.width ?? .infinity, spacing: spacing).size
    }

    func placeSubviews(in bounds: CGRect, proposal: ProposedViewSize, subviews: Subviews, cache: inout ()) {
        let tagProposal = ProposedViewSize(width: bounds.width, height: nil)
        let sizes = subviews.map { $0.sizeThatFits(tagProposal) }
        let origins = GlassTagCloudFlow.arrange(sizes, width: bounds.width, spacing: spacing).origins
        for (subview, origin) in zip(subviews, origins) {
            subview.place(at: CGPoint(x: bounds.minX + origin.x, y: bounds.minY + origin.y), proposal: tagProposal)
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)
nonisolated enum GlassTagCloudFlow {
    /// Places items left to right, starting a new row when the next item would not fit in `width`.
    static func arrange(_ sizes: [CGSize], width: CGFloat, spacing: CGFloat) -> (origins: [CGPoint], size: CGSize) {
        var origins: [CGPoint] = []
        var cursor = CGPoint.zero
        var rowHeight: CGFloat = 0
        var usedWidth: CGFloat = 0

        for size in sizes {
            if cursor.x > 0, cursor.x + size.width > width {
                cursor = CGPoint(x: 0, y: cursor.y + rowHeight + spacing)
                rowHeight = 0
            }
            origins.append(cursor)
            usedWidth = max(usedWidth, cursor.x + size.width)
            rowHeight = max(rowHeight, size.height)
            cursor.x += size.width + spacing
        }

        return (origins, CGSize(width: usedWidth, height: cursor.y + rowHeight))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassTagCloudDemo: View {
    @State private var selection: Set<String> = ["SwiftUI"]
    @State private var isTight = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let tags = [
        GlassTagCloudTag(title: "SwiftUI", tint: .blue),
        GlassTagCloudTag(title: "Animation", tint: .pink),
        GlassTagCloudTag(title: "Layout", tint: .orange),
        GlassTagCloudTag(title: "Glass", tint: .teal),
        GlassTagCloudTag(title: "Gestures", tint: .purple),
        GlassTagCloudTag(title: "Symbols", tint: .green),
        GlassTagCloudTag(title: "Charts", tint: .red),
        GlassTagCloudTag(title: "Navigation", tint: .indigo),
        GlassTagCloudTag(title: "Metal", tint: .mint),
        GlassTagCloudTag(title: "Widgets", tint: .yellow),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .black], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            // Scrolls only when Dynamic Type makes the content taller than the screen.
            ViewThatFits(in: .vertical) {
                content

                ScrollView {
                    content
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private var content: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 32) {
            Text("Pick your interests")
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                .foregroundStyle(.white)

            GlassTagCloud(tags: tags, selection: $selection, spacing: isTight ? 3 : 18)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)

            Toggle("Tight spacing", isOn: $isTight.animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.7)))
                .font(.headline)
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
        .padding(24)
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)
#Preview {
    GlassTagCloudDemo()
}
```

## Glass Tool Strip

A row of Liquid Glass tool buttons with related tools fused into one shape.

Category: Glass. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Glass/GlassToolStrip/GlassToolStrip.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassToolStripTool: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let systemImage: String
    /// Tools with the same group share one piece of glass. Nil keeps the tool on its own.
    var group: String?
}

/// A row of Liquid Glass tool buttons, with related tools fused into one shape.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, tools change without animating.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassToolStrip: View {
    let tools: [GlassToolStripTool]
    @Binding var selection: String?
    var isGrouped = true
    var tint: Color = .accentColor

    @Namespace private var namespace
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title3) private var buttonSize = 52.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        // Scrolls only when Dynamic Type makes the row wider than the space it has.
        ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
            strip

            ScrollView(.horizontal, showsIndicators: false) {
                strip
            }
            .scrollClipDisabled()
        }
    }

    private var strip: some View {
        GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 10) {
            HStack(spacing: 14) {
                ForEach(tools) { tool in
                    toolButton(tool)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private func toolButton(_ tool: GlassToolStripTool) -> some View {
        let isSelected = tool.id == selection

        return Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy) {
                selection = isSelected ? nil : tool.id
            }
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: tool.systemImage)
                .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))
                .foregroundStyle(isSelected ? tint : .primary)
                .frame(width: buttonSize, height: buttonSize)
                .contentShape(.capsule)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(tool.title)
        .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])
        // A union shares one shape across its members, so it has to be a capsule, and
        // selection only tints the symbol. A square capsule draws as a circle on its own.
        .glassEffect(.regular.interactive(), in: .capsule)
        .glassEffectUnion(id: isGrouped ? tool.group : nil, namespace: namespace)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassToolStripDemo: View {
    @State private var selection: String? = "pen"
    @State private var isGrouped = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

        GlassToolStripTool(id: "pen", title: "Pen", systemImage: "pencil.tip", group: "draw"),
        GlassToolStripTool(id: "marker", title: "Marker", systemImage: "highlighter", group: "draw"),
        GlassToolStripTool(id: "eraser", title: "Eraser", systemImage: "eraser", group: "draw"),
        GlassToolStripTool(id: "undo", title: "Undo", systemImage: "arrow.uturn.backward", group: "history"),
        GlassToolStripTool(id: "redo", title: "Redo", systemImage: "arrow.uturn.forward", group: "history"),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            MeshGradient(
                width: 2,
                height: 2,
                points: [[0, 0], [1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 1]],
                colors: [.pink, .orange, .purple, .blue]
            )
            .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 32) {
                GlassToolStrip(tools: tools, selection: $selection, isGrouped: isGrouped, tint: .indigo)

                Button("Group tools", systemImage: isGrouped ? "square.split.2x1" : "square.on.square") {
                    withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .bouncy(duration: 0.5)) { isGrouped.toggle() }
                }
                .buttonStyle(.glass)
                .accessibilityValue(isGrouped ? "On" : "Off")
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Before After Slider

Two stacked images split by a draggable handle that compares the before and after versions.

Category: Images. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Images/BeforeAfterSlider/BeforeAfterSlider.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Two stacked images split by a handle you drag to compare them.
///
/// `position` runs from 0, all after, to 1, all before. VoiceOver adjusts it by swiping up or down.
struct BeforeAfterSlider: View {
    let before: Image
    let after: Image
    @Binding var position: Double
    var beforeTitle = "Before"
    var afterTitle = "After"

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) private var knobSize = 44.0
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    private var clamped: Double { min(max(position, 0), 1) }

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let size = geometry.size
            let handleX = size.width * clamped

            ZStack {
                photo(after, in: size)
                photo(before, in: size)
                    .mask(alignment: .leading) {
                        Rectangle().frame(width: handleX)
                    }
                handle(height: size.height)
                    .position(x: handleX, y: size.height / 2)
            }
            .overlay(alignment: .topLeading) { tag(beforeTitle).opacity(min(clamped / 0.25, 1)) }
            .overlay(alignment: .topTrailing) { tag(afterTitle).opacity(min((1 - clamped) / 0.25, 1)) }
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .gesture(
                DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { value in
                    guard size.width > 0 else { return }
                    // Gestures report screen points, but the layout mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
                    let x = layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? size.width - value.location.x : value.location.x
                    position = min(max(x / size.width, 0), 1)
                }
            )
        }
        .clipped()
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel("\(beforeTitle) and \(afterTitle) comparison")
        .accessibilityValue("\(Int(clamped * 100)) percent \(beforeTitle)")
        .accessibilityAdjustableAction { direction in
            switch direction {
            case .increment: position = min(clamped + 0.1, 1)
            case .decrement: position = max(clamped - 0.1, 0)
            @unknown default: break
            }
        }
    }

    private func photo(_ image: Image, in size: CGSize) -> some View {
        image
            .resizable()
            .scaledToFill()
            .frame(width: size.width, height: size.height)
            .clipped()
    }

    private func handle(height: CGFloat) -> some View {
        ZStack {
            Rectangle()
                .fill(.white)
                .frame(width: 3, height: height)
            Circle()
                .fill(.white)
                .frame(width: knobSize, height: knobSize)
                .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.3), radius: 6, y: 2)
            Image(systemName: "arrow.left.and.right")
                .font(.body.weight(.bold))
                .foregroundStyle(.black.opacity(0.7))
        }
    }

    private func tag(_ title: String) -> some View {
        Text(title)
            .font(.caption.weight(.semibold))
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .padding(.horizontal, 10)
            .padding(.vertical, 5)
            .background(.black.opacity(0.5), in: .capsule)
            .padding(12)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct BeforeAfterSliderDemo: View {
    @State private var position = 0.5

    private let before = demoPhoto(sky: [Color(white: 0.55), Color(white: 0.78)], hill: Color(white: 0.34), label: "Flat landscape")
    private let after = demoPhoto(sky: [.indigo, .pink, .orange], hill: Color(red: 0.13, green: 0.16, blue: 0.4), label: "Graded landscape")

    var body: some View {
        BeforeAfterSlider(before: before, after: after, position: $position)
            .aspectRatio(3 / 4, contentMode: .fit)
            .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 24))
            .padding(16)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
    }
}

private func demoPhoto(sky: [Color], hill: Color, label: String) -> Image {
    let size = CGSize(width: 900, height: 1200)
    return Image(size: size, label: Text(label)) { context in
        context.fill(
            Path(CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size)),
            with: .linearGradient(Gradient(colors: sky), startPoint: .zero, endPoint: CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height))
        )
        context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: 540, y: 220, width: 200, height: 200)), with: .color(.white.opacity(0.85)))

        var ridge = Path()
        ridge.move(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height))
        ridge.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: 760))
        ridge.addCurve(to: CGPoint(x: size.width, y: 660), control1: CGPoint(x: 300, y: 480), control2: CGPoint(x: 600, y: 1020))
        ridge.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height))
        ridge.closeSubpath()
        context.fill(ridge, with: .color(hill))
    }
}
```

## Blur Up Image

An image that goes from a blurred preview into sharp focus once the full picture arrives.

Category: Images. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Images/BlurUpImage/BlurUpImage.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

private struct BlurUpImageFocus: Transition {
    let radius: CGFloat

    func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content
            .blur(radius: phase.isIdentity ? 0 : radius)
            .opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
    }
}

/// Shows a blurred preview until the full image arrives, then brings it into focus.
///
/// It fills the space it is given. With Reduce Motion on, the full image fades in without the
/// focus pull. Use `BlurUpImageRemote` to load the full image from a URL.
struct BlurUpImage: View {
    let preview: Image
    let image: Image?
    let label: LocalizedStringResource
    var blurRadius: CGFloat = 24
    var isLoading = true

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var radius: CGFloat { max(blurRadius, 0) }

    private var transition: AnyTransition {
        reduceMotion ? .opacity : AnyTransition(BlurUpImageFocus(radius: radius))
    }

    var body: some View {
        Color.clear
            .overlay {
                preview
                    .resizable()
                    .scaledToFill()
                    .blur(radius: radius, opaque: true)
            }
            .overlay {
                if let image {
                    image
                        .resizable()
                        .scaledToFill()
                        .transition(transition)
                }
            }
            .overlay {
                if image == nil, isLoading {
                    ProgressView()
                        .tint(.white)
                }
            }
            .clipped()
            .animation(.easeOut(duration: reduceMotion ? 0.2 : 0.8), value: image != nil)
            .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
            .accessibilityLabel(label)
            .accessibilityValue(image == nil && isLoading ? "Loading" : "")
            .accessibilityAddTraits(.isImage)
    }
}

/// Loads the full image from a URL. The preview stays on screen if the download fails.
struct BlurUpImageRemote: View {
    let url: URL?
    let preview: Image
    let label: LocalizedStringResource

    var body: some View {
        AsyncImage(url: url) { phase in
            BlurUpImage(preview: preview, image: phase.image, label: label, isLoading: url != nil && phase.error == nil)
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct BlurUpImageDemo: View {
    @State private var isLoaded = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let preview = demoPhoto(size: CGSize(width: 18, height: 24))
    private let full = demoPhoto(size: CGSize(width: 900, height: 1200))

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 20) {
            BlurUpImage(preview: preview, image: isLoaded ? full : nil, label: "Mountains at dusk")
                .aspectRatio(3 / 4, contentMode: .fit)
                .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 24))

            Text(isLoaded ? "Full image loaded" : "Loading the full image")
                .font(.headline)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
        .padding(16)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else {
                isLoaded = true
                return
            }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.3))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                isLoaded = true
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2.3))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                isLoaded = false
            }
        }
    }
}

private func demoPhoto(size: CGSize) -> Image {
    Image(size: size, label: Text("Mountains at dusk")) { context in
        context.fill(
            Path(CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size)),
            with: .linearGradient(
                Gradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple, .orange]),
                startPoint: .zero,
                endPoint: CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height)
            )
        )
        let sun = size.width * 0.22
        context.fill(
            Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: size.width * 0.6, y: size.height * 0.18, width: sun, height: sun)),
            with: .color(.white.opacity(0.85))
        )

        var ridge = Path()
        ridge.move(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height))
        ridge.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height * 0.63))
        ridge.addCurve(
            to: CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height * 0.55),
            control1: CGPoint(x: size.width / 3, y: size.height * 0.4),
            control2: CGPoint(x: size.width * 0.66, y: size.height * 0.85)
        )
        ridge.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height))
        ridge.closeSubpath()
        context.fill(ridge, with: .color(Color(red: 0.12, green: 0.12, blue: 0.32)))
    }
}

    BlurUpImageDemo()
}
```

## Circular Avatar Cropper

A photo you pan and pinch under a fixed circular window to choose an avatar crop.

Category: Images. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Images/CircularAvatarCropper/CircularAvatarCropper.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// The zoom and position of a photo under the crop window. `offset` is a fraction of the window's
/// diameter, so a crop survives a change of size.
struct CircularAvatarCropperTransform: Equatable, Sendable {
    var zoom: CGFloat = 1
    var offset = CGSize.zero

    /// The photo's size at zoom 1, where its shorter side matches a window of diameter 1.
    static func fillSize(aspectRatio: CGFloat) -> CGSize {
        guard aspectRatio.isFinite else { return CGSize(width: 1, height: 1) }
        let ratio = min(max(aspectRatio, 0.01), 100)
        return ratio >= 1 ? CGSize(width: ratio, height: 1) : CGSize(width: 1, height: 1 / ratio)
    }

    /// Keeps the zoom in range and the window fully covered by the photo.
    func clamped(aspectRatio: CGFloat, maxZoom: CGFloat) -> Self {
        let fill = Self.fillSize(aspectRatio: aspectRatio)
        let safeZoom = min(max(zoom, 1), max(maxZoom, 1))
        let limit = CGSize(width: (fill.width * safeZoom - 1) / 2, height: (fill.height * safeZoom - 1) / 2)
        return Self(
            zoom: safeZoom,
            offset: CGSize(
                width: min(max(offset.width, -limit.width), limit.width),
                height: min(max(offset.height, -limit.height), limit.height)
            )
        )
    }

    /// The part of the photo inside the window, with every value from 0 to 1.
    func normalizedCropRect(aspectRatio: CGFloat) -> CGRect {
        let fill = Self.fillSize(aspectRatio: aspectRatio)
        let shown = CGSize(width: fill.width * zoom, height: fill.height * zoom)
        let size = CGSize(width: 1 / shown.width, height: 1 / shown.height)
        return CGRect(
            x: 0.5 - offset.width / shown.width - size.width / 2,
            y: 0.5 - offset.height / shown.height - size.height / 2,
            width: size.width,
            height: size.height
        )
    }
}

nonisolated private struct CircularAvatarCropperDim: Shape {
    let diameter: CGFloat

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        var path = Path(rect)
        path.addEllipse(in: CGRect(x: rect.midX - diameter / 2, y: rect.midY - diameter / 2, width: diameter, height: diameter))
        return path
    }
}

/// A photo you pan and pinch under a fixed circular window to choose an avatar crop.
///
/// Read `normalizedCropRect(aspectRatio:)` from the binding to cut the real image. `aspectRatio`
/// is the photo's width divided by its height. VoiceOver zooms by swiping up or down, and pans
/// with custom actions.
struct CircularAvatarCropper: View {
    let image: Image
    let aspectRatio: CGFloat
    @Binding var crop: CircularAvatarCropperTransform
    var maxZoom: CGFloat = 4
    var windowInset: CGFloat = 24

    @GestureState private var translation = CGSize.zero
    @GestureState private var magnification: CGFloat = 1

    /// How far a VoiceOver action moves the photo, as a fraction of the window's diameter.
    private let panStep: CGFloat = 0.1

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let diameter = max(min(geometry.size.width, geometry.size.height) - 2 * max(windowInset, 0), 1)
            let fill = CircularAvatarCropperTransform.fillSize(aspectRatio: aspectRatio)
            let shown = liveCrop(diameter: diameter)

            image
                .resizable()
                .frame(width: fill.width * diameter, height: fill.height * diameter)
                .scaleEffect(shown.zoom)
                .offset(x: shown.offset.width * diameter, y: shown.offset.height * diameter)
                .frame(width: geometry.size.width, height: geometry.size.height)
                .overlay { window(diameter: diameter) }
                .contentShape(.rect)
                .gesture(pan(diameter: diameter).simultaneously(with: pinch))
        }
        // A photo is not mirrored in right-to-left layouts, so neither is the geometry that moves it.
        .environment(\.layoutDirection, .leftToRight)
        .clipped()
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel("Avatar crop")
        .accessibilityValue("\(Int(crop.clamped(aspectRatio: aspectRatio, maxZoom: maxZoom).zoom * 100)) percent zoom")
        .accessibilityAdjustableAction { direction in
            switch direction {
            case .increment: update { $0.zoom += 0.25 }
            case .decrement: update { $0.zoom -= 0.25 }
            @unknown default: break
            }
        }
        .accessibilityActions {
            Button("Move photo left") { update { $0.offset.width -= panStep } }
            Button("Move photo right") { update { $0.offset.width += panStep } }
            Button("Move photo up") { update { $0.offset.height -= panStep } }
            Button("Move photo down") { update { $0.offset.height += panStep } }
        }
    }

    private func window(diameter: CGFloat) -> some View {
        ZStack {
            CircularAvatarCropperDim(diameter: diameter)
                .fill(.black.opacity(0.6), style: FillStyle(eoFill: true))
            Circle()
                .stroke(.white, lineWidth: 2)
                .frame(width: diameter, height: diameter)
        }
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
    }

    private func liveCrop(diameter: CGFloat) -> CircularAvatarCropperTransform {
        var shown = crop
        shown.zoom *= magnification
        shown.offset.width += translation.width / diameter
        shown.offset.height += translation.height / diameter
        return shown.clamped(aspectRatio: aspectRatio, maxZoom: maxZoom)
    }

    private func pan(diameter: CGFloat) -> some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
            .updating($translation) { value, state, _ in
                state = value.translation
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                update {
                    $0.offset.width += value.translation.width / diameter
                    $0.offset.height += value.translation.height / diameter
                }
            }
    }

    private var pinch: some Gesture {
        MagnifyGesture()
            .updating($magnification) { value, state, _ in
                state = value.magnification
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                update { $0.zoom *= value.magnification }
            }
    }

    private func update(_ change: (inout CircularAvatarCropperTransform) -> Void) {
        var next = crop
        change(&next)
        crop = next.clamped(aspectRatio: aspectRatio, maxZoom: maxZoom)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CircularAvatarCropperDemo: View {
    @State private var crop = CircularAvatarCropperTransform()
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let aspectRatio: CGFloat = 3 / 4
    private let photo = demoPhoto()
    private let avatarSize: CGFloat = 56

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 0) {
            CircularAvatarCropper(image: photo, aspectRatio: aspectRatio, crop: $crop)

            HStack(spacing: 12) {
                avatar
                Spacer(minLength: 0)
                control("Zoom out", systemImage: "minus.magnifyingglass") { $0.zoom -= 0.75 }
                control("Zoom in", systemImage: "plus.magnifyingglass") { $0.zoom += 0.75 }
                control("Reset", systemImage: "arrow.counterclockwise") { $0 = CircularAvatarCropperTransform() }
            }
            .padding(16)
        }
        .background(.black)
        .preferredColorScheme(.dark)
    }

    private var avatar: some View {
        let fill = CircularAvatarCropperTransform.fillSize(aspectRatio: aspectRatio)
        return photo
            .resizable()
            .frame(width: fill.width * avatarSize, height: fill.height * avatarSize)
            .scaleEffect(crop.zoom)
            .offset(x: crop.offset.width * avatarSize, y: crop.offset.height * avatarSize)
            .frame(width: avatarSize, height: avatarSize)
            .clipShape(.circle)
            .accessibilityLabel("Avatar preview")
    }

    private func control(
        _ title: String,
        systemImage: String,
        change: @escaping (inout CircularAvatarCropperTransform) -> Void
    ) -> some View {
        Button {
            var next = crop
            change(&next)
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy) {
                crop = next.clamped(aspectRatio: aspectRatio, maxZoom: 4)
            }
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: systemImage)
                .font(.title3)
                .frame(width: 44, height: 44)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.bordered)
        .accessibilityLabel(title)
    }
}

private func demoPhoto() -> Image {
    let size = CGSize(width: 900, height: 1200)
    return Image(size: size, label: Text("Portrait")) { context in
        context.fill(
            Path(CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size)),
            with: .linearGradient(Gradient(colors: [.teal, .blue, .indigo]), startPoint: .zero, endPoint: CGPoint(x: 900, y: 1200))
        )
        context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: 310, y: 330, width: 280, height: 340)), with: .color(Color(red: 1, green: 0.84, blue: 0.7)))
        context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: 190, y: 740, width: 520, height: 700)), with: .color(.orange))
        context.fill(Path(CGRect(x: 310, y: 300, width: 280, height: 120)), with: .color(Color(red: 0.25, green: 0.15, blue: 0.1)))
    }
}

#Preview {
    CircularAvatarCropperDemo()
}
```

## Crop Rectangle Overlay

A crop frame with draggable corners and edges over an image, dimming the area outside the selection.

Category: Images. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Images/CropRectangleOverlay/CropRectangleOverlay.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A part of the crop frame that can be dragged. Rectangles are normalized, from 0 to 1.
enum CropRectangleOverlayHandle: CaseIterable, Hashable, Sendable {
    case body, top, right, bottom, left, topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft

    private var movesLeft: Bool { self == .left || self == .topLeft || self == .bottomLeft }
    private var movesRight: Bool { self == .right || self == .topRight || self == .bottomRight }
    private var movesTop: Bool { self == .top || self == .topLeft || self == .topRight }
    private var movesBottom: Bool { self == .bottom || self == .bottomLeft || self == .bottomRight }

    func adjusting(_ rect: CGRect, by delta: CGSize, minimumSide: CGFloat) -> CGRect {
        if self == .body {
            return CGRect(
                x: min(max(rect.minX + delta.width, 0), max(1 - rect.width, 0)),
                y: min(max(rect.minY + delta.height, 0), max(1 - rect.height, 0)),
                width: rect.width,
                height: rect.height
            )
        }

        let side = min(max(minimumSide, 0.01), 1)
        var left = rect.minX, right = rect.maxX, top = rect.minY, bottom = rect.maxY
        if movesLeft { left = max(min(left + delta.width, right - side), 0) }
        if movesRight { right = min(max(right + delta.width, left + side), 1) }
        if movesTop { top = max(min(top + delta.height, bottom - side), 0) }
        if movesBottom { bottom = min(max(bottom + delta.height, top + side), 1) }
        return CGRect(x: left, y: top, width: right - left, height: bottom - top)
    }

    /// The touch area for this handle around a crop frame in points.
    func hitArea(around rect: CGRect, grip: CGFloat) -> CGRect {
        let half = grip / 2
        switch self {
        case .body: return rect.insetBy(dx: min(half, rect.width / 2), dy: min(half, rect.height / 2))
        case .top: return CGRect(x: rect.minX + half, y: rect.minY - half, width: max(rect.width - grip, 0), height: grip)
        case .bottom: return CGRect(x: rect.minX + half, y: rect.maxY - half, width: max(rect.width - grip, 0), height: grip)
        case .left: return CGRect(x: rect.minX - half, y: rect.minY + half, width: grip, height: max(rect.height - grip, 0))
        case .right: return CGRect(x: rect.maxX - half, y: rect.minY + half, width: grip, height: max(rect.height - grip, 0))
        case .topLeft: return CGRect(x: rect.minX - half, y: rect.minY - half, width: grip, height: grip)
        case .topRight: return CGRect(x: rect.maxX - half, y: rect.minY - half, width: grip, height: grip)
        case .bottomLeft: return CGRect(x: rect.minX - half, y: rect.maxY - half, width: grip, height: grip)
        case .bottomRight: return CGRect(x: rect.maxX - half, y: rect.maxY - half, width: grip, height: grip)
        }
    }

    /// A rectangle that fits inside the unit square, whatever was passed in.
    static func sanitized(_ rect: CGRect) -> CGRect {
        let unit = CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 1, height: 1)
        let fitted = rect.standardized.intersection(unit)
        return fitted.isNull || fitted.isEmpty ? unit : fitted
    }
}

nonisolated private struct CropRectangleOverlayDim: Shape {
    let hole: CGRect

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        var path = Path(rect)
        path.addRect(hole)
        return path
    }
}

/// A crop frame with draggable corners and edges over an image, dimming what is outside it.
///
/// `crop` is normalized, from 0 to 1, and changes when a drag ends. `aspectRatio` is the image's
/// width divided by its height. VoiceOver moves and resizes the frame with custom actions.
struct CropRectangleOverlay: View {
    private struct ActiveDrag: Equatable {
        let handle: CropRectangleOverlayHandle
        let delta: CGSize
    }

    let image: Image
    let aspectRatio: CGFloat
    @Binding var crop: CGRect
    var minimumSide: CGFloat = 0.15

    @GestureState private var drag: ActiveDrag?

    /// How far a VoiceOver action moves or resizes the frame, as a fraction of the image.
    private let adjustmentStep: CGFloat = 0.05

    private var committed: CGRect { CropRectangleOverlayHandle.sanitized(crop) }

    private var shown: CGRect {
        guard let drag else { return committed }
        return drag.handle.adjusting(committed, by: drag.delta, minimumSide: minimumSide)
    }

    var body: some View {
        image
            .resizable()
            .aspectRatio(aspectRatio.isFinite ? max(aspectRatio, 0.01) : 1, contentMode: .fit)
            .overlay {
                GeometryReader { geometry in
                    cropInterface(in: geometry.size)
                }
            }
            // A photo is not mirrored in right-to-left layouts, so neither is the crop drawn over it.
            .environment(\.layoutDirection, .leftToRight)
            .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
            .accessibilityLabel("Crop area")
            .accessibilityValue(accessibilityDescription)
            .accessibilityActions { accessibilityButtons }
    }

    private func cropInterface(in size: CGSize) -> some View {
        let frame = CGRect(
            x: shown.minX * size.width,
            y: shown.minY * size.height,
            width: shown.width * size.width,
            height: shown.height * size.height
        )

        return ZStack {
            CropRectangleOverlayDim(hole: frame)
                .fill(.black.opacity(0.55), style: FillStyle(eoFill: true))
            thirds(in: frame)
                .stroke(.white.opacity(0.5), lineWidth: 0.5)
            Path(frame)
                .stroke(.white, lineWidth: 1.5)
            brackets(in: frame)
                .stroke(.white, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 4, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))

            ForEach(CropRectangleOverlayHandle.allCases, id: \.self) { handle in
                let area = handle.hitArea(around: frame, grip: 44)
                Color.clear
                    .frame(width: area.width, height: area.height)
                    .contentShape(.rect)
                    .gesture(dragGesture(for: handle, in: size))
                    .position(x: area.midX, y: area.midY)
            }
        }
    }

    private func thirds(in frame: CGRect) -> Path {
        Path { path in
            for part in [CGFloat(1) / 3, CGFloat(2) / 3] {
                path.move(to: CGPoint(x: frame.minX + frame.width * part, y: frame.minY))
                path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: frame.minX + frame.width * part, y: frame.maxY))
                path.move(to: CGPoint(x: frame.minX, y: frame.minY + frame.height * part))
                path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: frame.maxX, y: frame.minY + frame.height * part))
            }
        }
    }

    private func brackets(in frame: CGRect) -> Path {
        let length = min(22, min(frame.width, frame.height) / 2)
        return Path { path in
            for (corner, x, y) in [
                (CGPoint(x: frame.minX, y: frame.minY), length, length),
                (CGPoint(x: frame.maxX, y: frame.minY), -length, length),
                (CGPoint(x: frame.maxX, y: frame.maxY), -length, -length),
                (CGPoint(x: frame.minX, y: frame.maxY), length, -length),
            ] {
                path.move(to: CGPoint(x: corner.x + x, y: corner.y))
                path.addLine(to: corner)
                path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: corner.x, y: corner.y + y))
            }
        }
    }

    private func dragGesture(for handle: CropRectangleOverlayHandle, in size: CGSize) -> some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
            .updating($drag) { value, state, _ in
                state = ActiveDrag(handle: handle, delta: normalized(value.translation, in: size))
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                crop = handle.adjusting(committed, by: normalized(value.translation, in: size), minimumSide: minimumSide)
            }
    }

    private func normalized(_ translation: CGSize, in size: CGSize) -> CGSize {
        guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0 else { return .zero }
        return CGSize(width: translation.width / size.width, height: translation.height / size.height)
    }

    private var accessibilityDescription: String {
        let parts = [("left", committed.minX), ("top", committed.minY), ("width", committed.width), ("height", committed.height)]
        return parts.map { "\($0.0) \(Int(($0.1 * 100).rounded())) percent" }.joined(separator: ", ")
    }

    @ViewBuilder private var accessibilityButtons: some View {
        adjustment("Move left", .body, dx: -adjustmentStep, dy: 0)
        adjustment("Move right", .body, dx: adjustmentStep, dy: 0)
        adjustment("Move up", .body, dx: 0, dy: -adjustmentStep)
        adjustment("Move down", .body, dx: 0, dy: adjustmentStep)
        adjustment("Make wider", .right, dx: adjustmentStep, dy: 0)
        adjustment("Make narrower", .right, dx: -adjustmentStep, dy: 0)
        adjustment("Make taller", .bottom, dx: 0, dy: adjustmentStep)
        adjustment("Make shorter", .bottom, dx: 0, dy: -adjustmentStep)
    }

    private func adjustment(_ title: String, _ handle: CropRectangleOverlayHandle, dx: CGFloat, dy: CGFloat) -> some View {
        Button(title) {
            crop = handle.adjusting(committed, by: CGSize(width: dx, height: dy), minimumSide: minimumSide)
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CropRectangleOverlayDemo: View {
    private static let initialCrop = CGRect(x: 0.1, y: 0.1, width: 0.8, height: 0.8)

    @State private var crop = initialCrop
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let photo = demoPhoto()

    var body: some View {
        CropRectangleOverlay(image: photo, aspectRatio: 4 / 5, crop: $crop)
            .padding(16)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
            .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
                HStack {
                    Text("\(Int((crop.width * 100).rounded()))% × \(Int((crop.height * 100).rounded()))%")
                        .font(.headline.monospacedDigit())
                    Spacer()
                    Button("Reset", systemImage: "arrow.counterclockwise") {
                        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy) { crop = Self.initialCrop }
                    }
                    .buttonStyle(.bordered)
                }
                .padding(.horizontal, 24)
                .padding(.bottom, 8)
            }
            .background(.black)
            .preferredColorScheme(.dark)
    }
}

private func demoPhoto() -> Image {
    let size = CGSize(width: 800, height: 1000)
    return Image(size: size, label: Text("Coastline")) { context in
        context.fill(
            Path(CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size)),
            with: .linearGradient(Gradient(colors: [.cyan, .blue, .indigo]), startPoint: .zero, endPoint: CGPoint(x: 0, y: 1000))
        )
        context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: 120, y: 130, width: 180, height: 180)), with: .color(.yellow.opacity(0.9)))

        var shore = Path()
        shore.move(to: CGPoint(x: 800, y: 1000))
        shore.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: 1000))
        shore.addCurve(to: CGPoint(x: 800, y: 420), control1: CGPoint(x: 360, y: 820), control2: CGPoint(x: 460, y: 560))
        shore.closeSubpath()
        context.fill(shore, with: .color(Color(red: 0.95, green: 0.8, blue: 0.55)))
    }
}
```

## Double Tap Zoom Image

An image that zooms in on the point you double tap and returns to fit on the next double tap.

Category: Images. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Images/DoubleTapZoomImage/DoubleTapZoomImage.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum DoubleTapZoomImageMath {
    /// How far a zoomed image can move before showing an empty edge.
    static func clampedOffset(_ offset: CGSize, zoom: CGFloat, in size: CGSize) -> CGSize {
        let limit = CGSize(width: max((zoom - 1) * size.width / 2, 0), height: max((zoom - 1) * size.height / 2, 0))
        return CGSize(
            width: min(max(offset.width, -limit.width), limit.width),
            height: min(max(offset.height, -limit.height), limit.height)
        )
    }

    /// The offset that brings a tapped point as close to the center as the image's edges allow.
    static func offset(centering point: CGPoint, zoom: CGFloat, in size: CGSize) -> CGSize {
        let wanted = CGSize(width: (size.width / 2 - point.x) * zoom, height: (size.height / 2 - point.y) * zoom)
        return clampedOffset(wanted, zoom: zoom, in: size)
    }
}

/// An image that zooms in on the point you double tap and returns to fit on the next double tap.
///
/// While zoomed, a drag pans the image. At rest it leaves drags to the scroll view around it.
/// With Reduce Motion on, the zoom changes without animating.
struct DoubleTapZoomImage: View {
    let image: Image
    let label: LocalizedStringResource
    var zoom: CGFloat = 2.5
    /// Zooms in on this point without a touch, for demos. `nil` returns to fit.
    var programmaticZoom: UnitPoint? = nil

    @State private var isZoomed = false
    @State private var offset = CGSize.zero
    @GestureState private var translation = CGSize.zero
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var targetZoom: CGFloat { max(zoom, 1) }

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let size = geometry.size
            let shown = CGSize(width: offset.width + translation.width, height: offset.height + translation.height)

            image
                .resizable()
                .scaledToFill()
                .frame(width: size.width, height: size.height)
                .scaleEffect(isZoomed ? targetZoom : 1)
                .offset(isZoomed ? DoubleTapZoomImageMath.clampedOffset(shown, zoom: targetZoom, in: size) : .zero)
                .frame(width: size.width, height: size.height)
                .contentShape(.rect)
                .gesture(
                    SpatialTapGesture(count: 2).onEnded { value in
                        toggleZoom(at: value.location, in: size)
                    }
                )
                .gesture(pan(in: size), including: isZoomed ? .all : .subviews)
                .onChange(of: programmaticZoom) { _, target in
                    setZoom(target.map { CGPoint(x: $0.x * size.width, y: $0.y * size.height) }, in: size)
                }
                .accessibilityLabel(label)
                .accessibilityValue(isZoomed ? "Zoomed in" : "Fit")
                .accessibilityAddTraits(.isImage)
                .accessibilityAction(named: isZoomed ? "Zoom out" : "Zoom in") {
                    toggleZoom(at: CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2), in: size)
                }
        }
        // A photo is not mirrored in right-to-left layouts, so neither is the geometry that moves it.
        .environment(\.layoutDirection, .leftToRight)
        .clipped()
    }

    private func pan(in size: CGSize) -> some Gesture {
        DragGesture()
            .updating($translation) { value, state, _ in
                state = value.translation
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                let moved = CGSize(width: offset.width + value.translation.width, height: offset.height + value.translation.height)
                offset = DoubleTapZoomImageMath.clampedOffset(moved, zoom: targetZoom, in: size)
            }
    }

    private func toggleZoom(at point: CGPoint, in size: CGSize) {
        setZoom(isZoomed ? nil : point, in: size)
    }

    private func setZoom(_ point: CGPoint?, in size: CGSize) {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.15)) {
            offset = point.map { DoubleTapZoomImageMath.offset(centering: $0, zoom: targetZoom, in: size) } ?? .zero
            isZoomed = point != nil
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct DoubleTapZoomImageDemo: View {
    private let photo = demoPhoto()

    @State private var zoomTarget: UnitPoint?
    /// Only for this demo: it plays by itself until someone touches it.
    @State private var isAutoPlaying = true
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 16) {
            DoubleTapZoomImage(image: photo, label: "City skyline at night", programmaticZoom: zoomTarget)
                .aspectRatio(3 / 4, contentMode: .fit)
                .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 24))

            Label("Double tap anywhere", systemImage: "hand.tap.fill")
                .font(.headline)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
        .padding(16)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .simultaneousGesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { _ in isAutoPlaying = false })
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            await playZooms()
        }
    }

    // Only the demo plays by itself, because a real double tap needs a finger.
    private func playZooms() async {
        let targets: [UnitPoint?] = [UnitPoint(x: 0.75, y: 0.2), nil, UnitPoint(x: 0.3, y: 0.7), nil]
        while isAutoPlaying {
            for target in targets {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.2))
                guard !Task.isCancelled, isAutoPlaying else { return }
                zoomTarget = target
            }
        }
    }
}

private func demoPhoto() -> Image {
    let size = CGSize(width: 900, height: 1200)
    return Image(size: size, label: Text("City skyline at night")) { context in
        context.fill(
            Path(CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size)),
            with: .linearGradient(Gradient(colors: [.black, .indigo, .purple]), startPoint: .zero, endPoint: CGPoint(x: 0, y: 1200))
        )
        context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: 620, y: 140, width: 150, height: 150)), with: .color(.white.opacity(0.9)))

        let heights: [CGFloat] = [520, 760, 440, 880, 620, 700, 480]
        for (column, height) in heights.enumerated() {
            let x = CGFloat(column) * 130 - 5
            let tower = CGRect(x: x, y: 1200 - height, width: 120, height: height)
            context.fill(Path(tower), with: .color(Color(white: 0.09)))

            for row in stride(from: tower.minY + 30, to: tower.maxY - 30, by: 64) {
                for offset in [CGFloat(18), 70] where (column + Int(row) / 64 + Int(offset)).isMultiple(of: 3) == false {
                    context.fill(Path(CGRect(x: x + offset, y: row, width: 32, height: 34)), with: .color(.yellow.opacity(0.8)))
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    DoubleTapZoomImageDemo()
}
```

## Ken Burns Image

A still picture that slowly zooms and pans so that it appears to move.

Category: Images. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Images/KenBurnsImage/KenBurnsImage.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A still picture that slowly zooms and pans so that it appears to move.
///
/// It fills the space it is given and never shows an edge, because it only scales up around a
/// point inside the image. With Reduce Motion on, the picture stays still.
struct KenBurnsImage: View {
    let image: Image
    let label: LocalizedStringResource
    var duration: Double = 12
    var zoom: CGFloat = 1.3
    var from: UnitPoint = .topLeading
    var to: UnitPoint = .bottomTrailing

    @State private var isAtEnd = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var animation: Animation? {
        reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: max(duration, 0.1)).repeatForever(autoreverses: true)
    }

    var body: some View {
        Color.clear
            .overlay {
                image
                    .resizable()
                    .scaledToFill()
                    .scaleEffect(isAtEnd ? max(zoom, 1) : 1.02, anchor: isAtEnd ? to : from)
            }
            .clipped()
            .animation(animation, value: isAtEnd)
            .task(id: reduceMotion) { isAtEnd = !reduceMotion }
            .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
            .accessibilityLabel(label)
            .accessibilityAddTraits(.isImage)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct KenBurnsImageDemo: View {
    private let photo = demoPhoto()

    var body: some View {
        KenBurnsImage(image: photo, label: "Mountains at sunset", duration: 4, zoom: 1.6)
            .ignoresSafeArea()
            .overlay(alignment: .bottomLeading) {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                    Text("Sunset Ridge")
                        .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                    Text("Golden hour in the valley")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .opacity(0.85)
                }
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.4), radius: 8, y: 2)
                .padding(24)
            }
    }
}

private func demoPhoto() -> Image {
    let size = CGSize(width: 900, height: 1600)
    return Image(size: size, label: Text("Mountains at sunset")) { context in
        context.fill(
            Path(CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size)),
            with: .linearGradient(
                Gradient(colors: [.indigo, .pink, .orange, .yellow]),
                startPoint: .zero,
                endPoint: CGPoint(x: 0, y: 1150)
            )
        )
        context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: 280, y: 600, width: 340, height: 340)), with: .color(.white.opacity(0.8)))

        let ridges: [(base: CGFloat, color: Color)] = [
            (980, Color(red: 0.42, green: 0.2, blue: 0.5)),
            (1140, Color(red: 0.26, green: 0.14, blue: 0.42)),
            (1320, Color(red: 0.12, green: 0.08, blue: 0.26)),
        ]
        for (index, ridge) in ridges.enumerated() {
            let flip: CGFloat = index.isMultiple(of: 2) ? 1 : -1
            var path = Path()
            path.move(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height))
            path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: ridge.base))
            path.addCurve(
                to: CGPoint(x: size.width, y: ridge.base - 40 * flip),
                control1: CGPoint(x: 300, y: ridge.base - 220 * flip),
                control2: CGPoint(x: 620, y: ridge.base + 200 * flip)
            )
            path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height))
            path.closeSubpath()
            context.fill(path, with: .color(ridge.color))
        }
    }
}
```

## Photo Adjustment Sliders

Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue sliders that update a photo live as they move.

Category: Images. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Images/PhotoAdjustmentSliders/PhotoAdjustmentSliders.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct PhotoAdjustmentSlidersValues: Equatable, Sendable {
    var brightness = 0.0
    var contrast = 1.0
    var saturation = 1.0
    var hue = 0.0
}

extension View {
    func adjusted(by values: PhotoAdjustmentSlidersValues) -> some View {
        saturation(values.saturation)
            .contrast(values.contrast)
            .brightness(values.brightness)
            .hueRotation(.degrees(values.hue))
    }
}

/// Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue sliders that update a photo live as they move.
///
/// The whole view scrolls, so every slider stays reachable at the largest text sizes.
struct PhotoAdjustmentSliders: View {
    let image: Image
    @Binding var values: PhotoAdjustmentSlidersValues
    var maxImageHeight: CGFloat = 340

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(spacing: 18) {
                image
                    .resizable()
                    .scaledToFit()
                    .adjusted(by: values)
                    .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 20))
                    .frame(maxHeight: max(maxImageHeight, 0))

                VStack(spacing: 12) {
                    row("Brightness", $values.brightness, in: -0.5...0.5, shown: percent(values.brightness))
                    row("Contrast", $values.contrast, in: 0.5...1.5, shown: percent(values.contrast - 1))
                    row("Saturation", $values.saturation, in: 0...2, shown: percent(values.saturation - 1))
                    row("Hue", $values.hue, in: -180...180, shown: "\(Int(values.hue.rounded()))°")
                }

                Button("Reset", systemImage: "arrow.counterclockwise") {
                    withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: 0.3)) {
                        values = PhotoAdjustmentSlidersValues()
                    }
                }
                .buttonStyle(.bordered)
                .disabled(values == PhotoAdjustmentSlidersValues())
            }
            .padding(16)
        }
        .scrollBounceBehavior(.basedOnSize)
    }

    private func row(_ title: String, _ value: Binding<Double>, in range: ClosedRange<Double>, shown: String) -> some View {
        VStack(spacing: 2) {
            HStack {
                Text(title)
                Spacer()
                Text(shown)
                    .monospacedDigit()
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
            .font(.subheadline)
            .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Slider(value: value, in: range)
                .accessibilityLabel(title)
                .accessibilityValue(shown)
        }
    }

    private func percent(_ value: Double) -> String {
        let whole = Int((value * 100).rounded())
        return whole > 0 ? "+\(whole)%" : "\(whole)%"
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct PhotoAdjustmentSlidersDemo: View {
    @State private var values = PhotoAdjustmentSlidersValues()
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let photo = demoPhoto()

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 0) {
            ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
                looks
                ScrollView(.horizontal) { looks }
            }
            .padding(.top, 8)

            PhotoAdjustmentSliders(image: photo, values: $values)
        }
    }

    private var looks: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 8) {
            look("Vivid", PhotoAdjustmentSlidersValues(brightness: 0.05, contrast: 1.2, saturation: 1.7))
            look("Noir", PhotoAdjustmentSlidersValues(brightness: -0.05, contrast: 1.35, saturation: 0))
            look("Dream", PhotoAdjustmentSlidersValues(brightness: 0.1, contrast: 0.85, saturation: 1.2, hue: 60))
        }
    }

    private func look(_ title: String, _ target: PhotoAdjustmentSlidersValues) -> some View {
        Button(title) {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: 0.6)) { values = target }
        }
        .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    }
}

private func demoPhoto() -> Image {
    let size = CGSize(width: 1000, height: 800)
    return Image(size: size, label: Text("Lake at sunrise")) { context in
        context.fill(
            Path(CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size)),
            with: .linearGradient(Gradient(colors: [.blue, .pink, .orange]), startPoint: .zero, endPoint: CGPoint(x: 0, y: 460))
        )
        context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: 400, y: 240, width: 200, height: 200)), with: .color(.yellow))
        context.fill(
            Path(CGRect(x: 0, y: 460, width: 1000, height: 340)),
            with: .linearGradient(Gradient(colors: [.orange, .teal, .indigo]), startPoint: CGPoint(x: 0, y: 460), endPoint: CGPoint(x: 0, y: 800))
        )

        var hills = Path()
        hills.move(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: 470))
        hills.addCurve(to: CGPoint(x: 1000, y: 470), control1: CGPoint(x: 300, y: 250), control2: CGPoint(x: 700, y: 620))
        hills.closeSubpath()
        context.fill(hills, with: .color(.green.opacity(0.8)))
    }
}
```
