```swift
                    Text("Today")
                        .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                    SubviewCardContainer {
                        Label("A static child", systemImage: "square.fill")
                            .font(.headline)
                            .subviewCardTint(.indigo)

                        Text("Plain text becomes a card too, with no wrapper around it.")
                            .subviewCardTint(.blue)

                        ForEach(0..<reminders, id: \.self) { index in
                            Label("Child \(index + 1) from a ForEach", systemImage: "bell.fill")
                                .subviewCardTint(Self.colors[index])
                        }
                    }
                }
                .padding(20)
            }

            HStack(spacing: 14) {
                Button("Remove", systemImage: "minus") { change(by: -1) }
                    .disabled(reminders == 0)
                Button("Add", systemImage: "plus") { change(by: 1) }
                    .disabled(reminders == Self.colors.count)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
            .controlSize(.large)
        }
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo.opacity(0.1), .teal.opacity(0.1)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
    }

    private func change(by amount: Int) {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.35)) { reminders += amount }
    }
}
```

## Accordion Section

A stack of sections where opening one section closes the others, with the content height animated.

Category: Lists. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Lists/AccordionSection/AccordionSection.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A stack of sections where opening one closes the others. Bind `expandedID`
/// to open or close a section from outside.
struct AccordionSection<Data: RandomAccessCollection, Content: View>: View where Data.Element: Identifiable {
    let data: Data
    @Binding var expandedID: Data.Element.ID?
    let title: (Data.Element) -> String
    @ViewBuilder let content: (Data.Element) -> Content

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let cornerRadius: CGFloat = 16

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 10) {
            ForEach(data) { element in
                section(element)
            }
        }
    }

    private func section(_ element: Data.Element) -> some View {
        let isExpanded = expandedID == element.id

        return VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
            Button {
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.32)) {
                    expandedID = isExpanded ? nil : element.id
                }
            } label: {
                HStack {
                    Text(title(element))
                        .font(.headline)
                        .multilineTextAlignment(.leading)
                    Spacer(minLength: 12)
                    Image(systemName: "chevron.down")
                        .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                        .rotationEffect(.degrees(isExpanded ? 180 : 0))
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
                .padding(16)
                .contentShape(.rect)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
            .accessibilityLabel(title(element))
            .accessibilityValue(isExpanded ? "Expanded" : "Collapsed")

            if isExpanded {
                content(element)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                    .padding([.horizontal, .bottom], 16)
                    .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .opacity.combined(with: .move(edge: .top)))
            }
        }
        .background(.background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
        .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
    }
}

        }

    }
```

## Disclosure Tree View

A nested tree of rows that expand and collapse, indenting each level, for folders or category hierarchies.

Category: Lists. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Lists/DisclosureTreeView/DisclosureTreeView.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A node of the tree. Ids must be unique across the whole tree.
struct DisclosureTreeViewNode: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable {
    let id: String
    var title: String
    var systemImage = "doc"
    var children: [DisclosureTreeViewNode] = []
}

/// The rows on screen: every node whose ancestors are all expanded, in order.
enum DisclosureTreeViewRows {
    struct Row: Identifiable, Equatable {
        let node: DisclosureTreeViewNode
        let depth: Int

        var id: String { node.id }
    }

    static func visible(in nodes: [DisclosureTreeViewNode], expanded: Set<String>, depth: Int = 0) -> [Row] {
        nodes.flatMap { node -> [Row] in
            let row = Row(node: node, depth: depth)
            guard expanded.contains(node.id) else { return [row] }
            return [row] + visible(in: node.children, expanded: expanded, depth: depth + 1)
        }
    }

    /// The indent of a row. Very deep rows and very large text stop adding to it, so the title has room.
    static func indent(depth: Int, step: Double) -> Double {
        Double(min(depth, 6)) * min(step, 24)
    }
}

/// A nested tree of rows that expand and collapse, indenting each level.
struct DisclosureTreeView: View {
    let nodes: [DisclosureTreeViewNode]
    @Binding var expandedIDs: Set<String>

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) private var indent = 20.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
            ForEach(DisclosureTreeViewRows.visible(in: nodes, expanded: expandedIDs)) { row in
                rowView(row)
                    .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .opacity.combined(with: .move(edge: .top)))
            }
        }
    }

    @ViewBuilder
    private func rowView(_ row: DisclosureTreeViewRows.Row) -> some View {
        if row.node.children.isEmpty {
            rowLabel(row, isExpanded: false)
                .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
                .accessibilityLabel(row.node.title)
                .accessibilityValue("Level \(row.depth + 1)")
        } else {
            let isExpanded = expandedIDs.contains(row.id)

            Button {
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.28)) {
                    if isExpanded {
                        expandedIDs.remove(row.id)
                    } else {
                        expandedIDs.insert(row.id)
                    }
                }
            } label: {
                rowLabel(row, isExpanded: isExpanded)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
            .accessibilityLabel(row.node.title)
            .accessibilityValue("\(isExpanded ? "Expanded" : "Collapsed"), level \(row.depth + 1)")
        }
    }

    private func rowLabel(_ row: DisclosureTreeViewRows.Row, isExpanded: Bool) -> some View {
        HStack(spacing: 10) {
            Image(systemName: "chevron.forward")
                .font(.caption.weight(.bold))
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                .rotationEffect(.degrees(isExpanded ? 90 : 0))
                .opacity(row.node.children.isEmpty ? 0 : 1)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Image(systemName: row.node.systemImage)
                .foregroundStyle(.tint)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Text(row.node.title)
                .font(.body)
                .multilineTextAlignment(.leading)

            Spacer(minLength: 0)
        }
        .padding(.vertical, 10)
        .padding(.horizontal, 12)
        .padding(.leading, DisclosureTreeViewRows.indent(depth: row.depth, step: indent))
        .contentShape(.rect)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct DisclosureTreeViewDemo: View {
    private static let tree = [
        DisclosureTreeViewNode(id: "sources", title: "Sources", systemImage: "folder.fill", children: [
            DisclosureTreeViewNode(id: "components", title: "Components", systemImage: "folder.fill", children: [
                DisclosureTreeViewNode(id: "button", title: "Button.swift", systemImage: "swift"),
                DisclosureTreeViewNode(id: "card", title: "Card.swift", systemImage: "swift"),
            ]),
            DisclosureTreeViewNode(id: "app", title: "App.swift", systemImage: "swift"),
        ]),
        DisclosureTreeViewNode(id: "tests", title: "Tests", systemImage: "folder.fill", children: [
            DisclosureTreeViewNode(id: "buttontests", title: "ButtonTests.swift", systemImage: "checkmark.seal"),
        ]),
        DisclosureTreeViewNode(id: "readme", title: "README.md", systemImage: "doc.text"),
    ]

    @State private var expandedIDs: Set<String> = []

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
                Text("Project")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                    .padding(.horizontal, 12)

                DisclosureTreeView(nodes: Self.tree, expandedIDs: $expandedIDs)
                    .padding(.vertical, 8)
                    .background(.background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 18, style: .continuous))

            .padding(20)
        }
```

## Edit Mode Multi Select

A list with a Select mode that shows selection circles on each row and a bottom bar of bulk actions.

Category: Lists. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Lists/EditModeMultiSelect/EditModeMultiSelect.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A list with a Select mode: selection circles on each row and a bottom bar of bulk actions.
///
/// Place it inside a `NavigationStack`, because Select and Done go in the toolbar.
/// With Reduce Motion on, the bar appears without sliding.
struct EditModeMultiSelect<Row: Identifiable, RowContent: View, Actions: View>: View {
    let rows: [Row]
    @Binding var selection: Set<Row.ID>
    @ViewBuilder var rowContent: (Row) -> RowContent
    /// The bulk actions. They are disabled while nothing is selected.
    @ViewBuilder var actions: () -> Actions

    @State private var editMode: EditMode = .inactive
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var isEditing: Bool { editMode.isEditing }
    private var allSelected: Bool { !rows.isEmpty && selection.count >= rows.count }

    var body: some View {
        List(rows, selection: $selection) { row in
            rowContent(row)
        }
        .environment(\.editMode, $editMode)
        .overlay {
            if rows.isEmpty {
                ContentUnavailableView("Nothing here", systemImage: "tray")
            }
        }
        .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom, spacing: 0) {
            if isEditing {
                bulkBar.transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .move(edge: .bottom).combined(with: .opacity))
            }
        }
        .toolbar {
            ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarTrailing) {
                Button(isEditing ? "Done" : "Select") { setEditing(!isEditing) }
                    .disabled(rows.isEmpty && !isEditing)
            }
            if isEditing {
                ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarLeading) {
                    Button(allSelected ? "Deselect All" : "Select All", action: toggleAll)
                }
            }
        }
        .onChange(of: rows.map(\.id)) { _, ids in
            selection.formIntersection(ids)
            if ids.isEmpty { setEditing(false) }
        }
    }

    private var bulkBar: some View {
        ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
            HStack(spacing: 16) {
                selectedCount
                Spacer(minLength: 0)
                actionRow
            }
            VStack(spacing: 10) {
                selectedCount
                actionRow
            }
        }
        .padding(.horizontal, 20)
        .padding(.vertical, 12)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
        .background(.bar)
    }

    private var selectedCount: some View {
        Text("\(selection.count) selected")
            .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
            .monospacedDigit()
    }

    private var actionRow: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 20) { actions() }
            .disabled(selection.isEmpty)
    }

    private func setEditing(_ editing: Bool) {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy) {
            editMode = editing ? .active : .inactive
            if !editing { selection.removeAll() }
        }
    }

    private func toggleAll() {
        selection = allSelected ? [] : Set(rows.map(\.id))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct EditModeMultiSelectDemoMail: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let subtitle: String
    let systemImage: String
    let tint: Color
}

        EditModeMultiSelectDemoMail(id: "Photos", subtitle: "12 new shared photos", systemImage: "photo.fill", tint: .purple),
        EditModeMultiSelectDemoMail(id: "Banking", subtitle: "Your statement is available", systemImage: "creditcard.fill", tint: .teal),
        EditModeMultiSelectDemoMail(id: "Podcasts", subtitle: "A new episode just landed", systemImage: "mic.fill", tint: .pink),
        EditModeMultiSelectDemoMail(id: "Fitness", subtitle: "You closed all your rings", systemImage: "figure.run", tint: .mint),
    ]
    @State private var selection = Set<String>()
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .headline) private var iconSize = 40.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {

                HStack(spacing: 14) {

                        .font(.headline)

                            .font(.subheadline)
```

## Load More Footer

An infinite list footer that requests the next page when it appears and shows loading, retry and end states.

Category: Lists. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Lists/LoadMoreFooter/LoadMoreFooter.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum LoadMoreFooterPhase: Equatable, Sendable {
    case idle, loading, failed, finished
}

struct LoadMoreFooterPage<Element> {
    let elements: [Element]
    let hasMore: Bool
}

/// Holds the loaded pages and makes sure only one request runs at a time.
@MainActor
@Observable
final class LoadMoreFooterPager<Element> {
    private(set) var elements: [Element] = []
    private(set) var phase = LoadMoreFooterPhase.idle

    private var nextPage = 0
    private let fetch: @MainActor (Int) async throws -> LoadMoreFooterPage<Element>

    init(fetch: @escaping @MainActor (Int) async throws -> LoadMoreFooterPage<Element>) {
        self.fetch = fetch
    }

    func loadNextPage() async {
        guard phase == .idle || phase == .failed else { return }
        phase = .loading
        do {
            let page = try await fetch(nextPage)
            elements += page.elements
            nextPage += 1
            phase = page.hasMore && !page.elements.isEmpty ? .idle : .finished
        } catch is CancellationError {
            phase = .idle
        } catch {
            phase = .failed
        }
    }
}

/// The last row of an infinite list. It asks for the next page as soon as it appears.
struct LoadMoreFooter: View {
    let phase: LoadMoreFooterPhase
    var finishedText = "You're all caught up"
    let onLoad: () -> Void

    var body: some View {
        Group {
            switch phase {
            case .idle:
                ProgressView()
                    .accessibilityLabel("Loading more")
                    .onAppear(perform: onLoad)
            case .loading:
                ProgressView()
                    .accessibilityLabel("Loading more")
            case .failed:
                Button("Try again", systemImage: "arrow.clockwise", action: onLoad)
                    .buttonStyle(.bordered)
            case .finished:
                Text(finishedText)
                    .font(.footnote)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
        .padding(.vertical, 20)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct LoadMoreFooterDemo: View {
    @State private var pager = LoadMoreFooterPager<Int>(fetch: Self.fetchPage)
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .headline) private var iconSize = 52.0

    private static func fetchPage(_ page: Int) async throws -> LoadMoreFooterPage<Int> {
        try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.9))
        return LoadMoreFooterPage(elements: Array((page * 8)..<((page + 1) * 8)), hasMore: page < 3)
    }

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            ScrollView {
                LazyVStack(spacing: 12) {
                    ForEach(pager.elements, id: \.self, content: row)

                    LoadMoreFooter(phase: pager.phase) {
                        Task { await pager.loadNextPage() }
                    }
                }
                .padding(.horizontal, 16)
            }
            .navigationTitle("Stories")
            .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)
        }
    }

    private func row(_ number: Int) -> some View {
        let hue = Double(number % 8) / 8
        return HStack(spacing: 14) {
            Image(systemName: "sparkles")
                .font(.title3)
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .frame(width: iconSize, height: iconSize)
                .background(Color(hue: hue, saturation: 0.65, brightness: 0.85).gradient, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 14))
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 3) {
                Text("Story \(number + 1)").font(.headline)
                Text("A short line about this story")
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }

            Spacer(minLength: 0)
        }
        .padding(14)
        .background(.fill.quaternary, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 20))
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
    }
}

#Preview {
    LoadMoreFooterDemo()
}
```

## Reorderable Card List

A stack of cards you can drag into a new order, without using List.

Category: Lists. Minimum: iOS 27.0. Path: Components/Lists/ReorderableCardList/ReorderableCardList.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A stack of cards the user can drag into a new order, without using `List`.
@available(iOS 27, *)
struct ReorderableCardList<Item: Identifiable & Sendable, Card: View>: View where Item.ID: Sendable {
    @Binding var items: [Item]
    @ViewBuilder let card: (Item) -> Card

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(spacing: 12) {
                ForEach(items) { item in
                    card(item)
                }
                .reorderable()
            }
            .padding()
            .reorderContainer(for: Item.self) { difference in
                let destination: Item.ID? = switch difference.destination.position {
                case .before(let id): id
                case .end: nil
                }
                items = CardReordering.moving(difference.sources, before: destination, in: items)
            }
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 27, *)
enum CardReordering {
    /// Moves `sources` in front of `destination`, or to the end when it is nil.
    static func moving<Item: Identifiable>(
        _ sources: [Item.ID],
        before destination: Item.ID?,
        in items: [Item]
    ) -> [Item] {
        if let destination, sources.contains(destination) { return items }

        let moved = sources.compactMap { source in items.first { $0.id == source } }
        var remaining = items.filter { !sources.contains($0.id) }
        let index = remaining.firstIndex { $0.id == destination } ?? remaining.endIndex
        remaining.insert(contentsOf: moved, at: index)
        return remaining
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 27, *)
struct ReorderableCardListDemo: View {
    nonisolated private struct Step: Identifiable, Sendable {
        let id: String
        let systemImage: String
        let color: Color
    }

        Step(id: "Build", systemImage: "hammer.fill", color: .orange),
        Step(id: "Test", systemImage: "checkmark.seal.fill", color: .green),
        Step(id: "Ship", systemImage: "paperplane.fill", color: .blue),
    ]

    var body: some View {

                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text(step.id)
                    .font(.title3.bold())

                Spacer()

                Image(systemName: "line.3.horizontal")
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .padding()
            .background(.background.secondary, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 20))
        }
    }
}
```

## Reorderable Grid

A grid of tiles the user can drag into a new order.

Category: Lists. Minimum: iOS 27.0. Path: Components/Lists/ReorderableGrid/ReorderableGrid.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A grid of tiles the user can drag into a new order.
@available(iOS 27, *)
struct ReorderableGrid<Item: Identifiable & Sendable, Tile: View>: View where Item.ID: Sendable {
    @Binding var items: [Item]
    var minimumTileWidth: CGFloat = 100
    var spacing: CGFloat = 14
    @ViewBuilder let tile: (Item) -> Tile

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            LazyVGrid(columns: [GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: minimumTileWidth), spacing: spacing)], spacing: spacing) {
                ForEach(items) { item in
                    tile(item)
                }
                .reorderable()
            }
            .padding()
            .reorderContainer(for: Item.self) { difference in
                let destination: Item.ID? = switch difference.destination.position {
                case .before(let id): id
                case .end: nil
                }
                items = ReorderableGridReordering.moving(difference.sources, before: destination, in: items)
            }
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 27, *)
enum ReorderableGridReordering {
    /// Moves `sources` in front of `destination`, or to the end when it is nil.
    ///
    /// When `destination` is itself being moved, the first unmoved item after it is the anchor.
    static func moving<Item: Identifiable>(
        _ sources: [Item.ID],
        before destination: Item.ID?,
        in items: [Item]
    ) -> [Item] {
        let moved = sources.compactMap { source in items.first { $0.id == source } }
        var remaining = items.filter { !sources.contains($0.id) }

        let start = items.firstIndex { $0.id == destination } ?? items.endIndex
        let anchor = items[start...].first { !sources.contains($0.id) }
        let index = remaining.firstIndex { $0.id == anchor?.id } ?? remaining.endIndex

        remaining.insert(contentsOf: moved, at: index)
        return remaining
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo
```

## Swipe Action Cards

A column of cards with the system's swipe actions, outside a List.

Category: Lists. Minimum: iOS 27.0. Path: Components/Lists/SwipeActionCards/SwipeActionCards.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum SwipeActionCardsLogic {
    /// The items left after one is removed, in their order.
    static func removing<Item: Identifiable>(_ id: Item.ID, from items: [Item]) -> [Item] {
        items.filter { $0.id != id }
    }

    /// The items with one moved to the front, which is what pinning does. An unknown one changes nothing.
    static func pinning<Item: Identifiable>(_ id: Item.ID, in items: [Item]) -> [Item] {
        guard let index = items.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == id }) else { return items }
        var items = items
        items.insert(items.remove(at: index), at: 0)
        return items
    }
}

/// A column of cards with the system's swipe actions, outside a `List`: swipe a card to the
/// side to show its buttons, or all the way to run the first one.
///
/// Until iOS 27, `swipeActions` only worked on the rows of a `List`. `swipeActionsContainer`
/// brings it to any stack, so the cards can look however you want and keep the system's
/// gesture, haptics and VoiceOver actions.
@available(iOS 27, *)
struct SwipeActionCards<Item: Identifiable, Card: View, Actions: View>: View {
    let items: [Item]
    var spacing: CGFloat = 12
    @ViewBuilder var card: (Item) -> Card
    /// The buttons a card shows when it is swiped from its trailing edge, the first one outermost.
    @ViewBuilder var actions: (Item) -> Actions

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            LazyVStack(spacing: spacing) {
                ForEach(items) { item in
                    card(item)
                        .swipeActions(edge: .trailing, allowsFullSwipe: true) {
                            actions(item)
                        }
                }
            }
            .padding(16)
            .swipeActionsContainer()
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 27, *)
private struct SwipeActionCardsDemoTask: Identifiable {
    let id: Int
    let title: String
    let detail: String
    let symbol: String
    let color: Color
}

@available(iOS 27, *)
struct SwipeActionCardsDemo: View {
    @State private var tasks = [
        SwipeActionCardsDemoTask(id: 0, title: "Water the plants", detail: "Balcony and kitchen", symbol: "leaf.fill", color: .green),
```

## Arc Segments Loader

A spinner with gradient arc segments of different lengths turning in opposite directions.

Category: Loaders. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Loaders/ArcSegmentsLoader/ArcSegmentsLoader.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Two rings of arcs with different lengths, turning in opposite directions.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the arcs stay still.
struct ArcSegmentsLoader: View {
    var colors: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .purple, .pink]
    /// The length of each arc, as a fraction of the ring.
    var lengths: [Double] = [0.32, 0.16, 0.07]
    var size: CGFloat = 64
    var period: TimeInterval = 1.8

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var lineWidth: CGFloat { size * 0.075 }

    private var arcs: [ClosedRange<Double>] {
        let gap = max(0, 1 - lengths.reduce(0, +)) / Double(max(lengths.count, 1))
        var start = 0.0
        return lengths.map { length in
            defer { start += length + gap }
            return start...(start + length)
        }
    }

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            let turns = reduceMotion ? 0 : context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate / period

            ZStack {
                ring(inset: 0)
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(turns * 360))

                ring(inset: size * 0.2)
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(-turns * 360 * 1.4 + 90))
                    .opacity(0.7)
            }
            .frame(width: size, height: size)
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Loading")
    }

    private func ring(inset: CGFloat) -> some View {
        ZStack {
            ForEach(arcs, id: \.lowerBound) { arc in
                Circle()
                    .trim(from: arc.lowerBound, to: arc.upperBound)
                    .stroke(
                        AngularGradient(colors: colors, center: .center),
                        style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round)
                    )
            }
        }
        .padding(lineWidth / 2 + inset)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ArcSegmentsLoaderDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .purple.opacity(0.6)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 40) {
                ArcSegmentsLoader(size: 260)

                VStack(spacing: 6) {
                    Text("Preparing your trip")
                        .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)

                    Text("Comparing the best routes")
                        .font(.body)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.75))
                }
                .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
    }
```

## Blob Morph Loader

A soft gradient blob drawn in a canvas that keeps changing shape while content loads.

Category: Loaders. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Loaders/BlobMorphLoader/BlobMorphLoader.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A soft blob that keeps changing shape, drawn in a canvas.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, it shows one still blob.
struct BlobMorphLoader: View {
    var colors: [Color] = [.pink, .purple, .indigo]
    var size: CGFloat = 96
    var speed: Double = 1

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed

            Canvas { canvas, canvasSize in
                let blob = BlobMorphOutline.path(in: canvasSize, time: time)
                let shading = BlobMorphOutline.shading(colors: colors, in: canvasSize, time: time)

                var glow = canvas
                glow.addFilter(.blur(radius: canvasSize.width * 0.08))
                glow.opacity = 0.55
                glow.fill(blob, with: shading)

                canvas.fill(blob, with: shading)
            }
            .frame(width: size, height: size)
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Loading")
    }
}

private enum BlobMorphOutline {
    static let pointCount = 16

    /// A closed curve through points whose distance from the center is a sum of moving sine waves.
    static func path(in size: CGSize, time: Double) -> Path {
        let center = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
        let base = min(size.width, size.height) * 0.31

        let points = (0..<pointCount).map { index -> CGPoint in
            let angle = Double(index) / Double(pointCount) * 2 * .pi
            let swell = 0.16 * sin(2 * angle + time * 1.4)
                + 0.10 * sin(3 * angle - time * 1.1)
                + 0.06 * sin(5 * angle + time * 0.7)
            let radius = base * (1 + swell)
            return CGPoint(x: center.x + cos(angle) * radius, y: center.y + sin(angle) * radius)
        }

        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: midpoint(points[pointCount - 1], points[0]))
        for index in 0..<pointCount {
            let next = points[(index + 1) % pointCount]
            path.addQuadCurve(to: midpoint(points[index], next), control: points[index])
        }
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }

    /// A gradient whose direction turns slowly, so the color drifts across the blob.
    static func shading(colors: [Color], in size: CGSize, time: Double) -> GraphicsContext.Shading {
        let center = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
        let reach = size.width * 0.4
        let offset = CGSize(width: cos(time * 0.6) * reach, height: sin(time * 0.6) * reach)

        return .linearGradient(
            Gradient(colors: colors),
            startPoint: CGPoint(x: center.x - offset.width, y: center.y - offset.height),
            endPoint: CGPoint(x: center.x + offset.width, y: center.y + offset.height)
        )
    }

    private static func midpoint(_ first: CGPoint, _ second: CGPoint) -> CGPoint {
        CGPoint(x: (first.x + second.x) / 2, y: (first.y + second.y) / 2)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct BlobMorphLoaderDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .indigo.opacity(0.7)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 12) {
                BlobMorphLoader(size: 300)

                Text("Thinking")
                    .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)

                Text("Your summary is almost ready")
                    .font(.body)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.75))
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    BlobMorphLoaderDemo()
}
```

## Dots Pulse Loader

Three dots that pulse in sequence, as in a typing indicator.

Category: Loaders. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Loaders/DotsPulseLoader/DotsPulseLoader.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Dots that pulse one after the other.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the dots stay still.
struct DotsPulseLoader: View {
    var color: Color = .indigo
    var dotCount: Int = 3
    var dotSize: CGFloat = 14

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Group {
            if reduceMotion {
                dots(activeIndex: nil)
            } else {
                PhaseAnimator(Array(0..<max(dotCount, 2))) { index in
                    dots(activeIndex: index)
                } animation: { _ in
                    .easeInOut(duration: 0.32)
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Loading")
    }

    private func dots(activeIndex: Int?) -> some View {
        HStack(spacing: dotSize * 0.6) {
            ForEach(0..<dotCount, id: \.self) { index in
                Circle()
                    .fill(color.gradient)
                    .frame(width: dotSize, height: dotSize)
                    .scaleEffect(scale(index: index, activeIndex: activeIndex))
                    .opacity(index == activeIndex || activeIndex == nil ? 1 : 0.4)
            }
        }
    }

    private func scale(index: Int, activeIndex: Int?) -> CGFloat {
        guard let activeIndex else { return 0.85 }
        return index == activeIndex ? 1.15 : 0.7
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct DotsPulseLoaderDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 48) {
            DotsPulseLoader(color: .indigo, dotSize: 44)

                    .padding(.horizontal, 16)
                    .padding(.vertical, 12)

                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .trailing)

                DotsPulseLoader(color: .secondary, dotSize: 10)
                    .padding(.horizontal, 18)
                    .padding(.vertical, 16)
                    .background(Color(.secondarySystemBackground), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 20))
            }
```

## Orbit Loader

A loading indicator with dots that orbit a glowing center.

Category: Loaders. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Loaders/OrbitLoader/OrbitLoader.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Dots that orbit a glowing center, bunching up and spreading out as they go.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the dots stay still, evenly spaced around the center.
struct OrbitLoader: View {
    var color: Color = .indigo
    var dotCount: Int = 3
    var size: CGFloat = 64
    var period: TimeInterval = 1.6

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            let turns = reduceMotion ? 0 : context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate / period

            ZStack {
                Circle()
                    .stroke(color.opacity(0.2), lineWidth: size * 0.02)
                    .padding(size * 0.1)

                Circle()
                    .fill(color.gradient)
                    .frame(width: size * 0.26, height: size * 0.26)
                    .shadow(color: color.opacity(0.6), radius: size * 0.1)

                ForEach(0..<dotCount, id: \.self) { index in
                    Circle()
                        .fill(color.gradient)
                        .frame(width: size * 0.16, height: size * 0.16)
                        .offset(dotOffset(index: index, turns: turns))
                }
            }
            .frame(width: size, height: size)
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Loading")
    }

    private func dotOffset(index: Int, turns: Double) -> CGSize {
        let position = turns + Double(index) / Double(max(dotCount, 1))
        let angle = (position + 0.1 * sin(position * 2 * .pi)) * 2 * .pi
        let radius = size * 0.4
        return CGSize(width: cos(angle) * radius, height: sin(angle) * radius)
    }
}

                        .foregroundStyle(.white)

                    Text("Looking for nearby devices")
                        .font(.body)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.75))
```

## Skeleton Shimmer Modifier

A view modifier that turns any view into a shimmering redacted placeholder while it loads.

Category: Loaders. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Loaders/SkeletonShimmerModifier/SkeletonShimmerModifier.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

extension View {
    /// Shows this view as a shimmering placeholder while `active` is true.
    ///
    /// Apply it to the content inside a card, not to the card: the shimmer masks the
    /// view, so a shadow drawn outside its bounds would be cut off.
    func skeletonShimmer(active: Bool) -> some View {
        modifier(SkeletonShimmerModifier(active: active))
    }
}

/// Redacts its content and sweeps a band of light across the placeholders.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the placeholders stay still and slightly dimmed.
struct SkeletonShimmerModifier: ViewModifier {
    var active: Bool
    var duration: TimeInterval = 1.4

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .redacted(reason: active ? .placeholder : [])
            .mask {
                TimelineView(.animation(paused: !active || reduceMotion)) { context in
                    mask(at: context.date)
                }
            }
            .allowsHitTesting(!active)
            .accessibilityElement(children: active ? .ignore : .contain)
            .accessibilityLabel("Loading", isEnabled: active)
    }

    private func mask(at date: Date) -> LinearGradient {
        guard active else {
            return LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .black], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing)
        }
        guard !reduceMotion else {
            let dimmed = Color.black.opacity(0.6)
            return LinearGradient(colors: [dimmed, dimmed], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing)
        }

        let progress = date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: duration) / duration
        let center = -0.5 + 2 * progress
        return LinearGradient(
            colors: [.black.opacity(0.35), .black, .black.opacity(0.35)],
            startPoint: UnitPoint(x: center - 0.5, y: 0.2),
            endPoint: UnitPoint(x: center + 0.5, y: 0.8)
        )
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow: Identifiable {
    let id = UUID()
    let name: String
    let message: String
    let time: String
    let color: Color
}

struct SkeletonShimmerModifierDemo: View {
    @State private var isLoading = true
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .headline) private var avatarSize = 46
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let rows = [
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Lucia Martin", message: "The photos from Sunday are up", time: "9:41", color: .pink),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Marco Rossi", message: "Can we move the call to four?", time: "9:12", color: .orange),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Aiko Tanaka", message: "Sent you the final invoice", time: "8:55", color: .teal),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Sam Porter", message: "Boarding now, see you tonight", time: "8:20", color: .indigo),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Nadia Haddad", message: "Loved the new onboarding", time: "Mon", color: .purple),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Tom Becker", message: "Tickets are booked for Friday", time: "Mon", color: .blue),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Elena Costa", message: "Recipe attached, enjoy it", time: "Sun", color: .green),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Ravi Patel", message: "The build is green again", time: "Sun", color: .mint),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        List {
            Section {
                ForEach(rows) { row in
                    rowContent(row)
                        .skeletonShimmer(active: isLoading)
                }
            } header: {
                Text("Messages")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                    .foregroundStyle(.primary)
                    .textCase(nil)
                    .padding(.bottom, 8)
            }
        }
        .task {
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2.2))
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: 0.35)) {
                    isLoading.toggle()
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private func rowContent(_ row: SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow) -> some View {
        HStack(spacing: 12) {
            Circle()
                .fill(isLoading ? Color(.systemGray4) : row.color)
                .frame(width: avatarSize, height: avatarSize)
                .overlay {
                    Image(systemName: "person.fill")
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .opacity(isLoading ? 0 : 1)
                }
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                Text(row.name)
                    .font(.headline)

                Text(row.message)
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }

            Spacer(minLength: 8)

            Text(row.time)
                .font(.caption)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
        .padding(.vertical, 4)
    }
}
```

## Wave Bars Loader

A loading indicator with bars that rise and fall like an audio equalizer.

Category: Loaders. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Loaders/WaveBarsLoader/WaveBarsLoader.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Bars that rise and fall like an equalizer.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the bars hold one uneven, still shape.
struct WaveBarsLoader: View {
    var colors: [Color] = [.blue, .cyan, .mint]
    var barCount: Int = 5
    var barWidth: CGFloat = 8
    var height: CGFloat = 44
    var speed: Double = 1

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed

            HStack(alignment: .bottom, spacing: barWidth * 0.6) {
                ForEach(0..<barCount, id: \.self) { index in
                    Capsule()
                        .fill(LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .bottom, endPoint: .top))
                        .frame(width: barWidth, height: barHeight(index: index, time: time))
                }
            }
            .frame(height: height, alignment: .bottom)
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Loading")
    }

    /// Two sine waves at different speeds keep the bars from looking like a plain wave.
    private func barHeight(index: Int, time: Double) -> CGFloat {
        let position = Double(index)
        let level = 0.55 + 0.3 * sin(time * 5 + position * 0.8) + 0.15 * sin(time * 9 + position * 1.7)
        return max(barWidth, height * level)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

                        .foregroundStyle(.white)

                    Text("Buffering your station")
                        .font(.body)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.75))
                }
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
    }
}
```

## Map Annotation Callout

Map pins with a short label that open a callout above them when tapped, while the camera moves to fit it.

Category: Maps. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Maps/MapAnnotationCallout/MapAnnotationCallout.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import MapKit
import SwiftUI

nonisolated struct MapAnnotationCalloutItem: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable {
    var id: String
    /// The short text on the pin, such as a price.
    var label: String
    var title: String
    var latitude: Double
    var longitude: Double

    var coordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D {
        CLLocationCoordinate2D(latitude: latitude, longitude: longitude)
    }
}

nonisolated enum MapAnnotationCalloutLogic {
    /// The latitude the camera centers on to show a pin together with its callout: a little north
    /// of the pin, because the callout opens above it. `span` is the latitude the map shows.
    static func centerLatitude(showing latitude: Double, span: Double, shift: Double = 0.2) -> Double {
        guard latitude.isFinite, span.isFinite else { return 0 }
        return min(max(latitude + max(span, 0) * shift, -90), 90)
    }

    /// The region that shows every item with some room around them. Nil when there are none.
    /// `smallest` keeps a single pin, or pins on one spot, from zooming all the way in.
    static func region(fitting items: [MapAnnotationCalloutItem], room: Double = 1.6, smallest: Double = 0.01) -> MKCoordinateRegion? {
        let latitudes = items.map(\.latitude).filter(\.isFinite)
        let longitudes = items.map(\.longitude).filter(\.isFinite)
        guard let south = latitudes.min(), let north = latitudes.max(),
              let west = longitudes.min(), let east = longitudes.max() else { return nil }

        return MKCoordinateRegion(
            center: CLLocationCoordinate2D(latitude: (south + north) / 2, longitude: (west + east) / 2),
            span: MKCoordinateSpan(
                latitudeDelta: min(max((north - south) * room, smallest), 180),
                longitudeDelta: min(max((east - west) * room, smallest), 360)
            )
        )
    }
}

/// A map of pins with a short label each. Tap one and it turns dark and opens a callout above
/// it with whatever you want to show, while the camera moves to fit both. Tap the map to close it.
///
/// VoiceOver reads each pin by its title and label. With Reduce Motion on, the callout fades in
/// and the camera does not fly.
struct MapAnnotationCallout<Callout: View>: View {
    let items: [MapAnnotationCalloutItem]
    @Binding var selection: MapAnnotationCalloutItem.ID?
    var calloutWidth: CGFloat = 220
    @ViewBuilder var callout: (MapAnnotationCalloutItem) -> Callout

    private let shadow = Color.black.opacity(0.2)

    @State private var position = MapCameraPosition.automatic
    @State private var visibleSpan = MKCoordinateSpan(latitudeDelta: 0.02, longitudeDelta: 0.02)
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Map(position: $position, selection: $selection) {
            ForEach(items) { item in
                Annotation(item.title, coordinate: item.coordinate, anchor: .bottom) {
                    pin(item)
                }
                .annotationTitles(.hidden)
                .tag(item.id)
            }
        }
        .mapStyle(.standard(pointsOfInterest: .excludingAll))
        .onMapCameraChange { context in
            visibleSpan = context.region.span
        }
        // The map starts on a region of its own, so the span is known from the start. With the
        // automatic camera it is not, and the first pin tapped also zoomed the map.
        .onAppear {
            guard let region = MapAnnotationCalloutLogic.region(fitting: items) else { return }
            position = .region(region)
            visibleSpan = region.span
        }
        .onChange(of: selection) { _, id in
            guard let item = items.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else { return }
            let latitude = MapAnnotationCalloutLogic.centerLatitude(showing: item.latitude, span: visibleSpan.latitudeDelta)
            let center = CLLocationCoordinate2D(latitude: latitude, longitude: item.longitude)
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.6)) {
                position = .region(MKCoordinateRegion(center: center, span: visibleSpan))
            }
        }
    }

    private func pin(_ item: MapAnnotationCalloutItem) -> some View {
        let isSelected = item.id == selection

        return VStack(spacing: 6) {
            if isSelected {
                callout(item)
                    .frame(width: calloutWidth, alignment: .leading)
                    .padding(12)
                    .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 18))
                    .shadow(color: shadow, radius: 10, y: 4)
                    .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .scale(scale: 0.6, anchor: .bottom).combined(with: .opacity))
            }

            Text(item.label)
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.bold))
                .padding(.horizontal, 10)
                .padding(.vertical, 6)
                .foregroundStyle(isSelected ? Color(.systemBackground) : Color.primary)
                .background(isSelected ? Color.primary : Color(.systemBackground), in: .capsule)
                .shadow(color: shadow, radius: 3, y: 1)
        }
        // Only opening is animated. The annotation shrinks at once when its callout goes, and a
        // callout still fading out would be drawn out of place.
        .animation(isSelected ? (reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.3)) : nil, value: isSelected)
        .accessibilityElement(children: isSelected ? .combine : .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel("\(item.title), \(item.label)")
        .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? [.isButton, .isSelected] : .isButton)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct MapAnnotationCalloutDemo: View {
    private let stays = [
        MapAnnotationCalloutItem(id: "loft", label: "$120", title: "Rooftop Loft", latitude: 38.7139, longitude: -9.1389),
        MapAnnotationCalloutItem(id: "studio", label: "$86", title: "Tiled Studio", latitude: 38.7109, longitude: -9.1422),

        MapAnnotationCalloutItem(id: "flat", label: "$145", title: "River View Flat", latitude: 38.7083, longitude: -9.1368),
        MapAnnotationCalloutItem(id: "attic", label: "$98", title: "Quiet Attic", latitude: 38.7157, longitude: -9.1338),
    ]

    @State private var selection: String?

    var body: some View {
        MapAnnotationCallout(items: stays, selection: $selection) { stay in
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
                LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                    .frame(height: 84)
                    .overlay {
                        Image(systemName: "house.fill")
                            .font(.title)
                            .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.9))
                    }
                    .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 10))

                Text(stay.title)

                Label("4.8 · 2 guests", systemImage: "star.fill")

            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Map Route Tracker

A route on a map with a marker that travels along it, the part done in solid and the rest dotted, like an order on its way.

Category: Maps. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Maps/MapRouteTracker/MapRouteTracker.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import MapKit
import SwiftUI

nonisolated struct MapRouteTrackerPoint: Hashable, Sendable {
    var latitude: Double
    var longitude: Double

    var coordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D {
        CLLocationCoordinate2D(latitude: latitude, longitude: longitude)
    }
}

nonisolated enum MapRouteTrackerMath {
    static let earthRadius = 6_371_000.0

    /// The meters between two points, over the surface of the Earth.
    static func distance(from start: MapRouteTrackerPoint, to end: MapRouteTrackerPoint) -> Double {
        let startLatitude = start.latitude * .pi / 180
        let endLatitude = end.latitude * .pi / 180
        let latitude = endLatitude - startLatitude
        let longitude = (end.longitude - start.longitude) * .pi / 180
        let chord = sin(latitude / 2) * sin(latitude / 2) + cos(startLatitude) * cos(endLatitude) * sin(longitude / 2) * sin(longitude / 2)
        return 2 * earthRadius * asin(min(sqrt(chord), 1))
    }

    /// The meters from the start of the route to each of its points.
    static func distances(along route: [MapRouteTrackerPoint]) -> [Double] {
        var total = 0.0
        return route.indices.map { index in
            if index > 0 { total += distance(from: route[index - 1], to: route[index]) }
            return total
        }
    }

    /// The point that is `progress` of the way along the route, from 0 at its start to 1 at its end.
    static func point(at progress: Double, on route: [MapRouteTrackerPoint]) -> MapRouteTrackerPoint? {
        split(route, at: progress).done.last
    }

    /// The route cut where `progress` falls: what is done, and what is left. Both have the cut point.
    static func split(_ route: [MapRouteTrackerPoint], at progress: Double) -> (done: [MapRouteTrackerPoint], left: [MapRouteTrackerPoint]) {
        guard let first = route.first else { return ([], []) }
        let distances = distances(along: route)
        let target = (progress.isFinite ? min(max(progress, 0), 1) : 0) * (distances.last ?? 0)
        // The first point the target has not passed yet. The cut is between it and the one before.
        guard let next = distances.indices.dropFirst().first(where: { distances[$0] >= target }) else {
            return ([first], route)
        }

        let length = distances[next] - distances[next - 1]
        let fraction = length > 0 ? (target - distances[next - 1]) / length : 0
        let cut = MapRouteTrackerPoint(
            latitude: route[next - 1].latitude + (route[next].latitude - route[next - 1].latitude) * fraction,
            longitude: route[next - 1].longitude + (route[next].longitude - route[next - 1].longitude) * fraction
        )
        return (Array(route[..<next]) + [cut], [cut] + Array(route[next...]))
    }
}

/// A route on a map with a marker that travels along it, like an order on its way: the part
/// already done is solid, the rest is dotted and the camera can follow the marker.
///
/// Set `progress` from 0 to 1 as the trip advances. The route is yours: take it from
/// `MKDirections` or from your own data.
struct MapRouteTracker: View {
    let route: [MapRouteTrackerPoint]
    /// How much of the route is done, from 0 to 1.
    var progress: Double
    var symbol = "bicycle"
    var color = Color.blue
    var markerTitle = "Courier"
    var destinationTitle = "Destination"
    /// Whether the camera travels with the marker. Otherwise it shows the whole route.
    var followsMarker = true
    /// How far above the marker the camera stays while it follows it, in meters.
    var followDistance = 2200.0

    private let lineWidth: CGFloat = 6

    @State private var position = MapCameraPosition.automatic
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) private var markerSize = 38.0

    var body: some View {
        let parts = MapRouteTrackerMath.split(route, at: progress)

        Map(position: $position) {
            if parts.left.count > 1 {
                MapPolyline(coordinates: parts.left.map(\.coordinate))
                    .stroke(color.opacity(0.45), style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round, dash: [1, lineWidth * 2]))
            }
            if parts.done.count > 1 {
                MapPolyline(coordinates: parts.done.map(\.coordinate))
                    .stroke(color, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
            }
            if let destination = route.last {
                Marker(destinationTitle, systemImage: "flag.checkered", coordinate: destination.coordinate)
                    .tint(color)
            }
            if let current = parts.done.last {
                Annotation(markerTitle, coordinate: current.coordinate) {
                    Image(systemName: symbol)
                        .font(.body.weight(.semibold))
                        .foregroundStyle(color)
                        .frame(width: markerSize, height: markerSize)
                        .background(.white, in: .circle)
                        .overlay { Circle().strokeBorder(color, lineWidth: 2) }
                        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.25), radius: 4, y: 2)
                        .accessibilityElement()
                        .accessibilityLabel(markerTitle)
                        .accessibilityValue(min(max(progress, 0), 1).formatted(.percent.precision(.fractionLength(0))))
                }
                .annotationTitles(.hidden)
            }
        }
        .mapStyle(.standard(pointsOfInterest: .excludingAll))
        .onChange(of: progress, initial: true) { follow() }
        .onChange(of: followsMarker) { follow() }
    }

    private func follow() {
        guard followsMarker, let current = MapRouteTrackerMath.point(at: progress, on: route) else {
            if !followsMarker { position = .automatic }
            return
        }
        position = .camera(MapCamera(centerCoordinate: current.coordinate, distance: followDistance))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct MapRouteTrackerDemo: View {
    private let route = [
        MapRouteTrackerPoint(latitude: 38.7158, longitude: -9.1420),
        MapRouteTrackerPoint(latitude: 38.7175, longitude: -9.1433),
        MapRouteTrackerPoint(latitude: 38.7193, longitude: -9.1448),
        MapRouteTrackerPoint(latitude: 38.7212, longitude: -9.1464),
        MapRouteTrackerPoint(latitude: 38.7232, longitude: -9.1481),
        MapRouteTrackerPoint(latitude: 38.7253, longitude: -9.1500),
    ]
    private let tripSeconds = 12.0
    private let tripMinutes = 9.0

    @State private var progress = 0.0
    @State private var isMoving = true
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        MapRouteTracker(route: route, progress: progress, color: .indigo, followsMarker: !reduceMotion)
            .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) {
                card
            }
            .task(id: isMoving) {
                guard isMoving else { return }
                let clock = ContinuousClock()
                var last = clock.now
                while !Task.isCancelled, progress < 1 {
                    try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(33))
                    let now = clock.now
                    progress = min(progress + (now - last) / .seconds(tripSeconds), 1)
                    last = now
                }
                if progress >= 1 { isMoving = false }
            }
    }

    private var card: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
            HStack {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
                    Text(progress < 1 ? "Arriving in \(Int(((1 - progress) * tripMinutes).rounded(.up))) min" : "Your order is here")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .contentTransition(.numericText())
                    Text("Alex is bringing your order")
                        .font(.subheadline)
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
                Spacer()
                Button(progress < 1 ? (isMoving ? "Pause" : "Resume") : "Restart", systemImage: progress < 1 ? (isMoving ? "pause.fill" : "play.fill") : "arrow.counterclockwise") {
                    if progress >= 1 {
                        progress = 0
                        isMoving = true
                    } else {
                        isMoving.toggle()
                    }
                }
                .labelStyle(.iconOnly)
                .buttonStyle(.bordered)
                .buttonBorderShape(.circle)
                // The regular size of an icon in a circle is too small to hit.
                .controlSize(.large)
            }

            ProgressView(value: progress)
                .accessibilityLabel("Trip progress")
        }
        .padding(18)
        .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 22))
        .padding(.horizontal, 16)
        .padding(.bottom, 8)
        .tint(.indigo)
    }
}

#Preview {
    MapRouteTrackerDemo()
}
```

## Map Search Sheet

A map with a sheet of places that rests at the bottom, filters as you type and flies to the place you choose.

Category: Maps. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Maps/MapSearchSheet/MapSearchSheet.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import MapKit
import SwiftUI

nonisolated struct MapSearchSheetPlace: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable {
    var id: String
    var name: String
    var kind: String
    var symbol: String
    var latitude: Double
    var longitude: Double

    var coordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D {
        CLLocationCoordinate2D(latitude: latitude, longitude: longitude)
    }
}

nonisolated enum MapSearchSheetLogic {
    /// The places whose name or kind has every word of `query`, whatever its case and accents.
    /// An empty query keeps them all.
    static func matches(_ places: [MapSearchSheetPlace], query: String) -> [MapSearchSheetPlace] {
        let words = folded(query).split(separator: " ")
        guard !words.isEmpty else { return places }
        return places.filter { place in
            let text = folded("\(place.name) \(place.kind)")
            return words.allSatisfy { text.contains($0) }
        }
    }

    private static func folded(_ text: String) -> String {
        text.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive], locale: nil)
    }
}

/// A map with a sheet of places that never goes away, like the one in Maps: it rests at the
/// bottom, at half height or full, and the map stays usable behind it.
///
/// Typing filters the list and the markers. Choosing a place, in the list or on the map, flies
/// the camera to it. The places are yours: fill them from `MKLocalSearch` or from your own data.
struct MapSearchSheet: View {
    let places: [MapSearchSheetPlace]
    var prompt: LocalizedStringResource = "Search places"
    /// How far above a chosen place the camera stops, in meters.
    var closeUpDistance = 1500.0

    private static let restingHeight: CGFloat = 76
    private static let resting = PresentationDetent.height(restingHeight)

    @State private var position = MapCameraPosition.automatic
    @State private var selection: MapSearchSheetPlace.ID?
    @State private var query = ""
    @State private var detent = PresentationDetent.medium
    @State private var isSheetPresented = false
    @State private var mapHeight: CGFloat = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var shown: [MapSearchSheetPlace] {
        MapSearchSheetLogic.matches(places, query: query)
    }

    var body: some View {
        Map(position: $position, selection: $selection) {
            ForEach(shown) { place in
                Marker(place.name, systemImage: place.symbol, coordinate: place.coordinate)
                    .tag(place.id)
            }
        }
        .mapStyle(.standard(pointsOfInterest: .excludingAll))
        // The whole height, safe area included: the padding below changes the safe area, and a
        // height that changed with it would never settle.
        .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { proxy in
            (proxy.size.height + proxy.safeAreaInsets.top + proxy.safeAreaInsets.bottom).rounded()
        } action: { mapHeight = $0 }
        // Keeps what the map centers on, and its legal label, in the part the sheet leaves free.
        .safeAreaPadding(.bottom, detent == Self.resting ? Self.restingHeight : mapHeight / 2)
        .onChange(of: selection) { _, id in
            guard let place = places.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else { return }
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.8)) {
                position = .camera(MapCamera(centerCoordinate: place.coordinate, distance: closeUpDistance))
            }
        }
        .onChange(of: query) {
            selection = nil
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth) { position = .automatic }
        }
        .sheet(isPresented: $isSheetPresented) {
            MapSearchSheetPanel(places: shown, prompt: prompt, query: $query, selection: $selection, detent: $detent)
                .presentationDetents([Self.resting, .medium, .large], selection: $detent)
                .presentationBackgroundInteraction(.enabled(upThrough: .medium))
                .presentationDragIndicator(.visible)
                .interactiveDismissDisabled()
        }
        .onAppear { isSheetPresented = true }
        .onDisappear { isSheetPresented = false }
    }
}

/// What the sheet shows: the search field and the places. It is a view of its own because the
/// focus of a field in a sheet has to be kept inside the sheet.
private struct MapSearchSheetPanel: View {
    let places: [MapSearchSheetPlace]
    let prompt: LocalizedStringResource
    @Binding var query: String
    @Binding var selection: MapSearchSheetPlace.ID?
    @Binding var detent: PresentationDetent

    @FocusState private var isSearching: Bool

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 0) {
            HStack(spacing: 8) {
                Image(systemName: "magnifyingglass")
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                TextField(text: $query) { Text(prompt) }
                    .focused($isSearching)
                    .submitLabel(.search)
                    .autocorrectionDisabled()

                if !query.isEmpty {
                    Button {
                        query = ""
                    } label: {
                        // The icon is too small to hit. The padding widens what answers to a
                        // touch, and the same padding taken back keeps the field as it was.
                        Label("Clear", systemImage: "xmark.circle.fill")
                            .padding(14)
                            .contentShape(.rect)
                            .padding(-14)
                    }
                    .labelStyle(.iconOnly)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .buttonStyle(.plain)
                }
            }
            .padding(10)
            .background(.fill.tertiary, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 12))
            .padding(.horizontal, 16)
            .padding(.top, 22)
            .padding(.bottom, 12)

            if places.isEmpty {
                ContentUnavailableView.search(text: query)
            } else {
                List(places) { place in
                    Button {
                        isSearching = false
                        selection = place.id
                        detent = .medium
                    } label: {
                        row(place)
                    }
                    .buttonStyle(.plain)
                    .listRowBackground(place.id == selection ? Color.accentColor.opacity(0.12) : Color.clear)
                    .accessibilityAddTraits(place.id == selection ? .isSelected : [])
                }
                .listStyle(.plain)
                .scrollContentBackground(.hidden)
            }
        }
        .frame(maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .top)
        .onChange(of: isSearching) { _, searching in
            if searching { detent = .large }
        }
    }

    private func row(_ place: MapSearchSheetPlace) -> some View {
        HStack(spacing: 12) {
            Image(systemName: place.symbol)
                .font(.body.weight(.semibold))
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .frame(width: 36, height: 36)
                .background(.tint, in: .circle)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
                Text(place.name)
                    .font(.headline)
                Text(place.kind)
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
            Spacer(minLength: 0)
        }
        .contentShape(.rect)
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct MapSearchSheetDemo: View {
    private let places = [
        MapSearchSheetPlace(id: "coffee", name: "Harbor Coffee", kind: "Café", symbol: "cup.and.saucer.fill", latitude: 38.7109, longitude: -9.1422),
        MapSearchSheetPlace(id: "bakery", name: "Blue Door Bakery", kind: "Bakery", symbol: "birthday.cake.fill", latitude: 38.7139, longitude: -9.1389),
        MapSearchSheetPlace(id: "books", name: "Old Town Books", kind: "Bookshop", symbol: "book.fill", latitude: 38.7118, longitude: -9.1331),
        MapSearchSheetPlace(id: "park", name: "Riverside Garden", kind: "Park", symbol: "tree.fill", latitude: 38.7076, longitude: -9.1362),
        MapSearchSheetPlace(id: "market", name: "Corner Market", kind: "Grocery", symbol: "cart.fill", latitude: 38.7163, longitude: -9.1432),
        MapSearchSheetPlace(id: "museum", name: "Tile Museum Café", kind: "Café", symbol: "cup.and.saucer.fill", latitude: 38.7157, longitude: -9.1338),
        MapSearchSheetPlace(id: "diner", name: "Tram Stop Diner", kind: "Restaurant", symbol: "fork.knife", latitude: 38.7095, longitude: -9.1301),

    var body: some View {
        MapSearchSheet(places: places)
            .tint(.indigo)
    }
}

    MapSearchSheetDemo()
```

## Audio Player Card

A podcast-style player card with artwork, a scrubber, skip buttons and a play and pause toggle.

Category: Media. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Media/AudioPlayerCard/AudioPlayerCard.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A podcast-style player card. It shows state and reports changes: wire it to your own player.
///
/// Pass any view as the artwork, usually `Image("cover").resizable().scaledToFill()`.
struct AudioPlayerCard<Artwork: View>: View {
    let title: String
    let subtitle: String
    let duration: TimeInterval
    @Binding var currentTime: TimeInterval
    @Binding var isPlaying: Bool
    /// Seconds per skip. Matching SF Symbols exist for 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90.
    var skipInterval = 15
    /// Called with `true` when a scrub starts and `false` when it ends.
    var onScrubbingChanged: (Bool) -> Void = { _ in }
    @ViewBuilder var artwork: () -> Artwork

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title) private var artworkSize = 84.0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var playSize = 62.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var safeDuration: TimeInterval { duration.isFinite ? min(max(duration, 0), 360_000) : 0 }
    private var position: TimeInterval { currentTime.isFinite ? min(max(currentTime, 0), safeDuration) : 0 }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 18) {
            HStack(spacing: 14) {
                artwork()
                    .frame(width: artworkSize, height: artworkSize)
                    .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 18))
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                    Text(title).font(.headline)
                    Text(subtitle).font(.subheadline).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            }

            VStack(spacing: 4) {
                Slider(
                    value: Binding(get: { position }, set: { currentTime = $0 }),
                    in: 0...max(safeDuration, 1),
                    onEditingChanged: onScrubbingChanged
                )
                .disabled(safeDuration == 0)
                .accessibilityLabel("Playback position")
                .accessibilityValue("\(timeText(position)) of \(timeText(safeDuration))")

                HStack {
                    Text(timeText(position))
                    Spacer()
                    Text("-" + timeText(safeDuration - position))
                }
                .font(.caption.monospacedDigit())
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }

            HStack(spacing: 36) {
                skipButton(forward: false)

                Button {
                    withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy) { isPlaying.toggle() }
                } label: {
                    Image(systemName: isPlaying ? "pause.fill" : "play.fill")
                        .font(.title)
                        .contentTransition(reduceMotion ? .identity : .symbolEffect(.replace))
                        .foregroundStyle(.background)
                        .frame(width: playSize, height: playSize)
                        .background(.primary, in: .circle)
                }
                .accessibilityLabel(isPlaying ? "Pause" : "Play")

                skipButton(forward: true)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
            .sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .light), trigger: isPlaying)
        }
        .padding(20)
        .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 28))
    }

    private func skipButton(forward: Bool) -> some View {
        let base = forward ? "goforward" : "gobackward"
        let hasNumberedSymbol = [5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90].contains(skipInterval)
        return Button {
            currentTime = min(max(position + Double(skipInterval) * (forward ? 1 : -1), 0), safeDuration)
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: hasNumberedSymbol ? "\(base).\(skipInterval)" : base)
                .font(.title2)
                .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44)
                .contentShape(.rect)
        }
        .disabled(safeDuration == 0)
        .accessibilityLabel(forward ? "Skip forward \(skipInterval) seconds" : "Skip back \(skipInterval) seconds")
    }

    private func timeText(_ seconds: TimeInterval) -> String {
        Duration.seconds(max(seconds, 0)).formatted(.time(pattern: .minuteSecond))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct AudioPlayerCardDemo: View {
    private let duration: TimeInterval = 96

    @State private var currentTime: TimeInterval = 18
    @State private var isPlaying = false
    @State private var isScrubbing = false

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple, .pink], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            ViewThatFits(in: .vertical) {
                card
                ScrollView { card }
            }
        }
        .task(id: isPlaying) {
            guard isPlaying else { return }
            while currentTime < duration {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(250))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                if !isScrubbing { currentTime += 0.25 }
            }
            isPlaying = false
        }
    }

    private var card: some View {
        AudioPlayerCard(
            title: "Small Screens, Big Ideas",
            subtitle: "Episode 12 · Design Notes",
            duration: duration,
            currentTime: $currentTime,
            isPlaying: $isPlaying,
            onScrubbingChanged: { isScrubbing = $0 }
        ) {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .overlay {
                    Image(systemName: "mic.fill")
                        .font(.largeTitle)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                }
        }
        .padding(20)
    }
}
```
