## Gooey Floating Menu

A floating button whose option bubbles melt and merge out of it like liquid.

Category: Menus. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Menus/GooeyFloatingMenu/GooeyFloatingMenu.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct GooeyFloatingMenuItem: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let systemImage: String
    let action: () -> Void
}

/// A floating button whose options melt out of it like liquid.
///
/// A `Canvas` blurs the circles and then cuts their alpha at a threshold, so shapes that
/// come close merge into one blob. It fits up to about five options, and the buttons
/// shrink when the width cannot hold the fan at their full size.
/// With Reduce Motion on, the options appear without moving.
struct GooeyFloatingMenu: View {
    let items: [GooeyFloatingMenuItem]
    var tint: Color = .indigo

    @State private var isOpen = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var animation: Animation? {
        reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.7, bounce: 0.25)
    }

    var body: some View {
        GooeyFloatingMenuStage(
            progress: isOpen ? 1 : 0,
            items: items,
            tint: tint,
            isOpen: isOpen,
            toggle: { withAnimation(animation) { isOpen.toggle() } },
            select: { item in
                withAnimation(animation) { isOpen = false }
                item.action()
            }
        )
        // The buttons only hold icons. The stage reads its size under this cap, which keeps the fan on screen.
        .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.xxxLarge)
    }
}

/// `Animatable` re-evaluates the body on every frame, so the drawing and the buttons share one progress.
private struct GooeyFloatingMenuStage: View, Animatable {
    var progress: Double
    let items: [GooeyFloatingMenuItem]
    let tint: Color
    let isOpen: Bool
    let toggle: () -> Void
    let select: (GooeyFloatingMenuItem) -> Void

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title2) private var scaledButtonSize = 64.0
    @State private var availableWidth = Double.infinity

    nonisolated var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    private var buttonSize: Double {
        GooeyFloatingMenuMath.fittedButtonSize(scaledButtonSize, availableWidth: availableWidth)
    }
    private var radius: Double { buttonSize * 2.1 }
    private var width: Double { (radius + buttonSize) * 2 }
    private var height: Double { radius + buttonSize * 2 }
    private var anchor: CGPoint { CGPoint(x: width / 2, y: height - buttonSize * 0.75) }

    private func center(of index: Int) -> CGPoint {
        let target = GooeyFloatingMenuMath.offset(index: index, count: items.count, radius: radius)
        let travel = GooeyFloatingMenuMath.staggered(progress, index: index, count: items.count)
        return CGPoint(x: anchor.x + target.width * travel, y: anchor.y + target.height * travel)
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Rectangle()
                .fill(tint.gradient)
                .mask { blobs }
                .shadow(color: tint.opacity(0.45), radius: 14, y: 8)
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, item in
                let travel = GooeyFloatingMenuMath.staggered(progress, index: index, count: items.count)

                Button { select(item) } label: {
                    Image(systemName: item.systemImage)
                        .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))
                        .foregroundStyle(GooeyFloatingMenuContrastingForeground(background: tint))
                        .frame(width: buttonSize * 0.8, height: buttonSize * 0.8)
                        .contentShape(.circle)
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
                .opacity(min(max(travel * 2 - 1, 0), 1))
                .position(center(of: index))
                .allowsHitTesting(isOpen)
                .accessibilityLabel(item.title)
                .accessibilityHidden(!isOpen)
            }

            Button(action: toggle) {
                Image(systemName: "plus")
                    .font(.title2.weight(.bold))
                    .foregroundStyle(GooeyFloatingMenuContrastingForeground(background: tint))
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(45 * progress))
                    .frame(width: buttonSize, height: buttonSize)
                    .contentShape(.circle)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
            .position(anchor)
            .accessibilityLabel("Menu")
            .accessibilityValue(isOpen ? "Open" : "Closed")
        }
        .frame(width: width, height: height)
        // The minimum makes this frame report the width on offer, not the wider stage inside it.
        .frame(minWidth: 0, maxWidth: width)
        .onGeometryChange(for: Double.self) { $0.size.width } action: { availableWidth = $0 }
    }

    private var blobs: some View {
        Canvas { context, _ in
            let blur = buttonSize * 0.2
            context.addFilter(.alphaThreshold(min: 0.5, color: .white))
            context.addFilter(.blur(radius: blur))

            context.drawLayer { layer in
                func circle(at center: CGPoint, diameter: Double) {
                    let rect = CGRect(x: center.x - diameter / 2, y: center.y - diameter / 2, width: diameter, height: diameter)
                    layer.fill(Path(ellipseIn: rect), with: .color(.white))
                }

                circle(at: anchor, diameter: buttonSize + blur * 0.5)
                for index in items.indices {
                    let travel = min(GooeyFloatingMenuMath.staggered(progress, index: index, count: items.count), 1)
                    circle(at: center(of: index), diameter: buttonSize * (0.55 + 0.3 * travel) + blur * 0.5)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

enum GooeyFloatingMenuMath {
    /// Where an option ends up, fanned across the top of the main button.
    static func offset(index: Int, count: Int, radius: Double) -> CGSize {
        let spread = Double.pi * 0.8
        let step = count > 1 ? spread / Double(count - 1) : 0
        let start = count > 1 ? -Double.pi / 2 - spread / 2 : -Double.pi / 2
        let angle = start + step * Double(index)
        return CGSize(width: cos(angle) * radius, height: sin(angle) * radius)
    }

    /// The size the width allows. The outer options reach just under 2.5 button sizes from the centre.
    static func fittedButtonSize(_ size: Double, availableWidth: Double) -> Double {
        min(size, availableWidth / 5)
    }

    /// Each option starts a little after the previous one, and all arrive together at 1.
    static func staggered(_ progress: Double, index: Int, count: Int) -> Double {
        guard count > 1 else { return max(progress, 0) }
        let delay = 0.35 * Double(index) / Double(count - 1)
        return max((progress - delay) / (1 - delay), 0)
    }
}

/// White or black, whichever reads better on `background`. Black only on a
/// light color, so the system's own colors keep white.
nonisolated struct GooeyFloatingMenuContrastingForeground: ShapeStyle {
    let background: Color

    func resolve(in environment: EnvironmentValues) -> Color {
        let color = background.resolve(in: environment)
        let luminance = 0.2126 * color.linearRed + 0.7152 * color.linearGreen + 0.0722 * color.linearBlue
        return luminance > 0.5 ? .black : .white
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct GooeyFloatingMenuDemo: View {
    @State private var lastAction = "Pick an option"

    private var items: [GooeyFloatingMenuItem] {
        [
            GooeyFloatingMenuItem(id: "camera", title: "Camera", systemImage: "camera.fill") { lastAction = "Camera" },
            GooeyFloatingMenuItem(id: "note", title: "Note", systemImage: "square.and.pencil") { lastAction = "Note" },
            GooeyFloatingMenuItem(id: "voice", title: "Voice", systemImage: "waveform") { lastAction = "Voice" },
            GooeyFloatingMenuItem(id: "favorite", title: "Favorite", systemImage: "heart.fill") { lastAction = "Favorite" },
        ]
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack(alignment: .bottom) {
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [Color(red: 0.07, green: 0.07, blue: 0.16), Color(red: 0.14, green: 0.1, blue: 0.3)],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )
            .ignoresSafeArea()

            Text(lastAction)
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)

            GooeyFloatingMenu(items: items, tint: .pink)
                .padding(.bottom, 24)
        }
```

## Animatable Ring

A progress ring whose arc animates through the @Animatable macro.

Category: Modern. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Modern/AnimatableRing/AnimatableRing.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// An arc from `start` to `end` degrees. `@Animatable` writes its `animatableData`.
@available(iOS 26, *)
@Animatable
nonisolated struct AnimatableRingArc: Shape {
    var start: Double
    var end: Double
    @AnimatableIgnored var clockwise = false

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        Path { path in
            path.addArc(
                center: CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY),
                radius: min(rect.width, rect.height) / 2,
                startAngle: .degrees(start - 90),
                endAngle: .degrees(end - 90),
                clockwise: clockwise
            )
        }
    }
}

/// A progress ring whose arc animates through the shape's own `animatableData`.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the ring jumps to the new value.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct AnimatableRing: View {
    let progress: Double
    var title: LocalizedStringKey = "Progress"
    var colors: [Color] = [.mint, .cyan, .blue, .mint]

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var lineWidth = 26.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var clamped: Double { min(max(progress, 0), 1) }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Circle()
                .stroke(.quaternary, lineWidth: lineWidth)

            AnimatableRingArc(start: 0, end: clamped * 360)
                .stroke(
                    AngularGradient(colors: colors, center: .center),
                    style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round)
                )

            Text(clamped, format: .percent.precision(.fractionLength(0)))
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .contentTransition(.numericText(value: clamped))
        }
        .padding(lineWidth / 2)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.8), value: clamped)
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(title)
        .accessibilityValue(Text(clamped, format: .percent.precision(.fractionLength(0))))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct AnimatableRingDemo: View {
    @State private var progress = 0.72
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 24) {
            AnimatableRing(progress: progress, title: "Daily goal")
                .frame(width: 260, height: 260)

            Text("Daily goal")
                .font(.title2.bold())
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .task {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            let values = [0.28, 0.91, 0.55, 0.72]
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                for value in values where !Task.isCancelled {
                    try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
                    progress = value
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)
#Preview {
    AnimatableRingDemo()
}
```

## Concentric Card

Nested cards whose corners stay concentric with ConcentricRectangle, however deep they sit.

Category: Modern. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Modern/ConcentricCard/ConcentricCard.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A card that publishes its corners, so `ConcentricCardSurface` views inside stay concentric.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct ConcentricCard<Background: ShapeStyle, Content: View>: View {
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat = 36
    var padding: CGFloat = 12
    let background: Background
    @ViewBuilder let content: () -> Content

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .padding(padding)
            .background(background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
            .containerShape(.rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
    }
}

/// A surface whose corners follow the nearest container shape, however deep or inset it sits.
///
/// `minimumRadius` stops corners from turning square far from the container's edge.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct ConcentricCardSurface<Background: ShapeStyle, Content: View>: View {
    var padding: CGFloat = 12
    var minimumRadius: CGFloat = 8
    let background: Background
    @ViewBuilder let content: () -> Content

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .padding(padding)
            .background(background, in: ConcentricRectangle(corners: .concentric(minimum: .fixed(minimumRadius))))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct ConcentricCardDemo: View {
    @State private var inset: CGFloat = 8
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            ConcentricCard(cornerRadius: 56, padding: inset, background: Color.white.opacity(0.16)) {
                ConcentricCardSurface(padding: inset, background: Color.orange.gradient) {
                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: inset) {
                        Label("Concentric", systemImage: "circle.circle")
                            .font(.title2.bold())
                            .foregroundStyle(.white)
                            .padding(16)
                            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: 170, alignment: .bottomLeading)

                        ConcentricCardSurface(background: Color.white) {
                            Text("One shared center")
                                .font(.headline)
                                .foregroundStyle(.black)
                                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.3))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.9)) { inset = inset == 8 ? 20 : 8 }
            }
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)
```

## Prominent Tab Bar

A tab view whose main action gets the system's prominent tab treatment.

```swift
import SwiftUI

@available(iOS 27, *)
struct ProminentTabBarItem<Value: Hashable>: Identifiable {

    let systemImage: String
    let value: Value

    var id: Value { value }

/// A tab view whose main action gets the system's prominent tab treatment.
@available(iOS 27, *)
struct ProminentTabBar<Value: Hashable, Content: View>: View {

        }
    }
```

## Symbol Draw On

An SF Symbol that draws itself on and off, stroke by stroke.

Category: Modern. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Modern/SymbolDrawOn/SymbolDrawOn.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// An SF Symbol that draws itself on and off, stroke by stroke.
///
/// Only symbols with Draw annotations trace their strokes. Others fall back to a simpler
/// appearance. With Reduce Motion on, the symbol fades.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct SymbolDrawOn: View {
    let systemName: String
    var isDrawn: Bool
    var label: LocalizedStringKey?

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Image(systemName: systemName)
            .symbolEffect(.drawOn.byLayer, isActive: !isDrawn)
            .symbolEffect(.drawOff.byLayer, isActive: !isDrawn)
            .symbolEffectsRemoved(reduceMotion)
            .opacity(reduceMotion && !isDrawn ? 0 : 1)
            .accessibilityRepresentation {
                if let label {
                    Image(systemName: systemName).accessibilityLabel(label)
                }
            }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct SymbolDrawOnDemo: View {
    @State private var isDrawn = true
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var cellSize = 104.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .black], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            LazyVGrid(columns: [GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: cellSize))], spacing: 28) {
                ForEach(symbols, id: \.self) { symbol in
                    SymbolDrawOn(systemName: symbol, isDrawn: isDrawn)
                        .font(.largeTitle.weight(.medium))
                        .imageScale(.large)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .frame(height: cellSize)
                }
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
        .task {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(isDrawn ? 1.8 : 1.3))
                withAnimation { isDrawn.toggle() }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```swift
import SwiftUI

@available(iOS 27, *)

    let systemImage: String

    let perform: () -> Void

                        ForEach(overflowActions, content: button(for:))
                    }
                }
        }
    }
```

## Adaptive Sidebar Layout

A split view driven by one Boolean that collapses to the detail on iPad and swaps columns on iPhone.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/AdaptiveSidebarLayout/AdaptiveSidebarLayout.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A split layout driven by one Boolean: the sidebar is either showing or it is not.
///
/// On iPad the toolbar button collapses the view to the detail alone. On iPhone the same
/// value decides whether the sidebar or the detail is on top of the stack.
struct AdaptiveSidebarLayout<Sidebar: View, Detail: View>: View {
    @Binding var showsSidebar: Bool
    @ViewBuilder let sidebar: () -> Sidebar
    @ViewBuilder let detail: () -> Detail

    @Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass) private var horizontalSizeClass
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        NavigationSplitView(
            columnVisibility: columnVisibility,
            preferredCompactColumn: compactColumn
        ) {
            sidebar()
                .toolbar(removing: .sidebarToggle)
        } detail: {
            detail()
                .toolbar {
                    // On iPhone the system back button already does this job.
                    if horizontalSizeClass == .regular {
                        ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarLeading) {
                            Button(showsSidebar ? "Hide sidebar" : "Show sidebar", systemImage: "sidebar.left") {
                                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .default) { showsSidebar.toggle() }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
        }
    }

    private var columnVisibility: Binding<NavigationSplitViewVisibility> {
        let binding = $showsSidebar
        return Binding(
            get: { binding.wrappedValue ? .all : .detailOnly },
            set: { binding.wrappedValue = $0 != .detailOnly }
        )
    }

    private var compactColumn: Binding<NavigationSplitViewColumn> {
        let binding = $showsSidebar
        return Binding(
            get: { binding.wrappedValue ? .sidebar : .detail },
            set: { binding.wrappedValue = $0 == .sidebar }
        )
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct AdaptiveSidebarLayoutDemoFolder: Identifiable, Hashable {
    var id: String { title }
    let title: String
    let systemImage: String
    let color: Color
    let count: Int
}

struct AdaptiveSidebarLayoutDemo: View {
    private let folders = [
        AdaptiveSidebarLayoutDemoFolder(title: "Inbox", systemImage: "tray.fill", color: .blue, count: 12),
        AdaptiveSidebarLayoutDemoFolder(title: "Starred", systemImage: "star.fill", color: .orange, count: 3),
        AdaptiveSidebarLayoutDemoFolder(title: "Drafts", systemImage: "doc.fill", color: .purple, count: 5),
        AdaptiveSidebarLayoutDemoFolder(title: "Archive", systemImage: "archivebox.fill", color: .teal, count: 248),
    ]

    @State private var showsSidebar = true
    @State private var selected: AdaptiveSidebarLayoutDemoFolder?

    var body: some View {
        AdaptiveSidebarLayout(showsSidebar: $showsSidebar) {
            List(folders) { folder in
                Button {
                    selected = folder
                    showsSidebar = false
                } label: {
                    Label(folder.title, systemImage: folder.systemImage)
                        .foregroundStyle(folder.color)
                }
                .listRowBackground(selected == folder ? folder.color.opacity(0.15) : nil)
            }
            .navigationTitle("Mail")
        } detail: {
            detail
        }
    }

    @ViewBuilder
    private var detail: some View {
        if let selected {
            ZStack {
                LinearGradient(colors: [selected.color, selected.color.opacity(0.55)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                    .ignoresSafeArea()

                VStack(spacing: 14) {
                    Image(systemName: selected.systemImage)
                        .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded))
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)

                    Text(selected.title)
                        .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                    Text("\(selected.count) messages")
                        .font(.headline)

                    Button("Folders", systemImage: "sidebar.left") {
                        showsSidebar = true
                    }
                    .buttonStyle(.bordered)
                    .tint(.white)
                    .padding(.top, 10)
                }
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .padding()
            }
            .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)
        } else {
            ContentUnavailableView("Choose a folder", systemImage: "folder")
        }
    }
}
```

## Animated Tab Bar

A custom tab bar with a sliding indicator and icons that bounce on selection.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/AnimatedTabBar/AnimatedTabBar.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct AnimatedTabBarItem<Value: Hashable>: Identifiable {
    let value: Value
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let systemImage: String

    var id: Value { value }
}

/// A custom tab bar whose indicator slides to the selected tab while its icon bounces.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the indicator jumps and the icons stay still.
struct AnimatedTabBar<Value: Hashable>: View {
    let items: [AnimatedTabBarItem<Value>]
    @Binding var selection: Value
    var tint: Color = .indigo

    @State private var bounces: [Value: Int] = [:]
    @Namespace private var indicator
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title3) private var iconHeight = 26.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 4) {
            ForEach(items) { item in
                tabButton(item)
            }
        }
        .padding(6)
        .background(.regularMaterial, in: .capsule)
        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.15), radius: 16, y: 8)
        .symbolEffectsRemoved(reduceMotion)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.3), value: selection)
        .onChange(of: selection) { _, newValue in
            bounces[newValue, default: 0] += 1
        }
    }

    private func tabButton(_ item: AnimatedTabBarItem<Value>) -> some View {
        let isSelected = item.value == selection

        return Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.3)) {
                selection = item.value
            }
        } label: {
            VStack(spacing: 2) {
                Image(systemName: item.systemImage)
                    .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))
                    .symbolEffect(.bounce, value: bounces[item.value, default: 0])
                    .frame(height: iconHeight)

                Text(item.title)
                    .font(.caption2.weight(.semibold))
                    .lineLimit(1)
            }
            .foregroundStyle(isSelected ? tint : Color.secondary)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .padding(.vertical, 8)
            .background {
                if isSelected {
                    Capsule()
                        .fill(tint.opacity(0.18))
                        .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "indicator", in: indicator)
                }
            }
            .contentShape(.capsule)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(item.title)
        .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct AnimatedTabBarDemo: View {
    private enum Destination: Hashable {
        case home, search, saved, profile
    }

    private let items: [AnimatedTabBarItem<Destination>] = [
```

## Bottom Drawer

A draggable bottom drawer that snaps to detents, built as a custom overlay.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/BottomDrawer/BottomDrawer.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum BottomDrawerSnapping {
    /// The stop closest to where a drag would come to rest. A drag upwards has a negative `predictedDrag`.
    static func stop(from current: CGFloat, predictedDrag: CGFloat, stops: [CGFloat]) -> CGFloat {
        let projected = current - predictedDrag
        return stops.min { abs($0 - projected) < abs($1 - projected) } ?? current
    }

    /// The stop `step` places away from `current`, held at the ends. With no stops it keeps `current`.
    static func stop(from current: CGFloat, step: Int, stops: [CGFloat]) -> CGFloat {
        let sorted = stops.sorted()
        guard !sorted.isEmpty else { return current }
        let index = sorted.firstIndex(of: current) ?? 0
        return sorted[min(max(index + step, 0), sorted.count - 1)]
    }

    /// Keeps the drawer between its lowest and highest stop while it is dragged.
    static func clamped(_ value: CGFloat, stops: [CGFloat]) -> CGFloat {
        guard let lowest = stops.min(), let highest = stops.max() else { return value }
        return min(max(value, lowest), highest)
    }
}

/// A drawer that rests on detents, given as fractions of the available height.
///
/// Place it above your content in a `ZStack`. The whole drawer is draggable, so keep scrolling
/// content out of it. VoiceOver adjusts the handle. With Reduce Motion on, the drawer snaps without a spring.
struct BottomDrawer<Content: View>: View {
    @Binding var detent: CGFloat
    var detents: [CGFloat] = [0.16, 0.5, 0.88]
    @ViewBuilder var content: Content

    @State private var dragTranslation: CGFloat = 0
    @GestureState private var isDragging = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var animation: Animation? {
        reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.2)
    }

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            let total = max(proxy.size.height, 1)
            let visible = BottomDrawerSnapping.clamped(detent - dragTranslation / total, stops: detents)

            VStack(spacing: 0) {
                handle
                content
                Spacer(minLength: 0)
            }
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .frame(height: (detents.max() ?? 1) * total, alignment: .top)
            .background(.regularMaterial, in: UnevenRoundedRectangle(topLeadingRadius: 28, topTrailingRadius: 28))
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.18), radius: 18, y: -4)
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .offset(y: total * (1 - visible))
            .gesture(dragGesture(total: total))
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea(edges: .bottom)
        .onChange(of: isDragging) { _, dragging in
            if !dragging { withAnimation(animation) { dragTranslation = 0 } }
        }
    }

    private var handle: some View {
        Capsule()
            .fill(.secondary)
            .frame(width: 40, height: 5)
            .padding(.vertical, 12)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .accessibilityElement()
            .accessibilityLabel("Drawer")
            .accessibilityValue("Position \(sortedIndex + 1) of \(detents.count)")
            .accessibilityAdjustableAction { direction in
                switch direction {
                case .increment: moveDetent(by: 1)
                case .decrement: moveDetent(by: -1)
                @unknown default: break
                }
            }
    }

    private var sortedDetents: [CGFloat] { detents.sorted() }
    private var sortedIndex: Int { sortedDetents.firstIndex(of: detent) ?? 0 }

    private func moveDetent(by step: Int) {
        withAnimation(animation) { detent = BottomDrawerSnapping.stop(from: detent, step: step, stops: detents) }
    }

    private func dragGesture(total: CGFloat) -> some Gesture {
        DragGesture()
            .updating($isDragging) { _, state, _ in state = true }
            .onChanged { dragTranslation = $0.translation.height }
            .onEnded { value in
                let target = BottomDrawerSnapping.stop(
                    from: detent,
                    predictedDrag: value.predictedEndTranslation.height / total,
                    stops: detents
                )
                withAnimation(animation) {
                    detent = target
                    dragTranslation = 0
                }
            }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct BottomDrawerDemo: View {
    @State private var detent: CGFloat = 0.16

    private let places = [
        ("Harbor Coffee", "cup.and.saucer.fill", Color.brown),
        ("City Library", "books.vertical.fill", Color.indigo),
        ("Riverside Park", "leaf.fill", Color.green),
        ("Old Town Bakery", "birthday.cake.fill", Color.pink),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.teal, .cyan, .mint], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            Image(systemName: "mappin.and.ellipse")
                .font(.largeTitle)
                .imageScale(.large)
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .shadow(radius: 6)
                .offset(y: -180)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            BottomDrawer(detent: $detent) {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 18) {
                    Text("Nearby")
                        .font(.title2.bold())

                    ForEach(places, id: \.0) { name, symbol, color in
                        Label {
                            Text(name).font(.headline)
                        } icon: {
                            Image(systemName: symbol).foregroundStyle(color.gradient)
                        }
                    }
                }
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                .padding(.horizontal, 24)
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    BottomDrawerDemo()
}
```

## Breadcrumb Trail

A breadcrumb path that moves its middle crumbs into a menu when it runs out of width.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/BreadcrumbTrail/BreadcrumbTrail.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct BreadcrumbTrailItem: Identifiable, Hashable {
    let id: String
    let title: String
}

/// A breadcrumb path. When it is wider than its space, the middle crumbs move into a menu.
///
/// If even the shortest form does not fit, as at the largest text sizes, the row scrolls.
struct BreadcrumbTrail: View {
    let items: [BreadcrumbTrailItem]
    let onSelect: (BreadcrumbTrailItem) -> Void

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// A crumb is a short line of text, too small to hit. This padding widens what answers to a
    /// touch, and the same padding taken back keeps the trail as compact as it was.
    private let touchPadding: CGFloat = 13

    var body: some View {
        ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
            fullRow

            ForEach(BreadcrumbTrailMath.collapsedTails(count: items.count), id: \.self) { tail in
                collapsedRow(tail: tail)
            }

            ScrollView(.horizontal) {
                fullRow
            }
            .scrollIndicators(.hidden)
        }
        .font(.subheadline)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy, value: items)
    }

    private var fullRow: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 6) {
            crumbs(items[...])
        }
    }

    private func collapsedRow(tail: Int) -> some View {
        let parts = BreadcrumbTrailMath.split(items, tail: tail)

        return HStack(spacing: 6) {
            crumbs(parts.head)
            separator
            Menu {
                ForEach(parts.hidden) { item in
                    Button(item.title) { onSelect(item) }
                }
            } label: {
                Image(systemName: "ellipsis.circle.fill")
                    .symbolRenderingMode(.hierarchical)
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .padding(touchPadding)
                    .contentShape(.rect)
                    .padding(-touchPadding)
            }
            .accessibilityLabel("More")
            separator
            crumbs(parts.tail)
        }
    }

    @ViewBuilder
    private func crumbs(_ slice: ArraySlice<BreadcrumbTrailItem>) -> some View {
        ForEach(slice) { item in
            if item != slice.first {
                separator
            }

            if item == items.last {
                Text(item.title)
                    .fontWeight(.semibold)
                    .lineLimit(1)
                    .fixedSize()
                    .accessibilityAddTraits(.isSelected)
            } else {
                Button {
                    onSelect(item)
                } label: {
                    Text(item.title)
                        .padding(.vertical, touchPadding)
                        .contentShape(.rect)
                        .padding(.vertical, -touchPadding)
                }
                .lineLimit(1)
                .fixedSize()
            }
        }
    }

    private var separator: some View {
        Image(systemName: "chevron.compact.forward")
            .foregroundStyle(.tertiary)
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

enum BreadcrumbTrailMath {
    /// How many trailing crumbs each collapsed form keeps, from the widest form to the narrowest.
    static func collapsedTails(count: Int) -> [Int] {
        guard count > 2 else { return [] }
        return Array((1...min(count - 2, 3)).reversed())
    }

    /// Keeps the first crumb and the last `tail` crumbs. The rest go in the menu.
    static func split<Element>(
        _ items: [Element],
        tail: Int
    ) -> (head: ArraySlice<Element>, hidden: ArraySlice<Element>, tail: ArraySlice<Element>) {
        guard let first = items.indices.first else { return ([], [], []) }
        let tailStart = max(items.count - max(tail, 0), first + 1)
        return (items[first...first], items[(first + 1)..<tailStart], items[tailStart...])
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct BreadcrumbTrailDemo: View {
    private let tree = ["Home", "Projects", "Mobile", "Catalog", "Components", "Navigation"]

    @State private var depth = 2

    private var trail: [BreadcrumbTrailItem] {
        tree.prefix(depth).map { BreadcrumbTrailItem(id: $0, title: $0) }
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.teal.opacity(0.35), .indigo.opacity(0.3)], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 28) {
                BreadcrumbTrail(items: trail) { item in
                    if let index = tree.firstIndex(of: item.title) {
                        depth = index + 1
                    }
                }

                Image(systemName: "folder.fill")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded))
                    .foregroundStyle(.teal.gradient)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Button("Open", systemImage: "arrow.forward") {
                    depth = depth < tree.count ? depth + 1 : 1
                }
                .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                .tint(.indigo)
            }
            .padding(24)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 24))
            .padding(16)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    BreadcrumbTrailDemo()
}
```

## Drag To Dismiss Screen

A full-screen page that follows a downward drag, shrinks and fades, then leaves when released past a threshold.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/DragToDismissScreen/DragToDismissScreen.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A full-screen page that follows a downward drag and leaves when released past a threshold.
///
/// Remove the view from `onDismiss`. With Reduce Motion on, the page does not scale and
/// leaves at once. VoiceOver users dismiss it with the escape gesture.
struct DragToDismissScreen<Content: View>: View {
    var threshold: CGFloat = 140
    let onDismiss: () -> Void
    @ViewBuilder let content: () -> Content

    @GestureState private var liveOffset: CGFloat = 0
    @State private var settledOffset: CGFloat = 0
    @State private var isDismissing = false
    @State private var screenHeight: CGFloat = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var progress: CGFloat {
        DragToDismissScreenMath.progress(offset: settledOffset + liveOffset, threshold: threshold)
    }

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
            .scaleEffect(reduceMotion ? 1 : 1 - 0.1 * progress)
            .opacity(1 - 0.3 * progress)
            .offset(y: settledOffset + liveOffset)
            .gesture(dragGesture)
            .allowsHitTesting(!isDismissing)
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.height } action: { screenHeight = $0 }
            .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
            .accessibilityAction(.escape) { dismiss(from: 0) }
    }

    private var dragGesture: some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 16)
            .updating($liveOffset) { value, state, _ in
                state = max(value.translation.height, 0)
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                let translation = max(value.translation.height, 0)
                let shouldDismiss = DragToDismissScreenMath.shouldDismiss(
                    translation: translation,
                    predicted: value.predictedEndTranslation.height,
                    threshold: threshold
                )
                if shouldDismiss {
                    dismiss(from: translation)
                } else {
                    // Takes over from the gesture state, which resets without animating.
                    settledOffset = translation
                    withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.2)) {
                        settledOffset = 0
                    }
                }
            }
    }

    private func dismiss(from offset: CGFloat) {
        guard !isDismissing else { return }
        isDismissing = true

        if reduceMotion {
            onDismiss()
            return
        }

        settledOffset = offset
        withAnimation(.easeIn(duration: 0.25), completionCriteria: .logicallyComplete) {
            settledOffset = max(screenHeight, threshold * 4)
        } completion: {
            onDismiss()
        }
    }
}

enum DragToDismissScreenMath {
    /// How far the drag has gone towards the threshold, from 0 to 1.
    static func progress(offset: CGFloat, threshold: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        guard threshold > 0 else { return offset > 0 ? 1 : 0 }
        return min(max(offset, 0) / threshold, 1)
    }

    /// A long drag dismisses, and so does a quick flick that was heading far enough.
    static func shouldDismiss(translation: CGFloat, predicted: CGFloat, threshold: CGFloat) -> Bool {
        guard translation > 0 else { return false }
        return translation >= threshold || predicted >= threshold * 2
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct DragToDismissScreenDemo: View {
    @State private var isOpen = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Color(red: 0.08, green: 0.08, blue: 0.14)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            Button("Open", systemImage: "arrow.up.left.and.arrow.down.right") {
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.35)) { isOpen = true }
            }
            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
            .controlSize(.large)
            .tint(.orange)

            if isOpen {
                DragToDismissScreen(onDismiss: { isOpen = false }) {
                    page
                }
                .transition(.move(edge: .bottom))
                .zIndex(1)
            }
        }
    }

    private var page: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink, .purple], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 16) {
                Capsule()
                    .fill(.white.opacity(0.7))
                    .frame(width: 44, height: 5)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Spacer()

                Image(systemName: "sun.horizon.fill")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded))
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text("Golden Hour")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                Text("Pull down to close")
                    .font(.headline)
                    .opacity(0.85)

                Spacer()
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .padding(.top, 12)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    DragToDismissScreenDemo()
}
```

## Embedded Web Browser

A small browser inside the app, with an address bar, back, forward, reload and a line that fills while the page loads.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Navigation/EmbeddedWebBrowser/EmbeddedWebBrowser.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI
import WebKit

nonisolated enum EmbeddedWebBrowserLogic {
    /// The address to load for what was typed: as it is when it names its scheme, with `https`
    /// in front when it looks like a host, and nothing when it is neither.
    static func url(from text: String) -> URL? {
        let typed = text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        guard !typed.isEmpty, !typed.contains(where: \.isWhitespace) else { return nil }
        if let url = URL(string: typed), let scheme = url.scheme, ["http", "https"].contains(scheme.lowercased()), url.host() != nil {
            return url
        }
        guard !typed.contains("://"), typed.contains("."), !typed.hasPrefix("."), !typed.hasSuffix(".") else { return nil }
        return URL(string: "https://\(typed)")
    }

    /// What the address bar shows for a page: its host, without `www.`, or nothing for a page with no address.
    static func host(of url: URL?) -> String {
        guard let host = url?.host() else { return "" }
        return host.hasPrefix("www.") ? String(host.dropFirst(4)) : host
    }
}

/// A small browser inside the app: a web page with an address bar, back, forward and reload,
/// and a line that fills while the page loads. It is built on the `WebView` and `WebPage`
/// that iOS 26 added, with no UIKit.
///
/// Create the `WebPage`, load what it should start on, and hand it over.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct EmbeddedWebBrowser: View {
    let page: WebPage

    @State private var address = ""
    @State private var selection: TextSelection?
    @FocusState private var isEditing: Bool

    private let touchTarget: CGFloat = 44

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 0) {
            WebView(page)

            if page.isLoading {
                ProgressView(value: page.estimatedProgress)
                    .progressViewStyle(.linear)
                    .accessibilityLabel("Loading page")
            }

            HStack(spacing: 2) {
                barButton("Back", systemImage: "chevron.backward") {
                    if let item = page.backForwardList.backList.last { _ = page.load(item) }
                }
                .disabled(page.backForwardList.backList.isEmpty)

                barButton("Forward", systemImage: "chevron.forward") {
                    if let item = page.backForwardList.forwardList.first { _ = page.load(item) }
                }
                .disabled(page.backForwardList.forwardList.isEmpty)

                TextField("Address", text: $address, selection: $selection)
                    .focused($isEditing)
                    .textInputAutocapitalization(.never)
                    .autocorrectionDisabled()
                    .keyboardType(.URL)
                    .submitLabel(.go)
                    .multilineTextAlignment(isEditing ? .leading : .center)
                    .padding(.horizontal, 12)
                    .padding(.vertical, 8)
                    .background(.fill.tertiary, in: .capsule)
                    .onSubmit {
                        if let url = EmbeddedWebBrowserLogic.url(from: address) { _ = page.load(url) }
                    }

                barButton(page.isLoading ? "Stop" : "Reload", systemImage: page.isLoading ? "xmark" : "arrow.clockwise") {
                    if page.isLoading {
                        page.stopLoading()
                    } else {
                        _ = page.reload()
                    }
                }
            }
            .labelStyle(.iconOnly)
            .font(.body.weight(.medium))
            .padding(.horizontal, 6)
            .padding(.vertical, 4)
            .background(.bar)
        }
        .onChange(of: page.url, initial: true) { _, url in
            if !isEditing { address = EmbeddedWebBrowserLogic.host(of: url) }
        }
        .onChange(of: isEditing) { _, editing in
            address = editing ? (page.url?.absoluteString ?? "") : EmbeddedWebBrowserLogic.host(of: page.url)
            // The whole address is selected, as in Safari, so typing replaces it.
            selection = editing ? TextSelection(range: address.startIndex..<address.endIndex) : nil
        }
    }

    /// An icon button with a touch target of the recommended size.
    private func barButton(_ title: LocalizedStringResource, systemImage: String, action: @escaping () -> Void) -> some View {
        Button(action: action) {
            Label { Text(title) } icon: { Image(systemName: systemImage) }
                .frame(minWidth: touchTarget, minHeight: touchTarget)
                .contentShape(.rect)
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

/// Serves the pages of the demo from the app under a scheme of its own, so it needs no network
/// and its links are real navigations, with a way back.
@available(iOS 26, *)
private nonisolated struct EmbeddedWebBrowserDemoPages: URLSchemeHandler {
    private static let walks = [
        "cliffs": ("The cliffs", "An hour along the edge, with the wind for company and gulls below your feet."),
        "lighthouse": ("The lighthouse", "Flat and easy. Go at dusk, when the lamp starts to turn."),
        "marsh": ("The marsh", "Boardwalks over still water. Bring binoculars and patience."),
    ]

    func reply(for request: URLRequest) -> AsyncThrowingStream<URLSchemeTaskResult, any Error> {
        AsyncThrowingStream { continuation in
            guard let url = request.url else { return continuation.finish(throwing: URLError(.badURL)) }
            let data = Data(Self.html(for: url.host() ?? "").utf8)
            continuation.yield(.response(URLResponse(url: url, mimeType: "text/html", expectedContentLength: data.count, textEncodingName: "utf-8")))
            continuation.yield(.data(data))
            continuation.finish()
        }
    }

    private static func html(for page: String) -> String {
        let content: String
        if let walk = walks[page] {
            content = "<h1>\(walk.0)</h1><p>\(walk.1)</p><a href=\"guide://home\">&larr; All walks</a>"
        } else {
            let links = walks.keys.sorted().map { "<a href=\"guide://\($0)\">\(walks[$0]?.0 ?? "") &rarr;</a>" }.joined()
            content = "<h1>Field Guide</h1><p>Three short walks near the harbor. Pick one to read about it.</p>\(links)"
        }
        return """
        <!doctype html><html><head><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
        <style>
        body { font: -apple-system-body; margin: 0; padding: 24px; color-scheme: light dark; }
        h1 { font: -apple-system-title1; font-weight: 700; margin: 0 0 8px; }
        p { line-height: 1.5; opacity: .8; }
        a { display: block; padding: 16px; margin: 12px 0; border-radius: 16px; background: color-mix(in srgb, CanvasText 8%, transparent); color: inherit; text-decoration: none; font-weight: 600; }
        </style></head><body>\(content)</body></html>
        """
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct EmbeddedWebBrowserDemo: View {
    @State private var page: WebPage = {
        var configuration = WebPage.Configuration()
        if let scheme = URLScheme("guide") {
            configuration.urlSchemeHandlers[scheme] = EmbeddedWebBrowserDemoPages()
        }
        return WebPage(configuration: configuration)
    }()

    var body: some View {
        EmbeddedWebBrowser(page: page)
            .task {
                if page.url == nil { _ = page.load(URL(string: "guide://home")) }
            }
    }
}

    EmbeddedWebBrowserDemo()
}
```

## Full Screen Menu Overlay

A full-screen menu that opens over the content and brings its links in one by one.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/FullScreenMenuOverlay/FullScreenMenuOverlay.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct FullScreenMenuOverlayLink: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let systemImage: String
    let action: () -> Void
}

/// A full-screen menu whose links arrive one by one. Add it on top of your content.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the menu and its links appear at once.
struct FullScreenMenuOverlay: View {
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    let links: [FullScreenMenuOverlayLink]
    var colors: [Color] = [.indigo, .purple, .pink]

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            if isPresented {
                FullScreenMenuOverlayPanel(
                    links: links,
                    colors: colors,
                    close: { isPresented = false }
                )
                .transition(.move(edge: .top).combined(with: .opacity))
            }
        }
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.4), value: isPresented)
    }
}

private struct FullScreenMenuOverlayPanel: View {
    let links: [FullScreenMenuOverlayLink]
    let colors: [Color]
    let close: () -> Void

    @State private var showsLinks = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ZStack(alignment: .topTrailing) {
            LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            // Scrolls only when large text makes the links taller than the screen.
            ScrollView {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 22) {
                    ForEach(Array(links.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, link in
                        row(for: link)
                            .opacity(showsLinks ? 1 : 0)
                            .offset(y: showsLinks ? 0 : 28)
                            .animation(animation(forRow: index), value: showsLinks)
                    }
                }
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                .padding(.horizontal, 32)
                .padding(.vertical, 90)
            }
            .scrollBounceBehavior(.basedOnSize)

            Button(action: close) {
                Image(systemName: "xmark")
                    .font(.title3.weight(.bold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    .padding(14)
                    .background(.white.opacity(0.2), in: .circle)
            }
            .accessibilityLabel("Close")
            .padding(20)
        }
        .onAppear { showsLinks = true }
        .accessibilityAddTraits(.isModal)
        .accessibilityAction(.escape, close)
    }

    private func animation(forRow index: Int) -> Animation? {
        guard !reduceMotion else { return nil }
        return .spring(duration: 0.55, bounce: 0.25).delay(0.12 + 0.08 * Double(min(index, 12)))
    }

    private func row(for link: FullScreenMenuOverlayLink) -> some View {
        Button {
            close()
            link.action()
        } label: {
            Label(link.title, systemImage: link.systemImage)
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

    @State private var page = "Studio"

                Text(page)
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                    .contentTransition(.opacity)

                Spacer()
            }
            .accessibilityHidden(isOpen)

            FullScreenMenuOverlay(isPresented: $isOpen, links: links)
        }
    }
```

## Navigation Path Router

A router that owns a NavigationPath so any view can push or pop screens by a typed value.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/NavigationPathRouter/NavigationPathRouter.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Owns a stack's path, so that any view can push or pop screens by a typed value.
///
/// Popping more screens than the stack holds is safe: it stops at the root.
@MainActor
@Observable
final class NavigationPathRouter<Destination: Hashable> {
    var path = NavigationPath()

    var depth: Int { path.count }

    func push(_ destination: Destination) {
        path.append(destination)
    }

    func pop(_ count: Int = 1) {
        let removable = min(max(count, 0), path.count)
        guard removable > 0 else { return }
        path.removeLast(removable)
    }

    func popToRoot() {
        pop(path.count)
    }
}

/// A navigation stack wired to a router, which it also places in the environment.
///
/// Read it from any screen with `@Environment(NavigationPathRouter<MyRoute>.self)`.
struct NavigationPathRouterStack<Destination: Hashable, Root: View, Screen: View>: View {
    let router: NavigationPathRouter<Destination>
    @ViewBuilder let root: () -> Root
    @ViewBuilder let screen: (Destination) -> Screen

    var body: some View {
        @Bindable var router = router

        NavigationStack(path: $router.path) {
            root()
                .navigationDestination(for: Destination.self, destination: screen)
        }
        .environment(router)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private enum NavigationPathRouterDemoRoute: String, Hashable, CaseIterable {
    case profile = "Profile"
    case settings = "Settings"
    case about = "About"

    var systemImage: String {
        switch self {
        case .profile: "person.crop.circle.fill"
        case .settings: "gearshape.fill"
        case .about: "info.circle.fill"
        }
    }

    var color: Color {
        switch self {
        case .profile: .blue
        case .settings: .purple
        case .about: .teal
        }
    }
}

private struct NavigationPathRouterDemoScreen: View {
    var current: NavigationPathRouterDemoRoute?

    @Environment(NavigationPathRouter<NavigationPathRouterDemoRoute>.self) private var router

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [current?.color ?? .indigo, .black.opacity(0.85)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 14) {
                Text("Depth \(router.depth)")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    .padding(.bottom, 10)

                ForEach(NavigationPathRouterDemoRoute.allCases.filter { $0 != current }, id: \.self) { route in
                    Button(route.rawValue, systemImage: route.systemImage) { router.push(route) }
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                }

                if router.depth > 0 {
                    Button("Root", systemImage: "house.fill") { router.popToRoot() }
                }
            }
            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
            .tint(.white.opacity(0.22))
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .padding(32)
        }
        .navigationTitle(current?.rawValue ?? "Router")
    }
}

struct NavigationPathRouterDemo: View {
    @State private var router = NavigationPathRouter<NavigationPathRouterDemoRoute>()

    var body: some View {
        NavigationPathRouterStack(router: router) {
            NavigationPathRouterDemoScreen()
        } screen: { route in
            NavigationPathRouterDemoScreen(current: route)
        }
    }
}

    NavigationPathRouterDemo()
```

## Scroll Spy Header

A bar of chips that highlights the section at the top of a scroll view and jumps to a section when tapped.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/ScrollSpyHeader/ScrollSpyHeader.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A bar of chips that follows a scroll view: the chip of the section at the top is highlighted,
/// and tapping a chip jumps to its section.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, jumps and the highlight happen without animation.
struct ScrollSpyHeader<Element: Identifiable, Content: View>: View where Element.ID: Sendable {
    let sections: [Element]
    let title: (Element) -> String
    @ViewBuilder let content: (Element) -> Content

    @State private var activeID: Element.ID?
    @State private var visibleIDs: Set<Element.ID> = []
    @State private var isAtEnd = false
    @State private var jumpTarget: Element.ID?
    @State private var isJumping = false
    /// A scroll view reader cannot jump to a section the lazy stack has not built yet. This can.
    @State private var position = ScrollPosition(idType: Element.ID.self)
    @Namespace private var chipNamespace
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// A jump wins, so the highlight does not flicker across the sections it passes.
    private var highlightedID: Element.ID? {
        jumpTarget ?? activeID ?? sections.first?.id
    }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 0) {
            chipBar
            Divider()

            ScrollView {
                LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 28) {
                    ForEach(sections) { section in
                        content(section)
                            .id(section.id)
                    }
                }
                .scrollTargetLayout()
                .padding()
            }
            .scrollPosition($position, anchor: .top)
            // The chip that was tapped stays chosen until the list moves again. A short
            // section near the end cannot reach the top, and would lose it to the last one.
            .onScrollPhaseChange { _, phase in
                if phase == .interacting || (phase == .animating && !isJumping) { jumpTarget = nil }
            }
            .onScrollTargetVisibilityChange(idType: Element.ID.self, threshold: 0.01) { ids in
                visibleIDs = Set(ids)
                refreshActiveID()
            }
            .onScrollGeometryChange(for: Bool.self) { geometry in
                ScrollSpyHeaderMath.isAtEnd(
                    visibleMaxY: geometry.visibleRect.maxY,
                    contentHeight: geometry.contentSize.height,
                    containerHeight: geometry.containerSize.height
                )
            } action: { _, newValue in
                isAtEnd = newValue
                refreshActiveID()
            }
        }
    }

    private var chipBar: some View {
        ScrollViewReader { chipProxy in
            ScrollView(.horizontal) {
                HStack(spacing: 8) {
                    ForEach(sections) { section in
                        chip(for: section)
                            .id(section.id)
                    }
                }
                .padding(.horizontal)
                .padding(.vertical, 10)
            }
            .scrollIndicators(.hidden)
            .onChange(of: highlightedID) { _, newValue in
                guard let newValue else { return }
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth) {
                    chipProxy.scrollTo(newValue, anchor: .center)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private func chip(for section: Element) -> some View {
        let isActive = section.id == highlightedID

        return Button {
            jump(to: section.id)
        } label: {
            Text(title(section))
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                .foregroundStyle(isActive ? Color.white : Color.primary)
                .padding(.horizontal, 14)
                .padding(.vertical, 8)
                .background {
                    if isActive {
                        Capsule()
                            .fill(.tint)
                            .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "active", in: chipNamespace)
                    } else {
                        Capsule()
                            .fill(.quaternary)
                    }
                }
                // A little taller for a touch than it looks, up to the size of a touch target.
                .padding(.vertical, 5)
                .contentShape(.rect)
                .padding(.vertical, -5)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityAddTraits(isActive ? .isSelected : [])
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy, value: highlightedID)
    }

    private func jump(to id: Element.ID) {
        jumpTarget = id
        isJumping = true
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.45), completionCriteria: .logicallyComplete) {
            position.scrollTo(id: id, anchor: .top)
        } completion: {
            isJumping = false
            refreshActiveID()
        }
    }

    private func refreshActiveID() {
        activeID = ScrollSpyHeaderMath.activeID(
            order: sections.map(\.id),
            visible: visibleIDs,
            isAtEnd: isAtEnd,
            previous: activeID
        )
    }
}

enum ScrollSpyHeaderMath {
    /// The first section still on screen, or the last one once the end is reached,
    /// because a short final section can never scroll to the top.
    static func activeID<ID: Hashable>(order: [ID], visible: Set<ID>, isAtEnd: Bool, previous: ID?) -> ID? {
        if isAtEnd, let last = order.last { return last }
        return order.first(where: visible.contains) ?? previous
    }

    static func isAtEnd(visibleMaxY: CGFloat, contentHeight: CGFloat, containerHeight: CGFloat) -> Bool {
        contentHeight > containerHeight && visibleMaxY >= contentHeight - 1
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct ScrollSpyHeaderDemoSection: Identifiable {
    var id: String { chip }
    let chip: String
    let heading: String
    let color: Color
    let dishes: [String]
}

struct ScrollSpyHeaderDemo: View {
    private let sections = [
        ScrollSpyHeaderDemoSection(chip: "Starters", heading: "To begin", color: .green, dishes: ["Garden salad", "Tomato bruschetta", "Crispy calamari", "Grilled halloumi", "Olive plate"]),
        ScrollSpyHeaderDemoSection(chip: "Mains", heading: "From the kitchen", color: .orange, dishes: ["Wood-fired pizza", "Pumpkin risotto", "Roast chicken", "Seared tuna", "Mushroom pasta"]),
        ScrollSpyHeaderDemoSection(chip: "Sides", heading: "On the side", color: .teal, dishes: ["Rosemary fries", "Charred greens", "Warm flatbread", "Slaw"]),
        ScrollSpyHeaderDemoSection(chip: "Desserts", heading: "Something sweet", color: .pink, dishes: ["Lemon tart", "Dark chocolate mousse", "Vanilla panna cotta", "Fig ice cream"]),
        ScrollSpyHeaderDemoSection(chip: "Drinks", heading: "To sip", color: .indigo, dishes: ["Sparkling water", "Iced tea", "Espresso"]),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        ScrollSpyHeader(sections: sections, title: \.chip) { section in
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
                Text(section.heading)
                    .font(.title2.bold())
                    .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)

                ForEach(section.dishes, id: \.self) { dish in
                    HStack(spacing: 14) {
                        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
                            .fill(section.color.gradient)
                            .frame(width: 52, height: 52)
                            .overlay {
                                Image(systemName: "fork.knife")
                                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
                            }
                            .accessibilityHidden(true)

                        Text(dish)
                            .font(.body.weight(.medium))
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        .tint(.indigo)
    }
}

#Preview {
    ScrollSpyHeaderDemo()
}
```

## Scroll To Top Button

A floating button that appears after scrolling down and returns the scroll view to the top.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/ScrollToTopButton/ScrollToTopButton.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A scroll view that shows a floating button after scrolling down, which returns to the top.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the button fades and the view jumps to the top.
struct ScrollToTopButton<Content: View>: View {
    var threshold: CGFloat = 320
    var tint: Color = .indigo
    @ViewBuilder var content: Content

    @State private var position = ScrollPosition(edge: .top)
    @State private var isVisible = false
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title3) private var buttonSize = 52.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            content
        }
        .scrollPosition($position)
        .onScrollGeometryChange(for: Bool.self) { geometry in
            geometry.contentOffset.y + geometry.contentInsets.top > threshold
        } action: { _, isPastThreshold in
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.35)) {
                isVisible = isPastThreshold
            }
        }
        .overlay(alignment: .bottomTrailing) {
            if isVisible {
                button
                    .padding(20)
                    .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .scale(scale: 0.4).combined(with: .opacity))
            }
        }
    }

    private var button: some View {
        Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.5)) {
                position.scrollTo(edge: .top)
            }
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: "arrow.up")
                .font(.title3.bold())
                .foregroundStyle(ScrollToTopButtonContrastingForeground(background: tint))
                .frame(width: buttonSize, height: buttonSize)
                .background(tint.gradient, in: .circle)
                .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.25), radius: 10, y: 5)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel("Back to top")
    }
}

/// White or black, whichever reads better on `background`. Black only on a
/// light color, so the system's own colors keep white.
nonisolated struct ScrollToTopButtonContrastingForeground: ShapeStyle {
    let background: Color

    func resolve(in environment: EnvironmentValues) -> Color {
        let color = background.resolve(in: environment)
        let luminance = 0.2126 * color.linearRed + 0.7152 * color.linearGreen + 0.0722 * color.linearBlue
        return luminance > 0.5 ? .black : .white
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ScrollToTopButtonDemo: View {
    private let colors: [Color] = [.indigo, .blue, .teal, .green, .orange, .pink]

    var body: some View {
        ScrollToTopButton {
            LazyVStack(spacing: 14) {
                ForEach(0..<30, id: \.self) { index in
                    HStack(spacing: 14) {
                        Image(systemName: "photo.fill")
                            .font(.title2)
                            .foregroundStyle(.white)
                            .frame(width: 60, height: 60)
                            .background(colors[index % colors.count].gradient, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 14))
                            .accessibilityHidden(true)

                        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                            Text("Story \(index + 1)")
                                .font(.headline)
                            Text("A short description of this story")
                                .font(.subheadline)
                                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                        }

                        Spacer(minLength: 0)
                    }
                    .padding(12)
                    .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 18))
                }
            }
            .padding(16)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ScrollToTopButtonDemo()
}
```

## Search Scopes And Suggestions

A modifier that adds a search field with scope buttons and suggestion rows that narrow as you type.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/SearchScopesAndSuggestions/SearchScopesAndSuggestions.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Adds a search field with scope buttons and suggestion rows. Apply it inside a `NavigationStack`.
///
/// Tapping a suggestion fills in the field. The suggestions narrow as the person types.
struct SearchScopesAndSuggestions<Scope: Hashable>: ViewModifier {
    @Binding var text: String
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    @Binding var scope: Scope
    let scopes: [Scope]
    let scopeTitle: (Scope) -> String
    let suggestions: [String]
    var prompt: LocalizedStringResource = "Search"

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .searchable(text: $text, isPresented: $isPresented, prompt: prompt)
            .searchScopes($scope, activation: .onSearchPresentation) {
                ForEach(scopes, id: \.self) { scope in
                    Text(scopeTitle(scope)).tag(scope)
                }
            }
            .searchSuggestions {
                ForEach(SearchScopesAndSuggestionsMath.matches(in: suggestions, for: text), id: \.self) { suggestion in
                    Label(suggestion, systemImage: "magnifyingglass")
                        .searchCompletion(suggestion)
                }
            }
    }
}

enum SearchScopesAndSuggestionsMath {
    /// The suggestions worth showing: unique, containing the text, and not what is already typed.
    static func matches(in suggestions: [String], for text: String, limit: Int = 5) -> [String] {
        let query = text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        var seen = Set<String>()
        let unique = suggestions.filter { seen.insert($0).inserted }

        let matching = query.isEmpty
            ? unique
            : unique.filter { $0.localizedStandardContains(query) && $0.localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare(query) != .orderedSame }
        return Array(matching.prefix(max(limit, 0)))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private enum SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoScope: String, CaseIterable {
    case all = "All"
    case fruit = "Fruit"
    case vegetable = "Vegetables"
}

private struct SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoProduce: Identifiable {
    var id: String { name }
    let name: String
    let symbol: String
    let scope: SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoScope
}

struct SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemo: View {
    private let produce = [
        SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoProduce(name: "Apple", symbol: "apple.logo", scope: .fruit),
        SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoProduce(name: "Apricot", symbol: "leaf.fill", scope: .fruit),
        SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoProduce(name: "Grape", symbol: "circle.grid.3x3.fill", scope: .fruit),
        SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoProduce(name: "Papaya", symbol: "sun.max.fill", scope: .fruit),
        SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoProduce(name: "Asparagus", symbol: "leaf", scope: .vegetable),
        SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoProduce(name: "Bell pepper", symbol: "flame.fill", scope: .vegetable),
        SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoProduce(name: "Carrot", symbol: "carrot.fill", scope: .vegetable),
        SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoProduce(name: "Spinach", symbol: "leaf.circle.fill", scope: .vegetable),
    ]

    @State private var text = ""
    @State private var isSearching = false
    @State private var scope = SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoScope.all

    private var results: [SearchScopesAndSuggestionsDemoProduce] {

            (scope == .all || item.scope == scope) && (text.isEmpty || item.name.localizedStandardContains(text))

            .onChange(of: isSearching) { _, isSearching in

            }
        }
    }
```
