## Pull Progress Refresh

A custom pull to refresh whose ring fills with the pull distance and starts a refresh when released past a threshold.

Category: Scrolling. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Scrolling/PullProgressRefresh/PullProgressRefresh.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum PullProgressRefreshMath {
    /// How far the content has been pulled past its resting position.
    static func pullDistance(contentOffsetY: CGFloat, topInset: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        max(0, -(contentOffsetY + topInset))
    }

    /// The fraction of the ring to fill, from 0 to 1.
    static func progress(pull: CGFloat, threshold: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        guard threshold > 0 else { return pull > 0 ? 1 : 0 }
        return min(max(pull / threshold, 0), 1)
    }
}

/// A scroll view whose ring fills as it is pulled, and refreshes when released past a threshold.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the content moves into place without a spring.
struct PullProgressRefresh<Content: View>: View {
    var threshold: CGFloat = 90
    var tint: Color = .accentColor
    let action: @MainActor () async -> Void
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @State private var pull: CGFloat = 0
    @State private var isRefreshing = false
    @State private var refreshToken: Int?
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title3) private var ringSize = 34.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var progress: CGFloat {
        isRefreshing ? 1 : PullProgressRefreshMath.progress(pull: pull, threshold: threshold)
    }

    private var slotHeight: CGFloat { ringSize + 28 }

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(spacing: 0) {
                Color.clear
                    .frame(height: isRefreshing ? slotHeight : 0)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                content()
            }
        }
        .onScrollGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { geometry in
            PullProgressRefreshMath.pullDistance(
                contentOffsetY: geometry.contentOffset.y,
                topInset: geometry.contentInsets.top
            )
        } action: { _, newValue in
            pull = newValue
        }
        .onScrollPhaseChange { oldPhase, newPhase in
            if oldPhase == .interacting, newPhase != .interacting, progress >= 1 {
                beginRefreshing()
            }
        }
        .overlay(alignment: .top) { indicator }
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.35), value: isRefreshing)
        .task(id: refreshToken) {
            guard refreshToken != nil else { return }
            await action()
            isRefreshing = false
            refreshToken = nil
        }
    }

    private var indicator: some View {
        ZStack {
            Circle().stroke(tint.opacity(0.2), lineWidth: 3)

            if isRefreshing {
                ProgressView().tint(tint)
            } else {
                Circle()
                    .trim(from: 0, to: progress)
                    .stroke(tint, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 3, lineCap: .round))
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(-90))

                Image(systemName: "arrow.down")
                    .font(.footnote.weight(.bold))
                    .foregroundStyle(tint)
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(progress >= 1 ? 180 : 0))
            }
        }
        .frame(width: ringSize, height: ringSize)
        .padding(.top, isRefreshing ? 14 : max(0, min(pull, slotHeight) - ringSize) / 2)
        // Never fully transparent, so VoiceOver can still find the refresh action.
        .opacity(isRefreshing ? 1 : max(progress, 0.01))
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel(isRefreshing ? "Refreshing" : "Refresh")
        .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)
        .accessibilityAction { beginRefreshing() }
    }

    private func beginRefreshing() {
        guard !isRefreshing else { return }
        isRefreshing = true
        refreshToken = (refreshToken ?? 0) + 1
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct PullProgressRefreshDemo: View {
    @State private var updates = 0

    var body: some View {
        PullProgressRefresh(tint: .indigo) {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.4))
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            updates += 1
        } content: {
            LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
                Text("Inbox")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())

                Text(updates == 0 ? "Pull down to refresh" : "Updated \(updates) times")
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .contentTransition(.numericText())

                ForEach(0..<16, id: \.self) { index in
                    row(index)
                }
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 20)
            .padding(.top, 12)
        }
    }

    private func row(_ index: Int) -> some View {
        HStack(spacing: 14) {
            Circle()
                .fill(.indigo.gradient)
                .frame(width: 44, height: 44)
                .overlay {
                    Image(systemName: "envelope.fill")
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                }
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
                Text("Message \(index + 1 + updates)")
                    .font(.headline)

                Text("A short preview of the message")
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
        .padding(12)
        .background(.quaternary.opacity(0.5), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 16))
    }
}

#Preview {
    PullProgressRefreshDemo()
}
```

## Scroll Fade Cards

A vertical scroll of cards that scale down and fade at its edges with scrollTransition.

Category: Scrolling. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Scrolling/ScrollFadeCards/ScrollFadeCards.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A vertical scroll of cards that shrink and fade as they reach its edges.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the cards fade without scaling.
struct ScrollFadeCards<Item: Identifiable, Card: View>: View {
    let items: [Item]
    var spacing: CGFloat = 16
    var minimumScale: Double = 0.84
    var minimumOpacity: Double = 0.2
    @ViewBuilder var card: (Item) -> Card

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        // `scrollTransition` takes a `@Sendable` closure, so it works with local copies.
        let lowestScale = reduceMotion ? 1 : minimumScale
        let lowestOpacity = minimumOpacity

        ScrollView {
            LazyVStack(spacing: spacing) {
                ForEach(items) { item in
                    card(item)
                        .scrollTransition(.interactive.threshold(.visible(0.9))) { content, phase in
                            let distance = abs(phase.value)
                            return content
                                .scaleEffect(1 - distance * (1 - lowestScale))
                                .opacity(1 - distance * (1 - lowestOpacity))
                        }
                }
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 20)
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct ScrollFadeDemoCard: Identifiable {
    let id: Int
    let title: String
    let systemImage: String
    let colors: [Color]
}

struct ScrollFadeCardsDemo: View {

        let themes: [(String, String, [Color])] = [
            ("Ocean", "water.waves", [.blue, .cyan]),
            ("Sunrise", "sunrise.fill", [.orange, .pink]),
            ("Meadow", "leaf.fill", [.green, .mint]),
            ("Dusk", "moon.haze.fill", [.purple, .indigo]),
        ]
        return (0..<16).map { index in
            let theme = themes[index % themes.count]
            return ScrollFadeDemoCard(id: index, title: theme.0, systemImage: theme.1, colors: theme.2)
        }
    }()

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title) private var cardHeight = 170.0

    var body: some View {
        ScrollFadeCards(items: cards) { card in
            HStack(spacing: 16) {
                Image(systemName: card.systemImage)
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text(card.title)
                    .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                Spacer(minLength: 0)
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .padding(.horizontal, 28)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: cardHeight)
            .background(
                LinearGradient(colors: card.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing),
                in: .rect(cornerRadius: 26)
            )
        }
        .background(Color.black.ignoresSafeArea())
    }
}
```

## Scroll Progress Bar

A thin bar pinned to the top of a scroll view that grows with the reading progress of the content.

Category: Scrolling. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Scrolling/ScrollProgressBar/ScrollProgressBar.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum ScrollProgressBarMath {
    /// How far through the content the reader is, from 0 to 1.
    static func progress(offsetY: CGFloat, topInset: CGFloat, bottomInset: CGFloat, contentHeight: CGFloat, containerHeight: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        let scrollable = contentHeight + topInset + bottomInset - containerHeight
        guard scrollable > 0 else { return 0 }
        return min(max((offsetY + topInset) / scrollable, 0), 1)
    }
}

/// A thin bar pinned to the top of a scroll view that grows with the reading progress.
///
/// Apply it to the `ScrollView` with `.scrollProgressBar()`. The bar follows the scroll
/// position directly, so it has no animation of its own.
struct ScrollProgressBar: ViewModifier {
    var tint: LinearGradient
    var height: CGFloat

    @State private var progress: CGFloat = 0

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .onScrollGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { geometry in
                ScrollProgressBarMath.progress(
                    offsetY: geometry.contentOffset.y,
                    topInset: geometry.contentInsets.top,
                    bottomInset: geometry.contentInsets.bottom,
                    contentHeight: geometry.contentSize.height,
                    containerHeight: geometry.containerSize.height
                )
            } action: { _, newValue in
                progress = newValue
            }
            .overlay(alignment: .top) { bar }
    }

    private var bar: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            ZStack(alignment: .leading) {
                Capsule().fill(.quaternary)
                Capsule()
                    .fill(tint)
                    .frame(width: proxy.size.width * progress)
            }
        }
        .frame(height: max(height, 0))
        .padding(.horizontal, 12)
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Reading progress")
        .accessibilityValue(Double(progress).formatted(.percent.precision(.fractionLength(0))))
    }
}

extension View {
    func scrollProgressBar(
        tint: LinearGradient = LinearGradient(colors: [.pink, .orange], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing),
        height: CGFloat = 5
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(ScrollProgressBar(tint: tint, height: height))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ScrollProgressBarDemo: View {
    @State private var position = ScrollPosition(y: 0)
    @State private var maxOffset: CGFloat = 0
    /// Only for this demo: it plays by itself until someone touches it.
    @State private var isAutoPlaying = true
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let paragraph = "Good interfaces explain themselves. A small sign of how much is left can turn a long read into something that feels easy to finish, and it asks nothing of the reader."

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 20) {
                Text("The long read")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())

                ForEach(0..<14, id: \.self) { index in
                    Text("Chapter \(index + 1)")
                        .font(.title2.bold())

                    Text(paragraph)
                        .font(.body)
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
            }
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            .padding(24)
        }
        .scrollPosition($position)
        .scrollProgressBar()
        .onScrollGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { geometry in
            max(geometry.contentSize.height + geometry.contentInsets.top + geometry.contentInsets.bottom - geometry.containerSize.height, 0)
        } action: { _, newValue in
            maxOffset = newValue
        }
        .simultaneousGesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { _ in isAutoPlaying = false })
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            await autoScroll()
        }
    }

    // Only the demo scrolls by itself: down for most of the loop, then quickly back up.
    private func autoScroll() async {
        var time = 0.0
        while isAutoPlaying {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(16))
            guard !Task.isCancelled, isAutoPlaying else { return }
            time = (time + 0.016).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 3)
            let fraction = time < 2.4 ? time / 2.4 : (3 - time) / 0.6
            position.scrollTo(y: maxOffset * fraction)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ScrollProgressBarDemo()
}
```

## Scroll Visibility Reveal

Sections fade and slide into place the first time they become visible while the user scrolls.

Category: Scrolling. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Scrolling/ScrollVisibilityReveal/ScrollVisibilityReveal.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Fades and slides a view into place the first time it becomes visible in a scroll view.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the view only fades in. With VoiceOver on, it is shown from the
/// start, so a section that has not been reached yet can still be found.
struct ScrollVisibilityReveal: ViewModifier {
    var threshold: Double
    var distance: CGFloat

    @State private var hasAppeared = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.accessibilityVoiceOverEnabled) private var voiceOverEnabled

    private var isVisible: Bool { hasAppeared || voiceOverEnabled }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .opacity(isVisible ? 1 : 0)
            .offset(y: isVisible || reduceMotion ? 0 : distance)
            .onScrollVisibilityChange(threshold: min(max(threshold, 0), 1)) { visible in
                guard visible, !hasAppeared else { return }
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeIn(duration: 0.2) : .smooth(duration: 0.6)) {
                    hasAppeared = true
                }
            }
    }
}

extension View {
    /// A low threshold means a section taller than the screen still gets revealed.
    func scrollVisibilityReveal(threshold: Double = 0.15, distance: CGFloat = 36) -> some View {
        modifier(ScrollVisibilityReveal(threshold: threshold, distance: distance))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ScrollVisibilityRevealDemo: View {
    private struct Section: Identifiable {
        let id: String
        let symbol: String
        let colors: [Color]
    }

    private let sections = [
        Section(id: "Sunrise", symbol: "sunrise.fill", colors: [.orange, .pink]),
        Section(id: "Forest", symbol: "leaf.fill", colors: [.green, .teal]),
        Section(id: "Ocean", symbol: "water.waves", colors: [.cyan, .blue]),
        Section(id: "Night", symbol: "moon.stars.fill", colors: [.indigo, .purple]),
        Section(id: "Storm", symbol: "cloud.bolt.rain.fill", colors: [.gray, .indigo]),
        Section(id: "Snow", symbol: "snowflake", colors: [.mint, .cyan]),
    ]

    @State private var position = ScrollPosition(y: 0)
    @State private var maxOffset: CGFloat = 0
    @State private var cycle = 0
    /// Only for this demo: it plays by itself until someone touches it.
    @State private var isAutoPlaying = true
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(spacing: 18) {
                ForEach(sections) { section in
                    card(section)
                        .scrollVisibilityReveal()
                }
            }
            .padding(20)
        }
        // A new identity forgets what has been revealed, so the demo can replay it.
        .id(cycle)
        .scrollPosition($position)
        .onScrollGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { geometry in
            max(geometry.contentSize.height + geometry.contentInsets.top + geometry.contentInsets.bottom - geometry.containerSize.height, 0)
        } action: { _, newValue in
            maxOffset = newValue
        }
        .simultaneousGesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { _ in isAutoPlaying = false })
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            await replay()
        }
    }

    private func card(_ section: Section) -> some View {
        VStack(spacing: 12) {
            Image(systemName: section.symbol)
                .font(.largeTitle)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Text(section.id)
                .font(.title.bold())
        }
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: 240)
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: section.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 28))
    }

    // Only the demo scrolls by itself. Each pass scrolls to the end, then starts over.
    private func replay() async {
        var time = 0.0
        while isAutoPlaying {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(16))
            guard !Task.isCancelled, isAutoPlaying else { return }
            time += 0.016
            if time >= 4 {
                time = 0
                cycle += 1
            }
            position.scrollTo(y: maxOffset * min(time / 3.6, 1))
        }
    }
}

    ScrollVisibilityRevealDemo()
}
```

## Sticky Parallax Header

A parallax header that stretches on overscroll and collapses into a pinned bar.

Category: Scrolling. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Scrolling/StickyParallaxHeader/StickyParallaxHeader.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum StickyParallaxHeaderMath {
    /// How far the backdrop drifts up: half the scroll, stopping before its bottom edge shows.
    static func drift(offset: CGFloat, fullHeight: CGFloat, height: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        min(max(offset, 0) * 0.5, max(fullHeight - height, 0))
    }
}

/// A header that stretches on overscroll, drifts at half speed and collapses into a pinned bar.
///
/// `title` receives how collapsed the header is, from 0 to 1.
/// With Reduce Motion on, the backdrop does not drift.
struct StickyParallaxHeader<Backdrop: View, Title: View, Content: View>: View {
    var expandedHeight: CGFloat = 260
    var collapsedHeight: CGFloat = 60
    @ViewBuilder var backdrop: () -> Backdrop
    @ViewBuilder var title: (_ collapse: CGFloat) -> Title
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @State private var offset: CGFloat = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            let fullHeight = expandedHeight + proxy.safeAreaInsets.top
            let pinnedHeight = collapsedHeight + proxy.safeAreaInsets.top
            let height = max(pinnedHeight, fullHeight - offset)
            let collapse = min(max(offset / max(fullHeight - pinnedHeight, 1), 0), 1)

            ZStack(alignment: .top) {
                ScrollView {
                    VStack(spacing: 0) {
                        Color.clear.frame(height: fullHeight)
                        content()
                    }
                }
                .onScrollGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { geometry in
                    geometry.contentOffset.y + geometry.contentInsets.top
                } action: { _, newOffset in
                    offset = newOffset
                }

                header(height: height, fullHeight: fullHeight, collapse: collapse)
            }
            .ignoresSafeArea(edges: .top)
        }
    }

    private func header(height: CGFloat, fullHeight: CGFloat, collapse: CGFloat) -> some View {
        backdrop()
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .frame(height: max(fullHeight, height))
            .offset(y: reduceMotion ? 0 : -StickyParallaxHeaderMath.drift(offset: offset, fullHeight: fullHeight, height: height))
            .frame(height: height, alignment: .top)
            .clipped()
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
            .overlay(alignment: .bottomLeading) {
                title(collapse)
                    .padding(.horizontal, 20)
                    .padding(.bottom, 10)
            }
            .allowsHitTesting(false)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct StickyParallaxHeaderDemo: View {
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var collapsedHeight = 60.0

    private let trails = ["Tre Cime", "Seceda Ridge", "Lago di Braies", "Alpe di Siusi", "Sass Pordoi", "Cinque Torri", "Val di Funes", "Marmolada", "Passo Giau", "Lagazuoi"]

    var body: some View {
        StickyParallaxHeader(collapsedHeight: collapsedHeight) {
            ZStack(alignment: .bottom) {
                LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple, .orange], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                Image(systemName: "mountain.2.fill")
                    .resizable()
                    .scaledToFit()
                    .foregroundStyle(.black.opacity(0.35))
                    .padding(.horizontal, 24)
                    .offset(y: 30)
            }
        } title: { collapse in
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
                Text("Dolomites")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                    .scaleEffect(1 - 0.3 * collapse, anchor: .bottomLeading)
                Text("10 trails nearby")
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .opacity(1 - collapse * 2)
                    .frame(height: collapse > 0.5 ? 0 : nil, alignment: .top)
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        } content: {
            LazyVStack(spacing: 12) {
                ForEach(trails, id: \.self) { trail in
                    HStack(spacing: 14) {
                        Image(systemName: "figure.hiking")
                            .font(.title3)
                            .foregroundStyle(.indigo)
                            .accessibilityHidden(true)
                        Text(trail)
                            .font(.headline)
                        Spacer()
                    }
                    .padding(18)
                    .background(.indigo.opacity(0.1), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 18))
                }
            }
            .padding(16)
        }
    }
}
```

## Sticky Stacked Cards

Cards that pile up at the top of the screen as the next card scrolls over them.

Category: Scrolling. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Scrolling/StickyStackedCards/StickyStackedCards.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum StickyStackedCardsMath {
    /// How far down the card must move to stay pinned, 0 while it has not reached its pin.
    static func pinOffset(cardTop: CGFloat, pinY: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        max(pinY - cardTop, 0)
    }

    /// Where a card pins. The first few step down, so the edges of the pile stay visible.
    static func pinY(index: Int, top: CGFloat, peek: CGFloat, maxPeeking: Int) -> CGFloat {
        top + CGFloat(min(max(index, 0), max(maxPeeking, 0))) * max(peek, 0)
    }

    /// How much smaller a card gets as the next ones cover it.
    static func scale(pinOffset: CGFloat, cardHeight: CGFloat, spacing: CGFloat, step: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        let travel = cardHeight + max(spacing, 0)
        guard travel > 0 else { return 1 }
        return max(1 - min(pinOffset / travel, 4) * max(step, 0), 0.6)
    }
}

/// Cards that pile up at the top of the screen as the next card scrolls over them.
///
/// Place it inside a vertical `ScrollView`. With Reduce Motion on, the cards still pin in
/// place but do not shrink.
struct StickyStackedCards<Data: RandomAccessCollection, Card: View>: View where Data.Element: Identifiable {
    let data: Data
    var spacing: CGFloat = 20
    var top: CGFloat = 12
    var peek: CGFloat = 12
    var maxPeeking = 3
    @ViewBuilder var card: (Data.Element) -> Card

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        // `visualEffect` takes a `@Sendable` closure, so it works with local copies.
        let spacing = spacing
        let top = top
        let peek = peek
        let maxPeeking = maxPeeking
        let step: CGFloat = reduceMotion ? 0 : 0.05

        VStack(spacing: spacing) {
            ForEach(Array(data.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, element in
                card(element)
                    .visualEffect { content, proxy in
                        let pin = StickyStackedCardsMath.pinOffset(
                            cardTop: proxy.frame(in: .scrollView).minY,
                            pinY: StickyStackedCardsMath.pinY(index: index, top: top, peek: peek, maxPeeking: maxPeeking)
                        )
                        let scale = StickyStackedCardsMath.scale(pinOffset: pin, cardHeight: proxy.size.height, spacing: spacing, step: step)
                        return content
                            .scaleEffect(scale, anchor: .top)
                            .offset(y: pin)
                    }
            }
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct StickyStackedCardsDemo: View {
    private struct Plan: Identifiable {
        let id: String
        let symbol: String
        let colors: [Color]
    }

    private let plans = [
        Plan(id: "Design", symbol: "paintpalette.fill", colors: [.pink, .orange]),
        Plan(id: "Build", symbol: "hammer.fill", colors: [.indigo, .blue]),
        Plan(id: "Test", symbol: "checkmark.seal.fill", colors: [.teal, .green]),
        Plan(id: "Ship", symbol: "paperplane.fill", colors: [.purple, .pink]),
        Plan(id: "Learn", symbol: "lightbulb.fill", colors: [.orange, .yellow]),
    ]

    @State private var position = ScrollPosition(y: 0)
    @State private var maxOffset: CGFloat = 0
    /// Only for this demo: it plays by itself until someone touches it.
    @State private var isAutoPlaying = true
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            StickyStackedCards(data: plans) { plan in
                card(plan)
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 20)
            // Matches the default `top`, so the first card starts exactly at its pin.
            .padding(.top, 12)
            .padding(.bottom, 40)
        }
        .scrollPosition($position)
        .onScrollGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { geometry in
            max(geometry.contentSize.height + geometry.contentInsets.top + geometry.contentInsets.bottom - geometry.containerSize.height, 0)
        } action: { _, newValue in
            maxOffset = newValue
        }
        .simultaneousGesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { _ in isAutoPlaying = false })
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            await autoScroll()
        }
    }

    private func card(_ plan: Plan) -> some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10) {
            Image(systemName: plan.symbol)
                .font(.largeTitle)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Spacer(minLength: 24)

            Text(plan.id)
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())

            Text("Each step stacks on the last one as you scroll.")
                .font(.subheadline)
        }
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: 300, alignment: .leading)
        .padding(24)
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: plan.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 32))
    }

    // Only the demo scrolls by itself: slowly down, then quickly back to the top.
    private func autoScroll() async {
        var time = 0.0
        while isAutoPlaying {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(16))
            guard !Task.isCancelled, isAutoPlaying else { return }
            time = (time + 0.016).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 5)
            let fraction = time < 4 ? time / 4 : 5 - time
            position.scrollTo(y: maxOffset * fraction)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    StickyStackedCardsDemo()
}
```

## Vertical Full Screen Feed

A vertical feed where each item fills the screen and snaps into place, in the style of short-video apps.

Category: Scrolling. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Scrolling/VerticalFullScreenFeed/VerticalFullScreenFeed.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct VerticalFullScreenFeedItem: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let image: Image
    let title: String
    let subtitle: String
    /// What the image shows, for VoiceOver. Leave it nil when the image is decoration.
    var imageLabel: String?
}

/// A vertical feed where each item fills the screen and snaps into place.
///
/// The paging is driven by the finger, so Reduce Motion does not change it.
struct VerticalFullScreenFeed: View {
    let items: [VerticalFullScreenFeedItem]
    var selection: Binding<String?> = .constant(nil)

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { outer in
            ScrollView {
                LazyVStack(spacing: 0) {
                    ForEach(items) { item in
                        page(item, bottomInset: outer.safeAreaInsets.bottom)
                            .containerRelativeFrame([.horizontal, .vertical])
                    }
                }
                .scrollTargetLayout()
            }
            .scrollTargetBehavior(.paging)
            .scrollPosition(id: selection)
            .scrollIndicators(.hidden)
            .ignoresSafeArea()
        }
        .background(.black)
    }

    private func page(_ item: VerticalFullScreenFeedItem, bottomInset: CGFloat) -> some View {
        // The clear base takes the page size, so a large image cannot change the layout.
        Color.clear
            .overlay { pageImage(item) }
            .clipped()
            .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
                LinearGradient(colors: [.clear, .black.opacity(0.75)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                    .frame(height: 320)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .overlay(alignment: .bottomLeading) {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
                    Text(item.title)
                        .font(.title.bold())

                    Text(item.subtitle)
                        .font(.body)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.85))
                }
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .padding(.horizontal, 20)
                .padding(.bottom, bottomInset + 20)
                .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
            }
    }

    @ViewBuilder
    private func pageImage(_ item: VerticalFullScreenFeedItem) -> some View {
        let image = item.image.resizable().scaledToFill()

        if let label = item.imageLabel {
            image.accessibilityLabel(label)
        } else {
            image.accessibilityRepresentation { EmptyView() }
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct VerticalFullScreenFeedDemo: View {
    @State private var items = [
        VerticalFullScreenFeedDemo.item("Mountains at dawn", symbol: "mountain.2.fill", colors: [.orange, .pink, .indigo], imageLabel: "Two mountain peaks on a pink sky"),
        VerticalFullScreenFeedDemo.item("A walk in the forest", symbol: "tree.fill", colors: [.mint, .green, .teal], imageLabel: "A tree on a green background"),
        VerticalFullScreenFeedDemo.item("Deep blue water", symbol: "water.waves", colors: [.cyan, .blue, .indigo], imageLabel: "Waves on a blue background"),
        VerticalFullScreenFeedDemo.item("Under the stars", symbol: "moon.stars.fill", colors: [.purple, .indigo, .black], imageLabel: "A moon and stars on a dark sky"),
    ]
    @State private var selection: String?
    /// Only for this demo: it plays by itself until someone touches it.
    @State private var isAutoPlaying = true
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VerticalFullScreenFeed(items: items, selection: $selection)
            .simultaneousGesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { _ in isAutoPlaying = false })
            .task(id: reduceMotion) {
                guard !reduceMotion else { return }
                await autoAdvance()
            }
    }

    // Only the demo advances by itself. In an app the user swipes between pages.
    private func autoAdvance() async {
        var index = 0
        while isAutoPlaying {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.6))
            guard !Task.isCancelled, isAutoPlaying, !items.isEmpty else { return }
            index = (index + 1) % items.count
            withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.6)) {
                selection = items[index].id
            }
        }
    }

    // Draws a placeholder poster, so the demo needs no image files or network.
    private static func item(_ title: String, symbol: String, colors: [Color], imageLabel: String) -> VerticalFullScreenFeedItem {
        let poster = ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)

            Image(systemName: symbol)
                .font(.system(size: 170))
                .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.85))
        }
        .frame(width: 402, height: 874)

        let renderer = ImageRenderer(content: poster)
        renderer.scale = 2
        let image = renderer.uiImage.map(Image.init(uiImage:)) ?? Image(systemName: symbol)
        return VerticalFullScreenFeedItem(id: title, image: image, title: title, subtitle: "A placeholder drawn with a gradient and a symbol.", imageLabel: imageLabel)
    }
}

#Preview {
    VerticalFullScreenFeedDemo()
}
```

## Custom Detent Sheet

A system sheet that snaps between custom heights using presentationDetents and a CustomPresentationDetent.

Category: Sheets. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Sheets/CustomDetentSheet/CustomDetentSheet.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A system sheet that snaps between custom heights with `presentationDetents`.
///
/// Set `interactiveUpThrough` to keep the content behind usable up to that height. The
/// system sheet animation already honours Reduce Motion.
struct CustomDetentSheet<SheetContent: View>: ViewModifier {
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    var detents: Set<PresentationDetent>
    @Binding var selection: PresentationDetent
    var interactiveUpThrough: PresentationDetent?
    @ViewBuilder var sheetContent: () -> SheetContent

    private var backgroundInteraction: PresentationBackgroundInteraction {
        interactiveUpThrough.map { .enabled(upThrough: $0) } ?? .automatic
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.sheet(isPresented: $isPresented) {
            sheetContent()
                .presentationDetents(detents.isEmpty ? [selection] : detents, selection: $selection)
                .presentationDragIndicator(.visible)
                .presentationBackgroundInteraction(backgroundInteraction)
                .presentationCornerRadius(30)
        }
    }
}

extension View {
    func customDetentSheet<SheetContent: View>(
        isPresented: Binding<Bool>,
        detents: Set<PresentationDetent>,
        selection: Binding<PresentationDetent>,
        interactiveUpThrough: PresentationDetent? = nil,
        @ViewBuilder content: @escaping () -> SheetContent
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(CustomDetentSheet(
            isPresented: isPresented,
            detents: detents,
            selection: selection,
            interactiveUpThrough: interactiveUpThrough,
            sheetContent: content
        ))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct CustomDetentSheetPeek: CustomPresentationDetent {
    static func height(in context: Context) -> CGFloat? {
        guard context.maxDetentValue > 0 else { return nil }
        return max(context.maxDetentValue * 0.22, min(context.maxDetentValue, 150))
    }
}

struct CustomDetentSheetDemo: View {
    private let peek = PresentationDetent.custom(CustomDetentSheetPeek.self)
    private let middle = PresentationDetent.height(400)
    private let stops = ["Museum", "Old town", "Riverside", "Market", "Viewpoint", "Harbour"]

    @State private var isPresented = false
    @State private var selection = PresentationDetent.height(400)
    /// Only for this demo: it plays by itself until someone touches it.
    @State private var isAutoPlaying = true
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.teal, .blue, .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 16) {
                Text("City walk")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)

                Button("Show stops") { isPresented = true }
                    .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                    .tint(.white.opacity(0.25))
            }
            .frame(maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .top)
            .padding(.top, 60)
        }
        .customDetentSheet(
            isPresented: $isPresented,
            detents: [peek, middle, .large],
            selection: $selection,
            interactiveUpThrough: peek
        ) {
            sheet
        }
        .simultaneousGesture(stopAutoPlay)
        .task { isPresented = true }
        .task(id: isPresented && !reduceMotion) {
            guard isPresented, !reduceMotion else { return }
            await cycleDetents()
        }
    }

    private var sheet: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 14) {
                Text("Today's stops")
                    .font(.title2.bold())

                ForEach(stops, id: \.self) { stop in
                    Label(stop, systemImage: "mappin.circle.fill")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                        .padding(14)
                        .background(.quaternary.opacity(0.6), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 16))
                }
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
        // The sheet is its own presentation, so a touch in it does not reach the gesture behind.
        .simultaneousGesture(stopAutoPlay)
    }

    private var stopAutoPlay: some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { _ in isAutoPlaying = false }
    }

    // Only the demo moves the sheet by itself, by changing the selected detent.
    private func cycleDetents() async {
        let order = [peek, middle, .large, middle]
        var index = 0
        var expected = selection
        while isAutoPlaying {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.1))
            guard !Task.isCancelled, isAutoPlaying else { return }
            // Dragging the sheet by its grabber does not touch its content, but it changes the detent.
            guard selection == expected else {
                isAutoPlaying = false
                return
            }
            expected = order[index]
            withAnimation(.snappy(duration: 0.4)) {
                selection = expected
            }
            index = (index + 1) % order.count
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    CustomDetentSheetDemo()
}
```

## Dynamic Height Tray

A sheet exactly as tall as its content, which grows and shrinks as one step of a flow gives way to the next.

Category: Sheets. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Sheets/DynamicHeightTray/DynamicHeightTray.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum DynamicHeightTrayLogic {
    /// The height the tray takes for content that is `content` tall: never under `minimum` nor
    /// over `maximum`, and a whole number of points, so a measure that is off by a fraction
    /// does not start another round of layout.
    static func height(content: Double, minimum: Double = 80, maximum: Double) -> Double {
        guard content.isFinite, maximum.isFinite else { return minimum }
        return min(max(content.rounded(.up), minimum), max(maximum, minimum))
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Presents a sheet that is exactly as tall as its content, and that grows or shrinks with
    /// it when the content changes, as when one step of a flow gives way to the next.
    ///
    /// Change the content inside `withAnimation` and the tray follows it. The content is measured
    /// at the height it asks for, so give a list too long for the screen a frame of its own.
    func dynamicHeightTray<Tray: View>(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping () -> Tray) -> some View {
        modifier(DynamicHeightTrayModifier(isPresented: isPresented, tray: content))
    }
}

private struct DynamicHeightTrayModifier<Tray: View>: ViewModifier {
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    @ViewBuilder var tray: () -> Tray

    /// The share of the screen the tray may take at most.
    private let maximumShare = 0.9

    @State private var detents: Set<PresentationDetent> = [.height(240)]
    @State private var detent = PresentationDetent.height(240)
    @State private var available: CGFloat = 800

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.height } action: { available = $0 }
            .sheet(isPresented: $isPresented) {
                tray()
                    .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
                    .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.height } action: { measured in
                        // A sheet animates from one detent to another, but not a detent that
                        // changes its height. So the new height joins the old one, the sheet
                        // moves to it, and the old one goes once it has arrived.
                        let fitted = PresentationDetent.height(DynamicHeightTrayLogic.height(content: measured, maximum: available * maximumShare))
                        detents.insert(fitted)
                        detent = fitted
                    }
                    .frame(maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .top)
                    .presentationDetents(detents, selection: $detent)
                    .presentationDragIndicator(.visible)
                    .task(id: detent) {
                        try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.6))
                        if !Task.isCancelled { detents = [detent] }
                    }
            }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct DynamicHeightTrayDemo: View {
    private enum Step {
        case options, confirm, done
    }

    @State private var isPresented = false
    @State private var step = Step.options
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 14) {
            Image(systemName: "wallet.bifold.fill")
                .font(.system(size: 52))
                .foregroundStyle(.tint)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            Text("Main Wallet")
                .font(.title2.bold())

            Button("Manage Wallet") {
                step = .options
                isPresented = true
            }
            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
            .controlSize(.large)
            .padding(.top, 8)
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground))
        .dynamicHeightTray(isPresented: $isPresented) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
                switch step {
                case .options: options
                case .confirm: confirm
                case .done: done
                }
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 24)
            .padding(.top, 32)
            .padding(.bottom, 16)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
        }
    }

    private func go(to next: Step) {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.35)) { step = next }
    }

    @ViewBuilder private var options: some View {
        Text("Manage Wallet")
            .font(.title3.bold())

        row("View Recovery Phrase", symbol: "key.fill") {}
        row("Rename Wallet", symbol: "pencil") {}
        row("Hide Small Balances", symbol: "eye.slash.fill") {}
        row("Remove Wallet", symbol: "trash.fill", role: .destructive) {
            go(to: .confirm)
        }
    }

    @ViewBuilder private var confirm: some View {
        Text("Remove this wallet?")
            .font(.title3.bold())
        Text("You will need its recovery phrase to add it again.")
            .font(.subheadline)
            .foregroundStyle(.secondary)

        HStack(spacing: 12) {
            Button("Cancel") {
                go(to: .options)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.bordered)

            Button("Remove", role: .destructive) {
                go(to: .done)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
        }
        .controlSize(.large)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
    }

    @ViewBuilder private var done: some View {
        Label("Wallet removed", systemImage: "checkmark.circle.fill")
            .font(.title3.bold())
            .foregroundStyle(.green)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .padding(.vertical, 8)
    }

    private func row(_ title: String, symbol: String, role: ButtonRole? = nil, action: @escaping () -> Void) -> some View {
        Button(role: role, action: action) {
            Label(title, systemImage: symbol)
                .font(.body.weight(.medium))
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                .padding(.vertical, 14)
                .padding(.horizontal, 16)
                .background(.fill.quaternary, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 14))
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .foregroundStyle(role == .destructive ? AnyShapeStyle(.red) : AnyShapeStyle(.primary))
    }
}
```

## What's New Sheet

A sheet that lists what a new version brings and comes up once for each version.

Category: Sheets. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Sheets/WhatsNewSheet/WhatsNewSheet.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum WhatsNewSheetLogic {
    /// Whether `version` comes after the one that was already shown, comparing number by number,
    /// so 2.10 is newer than 2.9 and 2.0 is the same as 2. Nothing shown yet counts as older.
    static func isNewer(_ version: String, than seen: String) -> Bool {
        let new = numbers(in: version)
        let old = numbers(in: seen)
        for index in 0..<max(new.count, old.count) {
            let left = index < new.count ? new[index] : 0
            let right = index < old.count ? old[index] : 0
            if left != right { return left > right }
        }
        return false
    }

    static func numbers(in version: String) -> [Int] {
        version.split(separator: ".").map { Int($0) ?? 0 }
    }

    /// How long a row waits before it comes in, so they arrive one after another without the
    /// last ones of a long list taking too long.
    static func delay(for index: Int, step: Double = 0.12, limit: Double = 0.6) -> Double {
        min(Double(max(index, 0)) * step, limit)
    }
}

struct WhatsNewSheetFeature: Identifiable {
    var symbol: String
    var title: LocalizedStringResource
    var text: LocalizedStringResource
    var tint: Color = .accentColor

    var id: String { title.key }
}

/// The page that tells what a new version brings: a title, a row per feature and a button.
///
/// Show it yourself in a sheet, or let `whatsNewSheet(version:features:)` show it once per version.
/// The rows come in one after another. With Reduce Motion on, they fade in together.
struct WhatsNewSheet: View {
    var title: LocalizedStringResource = "What’s New"
    let features: [WhatsNewSheetFeature]
    var buttonTitle = "Continue"
    var onContinue: () -> Void

    private let margin: CGFloat = 32

    @State private var hasAppeared = false
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title) private var symbolWidth = 44.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(spacing: 40) {
                Text(title)
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                    .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                    .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)

                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 28) {
                    ForEach(Array(features.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, feature in
                        row(feature)
                            .opacity(hasAppeared ? 1 : 0)
                            .offset(y: hasAppeared || reduceMotion ? 0 : 18)
                            .animation(animation(for: index), value: hasAppeared)
                    }
                }
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, margin)
            .padding(.top, 56)
            .padding(.bottom, 24)
            .frame(maxWidth: 520)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
        }
        .scrollBounceBehavior(.basedOnSize)
        .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) {
            Button(action: onContinue) {
                Text(buttonTitle)
                    .font(.headline)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
            .controlSize(.large)
            .padding(.horizontal, margin)
            .padding(.vertical, 12)
            .frame(maxWidth: 520)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .background(.bar)
        }
        .onAppear { hasAppeared = true }
    }

    private func row(_ feature: WhatsNewSheetFeature) -> some View {
        HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 16) {
            Image(systemName: feature.symbol)
                .font(.title)
                .foregroundStyle(feature.tint)
                .frame(width: symbolWidth)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
                Text(feature.title)
                    .font(.headline)
                Text(feature.text)
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
    }

    private func animation(for index: Int) -> Animation {
        reduceMotion
            ? .easeOut(duration: 0.25)
            : .spring(duration: 0.5).delay(WhatsNewSheetLogic.delay(for: index))
    }
}

struct WhatsNewSheetModifier: ViewModifier {
    let version: String
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let features: [WhatsNewSheetFeature]

    @AppStorage private var seenVersion: String
    @State private var isPresented = false

    init(version: String, title: LocalizedStringResource, features: [WhatsNewSheetFeature], storageKey: String) {
        self.version = version
        self.title = title
        self.features = features
        _seenVersion = AppStorage(wrappedValue: "", storageKey)
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .onChange(of: seenVersion, initial: true) {
                if WhatsNewSheetLogic.isNewer(version, than: seenVersion) { isPresented = true }
            }
            .sheet(isPresented: $isPresented) {
                seenVersion = version
            } content: {
                WhatsNewSheet(title: title, features: features) {
                    isPresented = false
                }
            }
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Shows `WhatsNewSheet` the first time the app runs a `version` newer than the last one it
    /// was shown for, and remembers it in `UserDefaults` when the sheet closes.
    func whatsNewSheet(version: String, title: LocalizedStringResource = "What’s New", features: [WhatsNewSheetFeature], storageKey: String = "WhatsNewSheet.seenVersion") -> some View {
        modifier(WhatsNewSheetModifier(version: version, title: title, features: features, storageKey: storageKey))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct WhatsNewSheetDemo: View {
    private let storageKey = "WhatsNewSheetDemo.seenVersion"
    private let features = [
        WhatsNewSheetFeature(symbol: "square.and.pencil", title: "Quick Notes", text: "Start a note from anywhere and find it later in its own folder.", tint: .orange),
        WhatsNewSheetFeature(symbol: "tag.fill", title: "Smart Tags", text: "Add a tag as you write and browse every note that shares it.", tint: .teal),
        WhatsNewSheetFeature(symbol: "person.2.fill", title: "Shared Folders", text: "Invite people to a folder and see their changes as they make them.", tint: .indigo),
        WhatsNewSheetFeature(symbol: "lock.fill", title: "Locked Notes", text: "Keep a note behind Face ID, so only you can open it.", tint: .pink),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 16) {
            Image(systemName: "note.text")
                .font(.system(size: 56))
                .foregroundStyle(.tint)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            Text("Notes 2.4")
                .font(.title2.bold())
            Text("The sheet comes up once for each new version.")
                .font(.subheadline)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                .multilineTextAlignment(.center)

            Button("Show Again", action: forget)
                .buttonStyle(.bordered)
                .padding(.top, 8)
        }
        .padding(32)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground))
        .whatsNewSheet(version: "2.4", features: features, storageKey: storageKey)
        .onAppear(perform: forget)
    }

    /// Forgets the version the sheet was shown for, as if the app had just been updated.
    private func forget() {
        UserDefaults.standard.removeObject(forKey: storageKey)
    }
}

#Preview {
    WhatsNewSheetDemo()
}
```

## Minimizing Tab Bar

A tab bar that shrinks into a compact capsule while scrolling using the system tab bar minimize behavior.

Category: Tabs. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Tabs/MinimizingTabBar/MinimizingTabBar.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A tab view whose tab bar shrinks into a compact capsule while the content scrolls.
///
/// The system draws and animates the bar, and honours Reduce Motion. Each tab needs a
/// scroll view for the bar to react.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct MinimizingTabBar<Selection: Hashable, Tabs: TabContent>: View where Tabs.TabValue == Selection {
    @Binding var selection: Selection
    var behavior: TabBarMinimizeBehavior = .onScrollDown
    @TabContentBuilder<Selection> var tabs: () -> Tabs

    var body: some View {
        TabView(selection: $selection) {
            tabs()
        }
        .tabBarMinimizeBehavior(behavior)
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)

        case listen, browse, library
    }

    @State private var selection = Screen.listen

        MinimizingTabBar(selection: $selection) {
            Tab("Listen", systemImage: "play.circle.fill", value: Screen.listen) {
                screen(title: "Listen now", symbol: "music.note", colors: [.pink, .orange])
            }

            Tab("Browse", systemImage: "square.grid.2x2.fill", value: Screen.browse) {
                screen(title: "New releases", symbol: "sparkles", colors: [.purple, .indigo])
            }

            Tab("Library", systemImage: "books.vertical.fill", value: Screen.library) {

                            .frame(width: 56, height: 56)

                            .accessibilityHidden(true)

                }
            }
            .padding(20)
        }
    }
}
```

## Notched Tab Bar

A tab bar whose background path carves a smooth notch under the selected tab that slides between items.

Category: Tabs. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Tabs/NotchedTabBar/NotchedTabBar.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct NotchedTabBarItem: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let systemImage: String
}

nonisolated enum NotchedTabBarMath {
    /// The middle of a tab, with the tabs spread evenly inside the horizontal inset.
    static func centerX(index: Int, count: Int, width: CGFloat, inset: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        let usable = max(width - 2 * max(inset, 0), 0)
        guard count > 0, usable > 0 else { return max(width, 0) / 2 }
        let clamped = min(max(index, 0), count - 1)
        return max(inset, 0) + usable * (CGFloat(clamped) + 0.5) / CGFloat(count)
    }

    /// Half the width of the notch, narrowed so it never runs into a rounded corner.
    static func halfSpan(centerX: CGFloat, width: CGFloat, corner: CGFloat, desired: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        max(min(desired, centerX - corner, width - centerX - corner), 0)
    }
}

/// A rounded bar with a smooth notch that can slide along its top edge.
nonisolated struct NotchedTabBarShape: Shape {
    var centerX: CGFloat
    var desiredHalfSpan: CGFloat
    var depth: CGFloat
    var corner: CGFloat

    var animatableData: CGFloat {
        get { centerX }
        set { centerX = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        guard rect.width > 0, rect.height > 0 else { return Path() }

        let radius = min(corner, rect.width / 2, rect.height / 2)
        let span = NotchedTabBarMath.halfSpan(centerX: centerX, width: rect.width, corner: radius, desired: desiredHalfSpan)
        let dip = min(depth, rect.height)
        let (w, h) = (rect.width, rect.height)

        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: radius))
        path.addArc(tangent1End: .zero, tangent2End: CGPoint(x: radius, y: 0), radius: radius)
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: centerX - span, y: 0))
        // Each side is two curves that share a tangent, so the notch has no visible seam.
        path.addQuadCurve(to: CGPoint(x: centerX - span * 0.5, y: dip * 0.5), control: CGPoint(x: centerX - span * 0.62, y: 0))
        path.addQuadCurve(to: CGPoint(x: centerX, y: dip), control: CGPoint(x: centerX - span * 0.38, y: dip))
        path.addQuadCurve(to: CGPoint(x: centerX + span * 0.5, y: dip * 0.5), control: CGPoint(x: centerX + span * 0.38, y: dip))
        path.addQuadCurve(to: CGPoint(x: centerX + span, y: 0), control: CGPoint(x: centerX + span * 0.62, y: 0))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: w - radius, y: 0))
        path.addArc(tangent1End: CGPoint(x: w, y: 0), tangent2End: CGPoint(x: w, y: radius), radius: radius)
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: w, y: h - radius))
        path.addArc(tangent1End: CGPoint(x: w, y: h), tangent2End: CGPoint(x: w - radius, y: h), radius: radius)
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: radius, y: h))
        path.addArc(tangent1End: CGPoint(x: 0, y: h), tangent2End: CGPoint(x: 0, y: h - radius), radius: radius)
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

/// A tab bar whose background carves a smooth notch under the selected tab.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the notch moves to the new tab without sliding.
struct NotchedTabBar: View {
    let items: [NotchedTabBarItem]
    @Binding var selection: String
    var tint: Color = .indigo

    var body: some View {
        NotchedTabBarStage(items: items, selection: $selection, tint: tint)
            // The bar only holds short labels. The stage reads its sizes under this cap, which keeps every tab on screen.
            .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.xxxLarge)
    }
}

private struct NotchedTabBarStage: View {
    let items: [NotchedTabBarItem]
    @Binding var selection: String
    let tint: Color

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) private var barHeight = 72.0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title3) private var bubbleSize = 52.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let inset: CGFloat = 14

    private var selectedIndex: Int {
        items.firstIndex { $0.id == selection } ?? 0
    }

    var body: some View {
        let depth = bubbleSize * 0.7
        let bubbleY = depth - bubbleSize / 2 - 6

        GeometryReader { proxy in
            let center = NotchedTabBarMath.centerX(index: selectedIndex, count: items.count, width: proxy.size.width, inset: inset)

            ZStack(alignment: .topLeading) {
                NotchedTabBarShape(centerX: center, desiredHalfSpan: bubbleSize * 0.95, depth: depth, corner: 26)
                    .fill(.background)
                    .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.15), radius: 14, y: 6)

                if !items.isEmpty {
                    Circle()
                        .fill(tint.gradient)
                        .frame(width: bubbleSize, height: bubbleSize)
                        .position(x: center, y: bubbleY)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }

                HStack(spacing: 0) {
                    ForEach(items) { item in
                        tabButton(item, iconLift: barHeight / 2 - 10 - bubbleY)
                    }
                }
                .padding(.horizontal, inset)
            }
        }
        .frame(height: barHeight)
        .padding(.top, bubbleSize / 2)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.4), value: selection)
    }

    private func tabButton(_ item: NotchedTabBarItem, iconLift: CGFloat) -> some View {
        let isSelected = item.id == selection

        return Button {
            selection = item.id
        } label: {
            VStack(spacing: 4) {
                Image(systemName: item.systemImage)
                    .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))
                    .foregroundStyle(isSelected ? .white : .secondary)
                    .offset(y: isSelected ? -iconLift : 0)

                Text(item.title)
                    .font(.caption)
                    .fontWeight(isSelected ? .semibold : .regular)
                    .foregroundStyle(isSelected ? tint : .secondary)
            }
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
            .contentShape(.rect)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(item.title)
        .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct NotchedTabBarDemo: View {
    private let items = [
        NotchedTabBarItem(id: "home", title: "Home", systemImage: "house.fill"),
        NotchedTabBarItem(id: "search", title: "Search", systemImage: "magnifyingglass"),
        NotchedTabBarItem(id: "saved", title: "Saved", systemImage: "bookmark.fill"),
        NotchedTabBarItem(id: "profile", title: "Profile", systemImage: "person.fill"),
    ]

    @State private var selection = "home"

    private var heading: LocalizedStringResource {
        items.first { $0.id == selection }.map { "\($0.title) page" } ?? ""
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack(alignment: .bottom) {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo.opacity(0.35), .pink.opacity(0.25)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            Text(heading)
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)

            NotchedTabBar(items: items, selection: $selection)
                .padding(.horizontal, 16)
                .padding(.bottom, 8)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    NotchedTabBarDemo()
}
```

## Scrolling Tab Strip

A horizontal row of tabs that scrolls the selected tab into the middle, with an underline that slides between tabs.

Category: Tabs. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Tabs/ScrollingTabStrip/ScrollingTabStrip.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A horizontal row of tabs that scrolls the selected tab into the middle.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the row and the underline jump to the new tab.
struct ScrollingTabStrip: View {
    let tabs: [String]
    @Binding var selection: String
    var tint: Color = .pink

    @Namespace private var namespace
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var animation: Animation? {
        reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.35)
    }

    var body: some View {
        ScrollViewReader { proxy in
            ScrollView(.horizontal) {
                HStack(spacing: 22) {
                    ForEach(tabs, id: \.self) { tab in
                        tabButton(tab)
                            .id(tab)
                    }
                }
                .padding(.horizontal, 20)
            }
            .scrollIndicators(.hidden)
            .onChange(of: selection, initial: true) { _, newValue in
                withAnimation(animation) {
                    proxy.scrollTo(newValue, anchor: .center)
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private func tabButton(_ tab: String) -> some View {
        let isSelected = tab == selection

        return Button {
            withAnimation(animation) { selection = tab }
        } label: {
            VStack(spacing: 8) {
                Text(tab)
                    .font(.headline)
                    .foregroundStyle(isSelected ? .primary : .secondary)

                ZStack {
                    Capsule().fill(.clear)

                    if isSelected {
                        Capsule()
                            .fill(tint)
                            .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "underline", in: namespace)
                    }
                }
                .frame(height: 3)
            }
            .fixedSize()
            // A tab is shorter than a touch target. The padding widens what answers to a
            // touch, and the same padding taken back keeps the strip as it was.
            .padding(.horizontal, 2)
            .padding(.vertical, 7)
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .padding(.horizontal, -2)
            .padding(.vertical, -7)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(tab)
        .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ScrollingTabStripDemo: View {
    private let tabs = ["For You", "Trending", "Music", "Sports", "Travel", "Food", "Science", "Design", "Movies", "Gaming"]
    private let symbols = ["sparkles", "flame.fill", "music.note", "figure.run", "airplane", "fork.knife", "atom", "paintbrush.fill", "film.fill", "gamecontroller.fill"]

    @State private var selection = "For You"

    private var index: Int { tabs.firstIndex(of: selection) ?? 0 }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 18) {
            ScrollingTabStrip(tabs: tabs, selection: $selection)
                .padding(.top, 12)

            ZStack {
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 32)
                    .fill(LinearGradient(colors: [.pink, .orange], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
                    .hueRotation(.degrees(Double(index) * 34))

                VStack(spacing: 16) {
                    Image(systemName: symbols[index])
                        .font(.largeTitle)
                        .imageScale(.large)
                        .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)

                    Text("Stories about \(selection)")
                        .font(.title.bold())
                        .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                }
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .padding(24)
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 20)
            .padding(.bottom, 20)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ScrollingTabStripDemo()
}
```

## Tabs Picker Pages

A row of tabs over a page that slides in with them, on the tabs picker style of iOS 27.

Category: Tabs. Minimum: iOS 27.0. Path: Components/Tabs/TabsPickerPages/TabsPickerPages.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum TabsPickerPagesLogic {
    /// Whether going from one option to another moves forward through the options, which decides
    /// the side the new page comes in from. An option that is not listed counts as the first.
    static func movesForward<Option: Equatable>(from old: Option, to new: Option, in options: [Option]) -> Bool {
        (options.firstIndex(of: new) ?? 0) >= (options.firstIndex(of: old) ?? 0)
    }
}

/// A row of tabs over a page that changes with them, using the tabs picker style that iOS 27
/// added to `Picker`. On an iPhone the system draws it much like a segmented control, with
/// the text of each label.
///
/// The new page slides in from the side its tab is on. It is a system `Picker`, so VoiceOver
/// and the keyboard are the system's. With Reduce Motion on, the pages cross-fade.
@available(iOS 27, *)
struct TabsPickerPages<Option: Hashable, Label: View, Page: View>: View {
    let options: [Option]
    @Binding var selection: Option
    var title = "Section"
    @ViewBuilder var label: (Option) -> Label
    @ViewBuilder var page: (Option) -> Page

    @State private var movesForward = true
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 16) {
            Picker(title, selection: $selection) {
                ForEach(options, id: \.self) { option in
                    label(option)
                        .tag(option)
                }
            }
            .pickerStyle(.tabs)

            page(selection)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .top)
                .id(selection)
                .transition(transition)
        }
        .onChange(of: selection) { old, new in
            movesForward = TabsPickerPagesLogic.movesForward(from: old, to: new, in: options)
        }
        .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .snappy(duration: 0.35), value: selection)
    }

    private var transition: AnyTransition {
        guard !reduceMotion else { return .opacity }
        return .asymmetric(
            insertion: .move(edge: movesForward ? .trailing : .leading).combined(with: .opacity),
            removal: .move(edge: movesForward ? .leading : .trailing).combined(with: .opacity)
        )
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 27, *)
struct TabsPickerPagesDemo: View {
    private enum Section: String, CaseIterable {
        case overview = "Overview"
        case activity = "Activity"
        case files = "Files"

            case .overview: "square.grid.2x2"
```

## Animated Gradient Text

Text filled with a gradient that drifts endlessly through its letters.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/AnimatedGradientText/AnimatedGradientText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Text filled with a gradient that drifts endlessly through the letters.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the gradient stays still.
struct AnimatedGradientText: View {
    let text: String
    var colors: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .yellow, .mint, .cyan, .purple]
    /// Seconds for the colors to drift one full cycle.
    var duration: Double = 4

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 60.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            Text(text)
                .foregroundStyle(gradient(at: reduceMotion ? 0 : context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate))
        }
    }

    /// The gradient holds two copies of the colors and spans two text widths. Sliding it
    /// left by one width lands on an identical picture, so the loop has no visible seam.
    private func gradient(at time: TimeInterval) -> LinearGradient {
        let shift = time.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: duration) / duration

        return LinearGradient(
            colors: colors + colors + colors.prefix(1),
            startPoint: UnitPoint(x: -shift, y: 0.5),
            endPoint: UnitPoint(x: 2 - shift, y: 0.5)
        )
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct AnimatedGradientTextDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Color.black.ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 16) {
                AnimatedGradientText(text: "Colors that\nnever stand\nstill")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .black))
                    .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                    .scaleEffect(1.3)

                AnimatedGradientText(text: "Drifting through every letter", colors: [.mint, .cyan, .indigo], duration: 3)
                    .font(.headline)
                    .padding(.top, 48)
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
    }
}
```
