## Bouncy Letters Text

Letters that hop one after another in a repeating wave with squash and stretch.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/BouncyLettersText/BouncyLettersText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Letters that hop one after another, in a repeating wave.
///
/// Letters are laid out one by one, so it suits a short single line.
/// With Reduce Motion on, it is plain text.
struct BouncyLettersText: View {
    let text: String
    /// Seconds between one letter's hop and the next one's.
    var stagger: Double = 0.08
    /// Seconds of rest after the last letter lands.
    var pause: Double = 0.7

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var hopHeight = 28.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            Text(text)
        } else {
            let letters = Array(text)

            HStack(spacing: 0) {
                ForEach(letters.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                    letter(letters[index], index: index, count: letters.count)
                }
            }
            .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
            .accessibilityLabel(text)
        }
    }

    /// Every letter's timeline has the same total length, so they stay in step as they repeat.
    private func letter(_ character: Character, index: Int, count: Int) -> some View {
        let firstLead = 0.001
        let rise = 0.16
        let fall = 0.16
        let settle = 0.2
        let period = firstLead + Double(count - 1) * stagger + rise + fall + settle + pause
        let lead = max(Double(index) * stagger, firstLead)
        let rest = period - lead - rise - fall - settle
        let height = hopHeight

        return Text(String(character))
            .accessibilityRepresentation { EmptyView() }
            .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: BouncyLetterPose(), repeating: true) { view, pose in
                view
                    .scaleEffect(x: 2 - pose.stretch, y: pose.stretch, anchor: .bottom)
                    .offset(y: pose.lift)
            } keyframes: { _ in
                KeyframeTrack(\.lift) {
                    LinearKeyframe(0, duration: lead)
                    CubicKeyframe(-height, duration: rise)
                    CubicKeyframe(0, duration: fall)
                    LinearKeyframe(0, duration: settle + rest)
                }
                KeyframeTrack(\.stretch) {
                    LinearKeyframe(1, duration: lead)
                    CubicKeyframe(1.14, duration: rise)
                    CubicKeyframe(0.8, duration: fall)
                    SpringKeyframe(1, duration: settle, spring: .bouncy)
                    LinearKeyframe(1, duration: rest)
                }
            }
    }
}

private struct BouncyLetterPose {
    var lift = 0.0
    var stretch = 1.0
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct BouncyLettersTextDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 56) {
                BouncyLettersText(text: "Boing!")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .black))
                    .scaleEffect(1.5)

                BouncyLettersText(text: "Hop in sequence", stagger: 0.05)
                    .font(.system(.title2, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    BouncyLettersTextDemo()
}
```

## Counting Number Text

A number that counts to its new value with its digits rolling into place.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/CountingNumberText/CountingNumberText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum CountingNumberTextMath {
    /// The number at `progress`, from 0 to 1. Works in `Double`, so extreme values cannot overflow.
    static func value(from: Int, to: Int, progress: Double) -> Int {
        guard progress < 1 else { return to }
        let exact = (Double(from) + (Double(to) - Double(from)) * progress).rounded()
        let sample = Int(exactly: exact) ?? (exact > 0 ? .max : .min)
        return min(max(sample, min(from, to)), max(from, to))
    }
}

/// A number that counts to its new value, with its digits rolling into place.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, it jumps straight to the value.
struct CountingNumberText: View {
    let value: Int
    var duration: Double = 1.2
    var format: IntegerFormatStyle<Int> = .number

    @State private var shown = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Text(shown, format: format)
            .monospacedDigit()
            .contentTransition(.numericText(value: Double(shown)))
            .accessibilityLabel(Text(value, format: format))
            .task(id: value) { await count() }
    }

    /// Passes through intermediate values, slowing down as it gets close.
    private func count() async {
        guard !reduceMotion else {
            shown = value
            return
        }

        let from = shown
        let steps = max(Int(duration * 24), 1)

        for step in 1...steps {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(duration / Double(steps)))
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }

            let eased = 1 - pow(1 - Double(step) / Double(steps), 3)
            withAnimation(.snappy(duration: 0.2)) {
                shown = CountingNumberTextMath.value(from: from, to: value, progress: eased)
            }
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CountingNumberTextDemo: View {
    @State private var steps = 0
    @State private var calories = 0
    @State private var minutes = 0

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.teal, .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 18) {
                statistic("Steps", systemImage: "figure.walk", value: steps)
                statistic("Calories", systemImage: "flame.fill", value: calories)
                statistic("Minutes", systemImage: "timer", value: minutes)
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
        .task {
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.3))
                steps += 12_480
                calories += 2_347
                minutes += 86
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.9))
            }
        }
    }

    private func statistic(_ title: String, systemImage: String, value: Int) -> some View {
        HStack {
            Label(title, systemImage: systemImage)
                .font(.headline)

            Spacer()

            CountingNumberText(value: value)
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
        }
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .padding(24)
        .background(.white.opacity(0.16), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 24))
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
    }
}

#Preview {
    CountingNumberTextDemo()
}
```

## Glitch Text

Colored copies of the text that jump and flicker in short glitch bursts.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/GlitchText/GlitchText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Colored copies of the text that jump and flicker in short bursts.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the copies rest in a still, slightly split position.
struct GlitchText: View {
    let text: String
    var firstColor: Color = .cyan
    var secondColor: Color = .pink

    /// Ticks per second while flickering, one burst lasts `burstTicks` out of every `cycleTicks`.
    private let ticksPerSecond = 12.0
    private let burstTicks = 10
    private let cycleTicks = 30

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var maxOffset = 7.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1 / ticksPerSecond, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            let tick = Int(context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * ticksPerSecond)
            let isBursting = !reduceMotion && tick % cycleTicks < burstTicks

            ZStack {
                layer(color: firstColor, tick: tick, seed: 1, restingOffset: -0.3, isBursting: isBursting)
                layer(color: secondColor, tick: tick, seed: 2, restingOffset: 0.3, isBursting: isBursting)
                Text(text)
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(text)
    }

    private func layer(color: Color, tick: Int, seed: Double, restingOffset: Double, isBursting: Bool) -> some View {
        let x = isBursting ? (noise(tick, seed: seed) - 0.5) * 2 : restingOffset
        let y = isBursting ? (noise(tick, seed: seed + 10) - 0.5) * 0.8 : 0
        let isVisible = !isBursting || noise(tick, seed: seed + 20) > 0.2

        return Text(text)
            .accessibilityRepresentation { EmptyView() }
            .foregroundStyle(color)
            .offset(x: x * maxOffset, y: y * maxOffset)
            .opacity(isVisible ? 1 : 0)
    }

    /// A repeatable pseudo-random value in 0..<1.
    private func noise(_ tick: Int, seed: Double) -> Double {
        let value = sin(Double(tick) * 12.9898 + seed * 78.233) * 43_758.5453
        return value - value.rounded(.down)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct GlitchTextDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Color.black.ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 18) {
                GlitchText(text: "GLITCH")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .monospaced, weight: .black))
                    .scaleEffect(1.6)

                GlitchText(text: "SIGNAL LOST", firstColor: .green, secondColor: .purple)
                    .font(.system(.title3, design: .monospaced, weight: .bold))
                    .padding(.top, 36)
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    GlitchTextDemo()
}
```

## Glyph Wave Text

Text whose glyphs ride a travelling sine wave, drawn by a custom TextRenderer.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/GlyphWaveText/GlyphWaveText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Text whose glyphs ride a travelling sine wave.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the text sits still on its baseline.
struct GlyphWaveText: View {
    let text: String
    /// Full waves per second.
    var speed: Double = 0.8

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var amplitude = 12.0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var wavelength = 170.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 60.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            Text(text)
                .textRenderer(GlyphWaveTextRenderer(
                    phase: context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed * 2 * .pi,
                    amplitude: reduceMotion ? 0 : amplitude,
                    wavelength: wavelength
                ))
        }
    }
}

struct GlyphWaveTextRenderer: TextRenderer {
    var phase: Double
    var amplitude: Double
    var wavelength: Double

    /// Room for the glyphs that rise or fall outside the text's own frame.
    var displayPadding: EdgeInsets {
        EdgeInsets(top: amplitude, leading: 0, bottom: amplitude, trailing: 0)
    }

    func draw(layout: Text.Layout, in context: inout GraphicsContext) {
        for line in layout {
            for run in line {
                for glyph in run {
                    let position = glyph.typographicBounds.rect.midX / wavelength * 2 * .pi

                    var glyphContext = context
                    glyphContext.translateBy(x: 0, y: sin(position - phase) * amplitude)
                    glyphContext.draw(glyph)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct GlyphWaveTextDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.cyan, .blue, .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            Image(systemName: "water.waves")
                .resizable()
                .scaledToFit()
                .fontWeight(.ultraLight)
                .padding(40)
                .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.14))
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            GlyphWaveText(text: "Riding the\nsine wave")
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .heavy))
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                .lineSpacing(18)
        }
    }
}

    GlyphWaveTextDemo()
}
```

## Highlighted Search Text

Text with every match of a search query highlighted, ignoring case and accents.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/HighlightedSearchText/HighlightedSearchText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Text with every match of a search query highlighted, ignoring case and accents.
struct HighlightedSearchText: View {
    let text: String
    let query: String
    var highlightColor: Color = .yellow
    var highlightedTextColor: Color = .black

    var body: some View {
        Text(HighlightedSearchTextMatcher.highlighted(
            text,
            query: query,
            background: highlightColor,
            foreground: highlightedTextColor
        ))
    }
}

enum HighlightedSearchTextMatcher {
    /// The non-overlapping matches of `query` in `text`, from first to last.
    static func matches(of query: String, in text: String) -> [Range<String.Index>] {
        let needle = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        guard !needle.isEmpty else { return [] }

        var found: [Range<String.Index>] = []
        var searchStart = text.startIndex

        while let match = text.range(
            of: needle,
            options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive],
            range: searchStart..<text.endIndex
        ), !match.isEmpty {
            found.append(match)
            searchStart = match.upperBound
        }
        return found
    }

    static func highlighted(_ text: String, query: String, background: Color, foreground: Color) -> AttributedString {
        var result = AttributedString(text)

        for match in matches(of: query, in: text) {
            guard let range = Range(match, in: result) else { continue }
            result[range].backgroundColor = background
            result[range].foregroundColor = foreground
        }
        return result
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct HighlightedSearchTextDemo: View {
    @State private var query = ""
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let queries = ["cafe", "MANANA", "nino"]
    private let passage = """
    El café de la mañana sabe mejor. Un CAFE largo, una cafetería pequeña \
    y un niño que pide más café. Mañana volverá el NIÑO a la misma cafeteria.
    """

    private var matchCount: Int {
        HighlightedSearchTextMatcher.matches(of: query, in: passage).count
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.mint, .teal], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 20) {
                HStack {
                    Image(systemName: "magnifyingglass")
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                    Text(query.isEmpty ? "Search" : query)
                        .foregroundStyle(query.isEmpty ? .secondary : .primary)
                    Spacer()
                    Text("\(matchCount) found")
                        .font(.subheadline)
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
                .font(.title3)
                .padding(14)
                .background(.thinMaterial, in: .capsule)

                HighlightedSearchText(text: passage, query: query)
                    .font(.title2)
                    .lineSpacing(6)
            }
            .padding(24)
            .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 28))
            .padding(20)
        }
        .task { await typeQueries() }
    }

    /// Stands in for someone typing into a search field.
    private func typeQueries() async {
        guard !reduceMotion else {
            query = "cafe"
            return
        }

        while !Task.isCancelled {
            for word in queries {
                for count in 0...word.count {
                    query = String(word.prefix(count))
                    try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.11))
                }
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    HighlightedSearchTextDemo()
}
```

## Karaoke Lyrics Text

Lyrics that start dim and light up from the first letter to the last as they are sung.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/KaraokeLyricsText/KaraokeLyricsText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum KaraokeLyricsTextMath {
    /// How much of each line has been sung, from 0 to 1, when `progress` of the whole text has.
    ///
    /// Lines fill in order and a wider line takes longer, so the light moves at one speed.
    static func fills(widths: [Double], progress: Double) -> [Double] {
        let lengths = widths.map { $0.isFinite ? max($0, 0) : 0 }
        let total = lengths.reduce(0, +)
        guard total > 0, progress.isFinite else { return Array(repeating: 0, count: widths.count) }

        var remaining = min(max(progress, 0), 1) * total
        return lengths.map { length in
            guard length > 0 else { return 0 }
            let sung = min(remaining, length)
            remaining -= sung
            return sung / length
        }
    }

    /// The same fills without the sweep: a line lights up whole as soon as it starts.
    static func wholeLines(_ fills: [Double]) -> [Double] {
        fills.map { $0 > 0 ? 1 : 0 }
    }
}

/// Lyrics that light up as they are sung: the text starts dim and a brighter copy sweeps over it.
///
/// Set `progress` from 0 to 1 and animate it over the time the line takes. The text keeps its font,
/// color and alignment, wraps like any other, and follows the direction of its language.
/// With Reduce Motion on, each line lights up at once instead of filling.
struct KaraokeLyricsText: View {
    let text: String
    /// How much of the text has been sung, from 0 to 1.
    var progress: Double
    /// The opacity of the part that has not been sung yet.
    var restOpacity: Double = 0.35

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Text(text)
            .textRenderer(KaraokeLyricsTextRenderer(progress: progress, restOpacity: restOpacity, sweeps: !reduceMotion))
    }
}

struct KaraokeLyricsTextRenderer: TextRenderer {
    var progress: Double
    var restOpacity: Double
    var sweeps: Bool

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func draw(layout: Text.Layout, in context: inout GraphicsContext) {
        let lines = Array(layout)
        let filled = KaraokeLyricsTextMath.fills(widths: lines.map { Double($0.typographicBounds.rect.width) }, progress: progress)
        let fills = sweeps ? filled : KaraokeLyricsTextMath.wholeLines(filled)

        for (line, fill) in zip(lines, fills) {
            var rest = context
            rest.opacity = min(max(restOpacity, 0), 1)
            rest.draw(line)

            guard fill > 0 else { continue }

            // The sung part starts where the line starts to be read, which is the right edge in a right-to-left script.
            let bounds = line.typographicBounds.rect
            let width = bounds.width * fill
            let startsAtRight = line.first?.layoutDirection == .rightToLeft
            let sung = CGRect(x: startsAtRight ? bounds.maxX - width : bounds.minX, y: bounds.minY, width: width, height: bounds.height)

            var bright = context
            bright.clip(to: Path(sung))
            bright.draw(line)
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct KaraokeLyricsTextDemo: View {
    private let lines = [
        "City lights are calling",
        "We run where the night begins",
        "Hold on to the echo",
        "Until the morning sings",
    ]
    private let secondsPerLine = 2.2

    @State private var current = 0
    @State private var progress = 0.0

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 22) {
            Label("Night Run", systemImage: "music.mic")
                .font(.headline)
                .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.7))
                .padding(.bottom, 8)

            ForEach(lines.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                KaraokeLyricsText(text: lines[index], progress: index < current ? 1 : (index == current ? progress : 0))
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .heavy))
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
            }
        }
        .padding(28)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple, .pink], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing).ignoresSafeArea())
        .task { await sing() }
    }

    private func sing() async {
        while !Task.isCancelled {
            for index in lines.indices {
                current = index
                progress = 0
                withAnimation(.linear(duration: secondsPerLine)) { progress = 1 }
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(secondsPerLine + 0.25))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            }
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.8))
            current = 0
            progress = 0
        }
    }
}
```

## Marquee Text

A single line of text that scrolls horizontally only when it does not fit.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/MarqueeText/MarqueeText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A single line that scrolls horizontally, only when it does not fit.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, a long line is truncated instead of scrolling.
struct MarqueeText: View {
    let text: String
    /// Points per second.
    var speed: Double = 42
    /// Seconds to wait at the start of each lap.
    var pause: Double = 1

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) private var gap = 48.0
    @State private var textWidth = 0.0
    @State private var containerWidth = 0.0
    @State private var start = Date.now
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var scrolls: Bool {
        containerWidth > 0 && textWidth > containerWidth && speed > 0 && !reduceMotion
    }

    var body: some View {
        Text(text)
            .lineLimit(1)
            .opacity(scrolls ? 0 : 1)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            .onGeometryChange(for: Double.self) { $0.size.width } action: { containerWidth = $0 }
            .background {
                Text(text)
                    .lineLimit(1)
                    .fixedSize()
                    .hidden()
                    .onGeometryChange(for: Double.self) { $0.size.width } action: { textWidth = $0 }
            }
            .overlay(alignment: .leading) {
                if scrolls { scrollingCopies }
            }
            .mask {
                if scrolls {
                    LinearGradient(
                        stops: [
                            .init(color: .clear, location: 0),
                            .init(color: .black, location: 0.03),
                            .init(color: .black, location: 0.92),
                            .init(color: .clear, location: 1),
                        ],
                        startPoint: .leading,
                        endPoint: .trailing
                    )
                } else {
                    Color.black
                }
            }
            .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
            .accessibilityLabel(text)
            .task(id: text) { start = .now }
    }

    /// The second copy follows the first, so the end of a lap looks just like its start.
    private var scrollingCopies: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 60.0)) { context in
            HStack(spacing: gap) {
                Text(text)
                Text(text)
            }
            .lineLimit(1)
            .fixedSize()
            .accessibilityRepresentation { EmptyView() }
            .offset(x: -offset(at: context.date))
        }
    }

    private func offset(at date: Date) -> Double {
        let lapDistance = textWidth + gap
        let lapDuration = pause + lapDistance / speed
        let timeInLap = date.timeIntervalSince(start).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: lapDuration)
        return max(timeInLap - pause, 0) * speed
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct MarqueeTextDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.purple, .indigo, .black], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 24) {
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 32)
                    .fill(.linearGradient(colors: [.pink, .orange], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
                    .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
                    .overlay {
                        Image(systemName: "music.note")
                            .resizable()
                            .scaledToFit()
                            .fontWeight(.semibold)
                            .padding(80)
                            .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    }
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
                    MarqueeText(text: "The Very Long Song Title That Could Never Fit on One Line")
                        .font(.title2.bold())
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)

                    MarqueeText(text: "Short and still")
                        .font(.title3)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.7))
                }
            }
            .padding(32)
        }
    }
}

    MarqueeTextDemo()
}
```

## Read More Text

A paragraph truncated with a fade that expands in place when tapped.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/ReadMoreText/ReadMoreText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A paragraph truncated with a fade that expands in place when tapped.
///
/// The button only appears when the text does not fit. With Reduce Motion on, the
/// paragraph changes height at once. VoiceOver always reads the whole paragraph.
struct ReadMoreText: View {
    let text: String
    var collapsedLines = 3
    var moreLabel = "Read more"
    var lessLabel = "Show less"

    @State private var isExpanded = false
    @State private var fullHeight: CGFloat = 0
    @State private var collapsedHeight: CGFloat = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let touchPadding: CGFloat = 13

    private var isTruncated: Bool { fullHeight > collapsedHeight + 1 && collapsedHeight > 0 }
    private var isFaded: Bool { isTruncated && !isExpanded }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10) {
            Text(text)
                .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
                .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.height } action: { fullHeight = $0 }
                .background { collapsedMeasure }
                .frame(height: isTruncated ? (isExpanded ? fullHeight : collapsedHeight) : nil, alignment: .top)
                .clipped()
                .mask { fade }

            if isTruncated {
                Button {
                    isExpanded.toggle()
                } label: {
                    // A line of text is too short to hit. The padding widens what answers to a
                    // touch, and the same padding taken back keeps the layout as it was.
                    Text(isExpanded ? lessLabel : moreLabel)
                        .padding(.vertical, touchPadding)
                        .contentShape(.rect)
                        .padding(.vertical, -touchPadding)
                }
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                .foregroundStyle(.tint)
            }
        }
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.4), value: isExpanded)
    }

    // A hidden copy, limited to the collapsed lines, tells how tall the collapsed text is.
    private var collapsedMeasure: some View {
        Text(text)
            .lineLimit(max(collapsedLines, 1))
            .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
            .hidden()
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.height } action: { collapsedHeight = $0 }
            .accessibilityRepresentation { EmptyView() }
    }

    private var fade: LinearGradient {
        LinearGradient(
            stops: [
                .init(color: .black, location: 0),
                .init(color: .black, location: isFaded ? 0.55 : 1),
                .init(color: isFaded ? .clear : .black, location: 1),
            ],
            startPoint: .top,
            endPoint: .bottom
        )
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

    private let story = "The sea looks blue because water absorbs the red end of the spectrum and scatters the blue back towards your eyes. The deeper the water, the more red is lost, which is why the open ocean looks so much darker than a shallow bay. Near the coast, sand and algae add greens and browns, and a bright sky adds its own reflection to the surface."

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 24)
                    .fill(LinearGradient(colors: [.cyan, .blue, .indigo], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
                    .frame(height: 220)
                    .overlay {
                        Image(systemName: "water.waves")
                            .font(.largeTitle)
                            .imageScale(.large)
                            .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    }
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text("Why the sea is blue")
                    .font(.title.bold())

                ReadMoreText(text: story)
                    .font(.body)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
            .padding(20)
        }
    }
```

## Rotating Words Text

Words that take turns in the same spot, each one pushing the last out of the way.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/RotatingWordsText/RotatingWordsText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Words that take turns in the same spot, each one pushing the last out of the way.
///
/// It reserves the width of the longest word, so nothing around it moves.
/// With Reduce Motion on, the words crossfade.
struct RotatingWordsText: View {
    let words: [String]
    /// Seconds each word stays on screen.
    var interval: Double = 1.6

    @State private var index = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var transition: AnyTransition {
        reduceMotion ? .opacity : .push(from: .bottom)
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack(alignment: .leading) {
            ForEach(words.indices, id: \.self) { position in
                Text(words[position]).hidden()
            }

            if !words.isEmpty {
                Text(words[index % words.count])
                    .id(index)
                    .transition(transition)
            }
        }
        .clipped()
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(words.joined(separator: ", "))
        .task(id: words) { await rotate() }
    }

    private func rotate() async {
        guard words.count > 1 else { return }

        while !Task.isCancelled {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(interval))
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }

            withAnimation(.snappy(duration: 0.45)) {
                index = (index + 1) % words.count
            }
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct RotatingWordsTextDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [Color(white: 0.12), .black], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                Text("Made for")
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)

                RotatingWordsText(words: ["designers", "developers", "dreamers", "everyone"], interval: 1.2)
                    .foregroundStyle(.linearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing))
            }
            .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .heavy))
            .padding(32)
        }
    }
}
```

## Scramble Text

Random characters that settle from left to right into the final text.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/ScrambleText/ScrambleText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Random characters that settle, left to right, into the final text.
///
/// It plays again when `text` changes. With Reduce Motion on, the text appears directly.
struct ScrambleText: View {
    let text: String
    var duration: Double = 1.2
    var characters: [Character] = ScrambleTextScrambler.defaultCharacters

    @State private var displayed: String?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Text(displayed ?? text)
            .monospaced()
            .opacity(displayed == nil ? 0 : 1)
            .accessibilityLabel(text)
            .task(id: text) { await play() }
    }

    private func play() async {
        guard !reduceMotion else {
            displayed = text
            return
        }

        var generator = SystemRandomNumberGenerator()
        let steps = max(Int(duration * 30), 1)

        for step in 0...steps {
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            displayed = ScrambleTextScrambler.scrambled(
                text,
                progress: Double(step) / Double(steps),
                characters: characters,
                using: &generator
            )
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(duration / Double(steps)))
        }
    }
}

enum ScrambleTextScrambler {
    static let defaultCharacters = Array("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789#$%&*@")

    /// Keeps the first `progress` share of `text` and replaces the rest with random
    /// characters. Whitespace is kept, so words hold their shape and lines wrap the same.
    static func scrambled(
        _ text: String,
        progress: Double,
        characters: [Character] = defaultCharacters,
        using generator: inout some RandomNumberGenerator
    ) -> String {
        let letters = Array(text)
        let clamped = progress > 0 ? min(progress, 1) : 0
        let settled = Int(clamped * Double(letters.count))

        var result = ""
        for (index, letter) in letters.enumerated() {
            let isSettled = index < settled || letter.isWhitespace
            result.append(isSettled ? letter : characters.randomElement(using: &generator) ?? letter)
        }
        return result
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ScrambleTextDemo: View {
    @State private var index = 0

    private let phrases = ["ACCESS GRANTED", "DECRYPTING DATA", "SIGNAL ACQUIRED"]

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [Color(red: 0, green: 0.16, blue: 0.12), .black], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                Image(systemName: "lock.open.fill")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                ScrambleText(text: phrases[index])
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.mint)
            .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
            .padding(24)
        }
        .task {
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2.4))
                index = (index + 1) % phrases.count
            }
        }
    }
}

    ScrambleTextDemo()
}
```

## Shimmer Text

Text with a band of light that sweeps across its letters through a mask.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/ShimmerText/ShimmerText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A band of light that sweeps across the letters, masked by the text itself.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the text is drawn plainly in the highlight color.
struct ShimmerText: View {
    let text: String
    var baseColor: Color = .secondary
    var highlightColor: Color = .primary
    /// Seconds for one sweep.
    var duration: Double = 2.2

    /// Half the width of the band of light, as a fraction of the text's width.
    private let bandWidth = 0.3

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Text(text)
            .foregroundStyle(reduceMotion ? highlightColor : baseColor)
            .overlay {
                if !reduceMotion {
                    TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 60.0)) { context in
                        band(at: context.date)
                    }
                    .mask { Text(text).foregroundStyle(.black) }
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
            }
    }

    /// Start and end points beyond 0...1 place the band off to the side, between sweeps.
    private func band(at date: Date) -> LinearGradient {
        let cycle = date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: duration) / duration
        let center = -bandWidth + (1 + 2 * bandWidth) * cycle

        return LinearGradient(
            colors: [.clear, highlightColor, .clear],
            startPoint: UnitPoint(x: center - bandWidth, y: 0.5),
            endPoint: UnitPoint(x: center + bandWidth, y: 0.5)
        )
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ShimmerTextDemo: View {
    private let dimmed = Color.white.opacity(0.35)

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [Color(white: 0.16), .black], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)

                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .black))
                    .scaleEffect(1.5)

                ShimmerText(text: "slide to unlock", baseColor: dimmed, highlightColor: .white, duration: 1.8)

            }
            .padding(24)
        }
    }
```

## Streaming Text

Text that arrives in chunks, like the answer of a language model, and fades each new part in from its first letter to its last.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/StreamingText/StreamingText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

nonisolated enum StreamingTextMath {
    /// How opaque a character is when `visible` of them have arrived: whole once the front has
    /// passed it by `fade` characters, clear ahead of the front and in between on the way.
    static func opacity(of index: Double, visible: Double, fade: Double) -> Double {
        guard fade > 0 else { return index < visible ? 1 : 0 }
        return min(max((visible - index) / fade, 0), 1)
    }

    /// How long the front takes to cross `characters`: short for a word, capped for a long
    /// chunk, so a burst of text never keeps the reader waiting.
    static func duration(for characters: Double, charactersPerSecond: Double, limit: ClosedRange<Double> = 0.15...1.5) -> Double {
        guard characters > 0, charactersPerSecond > 0 else { return limit.lowerBound }
        return min(max(characters / charactersPerSecond, limit.lowerBound), limit.upperBound)
    }

    /// How many characters two texts have in common at their start.
    static func sharedPrefix(_ first: String, _ second: String) -> Int {
        zip(first, second).prefix { $0 == $1 }.count
    }
}

/// Text that arrives in chunks, like the answer of a language model: every time `text` grows,
/// the new part fades in from its first letter to its last instead of popping in.
///
/// The speed evens out the chunks, so a burst of words reads as smoothly as a single one.
/// Text that is replaced rather than extended starts again from where the two differ.
/// With Reduce Motion on, new text shows at once.
struct StreamingText: View {
    let text: String
    var charactersPerSecond = 80.0
    /// How many characters the soft edge of the new text spans.
    var fade = 10.0

    @State private var visible = 0.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Text(text)
            .textRenderer(StreamingTextRenderer(visible: visible, characters: text.count, fade: fade, isInstant: reduceMotion))
            .onChange(of: text, initial: true) { old, new in
                let kept = Double(StreamingTextMath.sharedPrefix(old, new))
                if kept < Double(old.count) { visible = min(visible, kept) }

                // The front ends past the last character, so that one becomes whole too.
                let target = Double(new.count) + fade
                let duration = StreamingTextMath.duration(for: target - visible, charactersPerSecond: charactersPerSecond)
                withAnimation(.linear(duration: duration)) { visible = target }
            }
    }
}

struct StreamingTextRenderer: TextRenderer {
    var visible: Double
    var characters: Int
    var fade: Double
    var isInstant: Bool

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { visible }
        set { visible = newValue }
    }

    func draw(layout: Text.Layout, in context: inout GraphicsContext) {
        let slices = layout.flatMap { line in line.flatMap { run in Array(run) } }
        // A character can be more than one glyph, or share one, so the glyphs are spread over the characters.
        let charactersPerSlice = slices.isEmpty ? 1 : Double(max(characters, 1)) / Double(slices.count)

        for (index, slice) in slices.enumerated() {
            let opacity = isInstant ? 1 : StreamingTextMath.opacity(of: Double(index) * charactersPerSlice, visible: visible, fade: fade)
            guard opacity > 0 else { continue }

            var copy = context
            copy.opacity = opacity
            copy.draw(slice)
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct StreamingTextDemo: View {
    private let answer = "Sourdough needs time more than effort. Mix flour, water, salt and a spoonful of starter in the evening, fold the dough a few times before bed, and let it rise overnight. In the morning, shape it, rest it for an hour and bake it in a hot pot with the lid on. The crust comes out crisp and the crumb stays open and soft."

    @State private var text = ""
    @State private var run = 0

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
            Text("How do I bake sourdough?")
                .padding(.horizontal, 14)
                .padding(.vertical, 10)
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .background(.blue, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 20))
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .trailing)

            StreamingText(text: text)
                .font(.body)
                .lineSpacing(4)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)

            Spacer()

            Button("Ask Again", systemImage: "arrow.clockwise") {
                run += 1
            }
            .buttonStyle(.bordered)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
        }
        .padding(20)
        .task(id: run) {
            // Stands in for a model that sends a few words at a time, at an uneven pace.
            text = ""
            var words = answer.split(separator: " ")[...]
            while !words.isEmpty, !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(Int.random(in: 120...380)))
                let chunk = words.prefix(Int.random(in: 2...6))
                words = words.dropFirst(chunk.count)
                if !Task.isCancelled { text += (text.isEmpty ? "" : " ") + chunk.joined(separator: " ") }
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    StreamingTextDemo()
}
```

## Text Blur Reveal

Text that appears line by line, coming into focus as it slides up, drawn by a custom TextRenderer.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/TextBlurReveal/TextBlurReveal.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Reveals text line by line: each line fades in, comes into focus and slides up.
///
/// Animate `progress` from 0 to 1 with `withAnimation`. With Reduce Motion on, the text is shown in full.
struct TextBlurReveal: View {
    let text: String
    var progress: Double = 1

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title) private var blurRadius = 12.0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title) private var rise = 18.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Text(text)
            .textRenderer(TextBlurRevealRenderer(
                progress: reduceMotion ? 1 : progress,
                blurRadius: blurRadius,
                rise: rise
            ))
    }
}

struct TextBlurRevealRenderer: TextRenderer {
    var progress: Double
    var blurRadius: Double
    var rise: Double

    /// How much of each line's animation overlaps with the next one.
    private let overlap = 0.55

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    /// Room for the blur and the slide, which draw outside the text's own frame.
    var displayPadding: EdgeInsets {
        let margin = blurRadius * 2
        return EdgeInsets(top: margin, leading: margin, bottom: margin + rise, trailing: margin)
    }

    func draw(layout: Text.Layout, in context: inout GraphicsContext) {
        for (index, line) in layout.enumerated() {
            let reveal = lineProgress(index: index, count: layout.count)

            var lineContext = context
            lineContext.opacity = reveal
            lineContext.addFilter(.blur(radius: (1 - reveal) * blurRadius))
            lineContext.translateBy(x: 0, y: (1 - reveal) * rise)
            lineContext.draw(line)
        }
    }

    private func lineProgress(index: Int, count: Int) -> Double {
        let step = 1 - overlap
        let lineDuration = 1 / (Double(count - 1) * step + 1)
        let lineStart = Double(index) * step * lineDuration
        return min(max((progress - lineStart) / lineDuration, 0), 1)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct TextBlurRevealDemo: View {
    @State private var progress = 0.0

    private let poem = """
    The morning arrives
    without asking anyone,
    one quiet line
    after another,
    until the page is full.
    """

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .black], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            TextBlurReveal(text: poem, progress: progress)
                .font(.system(.title, design: .serif, weight: .medium))
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                .lineSpacing(10)
                .padding(32)
        }
        .task {
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 2.2)) { progress = 1 }
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(3.4))
                progress = 0
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.2))
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    TextBlurRevealDemo()
}
```

## Typewriter Text

Text that types itself one character at a time, followed by a blinking cursor.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/TypewriterText/TypewriterText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Types its text one character at a time, followed by a blinking cursor.
///
/// It restarts when `text` changes. With Reduce Motion on, the text appears in full with no cursor.
struct TypewriterText: View {
    let text: String
    var charactersPerSecond: Double = 20
    var cursorColor: Color = .accentColor

    @State private var started: (text: String, date: Date)?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            Text(typed(at: context.date))
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(text)
        .task(id: text) { started = (text, .now) }
    }

    /// The characters not typed yet stay in the string as clear text, so lines wrap once and never jump.
    private func typed(at date: Date) -> AttributedString {
        guard !reduceMotion else { return AttributedString(text) }

        let elapsed = started.flatMap { $0.text == text ? date.timeIntervalSince($0.date) : nil } ?? 0
        let count = TypewriterTextProgress.visibleCount(
            elapsed: elapsed,
            charactersPerSecond: charactersPerSecond,
            total: text.count
        )
        let isTyping = count < text.count

        var cursor = AttributedString("|")
        cursor.foregroundColor = isTyping || Int(elapsed * 2).isMultiple(of: 2) ? cursorColor : .clear

        var remaining = AttributedString(String(text.dropFirst(count)))
        remaining.foregroundColor = .clear

        return AttributedString(String(text.prefix(count))) + cursor + remaining
    }
}

enum TypewriterTextProgress {
    /// How many characters are visible after `elapsed` seconds, from 0 to `total`.
    static func visibleCount(elapsed: TimeInterval, charactersPerSecond: Double, total: Int) -> Int {
        guard total > 0 else { return 0 }
        guard charactersPerSecond > 0 else { return total }

        let typed = (elapsed * charactersPerSecond).rounded(.down)
        guard typed > 0 else { return 0 }
        return typed >= Double(total) ? total : Int(typed)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct TypewriterTextDemo: View {
    @State private var index = 0

    private let lines = [
        "$ swift build\nCompiling your ideas...",
        "$ swift test\nAll tests passed, no bugs today.",
        "$ git push\nShipped before lunch.",
    ]

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Color.black.ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
                HStack(spacing: 8) {
                    ForEach([Color.red, .yellow, .green], id: \.self) { color in
                        Circle().fill(color).frame(width: 12, height: 12)
                    }
                }
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

                TypewriterText(text: lines[index], cursorColor: .green)
                    .font(.system(.title2, design: .monospaced, weight: .medium))
                    .foregroundStyle(.green)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: 160, alignment: .topLeading)
            }
            .padding(24)
            .background(.white.opacity(0.08), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 20))
            .padding(20)
        }
        .task {
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(3.2))
                index = (index + 1) % lines.count
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Collapsing Bottom Bar

A bottom toolbar that shrinks to a pill while scrolling down and expands back when scrolling up.

Category: Toolbars. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Toolbars/CollapsingBottomBar/CollapsingBottomBar.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct CollapsingBottomBarItem: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let systemImage: String
    let action: () -> Void
}

/// Decides when the bar collapses. A change of direction must travel past a threshold,
/// so small movements of the finger do not make the bar flicker.
struct CollapsingBottomBarState: Equatable {
    private(set) var isCollapsed = false
    private var anchor: CGFloat = 0

    mutating func update(offset: CGFloat, threshold: CGFloat) {
        guard offset > 0 else {
            isCollapsed = false
            anchor = 0
            return
        }

        let travel = offset - anchor
        let limit = max(threshold, 0)
        if isCollapsed ? travel < -limit : travel > limit {
            isCollapsed.toggle()
            anchor = offset
        } else if isCollapsed ? travel > 0 : travel < 0 {
            anchor = offset
        }
    }

    /// Removes the rubber band at both ends, which would otherwise look like a change of direction.
    static func clampedOffset(offsetY: CGFloat, topInset: CGFloat, bottomInset: CGFloat, contentHeight: CGFloat, containerHeight: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        let maxOffset = max(contentHeight + topInset + bottomInset - containerHeight, 0)
        return min(max(offsetY + topInset, 0), maxOffset)
    }
}

/// A bottom bar that shrinks to a pill while scrolling down and expands when scrolling up.
///
/// Apply it to a `ScrollView` with `.collapsingBottomBar(items:)`. With Reduce Motion on,
/// the bar changes size at once.
struct CollapsingBottomBar: ViewModifier {
    let items: [CollapsingBottomBarItem]

    @State private var state = CollapsingBottomBarState()
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .onScrollGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { geometry in
                CollapsingBottomBarState.clampedOffset(
                    offsetY: geometry.contentOffset.y,
                    topInset: geometry.contentInsets.top,
                    bottomInset: geometry.contentInsets.bottom,
                    contentHeight: geometry.contentSize.height,
                    containerHeight: geometry.containerSize.height
                )
            } action: { _, newValue in
                state.update(offset: newValue, threshold: 24)
            }
            .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom, spacing: 0) {
                CollapsingBottomBarSlot(items: items, isCollapsed: state.isCollapsed)
                    // The labels are short. The slot reads its height under this cap, which keeps every action on screen.
                    .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.xxxLarge)
            }
            .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.35), value: state.isCollapsed)
    }
}

private struct CollapsingBottomBarSlot: View {
    let items: [CollapsingBottomBarItem]
    let isCollapsed: Bool

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption2) private var slotHeight = 86.0

    var body: some View {
        // A fixed slot keeps the inset stable, so the bar's own resizing cannot move the scroll offset.
        bar.frame(height: slotHeight, alignment: .bottom)
    }

    private var bar: some View {
        HStack(spacing: isCollapsed ? 6 : 0) {
            ForEach(items) { item in
                Button(action: item.action) {
                    VStack(spacing: 3) {
                        Image(systemName: item.systemImage)
                            .font(.title3)

                        if !isCollapsed {
                            Text(item.title)
                                .font(.caption2)
                        }
                    }
                    .frame(minWidth: 44, maxWidth: isCollapsed ? nil : .infinity, minHeight: 44)
                    .contentShape(.rect)
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
                .accessibilityLabel(item.title)
            }
        }
        .padding(.horizontal, isCollapsed ? 10 : 14)
        .padding(.vertical, 8)
        .background(.regularMaterial, in: .capsule)
        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.15), radius: 12, y: 6)
        .padding(.horizontal, 20)
        .padding(.bottom, 6)
    }
}

extension View {
    func collapsingBottomBar(items: [CollapsingBottomBarItem]) -> some View {
        modifier(CollapsingBottomBar(items: items))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CollapsingBottomBarDemo: View {
    @State private var lastAction = "Scroll to collapse the bar"

    private var items: [CollapsingBottomBarItem] {
        [
            CollapsingBottomBarItem(id: "home", title: "Home", systemImage: "house.fill") { lastAction = "Home" },
            CollapsingBottomBarItem(id: "search", title: "Search", systemImage: "magnifyingglass") { lastAction = "Search" },
            CollapsingBottomBarItem(id: "add", title: "Add", systemImage: "plus.circle.fill") { lastAction = "Add" },
            CollapsingBottomBarItem(id: "inbox", title: "Inbox", systemImage: "tray.fill") { lastAction = "Inbox" },
        ]
    }

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 14) {
                Text(lastAction)
                    .font(.title.bold())

                ForEach(0..<20, id: \.self) { index in
                    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20)
                        .fill(LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing))
                        .hueRotation(.degrees(Double(index) * 18))
                        .frame(height: 110)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
            }
            .padding(20)
        }
        .collapsingBottomBar(items: items)
    }
}

#Preview {
    CollapsingBottomBarDemo()
}
```

## Floating Dock Bar

A row of icons that magnify under the finger, in the style of the macOS dock.

Category: Toolbars. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Toolbars/FloatingDockBar/FloatingDockBar.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

struct FloatingDockBarItem: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let title: LocalizedStringResource
    let systemImage: String
    let colors: [Color]
    let action: () -> Void
}

enum FloatingDockBarMath {
    /// Grows smoothly from 1 at `spread` away from the finger to `maxScale` right under it.
    static func scale(distance: CGFloat, spread: CGFloat, maxScale: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        guard spread > 0, maxScale > 1 else { return 1 }
        let normalized = min(abs(distance) / spread, 1)
        let falloff = cos(normalized * .pi / 2)
        return 1 + (maxScale - 1) * falloff * falloff
    }

    /// Shrinks the icons when they would not all fit in the space available.
    static func iconSize(preferred: CGFloat, available: CGFloat, count: Int, spacing: CGFloat, padding: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        guard count > 0, available > 0 else { return max(preferred, 0) }
        let usable = available - 2 * padding - CGFloat(count - 1) * spacing
        return max(min(preferred, usable / CGFloat(count)), 20)
    }

    static func centerX(index: Int, iconSize: CGFloat, spacing: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        iconSize / 2 + CGFloat(index) * (iconSize + spacing)
    }
}

/// A row of icons that magnify under the finger, in the style of the macOS dock.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the magnification is small and has no spring. The dock only
/// holds icons, so it stops growing past the larger text sizes.
struct FloatingDockBar: View {
    let items: [FloatingDockBarItem]
    var maxScale: CGFloat = 1.6

    var body: some View {
        FloatingDockBarStage(items: items, maxScale: maxScale)
            // The stage reads its icon size under this cap.
            .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.xxxLarge)
    }
}

private struct FloatingDockBarStage: View {
    let items: [FloatingDockBarItem]
    let maxScale: CGFloat

    private let spacing: CGFloat = 12
    private let padding: CGFloat = 12

    @GestureState private var fingerX: CGFloat?
    @State private var availableWidth: CGFloat = 0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title2) private var preferredIconSize = 56.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.layoutDirection) private var layoutDirection

    private var effectiveMaxScale: CGFloat { reduceMotion ? min(maxScale, 1.15) : maxScale }

    private var rowWidth: CGFloat {
        CGFloat(items.count) * iconSize + CGFloat(max(items.count - 1, 0)) * spacing
    }

    private var iconSize: CGFloat {
        FloatingDockBarMath.iconSize(preferred: preferredIconSize, available: availableWidth, count: items.count, spacing: spacing, padding: padding)
    }

    var body: some View {
        HStack(alignment: .bottom, spacing: spacing) {
            ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, item in
                iconButton(item, scale: scale(at: index))
                    .zIndex(Double(scale(at: index)))
            }
        }
        // Simultaneous, so the buttons inside keep working for taps and VoiceOver.
        .simultaneousGesture(
            DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).updating($fingerX) { value, state, _ in
                // Gestures report screen points, but the row of icons mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
                state = layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? rowWidth - value.location.x : value.location.x
            }
        )
        .padding(padding)
        .background(.ultraThinMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 26))
        .padding(.top, iconSize * max(effectiveMaxScale - 1, 0))
        // minWidth 0 makes this the width on offer, even while the icons are too wide for it.
        .frame(minWidth: 0, maxWidth: .infinity)
        .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.width } action: { availableWidth = $0 }
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(response: 0.25, dampingFraction: 0.72), value: fingerX)
    }

    private func scale(at index: Int) -> CGFloat {
        guard let fingerX else { return 1 }
        let center = FloatingDockBarMath.centerX(index: index, iconSize: iconSize, spacing: spacing)
        return FloatingDockBarMath.scale(distance: fingerX - center, spread: (iconSize + spacing) * 2.2, maxScale: effectiveMaxScale)
    }

    private func iconButton(_ item: FloatingDockBarItem, scale: CGFloat) -> some View {
        Button(action: item.action) {
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: iconSize * 0.25)
                .fill(LinearGradient(colors: item.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
                .frame(width: iconSize, height: iconSize)
                .overlay {
                    Image(systemName: item.systemImage)
                        .font(.title2)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                }
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .scaleEffect(scale, anchor: .bottom)
        .accessibilityLabel(item.title)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct FloatingDockBarDemo: View {
    @State private var opened = "Drag across the dock"

    private var items: [FloatingDockBarItem] {
        [
            FloatingDockBarItem(id: "mail", title: "Mail", systemImage: "envelope.fill", colors: [.cyan, .blue]) { opened = "Mail" },
            FloatingDockBarItem(id: "photos", title: "Photos", systemImage: "photo.fill", colors: [.yellow, .orange]) { opened = "Photos" },
            FloatingDockBarItem(id: "music", title: "Music", systemImage: "music.note", colors: [.pink, .red]) { opened = "Music" },
            FloatingDockBarItem(id: "notes", title: "Notes", systemImage: "note.text", colors: [.mint, .green]) { opened = "Notes" },
            FloatingDockBarItem(id: "settings", title: "Settings", systemImage: "gearshape.fill", colors: [.gray, .indigo]) { opened = "Settings" },
        ]
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple, .pink], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            FloatingDockBar(items: items)
                .padding(.horizontal, 16)
        }
        .overlay(alignment: .top) {
            Text(opened)
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                .padding(.top, 60)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    FloatingDockBarDemo()
}
```

## Blur Fade Transition

A custom transition that combines blur, fade and scale, available as .blurFade.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Transitions/BlurFadeTransition/BlurFadeTransition.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A transition that blurs, fades and scales a view. Use it as `.transition(.blurFade)`.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the view only fades.
struct BlurFadeTransition: Transition {
    var radius: CGFloat = 18
    var scale: CGFloat = 0.9

    func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.modifier(BlurFadeEffect(radius: radius, scale: scale, isIdentity: phase.isIdentity))
    }
}

extension Transition where Self == BlurFadeTransition {
    static var blurFade: BlurFadeTransition { BlurFadeTransition() }

    static func blurFade(radius: CGFloat, scale: CGFloat = 0.9) -> BlurFadeTransition {
        BlurFadeTransition(radius: radius, scale: scale)
    }
}

// The effect lives in a view modifier so it can read the environment.
private struct BlurFadeEffect: ViewModifier {
    let radius: CGFloat
    let scale: CGFloat
    let isIdentity: Bool

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .blur(radius: isIdentity || reduceMotion ? 0 : radius)
            .scaleEffect(isIdentity || reduceMotion ? 1 : scale)
            .opacity(isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct BlurFadeTransitionDemo: View {
    @State private var isShown = true

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            if isShown {
                VStack(spacing: 14) {
                    Image(systemName: "moon.stars.fill")
                        .font(.largeTitle)
                        .imageScale(.large)
                        .symbolRenderingMode(.hierarchical)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)

                    Text("Good night")
                        .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                    Text("Sleep mode starts in ten minutes.")
                        .font(.callout)
                        .opacity(0.8)
                }
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                .padding(36)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                .background(.white.opacity(0.12), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 32))
                .padding(28)
                .transition(.blurFade)
            }
        }
        .task {
            while (try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.3))) != nil {
                withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.6)) { isShown.toggle() }
            }
        }
    }
}

    BlurFadeTransitionDemo()
}
```

## Circle Reveal Transition

A custom transition that reveals a view through a circular mask growing from a point.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Transitions/CircleRevealTransition/CircleRevealTransition.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A transition that reveals a view through a circle growing from a point.
/// Use it as `.transition(.circleReveal(from: .bottomTrailing))`.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the view fades instead.
struct CircleRevealTransition: Transition {
    var origin: UnitPoint = .center

    func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.modifier(CircleRevealEffect(origin: origin, isIdentity: phase.isIdentity))
    }
}

extension Transition where Self == CircleRevealTransition {
    static func circleReveal(from origin: UnitPoint = .center) -> CircleRevealTransition {
        CircleRevealTransition(origin: origin)
    }
}

nonisolated enum CircleRevealTransitionGeometry {
    /// The radius of the smallest circle centered on `origin` that covers the whole of `size`.
    static func coverRadius(from origin: UnitPoint, in size: CGSize) -> CGFloat {
        let horizontal = max(origin.x, 1 - origin.x) * size.width
        let vertical = max(origin.y, 1 - origin.y) * size.height
        return hypot(horizontal, vertical)
    }
}

private struct CircleRevealEffect: ViewModifier {
    let origin: UnitPoint
    let isIdentity: Bool

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .clipShape(CircleRevealShape(origin: origin, progress: isIdentity || reduceMotion ? 1 : 0))
            .opacity(reduceMotion && !isIdentity ? 0 : 1)
    }
}

nonisolated private struct CircleRevealShape: Shape {
    let origin: UnitPoint
    var progress: CGFloat

    var animatableData: CGFloat {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let radius = CircleRevealTransitionGeometry.coverRadius(from: origin, in: rect.size) * progress
        let center = CGPoint(x: rect.minX + rect.width * origin.x, y: rect.minY + rect.height * origin.y)
        return Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: center.x - radius, y: center.y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CircleRevealTransitionDemo: View {
    @State private var isDark = false

    private let origin = UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 0.78)

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            ZStack {
                scene(colors: [.cyan, .blue], systemImage: "sun.max.fill", title: "Day")
                    .accessibilityHidden(isDark)

                if isDark {
                    scene(colors: [.indigo, .black], systemImage: "moon.stars.fill", title: "Night")
                        .transition(.circleReveal(from: origin))
                }

                Button(isDark ? "Sunrise" : "Sunset") {
                    withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.8)) { isDark.toggle() }
                }
                .font(.headline)
                .buttonStyle(.bordered)
                .controlSize(.large)
                .tint(.white)
                .position(x: proxy.size.width * origin.x, y: proxy.size.height * origin.y)
            }
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    }

    private func scene(colors: [Color], systemImage: String, title: String) -> some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)

            VStack(spacing: 14) {
                Image(systemName: systemImage)
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, weight: .semibold))
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text(title)
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    CircleRevealTransitionDemo()
}
```

## Content Swap Transition

A showcase of text value changes using numericText, interpolate and opacity content transitions.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Transitions/ContentSwapTransition/ContentSwapTransition.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

enum ContentSwapTransitionStyle {
    case numeric(Double)
    case interpolate
    case opacity
}

/// Text that swaps its value with a content transition: rolling digits, a morph or a fade.
/// Change the text inside an animation.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, numbers fade instead of rolling.
struct ContentSwapTransition: View {
    let text: String
    var style: ContentSwapTransitionStyle = .opacity

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var transition: ContentTransition {
        switch style {
        case .numeric(let value): reduceMotion ? .opacity : .numericText(value: value)
        case .interpolate: .interpolate
        case .opacity: .opacity
        }
    }

    var body: some View {
        Text(text)
            .contentTransition(transition)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ContentSwapTransitionDemo: View {
    @State private var step = 0

    private let amounts: [Double] = [1284, 1317, 2096, 1905]
    private let greetings = ["Hello", "Hola", "Bonjour", "Ciao"]

    private var amount: Double { amounts[step % amounts.count] }
    private var isHeavy: Bool { step.isMultiple(of: 2) }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 16) {
            card("numericText", systemImage: "number", tint: .blue) {
                ContentSwapTransition(text: amount.formatted(.currency(code: "EUR")), style: .numeric(amount))
            }

            card("interpolate", systemImage: "textformat", tint: .pink) {
                ContentSwapTransition(text: "Weight", style: .interpolate)
                    .fontWeight(isHeavy ? .black : .ultraLight)
                    .foregroundStyle(isHeavy ? .pink : .orange)
            }

            card("opacity", systemImage: "circle.lefthalf.filled", tint: .teal) {
                ContentSwapTransition(text: greetings[step % greetings.count], style: .opacity)
            }
        }
        .padding(20)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground).ignoresSafeArea())
        .task {
            while (try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.2))) != nil {
                withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.6)) { step += 1 }
            }
        }
    }

    private func card(
        _ title: String,
        systemImage: String,
        tint: Color,
        @ViewBuilder content: () -> some View
    ) -> some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
            Label(title, systemImage: systemImage)
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                .foregroundStyle(tint)

            content()
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .monospacedDigit()
                .lineLimit(1)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
        }
        .padding(24)
        .background(Color(.secondarySystemGroupedBackground), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 24))
    }
}

#Preview {
    ContentSwapTransitionDemo()
}
```

## Cross Fade Navigation

A sheet that fades in over the content with the iOS 27 cross-fade navigation transition.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 27.0. Path: Components/Transitions/CrossFadeNavigation/CrossFadeNavigation.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and Awesome SwiftUI Components contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Presents a sheet that fades in over the content with the iOS 27 `.crossFade` transition,
/// instead of moving up from the bottom.
///
/// Apple documents `.crossFade` for sheets. Keep `navigationTransition` on the root of the
/// sheet's content, outside any container such as `VStack`. A cross-fade has no movement,
/// so Reduce Motion needs nothing different.
@available(iOS 27, *)
struct CrossFadeNavigation<SheetContent: View>: ViewModifier {
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    @ViewBuilder var sheetContent: () -> SheetContent

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.sheet(isPresented: $isPresented) {
            sheetContent()
                .navigationTransition(.crossFade)
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 27, *)
extension View {
    func crossFadeSheet<SheetContent: View>(
        isPresented: Binding<Bool>,
        @ViewBuilder content: @escaping () -> SheetContent
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(CrossFadeNavigation(isPresented: isPresented, sheetContent: content))
    }
}
```
